title: Untitled
content:
BUSAN, South Korea -- Undercurrent News reported from this year's Busan International Seafood & Fisheries Expo (BISFE), which took place at the BEXCO exhibition center from Nov. 5-7.

Hosted by Busan Metropolitan City, BISFE ranks among Asia's top three seafood and fisheries trade fairs and is Korea's largest, featuring 430 exhibitors from 22 countries.

The event serves as a significant platform connecting South Korean and international seafood companies through buyer-matching sessions and industry tours.

It also showcases new products and technologies across aquaculture, seafood processing, marine bio, and fisheries equipment sectors.

Auto updates: On
NOV 67:13 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Canada’s Crustaces de Malbaie eyes Asia amid China tariffs, US trade uncertainty

Crustaces de Malbaie, a crustacean processor based in the Canadian province of Quebec, is seeking new overseas markets amid rising uncertainty in global trade, as China’s 25% tariff on Canadian seafood and unclear US policy clouds the outlook for its main export destinations.

“We need to find new markets as soon as possible,” production director Ricky Rehel told Undercurrent.

READ MORE
NOV 66:56 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Dongwon F&B partners with South Jeolla to boost seafood consumption

Dongwon F&B has signed a memorandum of understanding with South Jeolla Province to promote seafood consumption and expand sales channels for regional products.

The agreement, signed on Oct. 24, aims to develop co-branded seafood products that combine the province’s rich marine resources with Dongwon’s processing expertise.

READ MORE
NOV 66:49 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Korea moves to scrap 36 more coastal fishing vessels to boost resource recovery

South Korea’s Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) has announced plans to decommission 36 additional coastal fishing vessels as part of its ongoing structural reform to better align fishing capacity with depleted marine resources.

The measure, outlined in a public notice issued on Oct. 24, expands the 2025 coastal fleet reduction program initially announced in January. 

READ MORE
NOV 66:42 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Russia’s pollock surimi poised to surpass US in Korea’s imports

South Korea’s frozen surimi block imports rose 13% year-on-year to 99,128 metric tons in the first nine months of 2025, driven by strong shipments from Russia and steady demand for non-pollock grades, according to the latest data from the Korea Customs Service.

Imports of pollock surimi climbed 17% to 23,655t, with Russian volumes surging 41% to 12,364t, overtaking US shipments of 11,291t. 

READ MORE
NOV 64:16 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
India’s Gadre Marine sees slight dip in US imitation crab stick exports

India’s largest producer of surimi-based imitation crab sticks, Gadre Marine Export, has seen a slight decline in exports to the US due to the impact of Trump tariffs, a senior company executive told Undercurrent.

“When we use Alaska pollock surimi blocks as raw material, a significant portion of the product is exempt from reciprocal tariffs,” the executive said. “However, the 25% duty related to sanctions on Russia still applies in such cases.”

READ MORE
NOV 64:04 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Trident targets Korean retail market with pollock, cod value-added lines

US seafood giant Trident Seafoods is working to expand demand for its value-added products in South Korea’s retail market, Han Sol Kim, senior manager at subsidiary Trident Japan, told Undercurrent.

Since the pandemic, Trident has been gradually introducing finished retail products to the Korean market, Kim said. 

READ MORE
NOV 63:26 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
India’s Sea Star plans to boost itoyori surimi exports to Korea

India’s leading surimi block producer, Sea Star Frozen Foods, intends to step up exports to South Korea, as its owner, Dharmesh Chudasama, sees growing demand there for higher-grade products.

“Korea imposes a 10% tariff on Indian surimi, compared with 5% for Vietnamese products,” he said, noting the disadvantage against regional competitors. 

READ MORE
NOV 511:52 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Korean Pacific mackerel prices surge on tight supply, strong demand

Export prices for Pacific mackerel caught off South Korea are soaring amid tightening supplies and surging demand as buyers seek alternatives to costly Atlantic fish, sources told Undercurrent.

Prices have doubled from a year ago, with traders describing the rise as “skyrocketing.”

READ MORE
NOV 55:17 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Alaska pollock producers hold Busan inspections for 800t of B season roe

Alaska pollock producers held inspection sessions for their 2025 B season pollock roe auctions at bonded cold storage facilities in Busan on Wednesday, sources told Undercurrent. 

According to documents shared with Undercurrent, four producers offered a combined 798 metric tons of roe for viewing. 

READ MORE
NOV 512:49 AM GMT
By Masaiko Takeuchi
Indonesian sashimi-grade yellowfin tuna supplier ramps up export diversification as 19% US tariffs hit

Indonesian sashimi-grade tuna exporter Harta Samudra is accelerating efforts to expand its market presence in Asia and Europe after the Trump administration imposed a new 19% tariff on the country, chief sales officer Selvya Tjoanda told Undercurrent News.

“About 90% of our exports used to go to the US,” Tjoanda said, noting that the company primarily shipped smoked and gas-treated yellowfin loins, which had previously faced zero tariffs.

READ MORE
NOV 512:48 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
India diversifies seafood exports amid US tariffs but faces hurdles in Korea

India is accelerating efforts to diversify seafood exports to Asian markets such as South Korea, as the United States maintains combined tariffs of 50% on Indian seafood products, S. Shassi, deputy director of the Marine Products Export Development Authority, told Undercurrent.

“The US has imposed a 25% tariff, and an additional 25% due to its stance on India’s relations with Russia,” she said, noting that the punitive rates have sharply eroded the competitiveness of Indian shrimp and other seafood products in its largest market.

READ MORE
NOV 512:44 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
South Korea launches seafood distribution reform to cut costs, improve transparency

South Korea’s Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) has unveiled a comprehensive plan to streamline the country’s seafood distribution system, aiming to reduce costs by 10% and curb price volatility by 25% by 2030.

Announced on Nov. 4, the Seafood Distribution Structure Improvement Plan seeks to simplify the traditional six-step trading process — from fishermen to wholesalers and retailers — into four stages: producer, regional Fishery Product Center (FPC), Fresh Distribution Center (FDC), and retailer.

title: Untitled
content:
QINGDAO, China -- Undercurrent News reported from this year's China Fisheries and Seafood Exhibition (CFSE) held at the Hongdao International Convention and Exhibition Center in Qingdao, China, Oct. 29-31.

Before that, there was the Norway-China Seafood Summit and Canada Seafood Conference, held at the Haitian Center on Oct. 28, one day before the main show's opening.

CFSE is China's largest seafood trade show, central to the marketing calendars of international seafood companies in China. Domestic Chinese seafood companies are expected to turn out in force, too.

Auto updates: On
NOV 25:33 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Chilean coho farmer Aysen launches large-scale production of salted bone-in fillets

Chilean coho salmon farmer Salmones Aysen has begun producing salted (locally known as “teien”) bone-in fillets for export to Japan — the world’s largest market for the species — marking its first venture into a category traditionally dominated by Japanese secondary processors.

Production for the 2025/26 season has already been “fully sold out,” Jorge Guzman Espinola, the company’s commercial director, told Undercurrent.

READ MORE
OCT 3111:09 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Norwegian pelagic sector braces for second year of capelin fishing ban

Norway’s pelagic sector is bracing for a second consecutive year without a Barents Sea capelin season, as expectations mount that the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES) will again recommend a zero quota for 2026, multiple sources told Undercurrent.

Capelin fishing was already halted in 2025 after ICES advised a zero total allowable catch last autumn, and industry participants now fear a repeat for the coming year.

READ MORE
OCT 319:09 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Atlantic cod becomes ‘luxury item’ in China as prices hit record highs

The price of Atlantic cod continues to surge, reaching unprecedented levels and weighing on China’s consumer market, with sales now declining.

“Cod prices have gone up too much. Every product has a price ceiling—if prices rise too high, consumption will inevitably fall,” Peng Song, chairman of Qingdao Beiyang Jiamei Seafood, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 318:57 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Turkish group invests in Venezuela’s Grupo Lamar after gov’t takeover

A Turkish investment group has acquired a stake in Venezuela’s largest shrimp producer, Grupo Lamar, injecting capital into the company nearly a year after the government seized it from its former owners.

The investment — which was sealed three months ago — will fund expansion across Grupo Lamar’s entire value chain, from hatcheries to processing facilities, Frank Sanoja, the company’s sales manager, told Undercurrent at CFSE. The firm expects to reach 70,000 metric tons of annual shrimp production next year.

READ MORE
OCT 318:20 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Vietnam pangasius shortages expected in Q1 after typhoons

Vietnam’s pangasius industry faces supply shortages starting in early 2026 after typhoons disrupted fingerling production, said a director at major producer Vinh Hoan.

Recent typhoons lowered water temperatures by several degrees Celsius, hurting fingerling mortality rates and growth in the fourth quarter, Tien La told Undercurrent at CFSE.

READ MORE
OCT 315:36 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Ecuadorian shrimp prices won’t decline, says Omarsa’s boss

Raw shrimp prices in Ecuador are likely to continue rising — or at least remain steady — as global demand remains robust, according to Sandro Coglitore, general manager of Ecuadorian shrimp producer Omarsa.

During the Qingdao show week, Ecuadorian packers raised their offers to the Chinese market by $0.20 per kilogram, even as many buyers were still anticipating a price drop.

READ MORE
OCT 314:30 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Indian shrimp producer West Coast eyes tilapia farming

Indian black tiger shrimp producer West Coast is exploring tilapia farming as part of a “China plus one” strategy, a company director told Undercurrent.

The move comes as uncertainty over US-China trade relations prompts buyers to diversify their sourcing from the world’s largest producer.

READ MORE
OCT 314:11 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Pacific mackerel prices soar in Japan, South Korea amid tight Atlantic supply

Pacific mackerel prices in South Korea and Japan have surged sharply in recent weeks as buyers turn to the species as a cheaper substitute for increasingly expensive Northeast Atlantic mackerel, multiple sources told Undercurrent.

“In addition to strong domestic demand, inquiries from Japan and the EU have risen noticeably,” said a sales executive at a South Korean pelagic exporter. “Prices are climbing daily — in Korea, people are saying, ‘today’s price is the lowest.'”

READ MORE
OCT 313:42 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan’s seafood export resumption to China may be delayed until after Lunar New Year

Concerns are growing that Japan’s long-awaited resumption of seafood exports to China may not materialize until after the Lunar New Year in early 2026, despite earlier signs of progress between the two governments.

“Three Japanese companies were approved for facility registration in July, which was a necessary step for re-export, but there has been no movement since then,” a source operating several Japanese restaurants in Shanghai told Undercurrent. “Normally, this process should take only about a month.”

READ MORE
OCT 313:35 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
India’s Jeelani Marine targets 14,000t of black tiger exports in 2026

Indian seafood company Jeelani Marine plans to more than double its black tiger shrimp exports next year to 14,000 metric tons, primarily targeting China’s growing appetite for the crustacean, the company’s CEO said.

The expansion comes as black tiger shrimp prices in India have surged 15% in recent weeks amid tight global supplies and strong Chinese demand, with the Asian giant absorbing up to 45,000t of this year’s production.

READ MORE
OCT 313:09 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Russia’s Pacific sardine catches plummet after Kamchatka quake

Russia’s Pacific sardine catches have plummeted to just 100,000 metric tons this year, an 80% shortfall from the expected 500,000t harvest, according to an executive at a major Russian seafood processing company.

The dramatic decline followed an earthquake near Kamchatka in late July that appears to have disrupted fish migration patterns. Catches essentially halted from that point onward, the executive said at CFSE.

READ MORE
OCT 3011:19 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
China’s 25% additional tariff continues to hinder Canadian lobster exports

China’s additional tariff on Canadian products remains one of the major obstacles for Canadian lobster exports to the Chinese market, according to Geoff Irvine, executive director of The Lobster Council of Canada.

China imposed the 25% additional tariff on Canadian lobster in April in response to Canada’s 100% tariff on electric vehicles made in China. As of now, the Chinese tariff on Canadian lobster stands at 32%, with an additional 9% value-added tax (VAT).

READ MORE
OCT 3010:31 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Argentine red shrimp stocks already empty, disappointing China buyers

Chinese buyers were unable to secure Argentine red shrimp at this week’s Qingdao show, as suppliers’ inventories had already been sold out, a source told Undercurrent.

The 2025 offshore season was shorter than usual, as strikes delayed fishing operations and caused the industry to miss its initial months. The season has now concluded, with total landings reaching only about half of last year’s volume.

READ MORE
OCT 307:00 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Canadian roe capelin prices ease from record highs but remain well above 2024 levels

Frozen roe-bearing capelin prices from the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador have gradually fallen from the record-high offers seen right after the 2025 season, multiple trade sources told Undercurrent.

The step-by-step decline follows what buyers described as “unrealistically high” packer offers that the market could not absorb in the immediate post-season period.

READ MORE
OCT 306:52 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China eyes New Zealand hoki as Atlantic cod substitute

Soaring Atlantic cod prices may push Chinese seafood buyers toward cheaper alternatives like New Zealand hoki, according to a major Chinese importer and processor.

Norwegian headed and gutted (H&G) Atlantic cod hit $10,000 per metric ton this month while Russian cod reached $8,600, according to Joe Qiao, general manager of Qingdao Meichu Food. Prices have since increased further, according to Undercurrent’s weekly price assessment, with little relief in sight.

READ MORE
OCT 306:28 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Chilean jack mackerel export prices surge to record highs amid firm demand, tight Atlantic outlook

Chilean jack mackerel prices for southern Europe and Africa have soared to historic levels, driven by firm demand and expectations of a sharp cut in Atlantic mackerel quotas, multiple sources told Undercurrent.

“Although Chile is now in the off-season, it’s rare to see prices rise this high,” said a senior sales executive at one of the country’s producers. “Once fishing resumes and supply increases, prices should settle down,” he added.

READ MORE
OCT 305:56 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Russian H&G pollock prices for China rise further above UCN’s week 44 assessment

Headed and gutted (H&G) Russian pollock prices have climbed further this week, trading $20–$30 per metric ton above Undercurrent’s week 44 assessment, as Russian suppliers seek even higher levels, according to multiple Chinese processors.

The increases come as sellers maintain firm offers amid robust domestic demand in Russia and limited spot availability, while Chinese buyers grow increasingly cautious about taking new volumes. 

READ MORE
OCT 305:08 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
US reduces tariffs on Chinese tilapia to 45%, exempt haddock

The US has reduced the tariff on Chinese tilapia exports to 45%, following a recent meeting between the two countries’ leaders in Busan, South Korea, on Oct. 30, as reported by Chinese state media Xinhua.

The US will cancel the 10% “fentanyl tariff” imposed on Chinese goods, including those from Hong Kong and Macau. Additionally, the 24% reciprocal tariff on Chinese products will remain suspended for another year, according to Xinhua.

READ MORE
OCT 304:39 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Vietnamese pangasius exports to China see first decline 

Vietnam’s pangasius exports to China have declined for the first time in recent years, as more Chinese consumers question the reputation of the fish, according to industry sources.

Between January and August 2025, the value of Vietnam’s pangasius exports to China dropped by approximately 10% year-on-year, marking the first significant decline in recent years, said Xindong Chen, general manager of Octogone. Octogone is the sales agent for Vinh Hoan, Vietnam’s largest pangasius exporter, in China.

READ MORE
OCT 3012:47 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Norway’s Ode expands rapidly in China as premium ‘Snow Cod’ gains traction

Norwegian farmed cod producer Ode has seen China become its largest Asian market within a short period after entering the country earlier this year, sales manager Kristoffer Remo told Undercurrent.

Ode markets its Atlantic cod globally under the “Snow Cod” brand, which has earned strong praise from Chinese buyers for its distinctive firmness and “super white color,” in addition to its clean flavor. 

READ MORE
OCT 2910:33 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Peruvian jumbo squid exporters await clarity on Chinese stocks after bumper catches

Peruvian jumbo squid exporters are anxiously watching Chinese inventory levels after the South American nation’s bumper catch 600,000 metric tons this year, sources said at CFSE.

Peru, one of the world’s largest catchers of giant jumbo squid, is coming off what producers described as its best season in a decade, a dramatic reversal from 2024 when catches collapsed to less than 200,000t, said Rafael Romano, commercial manager at major exporter Pesquera Exalmar.

READ MORE
OCT 299:38 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Icelandic capelin processors expected to skip roe output amid low quota outlook

Icelandic capelin processors are preparing to forgo production of roe products — the raw material used to make “ebiko” — unless next season’s quota rises significantly, multiple sources told Undercurrent.

“At the current advisory level, we have no choice but to freeze roe-bearing capelin whole, rather than producing roe,” a senior sales executive at a leading Icelandic packer said. “To justify roe production, we would need a total quota of at least 150,000 metric tons.”

READ MORE
OCT 298:15 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Chilean coho farmers lift offers as Asian demand firms

Chilean coho salmon farmers have begun raising offer prices after months of steady declines, driven by recovering demand outside Japan, several industry sources told Undercurrent.

“The rebound is mainly due to stronger demand in non-Japanese markets,” a senior executive at one of Chile’s major producers said. “Even in Japan, higher retail prices for competing species such as Atlantic mackerel are providing some tailwind.”

READ MORE
OCT 297:21 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China, Russia sign deal to expand pollock roe cooperation

Russia’s Pollock Catchers Association and the China Aquatic Products Processing and Marketing Alliance have signed a memorandum of agreement to strengthen cooperation in the production, research, and marketing of pollock roe in China, a milestone move in Russia’s ongoing bid to diversify away from its traditional Northeast Asian markets.

The agreement was signed in Qingdao on Wednesday (Oct. 29) by Alexey Buglak, president of the PCA, and Wang Xueguang, vice president of CAPPMA, during the Russia–China Pollock Forum, held during the China Fisheries & Seafood Expo.

READ MORE
OCT 2912:46 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Ecuador shrimp prices for China rise at Qingdao show with reports of buyers low on stocks

Ecuadorian head-on, shell-on (HOSO) shrimp prices for shipments to China have risen by $0.20 per kilogram across all sizes and categories during week 44 of 2025 (Oct. 27–Nov. 2). 

That includes semi-IQF and brine-IQF in both retail and bulk packaging.

READ MORE
OCT 2911:47 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Indian fishmeal prices surge as Chinese demand outpaces Japan, EU

India’s fishmeal export prices have jumped in recent weeks amid surging demand from China’s aquaculture feed sector, sources told Undercurrent.

“Chinese buyers are actively seeking supplies for use in feed for species such as silver carp and vannamei shrimp,” a major Indian producer said. “Prices offered by China have already beaten those for Europe and Japan by a wide margin.”

READ MORE
OCT 2911:28 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Australian lobsters make a triumphant return to China

A year after China resumed imports of Australian live lobsters, around 80% of Aussie rock lobsters have returned to the Chinese market, accompanied by a sharp rise in prices.

“This is the first year since China lifted the trade ban. The first batch of live lobsters was allowed to enter the Chinese market on Dec. 24 last year, and sales have skyrocketed from zero,” said Cater Yu, China sales manager of Geraldton Fishermen’s Co-operative (GFC), the largest lobster quota holder in Australia.

READ MORE
OCT 2910:40 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
NSC: Cod supply challenges loom as US haddock market faces Russia ban

Cod and haddock markets face a turbulent 2026 as global cod supply drops 10% while a US ban on Russian haddock threatens to upend processing flows, a Norwegian industry analyst warned.

Norway confronts a sharp 21% quota reduction for cod based on joint scientific advice with Russia for Barents Sea stocks, while Iceland, now the world’s largest cod producer, will also trim output slightly, Eivind Braekkan, a seafood analyst at the Norwegian Seafood Council, told the Norway-China Seafood Summit in Qingdao.

READ MORE
OCT 298:09 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Russia approves 2% quota increase for 2026 Far East pollock

Russia’s Ministry of Agriculture has approved the country’s 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) for pollock at 2.42 million metric tons for its Far Eastern fisheries, up 1.7% from 2025, sources told Undercurrent at the show. 

The TAC for next year, detailed in the annex to Order No. 692, shows higher allocations across nearly all Far Eastern fishing zones, signaling the end of a precautionary reduction phase in the Sea of Okhotsk.

READ MORE
OCT 297:36 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Irish fishing co-op eyes more than doubling langoustine sales to China

Ireland’s Castletownbere Fisherman’s Co-op aims to boost langoustine (Nephrops norvegicus) sales to China to 500 metric tons in 2026 from just 200t this year.

The cooperative, which claims about 40% of Ireland’s langoustine catch with 62 vessels, began exporting to China in July after completing a 12-month registration process, sales manager Larkin Harrington told Undercurrent News at CFSE.

READ MORE
OCT 294:51 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu 
Ecuador’s AquaGold strikes partnership with Chinese supply chain company

Ecuador’s third-largest shrimp farmer, AquaGold, has entered into a strategic cooperation agreement with a Chinese supply chain service provider, coinciding with the first anniversary of its processing plant operations.

At the Qingdao expo, AquaGold announced that it has authorized Tianjin J-One Supply Chain Management Co. to serve as its sole designated representative office in China. The company will be responsible for AquaGold’s market promotion and sales within the Chinese market, effective Oct. 28, 2025.

READ MORE
OCT 294:02 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Chinese processors boost shrimp imports 

Chinese shrimp processing plants are stepping up raw material imports as inventories have run low.

Changgui Song, general manager of Guangdong Rainbow Aquatic Development — a major value-added seafood processor — told Undercurrent that more buyers are turning to Ecuador for additional supply amid depleted stocks.

READ MORE
OCT 291:19 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Norway’s pelagic sector faces possible consolidation amid sharp quota cuts

Norway’s pelagic industry could face structural changes as major reductions in catch quotas for key species, including mackerel, herring, capelin and blue whiting, loom for 2026, sources told Undercurrent.

“The country’s combined pelagic quota for 2026 may shrink to no more than one-third of this year’s level,” warned a senior sales executive at a major packer, noting that industry consolidation is “not unlikely.”

READ MORE
OCT 285:56 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Norway captures 27% of China’s coldwater shrimp market

Norway has seized a 27% share of China’s coldwater shrimp market in a dramatic surge from just 2% a year ago, capitalizing on tariffs that hobbled Canadian exporters and strong demand.

China has become the largest market for Norwegian coldwater shrimp “overnight,” with exports rocketing nearly 500% to add 6,200 metric tons through September, Sigmund Bjorgo, the Norwegian Seafood Council’s China director, told the Norway-China Seafood Summit in Qingdao.

READ MORE
OCT 285:39 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
‘Fresh-cut’ salmon shops take hold in China’s smaller cities

A new wave of community-based “fresh-cut” salmon outlets is rapidly spreading across China, driven by rising demand for convenience, transparency, and freshness in lower-tier urban markets.

At the Norway–China Seafood Summit, Sun Gaochao, co-founder and general manager of Jingzhe Salmon, said the Shanghai-headquartered chain now operates more than 700 outlets nationwide, with over 95% profitable. 

READ MORE
OCT 285:20 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Canadian coldwater shrimp set to gain ground in China

Canadian coldwater shrimp are expected to gain a stronger foothold in the Chinese market over the remainder of 2025 and into 2026, according to Bruce Chapman, executive director of the Canadian Association of Prawn Producers (CAPP).

Chapman told Undercurrent that Canada remains one of the main suppliers of coldwater shrimp to China, despite the 25% tariff imposed by Beijing. Meanwhile, Norwegian exports have also grown rapidly this year.

READ MORE
OCT 284:09 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
NSC: China poised to become fifth-largest salmon market in 2025

China is on track to surpass Italy and become the world’s fifth-largest market for Atlantic salmon before year-end, according to Sigmund Bjorgo, China director at the Norwegian Seafood Council.

The country has already climbed to sixth place globally with imports of 155,000 metric tons on a rolling 12-month basis. The Asian giant is now poised to leapfrog Italy in the final quarter, Bjorgo told the Norway-China Seafood Summit in Qingdao.

READ MORE
OCT 284:04 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Salmon, e-commerce lift China to No. 3 spot for Norwegian seafood exports

China has become Norway’s third-largest seafood market by both volume and value, nearly doubling from a year earlier, as the country’s recovering consumption and fast-developing e-commerce platforms drive new opportunities for exporters, Norwegian Seafood Council CEO Christian Chramer said.

Speaking at the Norway–China Seafood Summit, Chramer said that while the US remains Norway’s fastest-growing market overall, China’s rebound has been particularly strong, with salmon still the key species but “other traditional species such as mackerel, cod and shrimp gaining ground.”

READ MORE
OCT 2711:43 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Wholesale salmon prices in China fall for all origins

Wholesale Atlantic salmon prices in major Chinese cities declined in week 44 (Oct. 27–Nov. 2), as increased arrivals weighed on the market.

In Guangzhou, prices for Norwegian salmon — head-on, gutted (HOG), weighing 6–7 kilograms — fell by CNY 4 ($0.56) per kilogram week-on-week on Monday (Oct. 27), pushing some importers into losses.

READ MORE
OCT 2710:38 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu 
Ecuadorian shrimp offers rise ahead of busy week for deals

Ecuadorian shrimp companies raised their offerings to China in week 44 (Oct. 27- Nov. 2), with packers increasing their quoted prices by around $0.20 per kilogram during the Qingdao show, aiming to gauge buyers’ reactions.

According to company quotations, the mainstream 30/40 semi-IQF shrimp size rose to $5.00/kg CFR. Other semi-IQF shrimp sizes were quoted as follows:

READ MORE
OCT 2710:19 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Tilapia prices show signs of rebound 

Tilapia raw material prices in China have shown signs of rising, as the US confirmed it will maintain a 55% tariff instead of imposing an additional 100% tariff from November 1.

In Guangdong province, prices for 500–800 gram tilapia delivered to processing plants increased by CNY 0.1 per kilogram to CNY 6.8/kg ($0.96/kg) in week 44 (Oct. 27–Nov. 2). 

READ MORE

title: Seafood Show LATAM: Maris, Frumar talk expansion plans; Cod market in Brazil faces shifts amid high prices
content:
SAO PAULO, Brazil -- Undercurrent News reported from the Seafood Show Latin America 2025, the fourth edition of the event. It took place in Sao Paulo, Brazil, from Oct. 21 to 23.

According to the show's organizers, the event brings together the leading players of the Brazilian seafood industry, including producers, suppliers, retailers, wholesalers, distributors, foodservice professionals, importers, exporters and machinery manufacturers.

Organized by Francal in partnership with Seafood Brasil, the event aims to strengthen the seafood production chain, promote market growth in Brazil and drive trade across Latin America.

Auto updates: On
OCT 235:22 PM GMT
Winner of Brazil’s sushi championship announced

Brazil’s sushi championship took place during the Seafood Show Latin America. It crowned William Utida as the winner of this year’s edition. 

Iberconsa, a Spanish supplier of Argentine red shrimp and hake, Spanish bluefin tuna supplier Balfego, and local distributor Frumar were the official sponsors of the championship. 

READ MORE
OCT 234:23 PM GMT
Maris expands as a vertically integrated shrimp producer

Brazilian seafood company Maris Pescados is expanding its operations and moving toward full vertical integration, positioning itself among a small group of domestic producers that control every stage of the shrimp production process.

Although Maris was formally established in 2012, its origins go back to Copescal, a seafood group founded in 1985 in the state of Ceara. Copescal began with lobster exports and later helped introduce shrimp-farming technology in Brazil, contributing to the sector’s development.

READ MORE
OCT 234:16 PM GMT
Brazilian distributor Frumar aims to expand into retail, foodservice 

Brazilian distributor Frumar aims to reinforce its position as one of the country’s largest salmon processors and distributors, with strategic investments aimed at expanding its footprint in both the retail and foodservice sectors.

Frumar’s director, Eder Krummenauer, told Undercurrent News the firm operates a 7,000-square-meter industrial plant in Santa Catarina, employing about 400 people and processing around 180 metric tons of salmon per week. Salmon represents approximately half of the company’s business, with the rest divided among other frozen and fresh seafood lines.

READ MORE
OCT 237:13 AM GMT
Taxation reform might hit seafood consumption in Brazil

Brazil is implementing a major overhaul of its consumption tax system, which is currently being discussed in the country’s congress.

Those upcoming changes, unless modified, risk impacting the consumption of salmon and other seafood products in Brazil, according to industry sources.

READ MORE
OCT 228:53 PM GMT
Japanese cuisine drives seafood consumption, quality in Brazil

Japanese cuisine has become one of the main forces driving seafood consumption and improving product quality in Brazil, according to Roberto Kikuo Imai, deputy director of the agricultural department of FIESP, the fishing industry committee of the federation of industries of the state of Sao Paulo.

Representing the entire aquaculture and seafood production chain in the country, from feed and equipment suppliers to academics and restaurant owners, Imai (second from the left in the photo below) highlighted how Japanese culinary influence has reshaped Brazilian eating habits and strengthened the domestic seafood market. 

READ MORE
OCT 228:37 PM GMT
Cod market in Brazil faces shifts amid high prices

The cod market in Brazil is undergoing significant changes as suppliers adapt to new consumer habits, rising prices, and growing competition from direct imports, according to industry sources.

Industry sources with some cod distributors told Undercurrent News that customers are purchasing smaller quantities of cod, opting for more affordable species rather than abandoning the category entirely. 

READ MORE
OCT 228:40 AM GMT
US tariffs challenge Brazilian tilapia exporters, but domestic market cushions blow

Brazilian tilapia producers are grappling with the effects of the new US tariffs that have made exporting fish to their main international market far less profitable. 

While the US remains an attractive destination due to its high margins, the new 50% tariffs have forced Brazilian companies to reconsider their export strategies, negatively impacting their profit margins.

READ MORE
OCT 228:39 AM GMT
NSC: High prices pressure whitefish trade

Oystein Valanes, head of market access at the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC), pointed out that Brazil remains one of the most significant markets for salted and dried whitefish. 

He noted that the total volume of whitefish exports to Brazil has remained largely stable over the past four years, maintaining levels similar to the 10-year average. 

READ MORE
OCT 2111:05 PM GMT
High prices are testing Brazilian love of Norwegian cod

Leif Haagensen, head of the advisory division for conventional products at the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC), has described Brazil as a “price-sensitive market,” where cod remains both a cherished tradition and a financial challenge for consumers. 

“Price continues to be one of the most important factors in the consumer’s purchasing decision,” she said. 

READ MORE
OCT 2110:42 PM GMT
Norwegian cod fishery still ‘cornerstone’ of coastal economies despite lower quotas

Despite reduced quotas, Norway’s cod fishery remains a cornerstone of the country’s coastal economy, according to Charles Aas, CEO of the Norwegian Fishermen’s Sales Organization.

Norwegian fishermen live in the communities along the coast, Aas said, and the country’s fishing industry remains deeply tied to local economies. 

READ MORE
OCT 2111:31 AM GMT
Norway eyes opportunities in Brazil thanks to new FTA

Norway’s minister of fisheries and ocean policy, Marianne Sivertsen Naess, said the newly signed free trade agreement (FTA) between Norway and MERCOSUR is a “milestone” for global trade and the seafood industry.

Norway and MERCOSUR signed an FTA on Sept. 16, 2025, as part of the broader EFTA-MERCOSUR deal. 

READ MORE
OCT 2111:10 AM GMT
Seafood Show LATAM aims to become the region’s leading exhibition

The Seafood Show Latin America, now in its fourth edition, continues to grow in size and influence, solidifying its position as a key player in the Latin American seafood industry, according to its organizers. 

This year, the event is expected to welcome nearly 5,000 visitors and will occupy more than 10,000 square meters at the Anhembi exhibition center in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

READ MORE

title: Untitled
content:
TOKYO, Japan -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the annual conference of the Marine Ingredients Organisation, IFFO, held in Tokyo, Japan, Oct. 20-22.

This year's conference takes place against a backdrop of sharply rising fishmeal prices amid more scarce stocks in China, the world's largest fishmeal buyer. Expect a trove of data and analysis shared by experts and speakers from the industry.

Auto updates: On
OCT 2210:31 PM GMT
Maersk exec: Freight rates could plummet if Middle East peace holds

Freight rates for seafood shipments could fall dramatically if the Gaza ceasefire leads to the reopening of the Red Sea shipping lane, according to Thue Barfod, global director of fish and seafood at A.P. Moller-Maersk.

Rates currently stand just above $1,000 per container on the Shanghai Containerized Freight Index — elevated from the $1,000 level Barfod considers a balanced market — but could drop sharply as vessel capacity shifts from severe shortage to projected oversupply of approximately 10% by 2026 if the Suez Canal reopens, he said.

OCT 227:17 PM GMT
China fishmeal imports surge as domestic output falls, consumption rises

China appears set to require even higher fishmeal imports as domestic production continues to decline while consumption from aquaculture grows.

The country’s fishmeal imports jumped 19% to 1.96 million metric tons in 2024 from 1.65m metric tons the previous year, as domestic output tumbled 26% to 551,000t, down from 744,000t in 2023.

OCT 224:53 AM GMT
Japan fishmeal demand seen jumping to 380,000t by 2026

Japan’s fishmeal consumption is forecast to rise to 380,000 metric tons in 2026 from around 330,000t estimated for 2025, with more than half imported, as aquaculture production recovers from recent lows.

Peru and Chile will account for about 35% of imports by 2026, down from 46% in 2021, as Japan diversifies sourcing to India, Oman, the US and New Zealand, Hikaru Kondo, trader at Kanematsu Corporation in Japan, told the IFFO conference on Wednesday.

OCT 224:41 AM GMT
Fish oil exports fall as salmon sector tightens grip on supplies

Global fish oil exports declined to 973,000 metric tons in 2024, down from 1.04 million metric tons the previous year, IFFO data showed.

The reduced production left salmon farmers claiming an ever-larger share of available supplies, with the segment’s portion of aquaculture fish oil consumption rising to 59.1% in 2024 from 56.3% in 2023, according to figures presented by Enrico Bachis, market research director at IFFO, at the group’s Tokyo conference on Wednesday.

OCT 224:08 AM GMT
China devours half of world’s aquaculture fishmeal as imports surge

China consumed 50.7% of all fishmeal used in global aquaculture in 2024, a dramatic jump from 42.9% the previous year, according to data presented at the IFFO conference.

The world’s largest aquaculture producer accounted for 48.2% of global fishmeal imports last year, importing 1.96 million metric tons compared to 1.65m metric tons in 2023, Enrico Bachis, market research director at IFFO, told delegates.

OCT 216:44 PM GMT
Most single-cell protein startups have failed to reach commercial scale, says Calysta exec

Most companies trying to produce single-cell proteins as aquafeed ingredients have failed to reach commercial scale, said a senior executive at one of the few commercial producers.

“Most people have failed. Most people have not gone beyond those academic papers, those nice ideas,” Matt Longshaw, research and application manager at Calysta, told conference attendees.

OCT 217:36 AM GMT
Climate change forecast to hit forage fisheries less hard than other seafood sectors

Forage fisheries will take a smaller climate hit than larger fish species, facing just 5% productivity losses by century’s end — but unprecedented ocean changes threaten even well-managed stocks, a leading researcher warned.

Dr. Christopher Free, a research professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, said forage fisheries — which supply the fishmeal and fish oil sectors — would fare better than larger-bodied pelagics like tuna as climate impacts amplify up the food chain.

OCT 216:40 AM GMT
Aquafeed costs to remain subdued as soybean prices expected low through 2027

Aquaculture producers can expect relief on feed costs for at least the next two to three years as soybean prices remain in a low-price cycle, a senior Rabobank analyst said.

Oscar Tjakra, executive director of RaboResearch Food and Agribusiness at Rabobank Singapore, told IFFO attendees that soymeal prices — a key determinant of aquafeed maker margins — have trended downward since March 2025 and are likely to stay subdued through at least 2027.

OCT 207:55 PM GMT
Emerging markets in Africa, Asia to fuel next wave of seafood growth

Forget chasing China’s slowing economy. The seafood industry needs to pivot its attention to where the real long-term growth lies: Africa and South Asia.

That was the clear message from Robin Harding, Asia editor of the Financial Times, speaking on a panel discussion.

OCT 207:01 PM GMT
Seafood companies urged to stay course on sustainability as political winds shift 

Seafood companies should resist the temptation to abandon sustainability commitments despite the current political climate turning against environmental issues, according to Robin Harding, Asia editor at the Financial Times.

Speaking on a panel, Harding acknowledged that political winds are “blowing very strongly against worrying about anything like this — environment, sustainability, governance, whatever.”

OCT 204:58 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Reduction fisheries lag global sustainability standards, FAO study shows

Fisheries that supply the fishmeal and fish oil industry are less sustainable than the global average, with a higher percentage of stocks overexploited, according to new data from the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization.

Some 38% of reduction fishery stocks are unsustainably exploited, compared with 35.5% for all fisheries worldwide, Manuel Barange, FAO’s director of fisheries and aquaculture, said in a presentation.

Contact the author louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com

title: Groundfish Forum 2025: Chinese renege on May pollock fillet orders; Kyokuyo expects full output at US surimi plant in 2026
content:
TOKYO, Japan – Undercurrent News had three reporters in Tokyo, Japan, to meet top executives in the sector at the annual Groundfish Forum, being held in the opulent Okura Hotel. 

Recap all the coverage below, as prices rose and geopolitics impacted the sector to an unparalleled degree.

Auto updates: On
OCT 2411:06 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chinese renege on May pollock fillet orders for EU with H&G prices rising

Chinese pollock processors are reneging on fillet blocks orders placed by European processors around May when the headed and gutted (H&G) Russian raw material prices were $300-350 per metric ton lower than now, sources at the Groundfish Forum told Undercurrent.

The trend, which comes with Russian and US single frozen fillets largely sold out for B season, has been previously reported by Undercurrent, but was being widely discussed at the forum in Tokyo, Japan, this week.

READ MORE
OCT 2411:01 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Nissui plans to expand J.P. Klausen’s Peru red shrimp processing to other species

Denmark’s J.P. Klausen & Co. is successfully growing its peeling of Argentine red shrimp in Peru, with owner Nissui Corp. planning to expand the business into other species from within the group.

“Nissui sees what we are doing and wants to grow it, make it a group thing,” Jens Peter Klausen, managing director of the trader, told Undercurrent at the forum.

READ MORE
OCT 2410:37 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
US Bering Sea inshore pollock plants have 36,000t of B season quota left to catch as of Oct. 18

The inshore plant sector of the Bering Sea pollock fishery in the US state of Alaska still had 35,981 metric tons of B season quota remaining as of the week ended Oct. 18, according to the latest weekly catch report from the Genuine Alaska Pollock Producers.

The report showed total inshore catches at 294,894t out of a quota of 330,875t. The National Marine Fisheries Service has not updated its own weekly catch data since the start of the US federal government shutdown on Oct. 1, however.

READ MORE
OCT 244:34 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Kyokuyo expects full 3,000t output at US surimi stick plant in 2026

Japan’s Kyokuyo Co. expects to reach its initial annual output target of 3,000 metric tons of imitation crab surimi products at its new Kent, Washington, US, facility in 2026 — a year later than initially planned — executive vice president Shigeru Kondo told Undercurrent.

The plant, completed in December 2024 and operated by Kyokuyo’s US subsidiary Ocean’s Kitchen Corp., began production earlier this year. 

READ MORE
OCT 2412:29 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
South African hake quota expected to be stable-to-down for 2026

When looking through this year’s supply projections from the Grounfish Forum, for most wild-caught species, the outlook is for heavy catch reductions in both the Barents and Bering Seas in particular.

However, global hake supplies continue to buck the trend.

READ MORE
OCT 2311:54 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
French consumers making switch from cod to salmon, trader confirms

While some European countries like the UK and Portugal have such an inbuilt love affair with cod that substitution is unthinkable, others are less scrupulous.

Bruno Deshayes, commercial director with French trader Cornic-Novamer, told Undercurrent that in French restaurants, the transition to lower-cost species has already been happening this year.

READ MORE
OCT 2311:31 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Norwegian institute confirms cod stock should recover in 2027 – if advice is followed

Following five successive years of declining Barents Sea cod quota advice, Daniel Howell, a researcher with Norway’s Institute of Marine Research, told Undercurrent that 2027 should see the stock start to recover if the institute’s latest advice is followed by Norway and Russia.

“To start with, in 2021 it was really unusually high, because we had two good year classes coming together,” Howell explained. “That huge peak that we had was to do with an unusually good recruitment position that came in just as we were starting to reduce the fishing pressure, it was not a normal thing.”

READ MORE
OCT 2310:55 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
French imitation crab stick demand sees modest rebound, but market remains stagnant

France, Europe’s largest surimi consumer, has seen a “slight recovery” in imitation crab stick demand this year following several years of decline, a Paris-based distributor told Undercurrent.

“Consumption looks set to slightly exceed last year, aided by favorable summer weather,” the distributor said, noting that the category had finally halted its contraction.

READ MORE
OCT 238:14 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Maruha Nichiro reiterates no Russian pollock surimi policy, plans to up US fillet output in A season 2026

Maruha Nichiro, the world’s largest seafood company in revenue, won’t roll back on its commitment not to buy Russian pollock surimi, the executive overseeing the Tokyo, Japan-based company’s global operations told Undercurrent.

Japan’s imports of Russian surimi are rocketing, which is impacting prices for US producers, although both are recovering in 2026, as the data below from the Undercurrent trade portal shows.

READ MORE
OCT 238:08 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Westward is last US Bering Sea pollock plant standing after Trident, UniSea B season closures

Maruha Nichiro’s Westward Seafoods is still processing B-season pollock, after the other large operators in the East Bering Sea, Trident Seafoods and UniSea, have closed for the year, sources told Undercurrent.

Trident’s Akutan plant and Nissui Corp.’s UniSea factory have both closed earlier in October; the former for maintenance and the latter to install a fishmeal dryer.

READ MORE
OCT 232:47 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan consumes one-third of global surimi amid stagnant domestic demand

Global surimi consumption was estimated at 800,000 metric tons in 2024, with Asia, including Japan, accounting for nearly 70% of total demand, sources told Undercurrent.

Asia, excluding Japan, remained the largest consuming region, using about 300,000t in 2024. 

READ MORE
OCT 2211:40 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Farmed cod still restricted to fresh market despite tumbling wild-catch volumes

As Barents Sea cod quotas continue to slide with every passing year, the farmed cod sector has been expected to fill some of the gap. 

In September, for instance, farmed cod accounted for 59% of all Norway’s fresh cod exports, according to the Norwegian Seafood Council, albeit on very limited offseason volumes.

READ MORE
OCT 2211:31 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Kyokuyo eyes European distributor in next stage of M&A

Japan’s Kyokuyo plans to add a European distributor to its growing network in the region in the future, Shigeru Kondo, the company’s executive vice president, told Undercurrent.

Kyokuyo has made several strategic acquisitions in Europe as part of its global expansion strategy. Most recently, in September 2025, Kyokuyo Europe (the company’s Dutch subsidiary) signed an agreement to purchase 90% of shares in Engelsviken Canning Denmark, a seafood processor and distributor based in Skagen, Denmark.

READ MORE
OCT 2211:19 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Norway’s recent saithe price hikes driven by shortage of large fish

Speaking to Undercurrent at the Groundfish Forum in 2023, Nordic Group managing director Morten Jensen expressed his desire that Norwegian exporters grow demand for saithe outside of the country, as the species is traditionally restrained primarily to the saltfish sector.

Now, the price of frozen saithe is up 54% year-on-year, and processors like Nordic are struggling to keep up.

READ MORE
OCT 2211:00 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Some Norwegian quota rollover expected for haddock in 2026, but no cod

Speaking to Undercurrent on the current landings status for Barents Sea cod and haddock, Nordic Group’s Morten Jensen confirmed that with this year’s cod quotas set so low, no ‘rollover’ of quota is expected for next year’s season.

Typically, the Norwegian fleet is able to push up to 10% of the previous year’s catch quotas into the following season if it is not caught by the end of the year; in 2025, for instance, nearly 12,000 metric tons of cod was carried over from 2024’s total allowable catch (TAC).

READ MORE
OCT 227:14 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
US pollock producers continue to prioritize fillets over surimi for 2026 A season

US Alaska pollock producers are expected to prioritize fillet production over surimi for the 2026 A season, multiple industry sources told Undercurrent.

“Given the balance between surimi supply and demand in Asia and Europe, it’s only natural that producers will raise their PBO [pin-bone out] output,” a sales executive at one major Alaska producer said.

READ MORE
OCT 224:07 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Norwegian H&G cod prices move over $10,000/t, Russian pollock edges up

Undercurrent‘s week 43 (Oct. 20-26) delivered China price assessments for headed and gutted (H&G) Norwegian and Russian cod and haddock, and Russian pollock, went live on Oct. 22.

The level for Norwegian trawl-caught and frozen H&G cod rose past $10,000 per metric ton, delivered to China, in week 43. Russian H&G also rose.

READ MORE
OCT 221:22 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Former Trident veteran Suzuki sells Gidrostroy’s Russian surimi in Japan

A company owned by Koichi Suzuki, who previously ran Trident Seafoods’ Japanese operation until 2019, is selling surimi produced by the Russian giant Gidrostroy, sources told Undercurrent.

There’s fierce competition in the Japanese market between US surimi produced by Trident and others, and the newcomers from Russia, such as Russian Fishery Company and Gidrostroy. 

READ MORE
OCT 216:23 AM GMT
By Masaiko Takeuchi
Alaska pollock surimi prices to Europe rise by up to $100/t for B season

Prices for US Alaska pollock surimi blocks shipped to Europe for the 2025 B season rose by $50–$100 per metric ton compared with the A season, a sales executive at a major producer told Undercurrent.

Lower-grade materials such as RA grade blocks — with gel strength of 300 and below — accounted for an estimated 70% of total European-bound shipments, the executive said.

READ MORE
OCT 212:06 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China’s cod consumption boom may slow in 2026 amid high raw material costs

China’s fast-growing domestic market for cod could lose momentum next year after several years of around 20% annual growth, Joe Qiao, president of Winning Food Int’l, a Qingdao-based seafood importer and processor, told Undercurrent.

Qiao estimated current consumption at about 15,000 metric tons per year, split between roughly 10,000t of Atlantic cod and 5,000t of Pacific cod. 

READ MORE
OCT 211:51 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Channel sees US customers drop Pacific cod, haddock with prices ‘out of control’

The record-high price levels on Pacific cod and haddock are seeing US customers walk away, Channel Fish Processing’s Tom Zaffiro told Undercurrent.

Braintree, Massachusetts-based Channel is seeing customers “dropping” Pacific cod and especially haddock products, due to the pricing, he said during the 2025 Groundfish Forum week.

READ MORE
OCT 2011:05 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japanese co-op group to begin handling CSI-certified seafood products 

The Japanese Consumers’ Co-operative Union (JCCU), a major retail group representing more than 30 million members nationwide, plans to begin offering seafood products certified under Certified Seafood International (CSI) standards starting in fiscal year 2026, Satoshi Matsumoto of the union’s brand strategy division said Monday at the Certified Seafood Forum in Tokyo.

The move forms part of JCCU’s broader effort to expand the range of sustainably certified seafood products available under its Co-op brand.

READ MORE
OCT 207:21 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Global surimi output rebounds 6% to 437,000t in H1 as Russia reshapes supply balance

Global surimi production rose 6.3% year-on-year through the second quarter of 2025 to an estimated 437,000 metric tons, extending the recovery that began earlier in the year, according to a new quarterly report prepared for the Genuine Alaska Pollock Producers.

The increase marked the industry’s first broad-based expansion since the pandemic-era volatility of 2021–23, with stronger contributions from Russia and China, which helped offset continued export weakness in the US and lingering stagnation in Japan.

READ MORE
OCT 204:52 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Best Seafood Practices adds ‘above-the-waterline’ assurance to CSI program, says GSA CEO 

Best Seafood Practices (BSP) certification under the Global Seafood Alliance (GSA) complements Certified Seafood International’s (CSI) fishery program by adding “above-the-waterline” assurances covering vessels, processing plants, and social responsibility, CEO Mike Kocsis told the audience at the Certified Seafood Forum held Monday in Tokyo.

“We are not a fishery certification program,” Kocsis said. “Our goal is to complement, not duplicate, what CSI already does well, by adding assurances on social responsibility and operational integrity.”

READ MORE
OCT 204:48 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
CSI rolls out tiered partner fees to make certification more affordable

Certified Seafood International (CSI) is introducing a new tiered funding model designed to make fishery certification more affordable and globally accessible, CEO Mike Kraft said Monday at the Certified Seafood Forum in Tokyo.

Under the new CSI Partner Program, entities that package or sell certified seafood using CSI’s eco-label will pay annual fees ranging from $500 to $100,000, depending on the wholesale value of certified products sold, according to Kraft.

READ MORE
OCT 203:38 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Alaska pollock producers to hold Busan roe auction on Nov. 5

US Alaska pollock producers plan to hold an inspection and auction of roe from the 2025 B season on Nov. 5 in Busan, South Korea, a sales executive at a major at-sea processor told Undercurrent News at the Groundfish Forum venue hotel in Tokyo. 

Producers typically organize two roe auctions in Seattle, Washington, during the peak A season, when fish are more gravid. In recent years, companies have run their B season auctions separately in Busan to draw Japanese and South Korean buyers.

READ MORE
OCT 202:22 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Russian pollock fillet prices rise to parity with US if EU duty included

As the great and the good of the industry arrive in Tokyo, Japan, for the annual Groundfish Forum, pollock fillet prices are on the rise.

This is especially true of Russian pin-bone out (PBO) pollock fillet blocks, for which Undercurrent just adjusted its October price assessment up by $200 per metric ton month-on-month. Prices are up $900/t, or 35%, year-on-year.

READ MORE
OCT 202:20 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Geopolitical shockwaves drive cod, haddock prices to record highs

A combination of unparalleled geopolitical uncertainty and reduced supply has driven cod and haddock prices to record levels as the 2026 Groundfish Forum gets underway.

Undercurrent‘s pre-forum price assessments for week 42 on both Norwegian and Russian headed and gutted (H&G) cod and haddock, delivered China, show all four products at all-time highs. The reasons for this H&G level go beyond supply and demand.

READ MORE

Contact the authors tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, masahiko.takeuchi@undercurrentnews.com, dan.gibson@undercurrentnews.com

title: Untitled
content:
VIGO, Spain -- Undercurrent News reported from the Conxemar trade show in Vigo, Spain, on Oct. 6-9.

The main event, which ran Oct. 7-9, was preceded on Oct. 6 by a conference on global seafood supply and food security, organized by the Spanish industry association Conxemar, the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization and the Spanish ministry of agriculture, fisheries and food.

You can read all the news from both events below:

Auto updates: On
OCT 96:20 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Telemedicine brings lifesaving care to the high seas

A telemedicine project launched by the Vithas Group in Vigo, Spain, offers real-time medical support to crews on fishing vessels.

The initiative, active since March 2022, connects ships to hospital specialists through advanced telemedical equipment designed by doctors, explained Catalina Lamas Matilde, Vithas’ commercial manager (in the photo below showing the equipment).

OCT 96:08 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Brasmar advances integration of Spanish cod firm Giraldo 

Portuguese seafood processor Brasmar Group is moving forward with the integration of two industrial units acquired in September from Spain’s Giraldo Group, a producer of chilled cod and fish-based prepared dishes that had declared insolvency in February.

“We’ve been integrating for nearly two months,” explained a Brasmar executive who has been working with the La Balinesa brand and now also helps to promote Giraldo’s products.

OCT 910:18 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Chile eyes opportunity as Atlantic mackerel stocks face major catch advice cut

With the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES) urging a steep reduction in northeast Atlantic mackerel catches for 2026, Chilean suppliers are positioning their Marine Stewardship Council (MSC)-certified jack mackerel to fill the supply gap in global markets.

Following ICES’ announcement, UK canned food firm Princes Group immediately said it has shifted the sourcing of its mackerel, halting its purchases from the northeast Atlantic and instead buying MSC-certified Chilean jack mackerel.

OCT 99:29 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Faroese firm Hiddenfjord expands factory capacity to boost frozen salmon exports

Faroese salmon producer Hiddenfjord is moving forward with strategic expansions to strengthen its production and meet growing global demand. 

The company is currently expanding its processing plant by approximately 500 square meters to boost capacity for vacuum-packed frozen salmon fillets, alongside completing a significant hatchery enlargement.

OCT 99:13 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Spain’s Grupo Pereira deepens African presence with expansion in Namibia, South Africa

As it celebrates 70 years in the industry, Spain’s Grupo Pereira is deepening its presence in Namibia and South Africa, aimed at sustainable growth and high-value fisheries.

In Namibia, the company has become a shareholder in Southern Namibian Hake Fishing Industries, a firm based in Luderitz. There, it will modernize a 1,000-metric-ton hake processing plant and plans to build a new cold storage facility.

OCT 92:38 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Chile positions artisanal jumbo squid for global markets with sustainability push

Chile is taking decisive steps to elevate its artisanal jumbo squid (Dosidicus gigas) fishery to international prominence. 

This is driven by a renewed focus on sustainability, traceability, and responsible sourcing, said Miguel Espindola, director of ocean conservation at the Chilean NGO Pesca Sustentable.

OCT 92:19 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Seafood industry calls for more time to adapt to EU’s CATCH system rollout

The EU’s push for greater transparency and sustainability in seafood imports is gaining ground, with the full implementation of the CATCH system set for Jan. 10, 2026. 

However, while the industry supports the fight against illegal fishing, some are urging the EU to give more time for adaptation.

OCT 811:04 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Profand expands product portfolio with focus on tuna-based innovation

Profand has expanded its product portfolio with a new line of tuna-based innovations, showcased for the first time this year in Conxemar.

The launch marks a major step in the company’s strategy to deliver sustainable, ready-to-eat seafood products that align with changing consumer habits, said the firm’s communications director, Maria Montero.

OCT 810:43 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Chile launches new FIP to move artisanal southern hake fishery toward MSC certification

Chile has launched a new fishery improvement project (FIP) through the FisheryProgress platform aimed at helping its artisanal southern hake fishery advance toward Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) certification.

The initiative, now in its final development phase, was presented by a team from the Federacion de Sindicatos de Pescadores Artesanales de Hualaihue, a Chilean local federation representing artisanal fishers, on the sidelines of the trade show.

OCT 810:10 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Marfrio waits for Atunlo’s liquidation to finalize takeover offer of Central Lomera Portuguesa

Spanish seafood company Marfrio is poised to take full control of Central Lomera Portuguesa (CLP), a key tuna processing operation in Portugal, the firm’s CEO, Pedro Otaegui, told Undercurrent News.

However, it is waiting for the completion of Atunes y Lomos (Atunlo)’s liquidation before finalizing its takeover offer.

OCT 87:38 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Seafood giant Profand backs ocean regeneration with new R&D push

Octolarvae, the R&D arm of Grupo Profand, is breaking new ground with a pioneering initiative in regenerative aquaculture, it claims.

The company has successfully completed the world’s first controlled releases of juvenile spider crab and shrimp along the Galician coast.

OCT 85:41 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Spain’s Union Martin appoints new CEO

Grupo Union Martin, a Canary Islands, Spain-based seafood supplier backed by Alantra Private Equity, appointed Miguel Antonio Sanchez Fuertes as its new CEO as of July 1. 

Following various leadership changes at the group, the appointment marks the beginning of a new phase for the seafood company, which specializes in octopus, squid, Illex squid, jumbo flying squid and tuna, according to the firm.

OCT 82:45 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti 
Salmon giant Mowi pushes branded, value-added sales in Spain with prices at lowest since COVID

Norwegian seafood giant Mowi is ramping up efforts to expand its branded and value-added salmon sales in Spain, as global salmon prices have this year fallen to their lowest level since the COVID-19 pandemic.

Spain remains one of Mowi’s strategic markets for expanding its portfolio of ready-to-eat and premium seafood products, according to Isabel Lorea Dams, product manager at Mowi Iberia. 

OCT 82:20 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Spain’s fishing sector launches campaign to defend bottom trawling

Spain’s fishing sector has launched a new national campaign, “La Pesca que Sabe” (“Fishing that Knows” or “Fishing that Tastes”), aimed at defending bottom trawling and promoting its role in providing healthy, sustainable seafood.

Led by Pesca Espana, a national association of fishing producer organizations in the country, with support from two major producers’ organizations — OPPC-3, which represents Spain’s fleet of freezer trawlers fishing for species like hake and squid, and OPPF-4, the organization of fresh fish producers based in the Port of Vigo — the campaign seeks to counter growing public criticism of trawling. 

OCT 82:05 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti 
Chilean mussel prices expected to hold steady or rise through early 2025

Chilean mussel prices are expected to remain firm or increase slightly in the coming months, as limited supply and high raw material costs continue to shape the market ahead of the next harvest.

Industry sources report that last season’s low seeding in 2023 resulted in reduced harvest volumes for 2024. Although seeding conditions improved this year, the impact of that recovery will not be felt until the next harvest cycle, expected around March 2025. As a result, current inventories are tight, and available mussels tend to be smaller in size.

OCT 710:45 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Spanish minister blasts EU’s proposed fisheries budget cuts: ‘No country will support this’

Spain’s minister of agriculture, fisheries and food, Luis Planas, has strongly criticized the European Commission’s proposal to slash fisheries funding by 67% in the next EU budget framework.

He called the cuts unacceptable and warned that no country would support this.

OCT 710:20 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
WOFCO partner ready to open new processing plant in Paraguay

After years of preparation, South Atlantic Company — a partner of Worldwide Fishing Company (WOFCO) founded in 2021 — expects to open its new seafood processing plant in Paraguay in early 2026, CEO Lucio Tortosa told Undercurrent News.

The 10,000-square-meter facility, located in Hohenau Industrial Park, will serve as a hub for freezing, packaging, and distributing red shrimp and is 100% operated by WOFCO.

OCT 710:07 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Argentina’s offshore shrimp season ends with 40,000t shortfall after months-long disruption

Argentina’s offshore shrimp fishing season has officially closed, ending a turbulent year marked by labor disputes, a delayed start and environmental constraints.

The season concluded on Oct. 4 — all vessels are required to return to port by Oct. 10 — with an estimated 40,000-metric-ton drop in landings compared to 2024, largely due to a four-month standstill at the start of the campaign.

OCT 75:49 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Argentina’s Conarpesa pushes ahead with new investments despite industry headwinds

Despite a challenging economic environment and a turbulent shrimp season, Argentina’s largest shrimp exporter, Continental Armadores de Pesca (Conarpesa), is moving forward with several key investments.

All of them aimed at boosting efficiency and long-term sustainability, the firm’s president, Fernando Alvarez, told Undercurrent News.

OCT 75:35 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Nueva Pescanova promotes Keith Decker to global commercial director

Nueva Pescanova has appointed Keith Decker as its new global sales, marketing, and innovation director, Undercurrent News confirmed at Conxemar. 

Decker succeeds Fernando Zaldivar, who left the company several months ago for personal reasons.

OCT 612:31 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Cultivated seafood firms race to industrial scale amid growing global demand

As the cultivated seafood industry races to meet growing global demand, its leaders are clear about the challenges ahead.

Cultivated seafood startups Bluu Seafood and Umami Bioworks said the industry is at a critical juncture, facing significant challenges in scaling production, securing regulatory approval, and bringing products to market.

OCT 612:17 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Umami Bioworks pushes cultivated seafood actives into global skincare industry

Singapore-based cultivated-seafood firm Umami Bioworks has introduced a new cultivated seafood-derived ingredient, the MRX1, into the global skincare market. 

In a new collaboration with Qurio, a beauty and wellness incubator in the country, the partnership has launched the first commercial skincare product featuring Umami Bioworks’ proprietary marine actives.

OCT 611:43 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
‘More culture, less capture’: Former EU commissioner urges shift in ocean management

In a call for reform, Karmenu Vella, former European Commissioner for Environment, Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, urged policymakers and stakeholders to rethink how humanity interacts with the ocean.

Following this, he advocated for a radical transition from traditional fishing to sustainable aquaculture.

OCT 68:22 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Expert calls for urgent overhaul of FAO’s fisheries code as sustainability gaps widen

Thirty years after its adoption, the FAO’s Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries (CCRF) faces criticism from experts who say it is no longer equipped to address the complex challenges of today’s ocean and fisheries landscape.

“The code has been foundational for sustainable fisheries management worldwide,” Alberto Prieto, chief coordinator at Fundacion Fish Nation, said. “But the world has changed, and the code has not changed enough with it.”

OCT 65:34 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Seafood industry faces ‘make or break’ moment, execs warn at global summit

The global seafood industry is at a critical turning point, say leaders gathered in Vigo for the 13th FAO-Conxemar Congress. 

With climate change, overfishing and global demand rising, calls for urgent reform echoed across the summit inauguration.

OCT 63:14 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Conxemar grows 4% in size, targets nearly €1bn in deals

The 26th edition of the Conxemar trade show kicks off on Tuesday (Oct. 7) in Vigo with record-breaking figures and a growing global reach, according to the organizers. 

Held from Oct. 7 to 9 at the IFEVI exhibition center, the show welcomes 797 exhibitors from 46 countries, a 4% increase from last year. 

Contact the authors Maria.Feijoo@undercurrentnews.com, matilde.mereghetti@undercurrentnews.com

title: Fisheries Council of Canada 2025: Chinese tariffs hammer Canada’s geoduck industry
content:
OTTAWA, Ontario, Canada -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the Fisheries Council of Canada (FCC) annual general meeting, Oct. 1-2,  in the nation's capital city.

The FCC is the national association that represents major players in Canada's wild-capture fisheries from the Pacific and Atlantic coasts and the Arctic.

Trade is the focus of this year's event, with the theme "Accessing Global Markets in Turbulent Waters." Over 175 delegates, representing the member companies of the FCC, are attending the event at the Chateau Laurier hotel, just steps away from Canada's Parliament buildings.

Speakers and panelists include: Dominic Barton, Canada's former ambassador to China; Ian Burney, Canada's former ambassador to Japan; and Steve Verheul, Canada's former chief trade negotiator for the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the Canada-US-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA), known as the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) in the US.

The event kicked off Wednesday evening (Oct. 1) with an address by Canadian fisheries minister Joanne Thompson.

Check back for updates during the event.

Auto updates: On
OCT 39:36 AM GMT
A lesson from Iceland: pitch your product to retail with a taste-test party

Want to increase your seafood sales in new or underdeveloped markets?

Make your product pitches directly to the protein buyers in retail with a taste-test dinner party in your target market.

READ MORE
OCT 37:55 AM GMT
Chinese tariffs continue to hammer Canada’s geoduck industry

The 25% Chinese tariff on Canadian seafood continues to erode profits for the geoduck industry in the province of British Columbia.

Dock prices for the meaty clams, which are considered a luxury food item, dropped by as much as 35% after China imposed tariffs on Canada in March, in retaliation for the tariffs Canada had imposed on electric vehicles from China in 2024, Grant Dovey, executive director of the Underwater Harvesters Association in British Columbia, told Undercurrent News on the sidelines of the FCC’s annual general meeting.

READ MORE
OCT 37:51 AM GMT
Canadian lobster industry anticipates bump in live exports during China’s Golden Week

Canadian lobster exporters are optimistic that Chinese demand for the crustacean will heat up this week during the Asian nation’s eight-day-long Golden Week holiday, which started Oct. 1.

“What we really need them to do is start buying some of our frozen lobster,” Geoff Irvine, executive director of the Lobster Council of Canada (LCC), told Undercurrent News on Wednesday (Oct. 1) during the opening night reception.

READ MORE
OCT 37:45 AM GMT
Canfisco vice president is new chair of Fisheries Council of Canada

Colin McMillan is the new chair of the Fisheries Council of Canada (FCC), the trade group that represents the interests of Canadian seafood companies that harvest and process wild-caught fish.

McMillan, the vice president of corporate relations for the British Columbia-based Canfisco Group, officially stepped into the role at the FCC annual general meeting. He replaces Alberto Wareham, owner of Newfoundland and Labrador-based Icewater Seafoods, who just finished his two-year term in the chairman spot.

READ MORE
OCT 26:26 PM GMT
Global sentiment on American trade attitudes could prove beneficial for Canadian exporters

Global negativity towards US trade deals is growing and that might be a silver lining for Canadian seafood exporters, a former Canadian diplomat told industry leaders Thursday afternoon (Oct. 2).

“Don’t underestimate the current negativity that exists in many of these markets towards the US brand,” said Ian Burney, who served as Canada’s ambassador to Japan from 2016 to 2021, during a panel discussion.

READ MORE
OCT 212:32 PM GMT
Canadian seafood industry needs strong brands, more in-person effort in China, says former envoy

Canada needs to do a better job of building its seafood brands and developing relationships with major retailers in China, to improve its presence in that market, says Canada’s former ambassador to China.

“We need to win on the ground in terms of our presence. And we’re not — we’re pathetic,” said keynote speaker Dominic Barton on Thursday morning (Oct. 2).

READ MORE
OCT 28:53 AM GMT
Canada’s fisheries minister vows to protect science

Sustainability is the foundation for Canada’s fishing and seafood industry, and science-based management is key to ensuring long-term stability, Canadian fisheries minister Joanne Thompson told members of the Fisheries Council of Canada (FCC) on Wednesday night (Oct.1).

“I’ve heard the concerns about science capacity, and I am committed to protecting the science we rely on, and to leveraging industry, [Canada’s Department of Fisheries and Oceans], collaborations [for] vessel time to [stock] surveys,” she said in a short address to delegates at the opening night reception.
