title: GAPP meeting: Senator Sullivan indicates Canada ‘close’ to banning Russian seafood processed in third countries
content:
SEATTLE, Washington, US -- Undercurrent News reported from the annual Genuine Alaska Pollock Producers (GAPP) meeting, held in Seattle, Washington. 

The GAPP meeting, which took place in the W Seattle hotel, came amid a slow Alaska pollock "B" season, erratic trade policies from US president Donald Trump's administration and booming USDA purchases for the US public sector. This year's event was reported to have close to 300 attendees, a record for the conference.

Auto updates: On
SEP 187:46 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
APFA’s PR blitz getting results among Alaskans

Veteran public relations professional Heather Handyside said Alaskans have historically viewed pollock less favorably than Pacific salmon and halibut, and much work has been done to address that.

“While Alaskans may have strong feelings about bycatch and trawl, they have very little to say about pollock,” said Handyside, chief executive officer of Thompson & Company, a leading PR firm in Anchorage, Alaska. 

READ MORE
SEP 186:20 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Murkowski pledged funding support for US federal agencies

US senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska delivered a short video address to the GAPP meeting in which she reaffirmed her commitment to ensuring federal agencies are funded to support science-based fishery management.

She described the current appropriations process in the US Congress as “chaotic.”

READ MORE
SEP 185:01 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
NOAA Fisheries chief pledges to increase competitiveness through deregulation of US seafood

Eugenio Pineiro Soler, the acting head of the National Marine Fisheries Service, pledged to “level the playing field” by removing red tape to increase the competitiveness of American seafood, a key policy goal of US president Donald Trump.

“We have the greatest seafood in the world, yet it is one of the most heavily regulated sectors in the country,” Soler told the GAPP meeting attendees.

READ MORE
SEP 184:53 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
US output of PBO, deepskin pollock fillets, surimi should be up in 2025 if quota is caught 

The US production of the three main product types, surimi, pin-bone out fillets and deepskin fillets, should be up between 5-7% in 2025 if – and it’s a big if – the quota is caught.

Ron Rogness of GAPP said 143,534 metric tons of quota remain uncaught. But, if it is, the levels should be up, as you can see below from his forecast. 

READ MORE
SEP 184:14 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Pollock suffers in Brazil due to bad rep from Chinese products

Brazil is one market the US sector is targeting for increased pollock sales, but the product suffers from the poor reputation Chinese-produced product has in the market.

Some of the double-frozen pollock fillets from China which are available in the Brazil market create a bad association for the species generally, said Leonardo Silveira, of River Global, a Sao Paulo, Brazil-based marketing company working with the Alaskan sector.

READ MORE
SEP 183:16 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Senator Sullivan indicates Canada ‘close’ to banning Russian seafood processed in third countries

Canada is getting close to banning Russian seafood processed in third countries such as China, according to comments made by US Republican senator Dan Sullivan at the GAPP conference.

“I pitched leaders in Canada, Japan, the EU, Korea, to ban Russian seafood globally,” said Sullivan, speaking via video from Washington, DC.

READ MORE
SEP 183:15 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Sullivan talks bycatch, Russia, geographic indicator for ‘Alaska pollock’

US senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska said he’s working on legislation to study variable runs of wild Alaska salmon that some critics partially blame on bycatch in groundfish trawlers, an acknowledgement of the political pressures felt in Washington, DC by critics of the Alaska pollock fishery.

He said legislation is being written for “developing and employing technologies for bycatch reduction” in the commercial fishing fleets.

READ MORE
SEP 182:17 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Eco-label CSI works to expand to fisheries outside of Alaska

Mike Kraft, chief executive of Certified Seafood International (CSI), gave an update on the eco-label startup’s progress in reaching global recognition.

The former Bumble Bee exec said eco-labels are growing in importance for seafood exporters, not just for consumers but also suppliers looking for assurance on sustainability.

READ MORE
SEP 181:37 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Study: Alaska pollock sector reduces carbon footprint

New data suggests the US Alaska pollock industry has reduced its carbon emissions by nearly a fifth since 2018, making the wild-caught fish even more environmentally friendly than meat proteins like beef, chicken and pork, as Undercurrent News reported.

Preliminary research results from academics at Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada, presented on Thursday (Sept. 17), show Alaska pollock caught in the US last year produced 3.09 kilograms of carbon for every kilogram of protein, a fraction of competing land-raised protein sources, including plant-based meat substitutes.

READ MORE
SEP 181:03 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Study: Alaska pollock fishery generates $2.5b in impact

Northern Economics, an Anchorage, Alaska-based economic research group, touted the economic impact of the Alaska pollock fishery on the regional economy in the US Pacific Northwest.

“We found that in total in the United States, the fishery generated over $2.5 billion in economic output, of which $1.2 billion was directly in support of labor income,” fishery economist Melissa Errendi told GAPP attendees. 

READ MORE
SEP 1812:39 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
US surimi prices edge up after ‘supply shock’ from Russia

US surimi prices are slowly edging up, having seemingly hit the bottom.

However, the progress is slow, due to the “supply shock” in the market from Russia’s rapid increase in production, said GAPP’s Ron Rogness.

READ MORE
SEP 1812:34 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Rogness estimates 10,000-20,000t of US pollock quota could be left in water

The total of Eastern Bering Sea US pollock quota likely to be left in the water by US catchers in 2025 won’t be as bad as the 50,000 metric ton “worst case” figure given to Undercurrent News by some industry players.

According to GAPP’s Ron Rogness, around 10,000-20,000t will be left in the water, looking at the pace of fishing.

READ MORE
SEP 1812:30 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
GAPP: Alaska pollock generated $2.5b in 2023

Studies conducted by McKinley Research and Northern Economics say the Alaska pollock fishery is responsible for $2.5 billion in US economic activity in 2023. 

The data shows that the US pollock industry generated more than $337 million in wages for workers in the US state of Alaska in 2023, GAPP said.

READ MORE
SEP 1812:16 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Glacier CEO Johnson: ‘We had to introduce Alaska pollock to Alaskans’

Jim Johnson, the CEO of Glacier Fish Company and chair of the new Alaska Pollock Fishery Alliance (APFA) group, said the industry has been pushing hard on letting Alaska residents know about the fishery’s positive impact on the state.

APFA was created in March 2024, to push back against on attacks on the largely Seattle-based industry from anti-trawl groups.

READ MORE
SEP 1812:08 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
GAPP touts Trump administration’s support for US pollock industry

GAPP chairman Bob Desautel lauded the US pollock industry’s support from the administration of US president Donald Trump. He pointed to a recent op-ed penned by two Trump cabinet officials in the Anchorage Daily News supporting the Alaska fishery.

“By the end of this year,” Desautel said, “USDA will have purchased roughly 66 million pounds of Alaska pollock products.”

READ MORE
SEP 1811:41 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Trident takes it ‘one day at a time’ on Akutan closure date for B season 

Trident Seafoods aims to close its giant Akutan plant in the US state of Alaska in mid-October for maintenance, but will make a decision on the final date closer to the time, depending on fishing.

As previously reported by Undercurrent News, B season pollock harvesting in the east Bering Sea has been slow, meaning the shore-side processing sector still has a ways to go to complete its quota. B season officially ends on Oct. 31. 

READ MORE
SEP 1811:27 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
EU spot prices for US pollock fillet blocks move up; Chinese, Russian sellers push for more

US producers of pin-bone out (PBO) Alaska pollock fillet blocks are getting higher prices for small-volume spot deals than the large contracts made in the B season, which comes as Chinese and Russian suppliers hold for more, sources told Undercurrent News as the GAPP conference gets underway. 

The ex-coldstore spot level for small-volume US PBO fillet block deals to European buyers has edged up, with some sources giving prices close to $200 per metric ton higher than the level at which the large B season contracts were agreed upon around the Barcelona seafood show in April.

READ MORE

title: Vigo tuna conference 2025: Future bright as new markets open in China, Latin America
content:
Vigo, SPAIN -- Undercurrent News reported from Vigo, northern Spain, where the XII ANFACO World Tuna Conference ran Sept. 11-12.

This major event brought together over 400 top executives representing over 90% of global tuna production at the Afundacion headquarters for the event, organized by the Spanish canneries' association, ANFACO-CYTMA.

Featuring leading experts, the conference covers key innovations, market trends, and challenges shaping the future of the tuna sector. 

Auto updates: On
SEP 155:25 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Tuna industry sees bright future as new markets open in China, Latin America

The global tuna industry is entering a new growth phase, with expanding opportunities in China and Latin America driving optimism across the sector. 

At the close of the international tuna conference in Vigo, Roberto Alonso, secretary general of ANFACO-CYTMA, stated that the industry “is well-positioned to compete in a volatile global market.” 

READ MORE
SEP 154:47 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Ecuador defends its tuna industry: Sustainability, exports

Ecuador, one of the world’s largest hubs for tuna processing, is standing firm in its commitment to sustainability, competitiveness, and global food security, said Gustavo Nunez, former president of the Camara de industriales, procesadores y exportadores de atun (CEIPA) and former president of tuna processor Asiservy.

Ecuador leads tuna landings in the Eastern Pacific, he said, adding that favorable oceanic conditions between 2024 and 2025, including a neutral climate scenario between El Nino and La Nina, boosted tuna availability. 

READ MORE
SEP 1210:32 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
US market uncertainty under Trump forces Latin American tuna producers to rethink strategy

Trade policy changes under the US Trump administration have created uncertainty for Latin American tuna producers, prompting them to rethink their approaches to the market. 

Gustavo Nunez, founder of Ecuadorian processor Asiservy, acknowledged that president Trump’s government has shifted its commercial strategy. 

READ MORE
SEP 1210:23 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Spanish firm highlights tuna by-product opportunities

Santiago Silva Salgado, an executive with Spain’s Grupo Sarval, presented his firm’s work in valorizing tuna by-products, noting both the challenges and opportunities in this emerging market.

The family-owned company operates across logistics, recycling, and animal by-product management, with its subsidiary Saria leading efforts in processing tuna and other marine byproducts.

READ MORE
SEP 1210:06 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Selenium in fish protects against mercury harm, research shows

Nick Ralston, a research scientist at the University of North Dakota, challenged long-held fears about mercury in seafood, arguing that the mineral selenium is the key to understanding fish and human health.

Ralston described selenium as “the hero that never gives up,” explaining that it protects the brain, heart, and other organs from oxidative damage. He said mercury does not directly harm tissues but instead blocks selenium’s protective enzymes, which can lead to health problems.

READ MORE
SEP 129:41 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
New Colombian port expected to redefine tuna trade routes in the Atlantic

Colombia is poised for a transformative leap in its tuna industry with the upcoming inauguration of an $800 million deep-water port on the Atlantic coast, the Puerto de Uraba. 

This new facility is set to reduce shipping times and costs, boosting Colombia’s strategic position in global tuna exports, particularly to Europe and the US.

READ MORE
SEP 127:58 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Africa, Middle East seek EU investment in fisheries training, oversight: ‘We need more than compliance’

Industry representatives from Africa and the Middle East call on the EU to go beyond regulation and invest directly in fisheries oversight, training and infrastructure to support sustainable seafood development.

“The problem isn’t policy, it’s weak enforcement,” said Anthony Kim, spokesperson for Ghana’s Pacific Wide. 

READ MORE
SEP 127:41 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti 
Middle East canned tuna demand set to surge 

Canned tuna consumption in the Middle East and North Africa is poised for strong growth, driven by shifting consumer preferences, population expansion, and strategic trade opportunities, according to Lebanese food distributor C-FOODS’s regional purchasing negotiator, Wadad Lahad.

Traditionally viewed as a staple, canned tuna is evolving into a value-added category with rising demand for flavored tuna, ready-to-eat meals, and healthier low-fat options. Markets like Saudi Arabia are seeing a mix of price-sensitive buyers and a growing appetite for premium brands, she said.

READ MORE
SEP 127:13 AM GMT
By María Feijóo 
Yemen’s overlooked coastline fuels bold expansion plans in tuna production

Yemen’s long-overlooked coastline could become a vital driver of economic recovery for the Middle Eastern nation, as one of its leading seafood factories pushes to scale up tuna production and tap into global markets. 

According to Abdullah Bagazi, product manager at the National Fish Canning and Packing Factory, the ambitious vision is to transform Yemen’s artisanal fishing sector into a sustainable, industrial-scale tuna supply. 

READ MORE
SEP 125:53 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Tuna Australia CEO warns of marine spatial squeeze: ‘Up to 39% of our waters are off limits’

Australia’s tuna industry is being pushed out of its fishing grounds by a growing wave of competing ocean users, according to Tuna Australia CEO David Ellis.

“Nearly 40% of national waters are now inaccessible. We’re being squeezed,” he said. “With marine parks, wind farms, shipping, aquaculture, oil and gas, and even rocket testing, up to 39% of our exclusive economic zone is effectively off limits.”

READ MORE
SEP 125:34 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
PNG industry strengthens science, partnerships as catches grow

Papua New Guinea (PNG)’s tuna industry is charting strong growth through science-driven initiatives, global partnerships, and sustainable practices, according to Marcelo Hidalgo, chief operating officer of the Fishing Industry Association (FIA).

Hidalgo highlighted that PNG FIA now collaborates with over 20 international partners, including universities, NGOs, and research centers. These alliances, he said, are vital for advancing fisheries science, reducing environmental impact, and safeguarding labor rights.

READ MORE
SEP 125:01 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Vietnam’s tuna sector eyes value-added shift as 2025 growth levels off

Vietnam’s tuna exports surged to nearly $1 billion in 2024, but growth has stalled in 2025, prompting a strategic shift toward value-added products and new markets, according to Le Hang, general secretary of the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers.

“Tuna exports reached $989 million last year, up 17% compared to 2023,” she said. “This strong recovery reflects the dedication of our fishermen, processors and exporters working together after a very difficult period.”

READ MORE
SEP 124:50 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Thai cannery invests in expanding facilities, diversifies amid US tariffs

Thailand’s tuna sector must diversify and move swiftly to respond to newly imposed US reciprocal tariffs, according to an executive with a cannery there.

With 71 million people and a GDP of $526 billion in 2024, Thailand has cemented its position as a global tuna powerhouse, but the industry must act quickly to offset the impact of the new US tariffs, according to Antonio Sanchez of Thai firm S.P.A. International Food Group (SPA).

READ MORE
SEP 124:26 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Export momentum slows, but China tuna market still forecast to drive global supply through 2030

After a record-breaking year in 2024, China’s tuna export growth is expected to slow, but the country remains firmly positioned as a global supply powerhouse through 2030, according to Hu Deng, vice president of Shanghai Kaichuang and CEO of Hijos de Carlos Albo.

Deng highlighted China’s current position as the world’s third-largest tuna exporter, with over $1.4 billion in export value in 2024, a 33% increase year-on-year, accounting for between 8% and 10% of global export value. 

READ MORE
SEP 121:56 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Jealsa VP on EU trade policy: ‘Worse than the fire that nearly destroyed us’

Spanish tuna canner Jealsa’s vice president, Juan Alonso, issued a stark warning to industry leaders, comparing the impact of new EU trade agreements to a “hurricane” that could devastate the European canned tuna sector.

Speaking at the conference, Alonso began with a dramatic visual: a video showing the aftermath of a devastating fire that destroyed 60% of Jealsa’s processing facilities just three years ago.

READ MORE
SEP 1112:30 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Thai Union: French tuna market recovers after NGO mercury report shock

France’s canned tuna market is regaining ground after a slump triggered by an NGO report on mercury levels, according to Alexis Jacquand, managing director of brand Petite Navire, owned by Thai Union Group.

Jacquand pointed out that following the COVID-19 pandemic, tuna brands in France have been first battered by inflation, which cut volumes by double digits, and then by a mercury scare, which drove consumption down by more than 10% in November and December last year.

READ MORE
SEP 1110:31 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
World’s tuna supply under threat without urgent investment in processing, says FAO

The world’s growing appetite for tuna is on a collision course with processing bottlenecks that threaten future supply, according to William Griffin, consultant at the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization. 

“Tuna catches have increased tremendously — especially skipjack — but processing volumes have flatlined,” he stated. “Unless processing keeps pace, per capita consumption will continue to fall.”

READ MORE
SEP 118:55 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
EU to enforce world’s toughest forced labor import ban by 2027

The European Union will enforce a sweeping ban from December 2027 on all products linked to forced labor, marking the world’s toughest import restriction of its kind. 

The law will apply to all companies — regardless of size — including those selling online, and covers entire supply chains, not just final goods. 

READ MORE
SEP 118:33 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Private label canned tuna continues to surge as Spanish consumers shift to value

NielsenIQ analyst Miguel Barreiro highlighted the resilience of Spain’s private label canned tuna market amid shifting consumer habits and economic pressures. 

Volume growth remains modest, driven by demographic changes such as smaller households and an aging population. Barreiro noted that these trends are reshaping food baskets toward smaller, more affordable formats.

READ MORE
SEP 117:30 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Global foodservice spending hits $1.6 trillion as consumers prioritize eating out despite economic strains

The global foodservice industry reached over $1.6 trillion in consumer spending over the past year, growing 2.7%, said Edurne Uranga, vice president of Foodservice Europe at market consultancy Circana.

This gain was driven not only by inflation but also by a rise in traffic and consumption occasions, she said.

READ MORE
SEP 115:33 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
MSC-certified tuna fishery numbers continue to grow, challenges in stock management remain

The Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) has reported significant growth in the number of tuna fisheries achieving certification under its program, while cautioning that weak enforcement of harvest control rules remains a pressing challenge for sustainable management.

Bill Holden, the MSC’s senior fisheries outreach manager, pointed out that the number of certified tuna fisheries has doubled between 2020 and 2025.

READ MORE
SEP 114:58 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Conservative tuna management becoming the norm, says ISSF

Victor Restrepo, the chair of the International Seafood Sustainability Foundation (ISSF)’s scientific advisory committee, highlighted a growing global trend toward conservative tuna fishery management, noting that while there is biological room to increase catches, precaution and sustainability continue to drive policy decisions. 

“Conservative approaches to management are also becoming the norm and not the exception,” he said, referring to management decisions taken by regional fisheries management organizations (RFMOs), which oversee tuna stocks worldwide.

READ MORE
SEP 114:40 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Experts call for urgent reform as tuna fleets face operational crisis in the Atlantic

Despite healthy stock assessments for tropical tunas in the Atlantic, some fishing fleets are struggling to maintain operations, and experts say the problem isn’t the fish, but the system. 

According to Ernesto Penas, president of the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas, the main issues are a lack of uniform monitoring and major disparities in enforcement standards.

READ MORE
SEP 114:08 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
ICCAT: Canning industry must act now to prevent Atlantic tuna stocks collapse

Atlantic tuna stocks are under mounting threat, with key species facing overfishing and quota violations, and the canning industry is largely to blame, warned Ernesto Penas, president of the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas.

“We’ve been lucky so far, but that luck is running out,” he said.

READ MORE
SEP 113:28 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Skipjack holds strong in Ecuador as Indian Ocean prices weaken

Tuna prices remain a pressing concern across major markets as sector executives traveled from one industry event to another over the past seven days.

In Manta, Ecuador, skipjack prices continue to show strength, holding steady at around $1,700 per metric ton ex-vessel, according to sources. 

READ MORE
SEP 105:22 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Galician tuna industry goes high-tech with government-backed digital revolution

Galicia’s tuna canning industry is undergoing a digital transformation, fueled by strong support from the Spanish government. 

Pedro Blanco, the government delegate in Galicia, emphasized the pivotal role of new technologies in driving innovation and sustainability during the recent Tuna Awards 2025 ceremony held in Vigo.

READ MORE
SEP 104:59 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Marine Instruments, Grupo Profand win top honors at 2025 Tuna Awards

Spanish marine tech specialist Marine Instruments and seafood company Grupo Profand were awarded top honors at the 2025 Tuna Awards.

The biennial awards, now in their third edition, are organized by ANFACO-CECOPESCA in partnership with Spain’s ministry of agriculture, fisheries and food.

READ MORE

title: Untitled
content:
UTRECHT, the Netherlands -- Undercurrent News reported from the Global Shrimp Forum (GSF), held every September in Utrecht, the Netherlands. 

The GSF event, which ran from Tuesday, Sept. 2, until Thursday, Sept. 4, came at a time when global shrimp trade flows are reshuffling due to US tariffs. Click here for the full GSF program. 

During the GSF week, UCN launched a global shrimp tracker tool -- which allows users to monitor developments in global farmgate prices, in addition to downstream levels in China and the US. Click here to access the tool and here to read more about it. 

Auto updates: On
SEP 55:13 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Disease outbreaks drive consolidation in Vietnam as smaller farmers drop out

Tom That De, CEO of shrimp hatchery and nursery Viet Uc Seafood Group, painted a sobering picture of the current shrimp production picture in Vietnam, where a variety of diseases have been playing havoc with the country’s high-intensity farms.

“Our production [of PLs] is coming down compared to last year,” he said. “The monodon is not going up, and our big shrimp is not competitive with Ecuador, while the longer farming time means more risk.”

SEP 54:58 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
France challenges Spain’s position as EU’s top shrimp importer

While Spain remains Europe’s number one importer of shrimp by volume, the French market has been gaining in its rear-view mirror this year.

From 88,000 metric tons last year, France’s imports are up a stunning 26% over H1, which would leave them on track for roughly 111,000t of direct imports by the end of the year, according to the latest projections from Willem van der Pijl.

SEP 54:34 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese buyer warns imports may fall amid uptake of local frozen HOSO shrimp

China’s shrimp imports could plateau or decline within three to five years despite growing domestic consumption, as local production becomes more competitive with head-on frozen shrimp from Ecuador, according to a large importer.

Li Tongrui, chairman of Shandong Maibo, which imports 100 containers a month primarily from Ecuador, Thailand and India, said Chinese-farmed shrimp quality is “getting close to Ecuadorian quality” while maintaining lower costs without the burden of tariffs and import duties.

SEP 411:08 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
US shrimp buyers face higher costs as India dependency proves difficult to break

US shrimp buyers will absorb significant cost increases from tariffs on Indian imports, with no viable alternatives to replace the country’s market share, industry executives said at the Global Shrimp Forum.

“You cannot take India’s 40% of the market away right away,” said Angel Rubio, principal reporter at Urner Barry, referring to the country’s sales to the US. “So those costs [in the US] will have to move higher.”

SEP 410:56 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Ecuador now Japan’s fourth largest shrimp supplier

Speaking on behalf of the Japanese market, Maruha Nichiro’s Kotaro Mori said that here too, Ecuador has begun making inroads this year.

Japanese shrimp import numbers have been stable for the past three years, hovering around 220,000t annually. Even as consumption is dropping among Japanese citizens, high tourism levels have been supporting consumption.

SEP 410:14 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Algal oil halfway there, insect meal a long way from maturity: the latest feed data

Data supplied by DSM-Firmenich at GSF shows the current state of play for major alternative feed ingredients that are being used within the aquafeed sector.

Adolfo Fontes, head of business intelligence at DSM-Firmenich — which operates its own single-cell protein operation — said that last year there was an estimated 15,000 metric tons of single-cell proteins in circulation.

SEP 49:24 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Bearish outlook dominates slack agri-feed markets, soy prices in the gutter

Feed ingredient prices have been falling en masse this year and still have further to go, according to Charles Hart, an agri-commodity analyst with Rabobank.

The corn market has led declines, falling 12% in price since the start of the year, while wheat markets are themselves down 7%.

SEP 48:32 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Land-based shrimp farmers split on biofloc versus clear water RAS

Austria’s White Panther has transitioned from biofloc to clear water recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) technology and now targets high-end consumers at EUR 80 per kilogram ($93/kg), CEO Eva Keferbock told the Global Shrimp Forum.

This contrasts with Daniel Russek, CEO of US-based Atarraya, who is betting on the opposite approach, championing biofloc systems that require lower upfront investment.

SEP 45:58 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Skretting’s shrimp feed biz value now close to salmon

Nutreco chief strategy officer Joost Matthijssen was on hand to represent the feed sector at the forum’s annual M&A session, as Skretting replaced BioMar in the line-up from last year.

The aquafeed giant, whose business was originally centred around the salmon sector, has steadily grown its presence in shrimp since entering the market a decade ago.

SEP 45:35 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Land-based shrimp RAS faces investment drought as European facilities shutter

Investment in land-based shrimp farming using recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) has contracted sharply, after multiple closures of European facilities, according to analysis presented at the Global Shrimp Forum.

While RAS technology has attracted significant capital for salmon production, only a tiny fraction reaches shrimp farming operations, said Matt Craze of Spheric Research, a seafood industry consultancy firm.

SEP 45:35 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Surging Brazil on track for 500,000t of shrimp by 2030

Flying under Ecuador’s shadow among other major Latin American farmed shrimp producers, Brazil’s own harvests have been growing tremendously in recent years and are set to reach half a million metric tons by the end of the decade, according to Rafael Pedroza, a partner at Marchef Pescados.

“Five years ago, we produced 110,000t, now our area is almost double. And production and consumption is rising; last five years, per capita consumption was 500g, now it’s nearly 1kg, five year’s time should be 1.5-1.6kg.”

SEP 41:49 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Vietnam has done what India must do on diversifying from US, says van der Pijl

Vietnam is on track to hit an export record of close to 400,000 metric tons in 2025, having diversified its exports away from the US reliance seen by India and Indonesia.

“Vietnam has done what India needs to do on diversifying markets,” said Willem van der Pijl, co-founder and managing director of the GSF, during the export and import session on Wednesday.

SEP 312:17 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Tariff table for top US shrimp suppliers

Willem van der Pijl, co-founder and managing director of the GSF, presented a full table of the tariffs applied to the top US shrimp suppliers during the export and import session, with India well in the lead.

“This table is produced on a best-effort basis, but errors may occur due to ongoing changes,” said van der Pijl as a disclaimer.

SEP 312:01 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chicken of the Sea’s DelaLlana sees ‘negative sentiment’ grow in US over imported shrimp

There’s a “growing trend” of negative sentiment in the US over imported shrimp, adding to the issues created for suppliers by the Trump administration’s sweeping import tariffs, said a top executive.

“We are seeing this [negative sentiment over imports] get a platform with the government than we have never seen before,” said Henry DelaLlana, vice president for procurement with US importer Chicken of the Sea Frozen Foods, which is owned by Thai Union Group.

SEP 311:23 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China’s foodservice sector still wants imported shrimp

Major Chinese shrimp importers continue to source exclusively from international suppliers, citing demand for consistent quality that domestic producers can’t provide, according to a leading buyer at the Global Shrimp Forum.

Louis Zhou, CEO of Huaxin Food Group, told attendees his company has not purchased any shrimp from local Chinese producers. “We never bought any shrimp from local producers yet,” Zhou said. “For our customers, they require imported shrimp.”

SEP 310:40 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Novel feed startups may fail in short-term, but long-term remain necessity

Adolfo Fontes, head of business intelligence at DSM-Firmenich, gave a sobering short-term outlook for alternative ingredient manufacturers at the forum.

While the market needs novel ingredients to meet the growing demand from the aquaculture sector that fishmeal and fish oil cannot meet, the glut of fishmeal supply this year out of Peru has left many producers high and dry.

SEP 39:43 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Indian traders make serious tilapia investments as exports take off

Tilapia export data made a rare appearance at this year’s Global Shrimp Forum as Van der Pijl (below) explained how India’s ongoing efforts to diversify its seafood export basket were going beyond shrimp.

“There’s huge talk about diversification, not only within shrimp but also into the reprocessing of fish, for example, or to industrial tilapia farming,” he told listeners. “And these are not just words, we can already see it in the data.”

SEP 36:29 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China’s shrimp imports may fall below 900,000t in 2025 as domestic production surges

China’s shrimp imports are expected to decline to approximately 900,000 metric tons in 2025, down 4% from last year, even as domestic consumption rises, analysis shows.

Willem van der Pijl told conference attendees that quarterly imports have stabilized between 200,000 and 230,000t, but the overall trajectory remains downward. “If we continue the 4% drop in the first half of this year, it’s 880,000t more or less imported [for 2025],” van der Pijl said.

SEP 35:50 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Ecuador can’t replace India in US for processed products

Ecuador’s shrimp industry is seeing increased shipments to Asian processing hubs including Vietnam, Malaysia and Thailand, as the South American country struggles to meet demand for processed products, analysis shows.

While Ecuador has invested significantly in processing infrastructure — peeling and de-heading in particular — capacity constraints continue, particularly for the US market, said Sandro Coglitore, head of Ecuadorian shrimp exporter Omarsa.

SEP 35:18 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
EU shrimp market enjoys surprise raw shrimp import boom, heads toward 400,000t

While geopolitics play havoc with shrimp sales to the US and China this year, the EU is quietly enjoying a huge surge in imports, according to event host Willem van der Pijl.

In H1, imports of raw farmed shrimp from Asia and Latin America drastically increased, with Q2 the single highest quarter for shrimp imports into the bloc ever recorded, up a stunning 24% year-on-year.

SEP 34:41 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Ecuador shrimp exports could hit 1.5m metric tons in 2025

Ecuador’s shrimp exports are on track to reach an unprecedented 1.5 million metric tons this year, driven by farm consolidation and technology upgrades.

Willem van der Pijl, presenting market data at the Global Shrimp Forum, noted that Ecuador exported 150,000t in May alone this year. “If we assume growth in the second half less than first half, 10% year-on-year rather than 17%, exports could reach 1.4m metric tons, but I’d not be surprised if it exports 1.5m metric tons for the first time,” van der Pijl said.

SEP 33:41 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Indian diversification already underway pre-tariffs, 2025 to be flat

Presenting the export data for which the Global Shrimp Forum is famed, event organizer Willem van der Pijl noted that Indian shrimp exports are expected to stagnate this year after 2024’s 3% increase.

Exports are already up 3% in H1, with all of that growth occurring in Q2 — and May in particular — as a result of frontloaded exports to the US that aimed to beat the tariffs.

SEP 212:08 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
GSC campaign could offer Indonesian shrimp domestic lifeline

Speaking on the Global Shrimp Council (GSC) panel, Aris Utama, director of member processor Bumi Menara Internusa, believes that a Council-funded social media campaign in Indonesia could make a serious dent in increasing the country’s shrimp consumption.

“We have 385 million mobile phone users in Indonesia, out of 237m people — the phone, for most Indonesians, is the one luxury good that they can carry around.”

SEP 211:50 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Huge new US tariffs on shrimp will hit consumption shortly, warns analyst

Angel Rubio, principal economist with Urner Barry by Expana, did his best to predict what the future holds for US shrimp consumption in a trading environment where the rules seem to change every week.

As of the end of July, he said, US inventories are somewhere between 2% and 11% long on shrimp. “That’s not actually that much for all the front-loading that happened [in H1].”

SEP 211:42 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Trump administration will pursue tariffs ‘whatever it takes, wherever it takes us’

The ruling by the US Court of Appeals on Aug. 29 that president Trump’s ‘reciprocal tariffs’ are illegal is a setback for the US administration, but does not mean the tariff policy is going away any time soon, according to Rabobank’s head of global research, Eric Lambregts.

“The whole appeals process still has to go through; at the moment, the court has ruled that they think it’s illegal, but the tariffs will go on while the appeal is happening.”

SEP 29:39 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Track global shrimp prices from farm-gate to wholesale with new UCN tool

Undercurrent News has launched a new data tool, the global shrimp price tracker, which allows users to monitor prices along the supply chain — from farmgate to Chinese and US wholesale.

The global shrimp price tracker, which is free and open to non-subscribers until Sept. 15, is the latest iteration of UCN’s development into a global price reporting agency for seafood. 

SEP 27:59 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Global Shrimp Council campaign to hit France, Spain this month

In its first move beyond the US, the Global Shrimp Council’s (GSC) marketing campaign is set for its first European launch in the coming weeks, according to strategy consultant Miguel Barcenas.

“France and Spain are starting in September, so in the next few days you will start to see that,” he told listeners.

SEP 27:27 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Global Shrimp Council to target college football, but more cash needed

As the Global Shrimp Council’s (GSC) marketing campaigns in the US gather pace, strategy consultant Miguel Barcenas — the brains behind the Avocados from Mexico campaign — was on hand to detail some of the next moves.

The GSC’s campaigns on social media, and especially TikTok, have been gathering millions of views, tailored to driving home the taste and convenience benefits of well-cooked shrimp.

SEP 25:32 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Poor Barents Sea coldwater shrimp catches add to price pressure from Greenland quota cut

The lower-than-expected catches of coldwater shrimp in the Barents Sea for Norway and other countries are adding to price pressure caused by the reduced quota from Greenland.

“Greenland is down by 20,000 metric tons in two years and current Barents Sea landings are well down. Prices are moving, that’s for sure,” said Magnus Magnusson, a commercial manager with Northcoast Seafoods, a UK-based supplier owned by Japan’s Maruha Nichiro. “Barents Sea fishing has not been good enough; there is plenty of quota.”

SEP 25:27 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Sea-frozen Argentine shrimp prices finally rise after strike ends

Prices for head-on, sea-frozen Argentine red shrimp are finally rising as vessels get going catching after the end of a strike over labor costs.

Prior to the months-long strike ending on Aug. 1, prices had remained stable, even as the market knew of the situation in Argentina, said Jose Manuel Gomez of Iceland Seafood Iberica.

SEP 25:10 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
US wild-caught shrimp has problems that have ‘nothing to do with trade policy’

The US domestic wild-caught shrimp industry is facing a series of problems and challenges that have “nothing to do with trade policy,” according to Robert DeHaan, executive vice president and general counsel of the National Fisheries Institute (NFI).

Speaking on wild-caught shrimp trade statistics, DeHaan explained that boats are often tied up and won’t go out on the water due to prices. He said that this is often due to the availability of labor and the price of imported raw material, which is hitting the US domestic fleet pretty hard. 

SEP 24:19 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle 
Majority of global wild shrimp stocks not rated

An estimated 67.7% of global wild shrimp landings and fisheries are “not rated or assessed,” according to Camiel Derichs, program development director for the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC). 

Speaking at the GSF’s wild-caught shrimp summit, Derichs said that many shrimp stocks and fisheries seem to suffer from data gaps. Overfishing, he said, appears to be a serious issue, but bycatch is also a major issue.

SEP 23:21 AM GMT
Auchan, BioMar, Innovafeed target large-scale use of insect protein for Ecuador shrimp feed

On the opening day of the Global Shrimp Forum, BioMar Group, Innovafeed, and French retailer Auchan have announced a significant industry commitment: the large-scale integration of insect protein into commercial shrimp feed in Ecuador.

“This milestone marks a turning point for both the insect and aquaculture industries, demonstrating that insect protein is a viable part of the solution in responsible and resilient shrimp farming,” they said.

Contact the authors tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, amanda.buckle@undercurrentnews.com, dan.gibson@undercurrentnews.com, louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com

title: Shanghai 2025: Ecuador shrimp traders ride US demand wave; Chinese salmon imports enjoy summer surge
content:
SHANGHAI, China -- Undercurrent News is reporting from the 19th edition of the Shanghai International Fisheries and Seafood Exhibition (SIFSE), taking place at the Shanghai New International Expo Center, from Aug. 27 to 29, 2025.

This year’s show covers 120,000 square meters, bringing together more than 3,000 brands from over 30 countries and regions, and showcasing thousands of aquatic and marine products.

Organizers say the event draws more than 100,000 professional visitors, making it one of the seafood industry’s premier international gatherings.

SIFSE, also known as World Seafood Shanghai, runs alongside several related events, including exhibitions for landmark seafood, catering ingredients, supply chains, frozen products, and processing equipment, creating a hub that spans the entire seafood value chain.

In addition to the product displays, the show features more than 30 activities ranging from government and industry forums to expert seminars, culinary demonstrations, and cooking competitions.

Check below to follow all the updates from the show floor.

Auto updates: On
AUG 296:15 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China’s Atlantic salmon imports soar 58% in July as Norway tightens grip

China’s Atlantic salmon imports surged in July, highlighting the country’s growing role as a key global supply absorber during lower prices and rapid expansion in retail and online channels.

Monthly imports reached 13,673 metric tons in product weight, up 58% from the same month last year, according to new data from the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC). 

READ MORE
AUG 296:02 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Russia’s pollock surimi push into China squeezes Pakistan’s itoyori producers

China’s rising imports of Russian pollock surimi are dealing a heavy blow to Pakistani tropical surimi producers, sources told Undercurrent News.

Pakistan’s itoyori (threadfin bream) season, which began this month in parallel with India, has been marked by high raw fish prices. 

READ MORE
AUG 294:59 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Russia kicks off Far East red king crab season with China live shipments set to ramp up

Russia’s 2025 red king crab season will open on Sept. 1 in the Far East, with packers preparing for increased live shipments to China, sources told Undercurrent News.

The total allowable catch for the season is 15,848 metric tons, unchanged from the previous year, with fishing concentrated in the West Kamchatka grounds. 

READ MORE
AUG 291:17 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Ecuador’s Ceaexport doubles capacity with new plant, adds brine freezing line

Ecuadorian shrimp exporter Ceaexport will begin full-scale operations at a new processing plant in Duran in October, expanding capacity and introducing brine freezing to its product lineup, sales director Maria Elena Munoz told Undercurrent News.

Located in Duran, the new facility will consolidate the functions of two existing plants in Guayaquil, lifting monthly processing and packing capacity from a combined 2,500 metric tons to 5,000t. 

READ MORE
AUG 2912:22 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Ecuador’s AquaGold sees rising demand from US and other global markets

Ecuadorian shrimp joint venture AquaGold, formed by four local farmers, is experiencing accelerating demand from the US, while demand from Europe and China is also on the rise, according to Juan Gomez-Behr, Commercial Director of the company.

“Our company is currently the third-largest consolidated shrimp producer in Ecuador. As a group, we are producing 10,000 metric tons of shrimp per month, and exporting 5,000t per month. The group still sells some shrimp to local processors,” Gomez-Behr told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
AUG 2811:29 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Ecuador’s Nirsa still to send less shrimp to China amid stronger US and EU demand

Ecuadorian shrimp producer Nirsa plans to continue sending less shrimp to the Chinese market in the coming months due to low prices, according to an executive from the company. While demand for peeled shrimp is stronger in the US and Europe, prompting the shift in exports.

Although Nirsa’s “Real” brand commands a premium in China’s frozen shrimp market, Paulo Faidutti, sales manager of Nirsa, said that current prices for shipments to China are still too low, leading to losses.

READ MORE
AUG 2810:42 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Spain’s Albo expands into China’s e-commerce market

Spanish canned seafood producer Albo has officially entered China’s e-commerce market, with its products now available on Alibaba’s Tmall. The brand’s offerings, led by canned tuna, along with octopus, mackerel, and sardines, are all produced in Spain and imported in their original packaging.

According to a spokesperson from Shanghai Kaichuang Marine International, Albo’s parent company, the move is part of a broader strategy to introduce the full range of Albo products to international consumers.

READ MORE
AUG 287:25 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Norway’s Ode eyes China’s seafood boom as next frontier

Norwegian Atlantic cod farmer Ode is preparing to ramp up its presence in China, where the company sees strong potential for premium whitefish to complement salmon in the fast-expanding seafood market, sales manager Kristoffer Remo told Undercurrent News.

Ode has already conducted some sales in China, but with European demand now on a firmer footing, the company is set to accelerate shipments.

READ MORE
AUG 285:33 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Faroe Islands’ Vardin begins building fishmeal plant with 1,000t daily capacity

The Faroe Islands’ largest pelagic catcher, Vardin, has started construction of a fishmeal plant at its Tvoroyri site, aiming to begin production within the next two years, sales manager for Africa and Asia Eydin Djurhuus told Undercurrent News.

The facility will process blue whiting and other pelagic species, with a planned capacity of 1,000 metric tons of raw material per day on a continuous, 24-hour basis. 

READ MORE
AUG 283:19 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Indian shrimp suppliers pivot to China, EU amid US tariff impact

Indian shrimp exporters are losing ground in the US market following the rise of tariffs on Indian goods to 50% from Aug. 27. 

The sharp tariff increase has forced some exporters to suspend shipments to the US, their most important market.

READ MORE
AUG 282:59 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Tariffs advantage leads to Ecuadorian gains in US market, says Omarsa’s boss

Ecuadorian shrimp exporters are strengthening their position in the US market, gaining a notable edge over competitors from India and Indonesia. 

Sales have surged again in July and August, according to Sandro Coglitore, CEO of Omarsa, one of Ecuador’s largest shrimp suppliers.

READ MORE
AUG 281:52 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japanese surimi giant Kibun’s China sales rise 15% despite seafood ban

China sales for Japanese surimi giant Kibun Foods rose 15% in the first half of 2025, when Beijing’s ban on Japanese seafood imports was still in effect, CEO Tei Saya of Kibun China Co. told Undercurrent News.

The growth was not only driven by the company’s flagship imitation crab sticks but also by what she described as “side products,” including chikuwa (tube-shaped fish cakes), oden sets (assorted ingredients for a Japanese hot pot-style stew) and itatsuki kamaboko (board-mounted fish cakes).

READ MORE
AUG 281:21 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China’s salmon boom risks turning into ‘red ocean,’ warns major importer

China’s fast-expanding salmon market could soon become a “red ocean” of cutthroat competition despite strong growth, Joe Qiao, president of Meichu Foods, a Qingdao-based seafood importer and processor, told the 8th Global Salmon Industry Development Summit.

Qiao said imports of chilled salmon jumped sharply in 2025 as prices dropped to their lowest level in years. 

READ MORE
AUG 279:02 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
More Argentine red shrimp sales to China amid short offshore seasons

Argentine red shrimp suppliers are now accelerating shipments to the Chinese market amid a shorter-than-usual catching season.

Iberconsa, the largest supplier of Argentine red shrimp, showcased its products at the Shanghai show, highlighting its strong focus on the Chinese market for value-added products.

READ MORE
AUG 276:50 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China’s imports of Chilean coho salmon forecast to rise 25% by 2026, says AquaChile

China’s imports of Chilean coho salmon are projected to rise 6% year-on-year to 6,000 metric tons in 2025 and reach 7,500t in 2026, equivalent to a 25% increase from 2024 levels, according to Rafa Tong, general manager of AquaChile.

Speaking at the 8th Global Salmon Industry Development Summit, Tong noted that Chilean coho had long relied heavily on Japan, but its dependence on that market has eased, with the share of shipments to Japan now down to 40%. 

READ MORE
AUG 277:14 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
US tariffs push India to diversify shrimp export markets

Starting Aug. 27, tariffs on Indian goods exported to the US rose to 50%, following US President Donald Trump’s criticism of India for continuing to purchase oil from Russia.

For shrimp products, India now faces a total tax of 58.26%, which includes a 2.49% anti-dumping duty and a 5.77% countervailing duty—higher than that imposed by any other country in the world.

READ MORE
AUG 276:38 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Chinese market absorbs rising prices for Atlantic cod, coldwater shrimp

The Chinese market has accepted higher prices for wild whitefish—particularly Atlantic cod—as well as coldwater shrimp, according to an executive at Beiyang Jiamei, a Qingdao-based seafood importer and processor.

Xinghua Meng, vice manager of Beiyang Jiamei, told Undercurrent News that consumers have had to absorb the soaring prices of Atlantic cod and the 25% tariff on Canadian coldwater shrimp.

READ MORE
AUG 276:06 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Venezuela’s Lamar continues to face production challenges

Venezuela’s largest shrimp producer, Grupo Lamar, is still grappling with operational difficulties, according to a Chinese industry source. 

Grupo Lamar’s Antartica plant, located in the San Francisco municipality in the state of Zulia, Venezuela, suffered a major fire on April 20, as previously reported.

READ MORE
AUG 275:05 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
New Zealand King Salmon targets tenfold growth in China exports by 2035

New Zealand King Salmon (NZKS) aims to increase the share of its shipments to China from about 2% today to roughly 20% over the next decade, CEO Carl Carrington told the 8th Global Salmon Industry Development Summit.

Carrington said the company’s export ambitions will be underpinned by production growth. 

READ MORE
AUG 274:31 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China’s domestic trout output could reach 80,000t by 2030

China’s rainbow trout production could surge to 80,000 metric tons by 2030, while Atlantic salmon farming is projected to reach 10,000t, Joe Qiao, president of Meichu Foods, told the audience at the 8th Global Salmon Industry Development Summit.

Qiao highlighted that while official statistics put rainbow trout production in 2024 at 41,000t, industry insiders believe the actual figure is closer to 30,000t. 

READ MORE
AUG 273:47 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China’s Atlantic salmon imports may hit 168,000t in 2025, says Norwegian Seafood Council

China’s Atlantic salmon imports could theoretically expand to 167,752 metric tons in whole-fish equivalent terms this year, Sigmund Bjorgo, China director of the Norwegian Seafood Council, said at the 8th Global Salmon Industry Development Summit on Wednesday.

Bjorgo’s projection is based on this year’s first-half imports and the historical ratio of China’s half-year to full-year salmon volumes. “If we then just use mathematics, nothing else than mathematics, and expect the second half to be as strong as the last years, we can expect the Chinese market might reach nearly 168,000t this year,” he said. 

READ MORE
AUG 273:43 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Ecuadorian packers raise China offerings at Shanghai show

Ecuadorian shrimp exporters increased their cost and freight price offerings to China during the Shanghai show, following a market strategy commonly used at most seafood expos.

Prices for semi-IQF products rose by $0.10/kg week-on-week, although some Chinese buyers still expressed resistance. According to Undercurrent News’ week 35 assessment (in USD per kilogram):

READ MORE
AUG 273:26 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
China’s shrimp imports expected to rise in H2 2025

China’s shrimp imports are expected to grow in the second half of 2025, as the country’s economy shows signs of recovery, according to industry sources.

“The import volume in the second half will definitely increase, as consumer purchasing power is recovering,” said Song Changgui, general manager of Guangdong Rainbow Aquatic Development, a large importer and processor based in Zhanjiang, in an interview with Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
AUG 272:02 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Norwegian packers pitch record prices for new-season Atlantic mackerel

Norwegian packers are offering record prices for new-season Atlantic mackerel that began this month, multiple sources told Undercurrent News.

For Asia-bound shipments on a cost-and-freight basis, the key 400–600 gram size is being offered at $4,100 per metric ton, while the 300–500g size is priced at $4,000/t, the sources said.

READ MORE
AUG 267:57 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China’s seafood exports hit record high in H1 2025, while imports decline

China’s seafood exports reached an all-time high in the first half of 2025, even as imports fell for the second consecutive year, according to Undercurrent News’ trade portal.

Export volumes — under harmonized system HS codes 03, 1604 and 1605 — rose 12% year-on-year to 2.095 million metric tons in the six months to June, surpassing the previous 2017 record. 

READ MORE
AUG 267:51 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China’s total seafood output rises 3%, driven by farmed fish, shellfish 

China produced 73.6 million metric tons of aquatic products in 2024, up 3.4% from the previous year, according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs. 

Aquaculture accounted for 82.4% of the total, rising 4.3% to 60.6m metric tons, while capture fisheries fell 0.7% to 13.0m metric tons.

READ MORE

title: Untitled
content:
TRONDHEIM, Norway -- Undercurrent News reported from Trondheim for aquaculture technology event Aqua Nor 2025.

The expo ran from Aug. 19-21, 2025, welcoming international delegates looking for all the latest technological developments in the field of fish farming. 

Check back below for all the updates from the show.

Auto updates: On
AUG 229:29 AM GMT
Pelagia launches ‘next-gen’ fishmeal based on fresh ingredients

Norwegian-made aquaculture inputs are increasingly in demand as the government sets out targets for sustainable feed, such as wanting to increase the proportion of domestically-produced raw materials from the current 8% to 25%.

Pelagics processing giant Pelagia took the opportunity at Aqua Nor to show the results of a study it had conducted with Skretting on its “next-generation” fishmeal, Pro-Allo. 

AUG 226:41 AM GMT
Nordly touts huge potential of alternative plant-based aquafeed ingredients

Plant-based aquaculture feed ingredients are available in huge quantities and are relatively cheap, but come with negative aspects that have required careful testing, noted Jim Roger Nordly of Nordly Holding at Nordea’s seminar this week.

The holding company owns Polarfeed, which has been working with US bioethanol producer Green Plains. They have been testing the ingredient, keen to ensure that the novel raw material would not compromise fish health or biology, he said.

AUG 224:53 AM GMT
Gender sorting tech takes home innovation award

Gender-sorting technology firm GreenFox Marine won the Nor Fishing Foundation’s Innovation Award at this year’s Aqua Nor.

Gender sorting of fish has shown promising results with improved growth and lower mortality rates in sea cages, along with fewer wounds and injuries to the fish.

AUG 223:56 AM GMT
Political commentator: Salmon tax here to stay, whatever Norway’s election outcome

The “salmon tax,” which entered into force from the beginning of 2023, is unlikely to be altered much, if at all, regardless of who wins Norway’s general election early in September, said Torbjorn Roe Isaksen, political editor at newspaper E24, speaking at Nordea’s seminar this week.

Judging by polls and recent history, majority-led governments are a thing of the past, he said. That means — as was the case in passing the salmon tax — complicated negotiations and compromises are necessary in Norway’s parliament, the Storting, to come to any conclusions. 

AUG 222:58 AM GMT
Genetics giant ready to act if, or when, gene editing in salmon is legalized and accepted

Norway-headquartered salmon egg and genetics business AquaGen is busy doing research on gene editing and “CRISPR” technology, even while it is not allowed for industrial production, Trina Galloway, manager for external relations and sustainability, told Undercurrent News.

At present, gene editing in salmon is only allowed in a laboratory environment, and remains unregulated-for in Norwegian food production. But as senior advisor Jakob Soldal put it: “If and when Norway legalizes it, and the consumers accept it, we don’t want to be playing catch-up, we want to be ready.”

AUG 215:56 PM GMT
Lice laser firm Stingray targets H2 2026 for opening of second plant

Since taking investment from Danish firm Novo Holdings in October 2024, Norwegian sea lice laser manufacturer Stingray Marine Solutions has been a company in growth mode.

Driven by more demand than it can currently meet without a serious order backlog, it is building a new production factory next to its existing one in Oslo — “like putting another building on our campus,” Espen Borrud, software manager, told Undercurrent News.

AUG 215:40 PM GMT
Veramaris ready to increase algal oil production output 50% with offtake commitments

Algal oil producer Veramaris is ready to invest in two new fermenters at its facility in Nebraska, the US, increasing output by 50%, but will only take that capital decision when the “offtake commitments” are there, said global business development director Ian Carr.

This year, the company has been the first to supply algal oil in “true bulk,” he said, and it is working with a partner to establish a tank in the Netherlands from which it can supply European customers. 

AUG 216:20 AM GMT
Norway’s offshore regulation changes open door to profitable aquaculture

Norwegian offshore aquaculture business Utror is positive about the next steps based on the government’s ongoing final hearing on changes to how it will regulate the sector.

The government has finalized a move to change how it will license for offshore aquaculture, moving away from a site-based outline and towards area-based regulation. 

AUG 202:28 PM GMT
US tariffs not too concerning for New Zealand businesses eyeing fast-track approval

There are a number of aquaculture businesses in New Zealand that have applied for the environment ministry’s fast-track approvals scheme, launched at the start of 2025, Tauehe Jefferies — investment manager at New Zealand Trade & Enterprise — told Undercurrent News.

The scheme aims to give a range of infrastructure and development projects an answer to their business approvals within just three months. Also in January, the country established Invest New Zealand, which is “actively targeting large global investors and investment opportunities of scale” to bring in foreign capital.

AUG 201:22 PM GMT
M&A expert singles out Eide Fjordbruk as closed-containment system to watch

Norway’s “traffic light” system for determining whether salmon farmers can grow their biomass or must reduce it will remain for at least a few years yet, meaning closed-containment aquaculture systems could get wider commercial use.

That’s because farmers in “red” areas that must reduce their open net-pen stocking can switch to closed-containment units to retain their current volumes.

AUG 2011:03 AM GMT
No progress yet on vital aquafeed ingredient’s FIP

A quota-sharing agreement on vital aquaculture feed ingredient blue whiting in the North Atlantic does not seem to be any closer, Leif Kjetil Skjaeveland — sustainability manager at feed firm Skretting’s Norway division — told Undercurrent News.


“Time is running out, on mackerel and herring, but also for blue whiting. Up until now, there’s been no sign that an agreement is possible — still, it’s a blame culture, talking about principles, pointing fingers, when what we need is for everybody to make concessions.”

AUG 205:43 AM GMT
DNB sees progress on getting alternative feed ingredients to scale

With major fisheries important for fishmeal and oil supply increasingly subject to volatility, the aquaculture sector needs to see some alternatives move from pilot to scale, said DNB’s senior seafood advisor Dag Sletmo, speaking at an event hosted by algal oil producer Veramaris.

“We’ve seen a lot of pilots, and now we need a focus on the few that can be scaled up; and we have seen some progress on that,” he confirmed. 

AUG 205:15 AM GMT
DSM-Firmenich’s sale of animal nutrition division on track to conclude this year

Multinational business DSM-Firmenich is in the process of exiting its Animal Nutrition & Health division, which includes some important fish and shrimp aquaculture units.

The division’s marketing director, Ole Lund Svensen, said he could not provide any news on the new owner, but the process was on track and should “only take a few more months.” The parent business aims to have a deal in place this year.

AUG 191:34 PM GMT
First published field trial shows benefits of krill meal during transfer to sea

A new study has found that feeds containing krill meal can help Atlantic salmon perform better during one of the most challenging phases of their lifecycle: the transition from freshwater to seawater, Kiranpreet Kaur — R&D director for aquaculture at Aker QRILL Company (AQC) — told Undercurrent News.

Conducted by Skretting in collaboration with AQC, this is the first study on the impact of QRILL Aqua from a commercial-scale field trial during the seawater transfer period.

AUG 1912:47 PM GMT
DNV: Verifiable data the bedrock for growth in Norway

As mentioned in an earlier blog post, risk management solutions firm DNV is working on an “automated compliance solution” for aquaculture businesses — using AI to “watch over their shoulder and ensure they are complying with regulations.”

For now, that soft launch product is focused on preventing escapes, Mads Arild Eidem, area manager for Nordics, told Undercurrent News. But in the future, the team working on it hopes it can expand to cover fish health processes, environmental impacts, biodiversity footprint, and more.

AUG 199:55 AM GMT
Tidal launches autonomous AI sea lice control

Tidal, an aquaculture AI and robotics technology spin-off from Google X, the moonshot factory, has announced Tidal Lice Control, an AI-powered system that “operates continuously to detect and neutralize lice without stressful handling of fish.”

Lice Control enables salmon farmers to lower treatment costs, aid fish welfare, and increase yields, while running autonomously inside the pen.

AUG 199:37 AM GMT
Fishglobe ready to ramp up unit production in response to global demand

Fishglobe Technologies — a Norwegian company that produces closed-containment aquaculture units — is ready to ramp up its output in response to global demand, CEO Tor Magne Madsen told Undercurrent News.

The firm is currently constructing three of its units, one of each size bracket (the largest of which is a “30K,” with 30,000 cubic meters of capacity). By the summer of 2026, that should bring the number of operating units up to five, he said.

AUG 193:13 AM GMT
DNV launches industry-first ‘automated compliance solution’

DNV, the independent assurance and risk management provider, has announced the introduction of a new AI-powered fish farm technology, which it says addresses critical compliance requirements set out by the Norwegian government.

The technology is “poised to save man-hours, operational costs, and prevent loss of valuable fish stock.”

AUG 193:04 AM GMT
New Zealand to exhibit at Aqua Nor for first time

For the first time, New Zealand’s trade and investment promotion agencies — New Zealand Trade & Enterprise and Invest New Zealand — will attend Aqua Nor as exhibitors — boasting 12 companies under their umbrella, the event noted.

“After changes were made to the aquaculture regulations in New Zealand, it has become easier to develop the industry and utilize new technology,” Aqua Nor noted. 

Contact the author neil.ramsden@undercurrentnews.com

title: Seafood Expo Bharat: EU importers should expect to pay more for squid, cuttlefish
content:
CHENNAI, India -- Undercurrent News reported from the Seafood Expo Bharat, held in the Indian city of Chennai, deep within India's shrimp farming and processing heartlands.

The event was held by the Indian government's Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA), and brought together seafood producers, processors, technology providers and exporters at the Chennai Trade Centre.

Altogether, MPEDA said the event featured 116 stalls with more than 3,000 delegates.

Auto updates: On
JUL 39:25 AM GMT
EU importers should expect to pay more for squid, cuttlefish this year, says Jeelani chief

Even after last year’s highly limited catches, Abuthahir Aboobakar, CEO of Jeelani Marine Exports, doesn’t believe the coming season is likely to represent a reprieve.

The fishing season on India’s west coast, which produces the majority of the country’s cephalopods, begins Aug. 1 after a two-month gap.

READ MORE
JUL 39:03 AM GMT
India retains edge over Ecuador in small, peeled shrimp, say exporters

Although Ecuador continues to eat into India’s shrimp market share in the US with each passing week, the country still maintains hegemony over several product types, according to exporters at the show.

Chief among these are smaller sizes of peeled shrimp, KG Narayanan, CEO of processor and exporter Nature Fresh Foods, told Undercurrent.

READ MORE
JUL 34:23 AM GMT
MPEDA official suggests India should take larger role as int’l seafood reprocessing hub

Anil Kumar, deputy director of MPEDA, suggested that India could take a bigger role in the import and re-processing of seafood raw material given the hefty 55% US tariffs that remain imposed on Chinese imports.

“We need to import more raw material. Look at China, look at Vietnam — China is able to export more than $18bn, Vietnam is close to $9bn.”

READ MORE
JUL 33:17 AM GMT
Exporter Jeelani reaps rewards for lack of US focus

Abuthahir Aboobakar, CEO of Jeelani Marine Exports, a mid-level seafood exporter based in Maharashtra state, said the company is wildly bucking the broader industry trend this year.

According to the CEO, the firm, which predominantly sells to the Middle East, Europe and Asia, has seen a 40% year-on-year increase in sales since the start of the new Indian financial year on April 1.

READ MORE
JUL 29:56 AM GMT
Seed scarcity remains severe bottleneck for Indian black tiger prospects

For all the talk of Indian shrimp farmers going ‘back to black’, the relative scarcity of specific pathogen-free (SPF) black tiger broodstock in the country is still a serious problem four years after its introduction to India, according to Jaideep Kumar, editor and publisher of Chennai-based Aquaculture Outlook.

“There are only two suppliers of SPF monodon seed, and very few hatcheries,” he told listeners at the show. “There is a very narrow period of monodon farming from the end of February to mid-April, and during this period the entire country does stocking for the first crop.”

READ MORE
JUL 29:37 AM GMT
Avanti shipping to US as normal ahead of July 9 tariff deadline

It remains business as usual at Avanti Frozen Foods, according to COO Chidambar Nadiger, despite the upcoming end to the 90-day tariff freeze looming on the horizon.

Speaking to Undercurrent at the show, Chidambar confirmed that Avanti is continuing to receive and fulfil orders shipped to the US after the July 9 deadline.

READ MORE
JUL 212:32 AM GMT
Smaller Indian exporters would be unable to handle even 10% extra tariff to US

Vrushabh Narayanan, head of business development at Nature Fresh Foods, told Undercurrent that the threat of US tariffs are, understandably, the chief topic of conversation among exporters at the show.

Even if a trade deal is reached and the new additional tariff rate is reduced to just 10%, he said, most smaller exporters will not find it viable to continue trading with the country.

READ MORE
JUL 212:10 AM GMT
MPEDA data shows how Indian exports have stagnated since 2022

Data presented by Anil Kumar, assistant director of MPEDA, demonstrated the impact that Ecuador’s emergence as the world’s number one shrimp producer has had a chilling impact on Indian seafood exports in the last few years.

Indian seafood peaked in the financial year ended March 31, 2023, passing $8bn in export value for the first time.

READ MORE
JUL 111:22 AM GMT
Indian black tiger farmers in AP starting to shift to two crops a year

Panchu Duraisamy, director of Unibio Hatcheries, told Undercurrent at the show that many black tiger shrimp farmers in the south of the country are beginning to attempt two crops a year rather than one.

Traditionally, he said, demand for black tiger broodstock from Unibio is high in the early months of the year, with stocking at its peak from February to April, before farmers settle in for a long grow-out period in order to achieve a large, 50g (20-count) shrimp before the end of the season.

READ MORE
JUL 111:06 AM GMT
India must ‘diversify the export basket,’ urges MPEDA

The Indian shrimp industry’s a tough place to operate these days; if you’re not facing sweeping tariffs from the US, you’re being left off export permit lists to the EU.

With this in mind, Anil Kumar, assistant director of MPEDA, stressed that the country’s seafood sector must reduce its reliance on shrimp.

READ MORE
JUL 110:48 AM GMT
Shrimp exporters to US to keep buying in short term to keep Indian farms stocking

With the end of the 90-day freeze on new tariffs to the US now imminent, buyers are reportedly giving short-term reassurance to Indian shrimp farmers to ensure the industry doesn’t cease stocking.

“Right now, buyers are giving the comfort that whatever the tariffs, we will absorb,” Aquaconnect’s chief growth officer Arpan Bhalerao told Undercurrent at the show.

READ MORE
JUL 13:54 AM GMT
No US buyers at one-to-one networking

There are no traveling US buyers registered for Seafood Expo Bharat’s one-to-one networking event, according to a list of attendees.

Vietnam, Russia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Lebanon are well-represented, but there’s no sign — at least on the board pictured below — of US buyers.

READ MORE
JUL 112:06 AM GMT
Value-added products accounted for 10% of Indian seafood exports last year

In a release from MPEDA ahead of the event, the show’s organizers detailed how value-added production accounted for 10% of the country’s total seafood export value last year.

For the 2024-25 financial year ended March 31, 2025, India exported $7.44 billion worth of seafood, the body said.

READ MORE
JUL 112:03 AM GMT
MPEDA launches ‘National Skill Olympiad’ in effort to boost value-added output

Indian government department MPEDA is launching what it describes as a ‘National Skill Olympiad’ competition testing the processing skills of five trained professionals across the east and west coasts of India.

The final of the event is due to take place on July 1, with a prize of INR 100,000 ($1,100) on offer for the winner.

READ MORE
