title: Seoul Food 2025: K·FISH chef expedition to promote South Korean seafood globally
content:
SEOUL, South Korea -- Undercurrent News is reporting live this week from Seoul Food & Hotel 2025, South Korea’s largest international trade show for the food, beverage, and hospitality industries.

The four-day event, held at KINTEX just outside Seoul, runs from June 10-13 and features 1,603 exhibitors from 51 countries. Organizers expect more than 53,000 trade visitors across sectors, including seafood, processed foods, and hospitality equipment.

In the lead-up to the show, Undercurrent also attended the Norwegian Seafood Council's Seafood Forum, held June 9 in Seoul, where Norwegian exporters and South Korean importers discussed market trends and future collaboration.

Auto updates: On
JUN 125:11 PM GMT
K·FISH chef expedition launches to promote South Korean seafood globally

The Korea Fisheries Association officially launched its “K·FISH CHEF Expedition” project this month, aiming to promote the quality and value of South Korean seafood products to a global audience. 

The initiative brings together globally renowned chefs to develop and showcase dishes using South Korean seafood tailored to international palates.

READ MORE
JUN 124:57 PM GMT
South Korea fisheries leaders urge new president to restore marine affairs post, fulfill pledges

South Korea’s fisheries leaders have called on the new administration of President Lee Jae-myung to deliver on campaign promises and strengthen policy coordination for the sector, according to a recent statement released by the Korea Fisheries Association.

Noh Dong-jin, president of the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (Suhyup), said, “Fishers across the country have high expectations for President Lee’s pledge to realize ‘livable and vibrant fishing villages.'”

READ MORE
JUN 123:50 AM GMT
South Korea’s new president orders Oceans Ministry to relocate to Busan, kicking off fisheries reform

South Korea’s newly elected president Lee Jae-myung has ordered the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to relocate to the southeastern port city of Busan, marking the first major step in a broad effort to overhaul the country’s marine and fisheries sector.

The relocation is intended to consolidate policy planning and implementation in Busan and establish the city as a central hub for marine industries. It was one of Lee’s core campaign pledges aimed at revitalizing coastal regions and enhancing the efficiency of marine governance.

READ MORE
JUN 123:25 AM GMT
South Korea’s eel sector faces major threat from potential CITES listing

South Korea’s inland aquaculture industry is bracing for a potential blow as the European Union seeks to list japonica eel (Anguilla japonica) under Appendix II of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

The proposed listing — expected to be discussed at the CITES conference in November 2025 — would restrict imports of glass eels, the critical seed stock for farms. South Korea’s eel sector remains heavily reliant on these imports, which accounted for over 80% of the country’s 10.7 metric tons of stocking volume in 2024, according to a recent report from the Korea Maritime Institute (KMI). 

READ MORE
JUN 118:36 PM GMT
Russia overtakes US as South Korea’s top pollock surimi supplier

Russia has surpassed the US as South Korea’s largest supplier of frozen pollock surimi blocks in the first four months of 2025, according to newly released import data from the Korea Customs Service.

South Korea imported 4,579 metric tons of Russian-origin frozen pollock surimi between January and April, priced at an average $2.35 per kilogram. US shipments for the same period totaled 4,529t at a higher unit price of $2.59/kg. 

READ MORE
JUN 118:04 PM GMT
New Zealand weighs CSI certification program ahead of group’s first board meeting

Seafood New Zealand, the industry body representing the country’s commercial seafood sector, is actively considering joining Certified Seafood International (CSI), a new global seafood certification scheme aiming to offer an affordable, credible alternative for wild-capture fisheries, Akiko Yakata, trade representative for the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute, told Undercurrent News.

Yakata said CSI was “born in Alaska, raised in North America, and is now beginning its full internationalization,” with its first board meeting scheduled for later this month. She emphasized that the program is designed to allow fishers and stakeholders to participate, without facing the high costs often associated with other schemes.

READ MORE
JUN 117:22 PM GMT
E-commerce surge reshapes South Korea’s at-home mackerel consumption

E-commerce is rapidly becoming a major force in South Korea’s seafood retail sector, with mackerel and other frozen fish products seeing significant growth in online sales, according to data presented at the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC)’s forum.

In 2024, approximately 90% of mackerel consumption in South Korea took place at home. Of that, 30% occurred through e-commerce platforms — a notably high ratio compared to Japan, where online seafood purchases remain minimal, NSC advisor Paul Y. Tsai said during his presentation.

READ MORE
JUN 117:15 PM GMT
Domestic crab dominates South Korea’s market, Russia leads imports

South Korea’s crab market is still led by domestic species, which accounted for the majority of total consumption in 2024, with imported king and snow crab — primarily from Russia — continuing to play an important role in the premium segment, according to the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC).

More than 45,000 metric tons of crab were consumed in South Korea last year, with 78% coming from domestic sources. Imported snow crab made up 18%, while king crab represented just 4%, based on figures from the NSC and Korea Customs Service.

READ MORE
JUN 114:49 AM GMT
South Korea’s largest e-commerce platform wants to nearly triple seafood sales by 2027

Coupang, South Korea’s largest e-commerce platform, aims to grow its seafood sales by 2.7 times between 2023 and 2027 amid accelerating online demand for fresh and frozen products, according to Jason Shin, a representative of the company, speaking at the Norwegian Seafood Council forum.

Shin said the company is leveraging its nationwide “Rocket Delivery” system — capable of same-day, dawn, and next-day delivery year-round — to increase seafood purchases online. 

READ MORE
JUN 109:40 PM GMT
‘Alaska Premium’ push in Korea draws on Japan model amid Russian rivalry

The Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute (ASMI) is aiming to boost recognition of its “Alaska Premium” brand in South Korea by leveraging Japan’s successful marketing examples, as American seafood faces strong competition from Russian products across a wide range of species, ASMI trade representative Akiko Yakata told Undercurrent News.

“There’s no ASMI office in Korea. But, it is an important market for us,” Yakata said. “It’s not an emerging market like India — it’s a stable one. The challenge is that Russian seafood is dominant here.”

READ MORE
JUN 108:38 PM GMT
Norwegian salmon exporters face hurdles in South Korea over facility approvals

Norwegian salmon exporters are encountering logistical and regulatory hurdles when shipping to South Korea, due to the country’s requirements for prior approval of individual packing stations.

“With many packing stations in Norway, not all the exporters can have all the packing stations approved at one time — that would be too expensive,” Jorgen Roaldnes of Ocean Supreme, a leading Norwegian salmon exporter, said at the Norwegian Seafood Forum. 

READ MORE
JUN 106:26 PM GMT
South Korea’s first RAS Atlantic salmon farm advances with second fry transfer 

Eco Aquafarm, the first company in South Korea to raise Atlantic salmon on land, has transferred its second batch of fry to its recirculating aquaculture system (RAS), continuing its ramp-up of domestic production.

“The Atlantic salmon fry, which had absorbed their yolk sacs healthily in the hatchery, were successfully transferred to the RAS1 tank,” the company said in a LinkedIn post last week. “The Atlantic salmon from batch one, which were transferred to RAS1 in February, as well as those from batch zero, which were transferred to RAS2 last month, are all growing very healthily.”

READ MORE
JUN 109:52 AM GMT
South Korea appoints trade negotiator as newly elected president Lee Jae-myung asks for more time

Newly elected South Korean president Lee Jae-myung has appointed a veteran trade negotiator to be his lead in working out a trade deal with the US.

South Korea faces an increase in tariffs on its exports to the US from the current 10% to 25% on July 9.

READ MORE
JUN 1012:03 AM GMT
Norwegian seafood exports to South Korea rise 13% in value, with salmon driving growth

Norwegian seafood exports to South Korea reached NOK 5.3 billion ($500 million) in 2024, up 13% year-on-year in value and 7% in volume, according to Johan Kvalheim, regional director for Japan and South Korea at the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC).

Norway shipped 77,500 metric tons of seafood to South Korea last year, making it the country’s 12th largest market by export value, overtaking Japan in the rankings.

READ MORE
JUN 911:58 PM GMT
Fish consumption declines in Korea as meat remains dominant

Fish consumption in South Korea has been on a downward trend in recent years, with meat remaining the preferred source of animal protein by a wide margin, according to data presented at the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC) forum held Monday at the Four Seasons Hotel in Seoul.

Paul Y Tsai, advisor to the NSC, highlighted that while Korea is often regarded as a major seafood-consuming nation, a closer look shows that 40% of that consumption comes from seaweed. 

READ MORE
JUN 911:55 PM GMT
South Korean seafood exports face headwinds as US tariffs bite

South Korea’s seafood export growth slowed sharply in early 2025, as new US tariffs and tightening regulations began to weigh on shipments to one of its key markets.

Seafood exports totaled $1.05 billion between January and April, up 3.7% from a year earlier, according to data from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the Korea Maritime Institute. While the figure marks continued growth, it represents a significant deceleration compared to previous years.

title: Thaifex 2025: US stockpiling sees Thai canned tuna exports jump; Norway mackerel prices on track for new high
content:
BANGKOK, Thailand -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the Thaifex Anuga Asia food show, held at the IMPACT Muang Thong Thani events hall in Bangkok, Thailand, from May 27 to 31.

This year’s show is larger than last year's, featuring 3,233 exhibitors across 6,205 booths, representing Thailand and more than 56 countries worldwide. The event is expected to attract over 90,000 trade visitors from around the globe across five days. 

Thaifex Anuga Asia covers a wide range of food and beverage segments, with a significant portion dedicated to seafood. Many of Thailand's largest seafood traders and processors are present, including major conglomerates Charoen Pokphand Foods and Thai Union Group.

Auto updates: On
JUN 15:04 AM GMT
Thai canned tuna exports jump in Q1 on US tariff stockpiling

Thailand’s canned tuna exports got off to a solid start in 2025. From January to March, the country shipped 140,762 metric tons worth $599 million — up 5% in volume and 1% in value year-on-year, according to the Thai Tuna Industry Association (TTIA).

Strong demand came from the US, Africa, Latin America, and the EU, with US-bound exports alone rising 14% — partly due to buyers placing early orders ahead of the expected tariff hike.

READ MORE
MAY 315:37 AM GMT
Reduced quota set to push Norwegian mackerel prices to another record high

Prices for Norwegian mackerel for the upcoming season, which begins in August, will “no doubt” exceed the record levels seen in 2024–25, driven by intensified competition due to a reduced quota, multiple sources told Undercurrent News.

The International Council for the Exploration of the Sea recommended last September that the total allowable catch for Northeast Atlantic mackerel in 2025 be cut by 22% from 2024-25 to 576,958 metric tons, as reported by Undercurrent.

READ MORE
MAY 314:52 AM GMT
Thai importer Todokeru Foods targets regional growth for Japan’s premium seafood

Bangkok, Thailand-based importer and distributor Todokeru Foods is working with a major wholesaler from Toyosu Market in Tokyo — home to the world’s largest seafood trade volume — to expand sales of premium Japanese seafood in Thailand and neighboring countries.

“Thailand’s seafood market is already a red ocean, with intense competition,” sales manager Takami Tadasuke told Undercurrent News. “The local economy is getting weak, and demand for high-end seafood has declined. That’s why we’re now looking to grow our reach into nearby countries.”

READ MORE
MAY 3112:50 AM GMT
Vinh Hoan launches pangasius instant noodles to maximize fish use

Vietnamese pangasius giant Vinh Hoan Corp. has begun selling a new instant noodle product featuring pangasius surimi noodles in a kimchi-based soup, targeting Asian and European markets.

The noodles are made from surimi produced at a processing plant completed last year, and the final product is assembled at a facility operated by Sa Giang, a Vinh Hoan group company.

READ MORE
MAY 309:48 PM GMT
Chinese buyers rush for Hokkaido scallops ahead of Japan seafood ban reversal

Chinese seafood processors are scrambling to secure Japanese scallops, particularly from Hokkaido, following signs that Beijing will soon lift its ban on Japanese seafood imports, multiple sources at the Thaifex told Undercurrent News.

“Even before the official government announcement on Friday, it seems Chinese buyers had already gotten word. Inquiries from China began surging from Thursday,” said an exporter of Japanese scallops. 

READ MORE
MAY 2910:12 PM GMT
Maruha Nichiro expands ultra-low temperature tuna sashimi sales in Thailand

Maruha Nichiro Corp., the world’s largest seafood company, is expanding its sales of ultra-low temperature tuna in Thailand as part of a broader push to tap growing seafood demand in Southeast Asia.

“We see strong potential in this market,” Yasuhiro Hashimoto, managing director of Maruha Nichiro (Thailand) Co., told Undercurrent News. “We’ve moved into full-scale sales following a trial in 2023.”

READ MORE
MAY 296:57 PM GMT
Thaifex features 206 seafood companies this year

The Thaifex Anuga Asia show 2025 has featured 3,233 exhibitors representing Thailand and more than 56 countries, slightly up from 3,133 at last year’s event.

A total of 206 companies from the seafood sector had stands, accounting for 6% of the exhibitors.

READ MORE
MAY 2910:12 AM GMT
China’s HuaChang shifts focus from US to Southeast Asia amid trade tensions

Chinese seafood processor Dongshan HuaChang Foodstuff Co. is ramping up efforts to diversify beyond the US market, as ongoing trade tensions between China and the US put pressure on its core export business.

“About 60% of our sales are to the US, but we are actively working to reduce that ratio,” Frank Lin, a sales department representative at the company, told Undercurrent News. “We’re focusing especially on expanding sales of red swimming crabmeat and abalone products in Southeast Asia.”

READ MORE
MAY 299:54 AM GMT
JETRO pushes for menu shift to Japan-origin fish amid Japanese cuisine boom in Thailand

The Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) is stepping up efforts to promote Japanese farmed seafood in Thailand, with plans to host a chef-focused training course in late July in partnership with local culinary institutions.

The seminar will highlight species such as farmed salmon and red sea bream, targeting both professional chefs and culinary students, JETRO Bangkok director Yoshiaki Suda told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 297:34 AM GMT
CP-Uoriki expands to 24 retail stores, eyes 10 additional outlets in 2025

CP-Uoriki Co., a joint venture between CPF Global Food Solution — part of Thai protein giant Charoen Pokphand Foods — and Japanese seafood retailer Uoriki, is accelerating its sushi retail expansion in Thailand, with plans to grow its footprint beyond Bangkok.

Since opening its first outlet in October 2023 inside the Lotus’s Sukhumvit 50 store, CP-Uoriki has grown to 24 retail locations across the country, managing director Jatuphon Tantisuntharodom told Undercurrent News. The company aims to open 10 more by December 2025.

READ MORE
MAY 293:21 AM GMT
Ode taps emerging demand for premium sashimi in Southeast Asia

Norwegian Atlantic cod farmer Ode has officially begun expanding into Southeast Asia, with a focus on developing new markets in the region, according to sales manager Kristoffer Remo.

The company started shipping to Thailand last year and now plans to broaden its customer base to include Singapore — where a large, affluent population resides — and Vietnam, which is seeing rapid growth in its middle-income demographic, Remo told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 292:57 AM GMT
Some Norwegian salmon suppliers begin freezing early amid slumping fresh prices

Several Norwegian Atlantic salmon suppliers have begun freezing their fish earlier than usual this year due to a persistent decline in fresh market prices, sources at Thaifex told Undercurrent News.

“Last year, not a single company started freezing in May or June,” said a source with processing capabilities. “But now, with fresh prices falling, some are trying to secure profitability — even though there’s still a risk the market could drop further.”

READ MORE
MAY 292:41 AM GMT
Chile makes frozen coho salmon debut in Australia

Chilean frozen farmed coho salmon has entered the Australian market for the first time, reflecting a broader push by the South American industry to diversify exports beyond the traditional market of Japan, Jorge Guzman Espinola, commercial director of Salmones Aysen, told Undercurrent News.

The milestone comes after Australia’s Department of Agriculture, Water and the Environment approved Chile as an eligible salmon exporter in September 2024. 

READ MORE
MAY 288:24 PM GMT
Dongwon F&B rides K-Food wave with surimi street food, seaweed snacks in Southeast Asia

South Korean seafood and food conglomerate Dongwon Industries is accelerating the Southeast Asia expansion of its processed seafood and K-food business through its production arm, Dongwon F&B.

Dongwon F&B showcased a wide range of Korean-style ready-to-eat and snack products under its flagship brand “Yangban.” The brand is known for combining authentic Korean flavors with convenience, catering to a growing global demand for K-food.

READ MORE
MAY 287:59 PM GMT
Nissui aims to boost exports from Thai factory beyond Japan

Japanese seafood giant Nissui Corp. is stepping up efforts to expand exports of value-added products from its Thai factory to markets beyond Japan, including within Thailand.

“Currently, around 90% of the products we manufacture at our factory are exported to Japan, with the remainder going to other markets, including Thailand,” Yusuke Mano, assistant general manager of Nissui (Thailand) Co., the Tokyo-based group’s Thai production and sales arm. 

READ MORE
MAY 287:31 PM GMT
Sea Value hits record $1bn in revenue, eyes similar result in 2025 despite tariff risks

Sea Value, Thailand’s second-largest canned tuna producer, posted record revenue of $1 billion in 2024, up 20% from the previous year, CEO Amornphan Aramwatananont told Undercurrent News.

Both the company’s human food and pet food segments contributed to the strong growth, he said. Sea Value is targeting a similar result in 2025, despite growing uncertainty surrounding US trade policy.

READ MORE
MAY 284:30 AM GMT
Thailand’s tuna sector pushes sustainability, eyes growth amid market uncertainty

Thailand’s tuna export industry is showing signs of resilience and sustainable transformation, even as global markets face volatility, according to Amornphan Aramwatananont, director of the Thai Tuna Industry Association (TTIA).

Speaking Tuesday at a panel titled “The Future of Seafood Trade: Global Trends and Market Dynamics,” Amornphan offered insights into the sector’s performance, export growth, and long-standing sustainability efforts.

READ MORE
MAY 282:30 AM GMT
Stay alert amid trade shocks, focus on sustainability, culture, says Alaska seafood marketer

With global supply chains under stress and trade disruptions accelerating, Allen Kimball, chair of the board at the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute, urged the seafood industry to stay vigilant and adaptive during a Wednesday panel.

“It’s a time to pay attention,” Kimball said during the session. “Things can happen in a week, even in just a few days. As an industry, we sometimes need to hesitate — but the business has to go on.”

READ MORE
MAY 282:19 AM GMT
Trust, youth demand driving seafood’s future, says Norwegian Seafood Council CEO

Norwegian Seafood Council CEO Christian Chramer called on the seafood industry to shift focus toward younger consumers, transparency, and sustainability, speaking Wednesday at a Thaifex Anuga Asia panel titled The Future of Seafood Trade: Global Trends and Market Dynamics.

“Younger consumers expect ready-to-cook, ready-to-eat products with sustainable credentials,” Chramer said, citing a McKinsey report on shifting retail trends. “Companies need to be trend-focused and tap into what this generation values.”

READ MORE
MAY 275:35 PM GMT
Siam Canadian leans on diversification to withstand US tariff uncertainty

As uncertainty over US trade policy blows a cold chill through global seafood markets, seafood trader Siam Canadian Group is relying on a decades-old strategy of diversification and measured growth to weather the storm.

“Uncertainty is the enemy of business,” the company’s managing director, James Gulkin, told Undercurrent News. “We’ve never had a year that wasn’t profitable in nearly 40 years, but this kind of unpredictability makes it harder to plan than ever.”

READ MORE
MAY 279:39 AM GMT
Japan’s largest trout farmer turns profit in first full year of Thai seafood wholesale operation

Okamura Trading (Thailand) Co., the seafood wholesale arm of Japan’s largest trout farming company, Okamura Foods, has turned a profit in its first full fiscal year of operations,  managing director Sho Oba told Undercurrent News.

Established in July 2023, the Thai subsidiary is the group’s fourth offshore wholesale hub in Asia and part of a broader strategy to boost overseas sales. The company saw strong demand in Thailand for both its flagship “Aomori Salmon” brand and value-added products like pink salmon roe, with sales performing well across foodservice and retail sectors, said Oba.

READ MORE
MAY 273:38 AM GMT
Russia overtakes US as top pollock surimi supplier to Thailand

Thailand’s imports of pollock surimi from Russia surged nearly 20-fold year-on-year to 499 metric tons in the first quarter of 2025, surpassing US volumes and underscoring Russia’s growing presence in Asian surimi markets.

The sharp increase from just 24t a year earlier put Russia ahead of the US, which shipped 326t during the same period, according to Thai Customs Department data.

READ MORE
MAY 273:34 AM GMT
Norwegian seafood exports to Thailand hit record high as demand surges

Norway’s seafood exports to Thailand climbed to a record THB 10 billion ($306bn) and 42,500 metric tons in 2024, up 13% in value and 8% in volume from the previous year, Christian Chramer, CEO of the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC), said during his speech at a Teusday (May 27) press briefing.

Salmon and fjord trout made up 91% of the total shipment, driven by strong demand for fresh, high-quality products. “This shows what a strong global position our seafood has,” he added.

READ MORE

title: Untitled
content:
BARCELONA, Spain -- Eleven members of the Undercurrent News editorial and price reporting team covered Seafood Expo Global (SEG) in Barcelona, Spain. 

SEG took place from Tuesday, May 6, to Thursday, May 8, with Undercurrent reporting on Monday from a salmon-focused event organized by Euronext and Norwegian lender DNB Bank. 

Auto updates: On
MAY 94:55 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chinese processors restart shipping to US using Alaskan raw material

Chinese processing companies have started shipping again to US customers using Alaskan raw material, after the trade ground to a halt with 145% duties applied by president Donald Trump, a large player in the sector told Undercurrent News at SEG.

Shipping started again around two weeks ago, with companies using the onward processing relief (OPR) approach (click here for more on this system) used in Europe and the UK for domestic raw material sent to China and brought back as fillets, he said.

READ MORE
MAY 98:46 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese seafood processor squeezed by record raw material costs

In what is likely a sentiment shared by many whitefish processors currently, a Dalian, China-based company said they feel “extremely anxious” about buying cod and haddock for processing as record high prices leave them exposed to sudden shocks.

“Prices for all our raw materials are increasing, which is actually quite difficult for our factory,” a spokesperson, who wished to be quoted unnamed, told Undercurrent News. “We’re afraid to buy too much in case we’ve reached the peak in prices, and then when prices fall, all our fish will be too expensive.”

READ MORE
MAY 96:41 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Taiwanese exporters hoping for US tariff exception

Three Taiwanese exporters exhibiting at SEG told Undercurrent News they’re hoping their country’s special relationship with the US will eventually spare it from the brunt of the reciprocal tariffs imposed by US president Donald Trump.

On July 11, the US tariff rate on Taiwan is slated to bump up to 32% from the current global baseline of 10%.

READ MORE
MAY 95:17 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese tilapia exporter reels from US tariffs, 90% of sales at risk

A major Chinese tilapia processor is facing turmoil as punitive US tariffs of 170% collapse its primary export market, according to company executives.

The Guangdong-based firm, which shipped 800 containers of tilapia fillets last year with 90% destined for American consumers, has been forced to dramatically scale back operations while awaiting resolution on US-China trade.

READ MORE
MAY 94:52 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Indian loligo squid prices hit record level on ‘worst fishing season’

Indian loligo squid prices have surged to unprecedented levels following what an industry veteran described as one of the worst fishing seasons in recent memory.

Raw material prices for Loligo duvaucelii, a medium-sized squid species primarily found in Indian waters, have reached over INR 500 per kilogram ($5.85/kg) — a record high according to Vilas Joshi, export manager at Salet Group in Gujarat, India.

READ MORE
MAY 94:02 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Spanish bluefin tuna firm Balfego launches new product following plant opening 

Spain’s Balfego Group — which catches, ranches, and processes bluefin tuna — has launched a new sashimi grade Saku block, which is frozen at -60° C (see photo below).

The firm inaugurated a new 12,000-square-meter facility last month in L’Ametilla de Mar, Tarragona.

READ MORE
MAY 811:28 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan’s Kibun Foods to expand sales in Europe as US market outlook remains unclear

Kibun Foods, the world’s largest manufacturer of surimi-based products by revenue, is looking to expand its presence in the European market as uncertainty persists over its business outlook in the US due to the tariffs, Ryota Suganuma, sales representative at Kibun Europe, told Undercurrent News.

The company returned to exhibit at SEG for the first time in two years, introducing products such as imitation crab sticks produced at its factory in Thailand and chikuwa (fish cake tubes) manufactured at its Chiba plant in Japan, targeting European buyers.

READ MORE
MAY 811:13 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Channel plans to process H&G Alaskan, East Coast US flatfish

Channel Fish Processing plans to start cutting headed and gutted (H&G) flatfish from Alaska and also the US East Coast, president Tom Zaffiro told Undercurrent News.

The company plans to start buying H&G Alaskan yellowfin sole, rock sole, and flathead sole, in addition to some East Coast flatfish, as part of a drive to boost its US fish sourcing and processing, amid president Donald Trump’s import tariffs.

READ MORE
MAY 810:45 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Ecuadorian shrimp processor doubles down on value-added despite labor challenges

Frigolandia, an Ecuadorian shrimp processor and exporter, is ramping up its value-added processing capacity as part of a strategy to reduce its dependence on the Chinese market.

Milenko Martinez, the company’s international sales manager, told Undercurrent News that Frigolandia is introducing double shifts at its value-added processing plant and improved efficiency to increase production.

READ MORE
MAY 89:50 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Zalmhuys MD: ‘Everyone can live with 10%. But 20% would be unbearable’

With 75% of its business in Europe, Zalmhuys Group is in a better position to absorb US tariffs than many other companies in the seafood industry.

Nevertheless, Zalmhuys managing director Harm ten Napel said there’s trepidation about the long-term consequences of the trade war initiated by US president Donald Trump.

READ MORE
MAY 89:50 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
First direct flights of live lobsters from Newfoundland, Canada, to Europe begin this summer

Live lobster from the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador (NL) will soon enjoy something the citizens of the North Atlantic island don’t: regular direct flights to Europe.

This summer, likely before the end of June, the inaugural cargo flight of live North American lobsters (Homarus americanus) will take off from Gander airport, a small town located in the center of the island, to Madrid, Spain, Darrell Roche, president of St. John’s, NL-based Whitecap International Seafood Exporters, revealed this week to Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 87:34 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Iceland’s Isstormur gains recognition for ready-to-heat seafood meals

Founded in 2019, Sudurnesjabaer, Iceland-based Isstormur now sells 33 separate seafood value-added products, having introduced 13 in the past year alone.

Its Hawaiian salmon salad, mackerel with chickpeas in a spicy Moroccan sauce and tuna risoni, sold under its Storm brand, won the special prize for best seafood product line at the 2025 Seafood Excellence Awards.

READ MORE
MAY 86:28 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Bristol Bay sockeye season approaches with strong H&G price expectations

The Bristol Bay sockeye salmon season in Alaska, the US, is set to begin in late June, with major producers aiming to target frozen headed-and-gutted (H&G) export prices at levels at least equal to those seen during the second half of the previous season, sources told Undercurrent News.

Some packers are setting a benchmark of at least $5.00 per pound cost and freight for No. 1 grade, four-to-six-pound H&G, for the Europe and Asia markets. This represents an increase from early last year’s offers of around $4.50/lb, driven by strong demand in the US refresh market.

READ MORE
MAY 83:50 AM GMT
ASC, Labeyrie, Omarsa partner up to restore Ecuador’s mangrove forests

As part of a shared commitment to environmental stewardship and responsible aquaculture, the Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC), Labeyrie Fine Foods, and Ecuadorian shrimp producer Omarsa have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to collaborate on a 10-hectare mangrove restoration effort in Ecuador.

Under the newly signed MoU, the partners will collaborate on long-term efforts to restore degraded mangrove areas in Ecuador, promote community-based conservation, and integrate mangrove protection into sustainable seafood supply chains. The initiative will not only contribute to climate resilience and biodiversity but also empower local communities who depend on healthy coastal environments for their livelihoods, they said.

READ MORE
MAY 83:08 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese firm to fly small-sized Aussie bluefin tuna to Europe, Asia

A Chinese company aims to make fresh bluefin tuna available year-round in smaller, restaurant-friendly sizes, targeting global expansion after initial success in Asian markets.

Shanghai Xijingyang Supply Chain Management told Undercurrent News it has secured exclusive rights to distribute fresh bluefin tuna from an Australian fish farm in Port Lincoln, offering 15-25 kilogram specimens that cater to smaller restaurants unable to utilize the massive fish typically available in the market.

READ MORE
MAY 83:03 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Norway’s ‘superior’ salmon price dive doesn’t tell full story

The average prices on Norwegian farmed salmon are actually up in 2025, despite the drop in superior grade, a senior executive with one of the country’s largest exporters told Undercurrent News at SEG.

That’s due to the massive volumes of production grade fish seen in 2024, which spiked the prices for the smaller volumes of superior grade left, the high level executive said.

READ MORE
MAY 82:13 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Ecuador’s Santa Priscila to build 8th processing plant

Ecuadorian shrimp firm Industrial Pesquera Santa Priscila is moving forward with plans to build an additional processing plant as it continues to expand capacity to meet growing global demand. 

The company confirmed to Undercurrent News that the decision to construct the new facility has been made, though the specific site has not yet been finalized as it awaits approval from a local municipality. 

READ MORE
MAY 81:01 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan’s surimi manufacturer remains committed to doubling offshore sales despite global trade challenges

Despite growing uncertainty in global seafood trade, Japan-based finished surimi manufacturer Yamasa Kamaboko remains committed to its goal of doubling overseas sales to JPY 3 billion ($27 million), Homare Nada, an executive director at the company, told Undercurrent News.

Overseas markets currently account for around 15% of Yamasa Kamaboko’s annual revenue of JPY 10bn. Key export destinations include Taiwan, Singapore, and Hong Kong. 

READ MORE
MAY 711:11 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Nissui-backed Kunihiro supports Vietnam oyster sector to meet Japanese standard

Kunihiro, Japan’s largest oyster seller, has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Vietnam Fisheries Society to enhance production and processing, Hiroshi Kawasaki, the firm’s director and chief marketing executive, told Undercurrent News.

The firm, based in Onomichi, Hiroshima, is an “equity method affiliate” of the Japanese seafood company Nissui, meaning Nissui owns a significant share in the firm and includes the affiliate’s profits or losses in its financial reports. An agreement signed on April 23 details their partnership to create a supply chain for Vietnamese oysters that meet Japanese standards for both domestic and export markets.

READ MORE
MAY 71:32 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Profand’s fleet becomes first in Argentina to certify under BSP’s responsible fishing vessel standard

Spain-based cephalopod and shrimp fishing and processing firm Grupo Profand has become the first company in Argentina to achieve certification under the Best Seafood Practices (BSP) Responsible Fishing Vessel Standard (RFVS).

The certification, issued by the Global Seafood Alliance (GSA), recognizes Profand’s Argentinian fleet of squid and shrimp vessels for upholding high standards in crew safety and welfare. 

READ MORE
MAY 71:24 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese firm opens $27m eel processing facilities 

Fujian Haide Food, China’s largest producer of farmed eel, has invested CNY 200 million ($27m) in two new processing facilities in Fujian province amid an exceptionally strong glass eel harvesting season.

The significant investment comes during what a company spokesperson described as a peak year in the natural four-to-five-year cycle of eel fry abundance. Wild glass eel catches worldwide have reached over 100 metric tons this year, compared to just 30t in the previous season.

READ MORE
MAY 71:16 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Ecuadorian shrimp sector optimistic amid strong yields, stable prices

Ecuador’s shrimp industry is enjoying strong production, with levels exceeding internal expectations and prices holding steady, according to GLuna Shrimp owner Gabriel Luna.

“There’s a sense of optimism in Ecuador’s shrimp sector right now. Production levels are higher than I expected at this point in the year, and prices have remained stable, which makes for a very favorable scenario for us,” he, co-founder and co-chair of the Global Shrimp Council, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 71:14 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Octopus prices reach record highs amid surging demand in EU, US

Octopus prices in Morocco and Mauritania have soared to record highs, driven by strong demand from both Europe and the US.

The octopus winter fishing season in Mauritania and Morocco has recently concluded, leading to a surge in prices across international markets. Spanish and Portuguese processors are reporting price increases across all sizes of octopus, with no signs of relief ahead of the next season.

READ MORE
MAY 71:03 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Ghana’s Tropo Farms gears up for 5,000t tilapia boost with new cage installation

Tropo Farms, one of the biggest tilapia producers in sub-Saharan Africa, is preparing to scale up production by an additional 5,000 metric tons annually as it begins deploying new infrastructure funded by a $10 million investment secured in late 2024.

“The company is in the final stages of acquiring a new module of 12 fish cages, each 30 meters in diameter,” CEO Francisco Murillo told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 712:57 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Record Chinese exports in Q1 amid US stockpiling

China’s seafood exports hit a quarterly record volume in the first three months of 2025, primarily driven by US importers building inventory in anticipation of tariff increases under US president Donald Trump, according to the country’s leading industry association.

Cui He, president of the China Aquatic Products Processing and Marketing Alliance, told Undercurrent News he expects a reversal of this trend for the remainder of the year, largely due to escalating trade barriers with the US.

READ MORE
MAY 712:42 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
US tariff tensions stir Falklands toothfish exporters to seek alternative markets

A cloud of uncertainty is hanging over the Falkland Islands’ prized Patagonian toothfish (also marketed as Chilean seabass), as US trade policy once again threatens to shake one of its most important export relationships.

The sector is now facing renewed challenges as the US considers reinstating a steep tariff on Patagonian toothfish imports from the British overseas territory.

READ MORE
MAY 712:40 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Hundreds evacuated after toxic gas leak at Profand plant in Spain

A toxic ammonia leak at Spain-based cephalopod and shrimp fishing and processing firm Grupo Profand’s cold storage plant in Zaragoza, northern Spain triggered the evacuation of up to 800 workers on Tuesday (May 7) morning.

The leak, which occurred during routine maintenance work, has since been fully contained, and no serious injuries were reported, a company representative told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 712:08 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
World’s only black cod farmer to increase production in Canada

The world’s only egg-to-plate black cod aquaculture company is expanding its farm site in the Canadian province of British Columbia (BC), increasing production in order to meet growing demand.

Golden Eagle Farms is adding a third sea cage at its site in Kyuquot Sound, BC, which will be operational this October, the company’s marketing and innovation manager, Jade Berge, told Undercurrent News this week at Seafood Expo Global (SEG).

READ MORE
MAY 710:25 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Equipment needed for US firms to ‘re-shore’ processing hit by Trump tariffs

Much of the equipment US seafood companies need to “re-shore” production is made overseas and so is subject to tariffs, executives told Undercurrent News at SEG.

Channel Fish Company, a large processor based in Braintree, Massachusetts, had to put on hold an order for a plate freezer from China as the cost went from $80,000 to around $200,000, its president Thomas Zaffiro told Undercurrent.

READ MORE
MAY 79:31 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Aquaculture Stewardship Council launches new farm, feed standards

The Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) sustainability certification for farmed seafood formally launched its new farm standard and feed standard at SEG.

As previously reported by Undercurrent News, the new standard unifies previous species-specific standards into a single framework built around four core principles: legal compliance and effective business management; environmental stewardship; respecting and promoting human rights; and responsible animal health and welfare practices.

READ MORE
MAY 78:26 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Australia’s Abrolhos Octopus launches stir-in octopus sauce, cooked tentacles

Abrolhos Octopus has two new retail products drawing attention at SEG: octopus sauce and cooked tentacles.

Available at retail just for the last month, the sauce has become a favorite among Australian chefs for adding deeper flavor to pasta, seafood chowders and calamari dips, Dion van der Merwe, the managing director of the Darch, Western Australia-based company, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 76:48 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Vegan Fisherman: Analogs now cheaper than seafood

Plant-based fish substitutes are getting cheaper than traditional seafood, according to Simon Visscher, the owner of Vegan Fisherman, a Netherlands-based creator of vegan analogs.

Visscher spoke to Undercurrent News as he was touting samples of his company’s vegan shrimp croquettes, fish sticks and crab cakes on the show floor at SEG.

READ MORE
MAY 76:34 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Peruvian jumbo flying squid catches rebound after tough year

Peru’s jumbo flying squid fishery has seen a slow recovery in the first months of 2025, following a significant downturn that left many processing companies struggling for raw material throughout much of last year.

“Catches are recovering; however, sizes being caught are much smaller,” one industry source told Undercurrent News, noting that while catches have improved, squid being landed are generally smaller than usual. “It is too small to make some products such as rings, or other [value added products] that need bigger sized fish, so we are selling whole fish to China.

READ MORE
MAY 76:26 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Kvaroy Arctic introduces mini salmon corn dogs after scaling back hot dogs

Norway’s Kvaroy Arctic debuted a new addition to its line of kid-focused products while at SEG in Barcelona this week: mini salmon corn dogs. 

While the company told Undercurrent News that it is scaling back its salmon-based hot dog line of products in the US, Kvaroy Arctic is staying in the space with its corn dog alternative.

READ MORE
MAY 76:16 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Surging Chinese demand drives 10% increase in Indian itoyori surimi prices

Prices for Indian frozen threadfin bream surimi blocks, also known as itoyori, have risen by about 10% year-on-year, fueled by a surge in demand from China, a marketing director at a major Indian surimi producer told Undercurrent News.

“Since March, we’ve seen a sharp increase in inquiries from China,” the executive said. “Vietnam’s surimi production has dropped significantly, prompting buyers to turn to Indian-origin products.”

READ MORE
MAY 76:01 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Chinese 2x pollock fillet deals with Europe delayed due to high H&G prices, low ceiling from Alaskan PBO

Squeezed Chinese processors have closed far fewer double-frozen pollock fillet deals with Europe than normal by May as SEG gets underway, sources told Undercurrent News.

The high level for headed and gutted (H&G) pollock raw material, which has been $1,350-$1,420 per metric ton cost and freight (CFR) China these past few weeks, means Chinese processors are pushing for levels that buyers have not been willing to commit to, sources told Undercurrent. 

READ MORE
MAY 75:16 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Uncertainty looms over Falklands’ upcoming loligo squid fishing season after mixed first half

As the second loligo squid fishing season in the Falkland Islands’ approaches, the industry is bracing for uncertainty following an average but shorter-than-expected first season. 

While the initial season, which closed on April 28, yielded around 38,000 metric tons — a figure that would be considered average in historical terms — concerns linger about what lies ahead.

READ MORE
MAY 74:28 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Seabass prices surge amid shortages, outpacing bream

Seabass prices have outpaced seabream prices, with industry sources citing a significant supply shortage as the driving factor. 

Current free on board (FOB) prices for 400-600 (4-6) gram size seabass in Greece have climbed to €6.80 per kilogram, with CFR prices in markets like Spain reaching €7.30/kg. In contrast, bream of the same size is trading lower, around €5.80/kg to €6.20/kg FOB.

READ MORE
MAY 73:30 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
JETRO sets Japan pavilion amid global trade uncertainty 

The Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) has organized a Japan Pavilion at this year’s SEG, featuring 16 exhibitors, down from 19 companies last year, according to Takaharu Horinouchi, director general of JETRO’s Madrid office.

Despite the decrease in participants, Horinouchi told Undercurrent News, “Each company’s exhibit space has been increased from last year’s six square meters.” He added, “In 2024, we provided a shared consultation area. This year, we’ve expanded the space per company and equipped each booth with its own meeting area.”

READ MORE
MAY 72:43 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Norway’s salmon exports to China surge in early 2025

Norwegian exports of fresh Atlantic salmon to China have seen a significant increase in 2025, reaching a cumulative volume of 32,000 metric tons on a head-on, gutted basis by week 17, compared to just 17,000t during the same period last year, a sales executive at a major  Norwegian farmer told Undercurrent News.

The surge in shipments to China is largely due to a growing share of large-sized fish — those over seven kilograms per fish — in the total harvest, which aligns with Chinese market preferences. 

READ MORE
MAY 72:36 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Spain’s WOFCO launches new HPP chilled range 

Spanish vertically integrated firm Worldwide Fishing Company, also known as WOFCO, has launched a new range of high-pressure processed (HPP) chilled seafood products. 

The new line targets both European and US retailers, as the company aims to capitalize on opportunities in the value-added seafood category.

READ MORE
MAY 72:30 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Croatian bluefin tuna farmers face ongoing challenges amid yen depreciation

Croatia’s farmed bluefin tuna industry has rebounded from the historically low prices seen last season, but it still faces significant financial pressure due to the weak Japanese yen, Ante Gotovina Jr., board assistant at Pelagos Net Farm, told Undercurrent News.

As a key hub for bluefin tuna farming in the Mediterranean, Croatia relies heavily on the Japanese market, where prices are set in yen, as previously reported by Undercurrent.

READ MORE
MAY 72:29 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Podcast: Recap day 1 of Seafood Expo Global 2025 with Catch the Current

Seafood Expo Global kicked off on Tuesday, May 6, bringing 2,187 exhibiting companies from 87 countries to Barcelona, Spain, for the event. 

The Undercurrent News team met up at the end of day one to review and recap some highlights from the seafood industry’s biggest event in Europe. 

READ MORE
MAY 71:14 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
US Pacific whiting season begins amid tight global surimi supply

As global supply and demand for frozen surimi tighten, the Pacific whiting — also known as hake — fishing season officially opened on May 1 off the US West Coast, with full-scale operations expected to begin next week, a sales executive from the at-sea processing sector based in Seattle, Washington, told Undercurrent News.

“The quota is down roughly 20% compared to last year,” the executive said. “Last year’s quota wasn’t fully harvested, and if the same happens this year, the surimi supply situation in Europe and the US could become even tighter.”

READ MORE
MAY 611:52 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan’s top crab supplier plans 15% increase in procurement, expands focus on VAP

Japan’s top frozen crab supplier, Tsukiji Kanisho Co., aims to handle 20,000 metric tons of frozen crab in the current fiscal year, marking a 15% increase from the previous year, CEO Noriaki Nakamura told Undercurrent News.

The company plans to ramp up procurement of frozen snow crab, also known as opilio, particularly from Russia and Canada, increasing its intake from 11,700t last year to 15,000t.

READ MORE
MAY 65:24 PM GMT
By Cliff White
Viciunai’s smoked truffled salmon, Kalaneuvos Oy’s Bacon Trout win top prizes at 2025 Seafood Excellence Awards

Lithuania’s Viciunai Group and Finland’s Kalaneuvos Oy won top honors at the 2025 Seafood Excellence Awards, presented at SEG on Tuesday (May 6).

Viciunai won the Best Retail Prize for its Cold-Smoked Atlantic Salmon and Truffles, while Kalaneuovos Oy won the Best HORECA (hotel/restaurant/catering) Product for its Trout Bacon.

READ MORE
MAY 61:14 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
ASC recognizes Stolt Sea Farm as first fully certified turbot producer

Stolt Sea Farm (SSF) has become the world’s first turbot producer to achieve full Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) certification across all its farms.

The achievement was formally recognized today at SEG, where ASC CEO Chris Ninnes presented the certification to SSF president Jordi Trías. 

READ MORE
MAY 61:12 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese caviar prices set to drop as sturgeon investments materialize

Chinese caviar prices are projected to decline over the next two to three years as domestic sturgeon stocks continue to expand, according to industry experts.

“Prices are already falling and will continue to drop for the next two to three years,” Leon Xu, sales manager at Heilongjiang Tuopai Aquatic Products Processing, told Undercurrent News. “Sturgeon farming cycles are exceptionally long, typically five to ten years depending on the species, which means future supply volumes were determined years ago based on previous investments.” 

READ MORE
MAY 612:29 PM GMT
By Cliff White
Ecuadorian shrimp exporter Diosmar dumps China, bets big on US opportunity

Diosmar is making a huge swing away from China and toward the US market, where Ecuadorian shrimp now enjoys a big advantage.

The Guayaquil, Ecuador-based group, which farms, processes and exports more than 120 million pounds of shrimp annually, is reacting to rock-bottom prices in China and relatively low anti-dumping and countervailing duty rates set by the US in October 2024, as reported by Undercurrent News, in addition to favorable recripocal tariff rates.

READ MORE
MAY 611:02 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
JBT Marel enters salmon gutting market, signs first sales agreement with Bakkafrost

Seafood processing machinery giant JBT Marel has broadened its reach in the salmon sector with the sale of its first salmon gutting machine to Bakkafrost, it announced at the show.

The machine, named ‘EVi’ represents JBT Marel’s first product designed solely for the gutting of salmon, but also the latest addition to its rapidly growing salmon processing line-up.

READ MORE
MAY 610:32 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Canada’s Atlantic cod stock could reach MSC certification by 2026

An iconic cod fishery in Canada is moving closer to Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) certification, the gold standard for sustainable fisheries, thanks to a 10-year-long collaboration of Canadian and European partners to support more science on the Atlantic cod stock around the province of Newfoundland and Labrador (NL).

On the eve of SEG, UK-based retailer Marks and Spencer, the French division of US foodservice giant Sysco other supporters of the northern cod fisheries improvement program (FIP) were updated on the most recent status of the stock, which is now estimated to have a stock spawning biomass of about 542,000 metric tons, as recently reported by Undercurrent News. That’s nearly 62% better than the 324,000t estimated from the 2024 assessment.

READ MORE
MAY 610:31 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
India cuts surimi import duty by 25%, boosting imitation crab stick exports even to US

India’s imitation crab stick producers are gaining a stronger competitive edge in global markets following a steep reduction in import duties on frozen surimi blocks, a key raw material, a senior executive at an Indian surimi block producer told Undercurrent News.

“The 25% drop in import duty is a significant advantage for Indian exporters of surimi-based finished products,” the executive said. “This will especially boost our surimi stick price competitiveness even in the US market.”

READ MORE
MAY 69:52 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Podcast: Talking sustainability with American Seafoods’ Tim Fitzgerald

Catch the Current is recording “bonus bites” from SEG in Barcelona, Spain. So, who is our first guest to join the pod on the SEG show floor? It’s none other than American Seafoods’ chief sustainability officer, Tim Fitzgerald!

Tim joins the podcast to talk about Seattle, Washington-based American Seafoods’ latest sustainability report, and the work that the company is doing to reduce its carbon footprint and reduce emissions from its fishing vessels.

READ MORE
MAY 69:41 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Progress stalls on creation of Southwest Atlantic RFMO

Work on creating a regional fisheries management organization (RFMO) to govern the Southwest Atlantic Ocean continues, but progress has been hard to come by, Falkland Islands Fishing Companies Association executive secretary James Bates told Undercurrent News.

Distant-water fishing vessels from China, Taiwan and Europe annually descend on international waters around the Falkland Islands, a self-governing British overseas territory around 300 miles east of Argentina.

READ MORE
MAY 67:48 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Blumar set to catch all of its jack mackerel quota as prices firm

Chile’s jack mackerel quota rose an unprecedented 25% this year, providing Chilean multi-species seafood producer Blumar a challenge of catching it all.

With the fishing season slated to end in June, Blumar is on track to catch more than 100,000 metric tons of fish with its six fishing vessels, a significant slice of the quota of just over 1 million tons.

READ MORE
MAY 66:08 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Foppen launches individually-wrapped salmon breakfast sandwiches at Costco

The Netherlands-based Foppen is shaking up the breakfast space with a new ready-to-heat-and-eat salmon breakfast sandwich.

The salmon company’s new offering — it’s Smoked Norwegian Atlantic Bagel Sandwich — features a bagel with cream cheese and Norwegian smoked salmon. Simply take the individually wrapped sandwich from the freezer and put it in the oven, air fryer or grill for just a few minutes.

READ MORE
MAY 65:05 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Cermaq owner Mitsubishi in talks to buy $500m salmon processor  

Mitsubishi Corp., the owner of salmon farmer Cermaq Group, is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire salmon processor Milarex, a processor with revenue of around $500 million, sources told Undercurrent News.

For several months, Undercurrent sources have been reporting private equity-backed Milarex is negotiating with an Asian party, who is now said to be the Japanese conglomerate.

READ MORE
MAY 512:14 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Weaker 2026 salmon supply may offer price support, believes Kontali

While this year has seen — and is expected to continue seeing — a sharp supply growth for salmon out of both Norway and Chile, next year’s volume forecast is less rosy.

Addressing the crowd at the Euronext/DNB seminar ahead of the main SEG show, Philip Scrase with Kontali Analyse said the world was looking at more than 3 million metric tons of salmon (whole fish equivalent) for the very first time in 2025.

READ MORE
MAY 512:00 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Full impact of US tariffs not yet realized for salmon, but prices likely to drop

It’s been a month since the announcement of the Trump administration’s sweeping new tariffs on all imports, and the industry is yet to fully see the impact on prices, according to Steven Rafferty, CEO of Cermaq Group.

Cermaq, which sells 42% of all its Chilean salmon to the US, was originally nonplussed by the initial tariff on its Canadian operations. After all, a demand hit for Canadian salmon should, in turn, support prices for Chilean.

READ MORE
MAY 511:45 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US tariff costs Kvaroy Arctic $300,000 per month

Kvaroy Arctic, a boutique supplier of premium Norwegian salmon, is spending $300,000 per month to pay the 10% tariff imposed by the US beginning April 9.

“It definitely has strained our cashflow situation, as immediate tax payments are required upon clearance,” Kvaroy Arctic CEO Rune Mikalsen said at the 2025 Euronext/DNB seminar in Barcelona, Spain, on Monday (May 5). “You just need to pay up.”

READ MORE
MAY 511:04 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
DNB: Big questions still linger on Norway’s salmon white paper

Although the initial proposed changes to the aquaculture licensing system in Norway are not currently expected to get through parliament without alteration, the move does indicate the direction the government is heading in, according to Dag Sletmo, senior vice president of DNB Bank.

“Nothing has been decided yet, the lead times will be long, but sea lice and mortality are likely to be key elements in any new regulations,” he warned.

READ MORE
MAY 510:29 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Norwegian gov’t salmon proposal would have initial 31% hit on volumes if implemented today

Speaking at a Euronext salmon event ahead of the SEG event, Dag Sletmo, senior vice president of Norway’s DNB Bank, said the firm’s analysis of the government’s recently proposed aquaculture licensing regulation would, in theory, prompt a very steep, immediate cut in salmon production volumes.

How steep? A 31% cut from last year’s 1.5 million metric tons, Sletmo estimates.

READ MORE
MAY 510:20 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Europe could escape worst tariff impacts

US tariffs could harm global economic growth, but Europe might get off easier than other regions.

European governments have passed or are considering economic stimulus to insulate their nations from the impact of the tariffs implemented in April by US president Donald Trump – for example, Germany recently approved a $500 billion, 12-year investment package. 

READ MORE
MAY 57:43 AM GMT
By Cliff White
2025 SEG near last year’s record for event space

There will be 2,187 exhibitors and 51,217 net square meters of exhibit space at the 2025 SEG, running from May 6 to 8 in Barcelona, Spain.

That’s just off the record for the show, which is run by Portland, Maine-headquartered Diversified Communications, which also operates Seafood Expo North America, held each March in Boston, Massachusetts, and Seafood Expo Asia, which takes place annually in Singapore in September.

READ MORE
MAY 55:17 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Chilean farmer Ventisqueros targets Europe with ASC-certified silverside salmon

Chilean salmon farmer Ventisqueros will present its silverside Pacific salmon at SEG, aiming to reach the European market. 

Silverside is an Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC)-certified Pacific salmon developed with a low-impact, high-nutrition feed and traceable production. It also carries the “Cosecha Viva” seal. 

READ MORE
MAY 54:56 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Pregame for Barcelona week with UCN Catch the Current podcast

If you’re heading to Barcelona, Spain, for SEG, then this is one episode of Catch the Current that you won’t want to miss.

Prepare for the biggest seafood industry event in Europe with the team at Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
MAY 54:54 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Trump tariffs set to dominate Barcelona discussions

US president Donald Trump’s 145% additional tariffs on China, with 10% applied to all other nations, are set to dominate discussions at SEG.

Whether it’s Norwegian salmon or canned tuna from Thailand, the tariffs will have global seafood suppliers scrambling in Barcelona.

READ MORE

Contact the authors tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com, Cliff.White@undercurrentnews.com, ben.fisher@undercurrentnews.com, matilde.mereghetti@undercurrentnews.com, Maria.Feijoo@undercurrentnews.com, masahiko.takeuchi@undercurrentnews.com, amanda.buckle@undercurrentnews.com, gary.morrison@undercurrentnews.com, barb.simmons@undercurrentnews.com, dan.gibson@undercurrentnews.com

title: Untitled
content:
KODIAK, Alaska, US -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from ComFish Alaska, the commercial fishing trade show held here Tuesday-Thursday (April 15-17, 2025).

The annual event – now in its 46th year – has welcomed nearly 50 exhibitors from industry groups, vendors, suppliers and government agencies. Organizers reported more than 400 registrations from exhibitors and attendees. But with no admission barriers organizers estimate actual attendance could be nearly twice that.

The event kicked off Tuesday with an in-person federal legislative update from US senators Lisa Murkowski and Dan Sullivan, both Republicans. Murkowski is here and Sullivan beamed in remotely from his office in Washington, DC.

Auto updates: On
APR 189:18 AM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
House fisheries committee chair blocks controversial Alaska fish farm bill

Alaska governor Mike Dunleavy’s fish farming bill won’t be advancing out of the House Fisheries Committee where Kodiak representative Louise Stutes holds sway.

Stutes told the ComFish audience on Thursday (April 17) that she had only allowed the bill, HB 111, to its single hearing as a courtesy to Alaska Department of Fish and Game commissioner Doug Vincent-Lang.

APR 177:08 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
NOAA’s Kodiak Lab director talks crab recovery

Three commercially harvested Bering Sea crab species have had some major challenges in recent years and scientists are only now starting to understand potential factors behind their decline.

That was the jist of a briefing by Kodiak Laboratory director Mike Litzow told the ComFish audience.

APR 172:29 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Kelp farms pitched as economic engine to replace commercial fishing in rural communities

Alaska’s burgeoning mariculture industry is giving an industry update on the final day at ComFish. Kodiak Island’s villages have lost a lot of fishing permits in recent decades as commercial fishing permits are sold off. It’s a limited entry system that locks out the younger generations in some of the communities on the island.

“As we’re well aware, permits have disappeared from communities,” Lexa Meyer, hatchery manager of Kodiak-based Alaska Ocean Farms, which raises kelp and oysters.

APR 176:49 AM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Alaska governor quietly nominates 2 for return to North Pacific Fishery Management Council, riles salmon groups

Alaska governor Mike Dunleavy has recommended the reappointment of Nicole Kimball and Angela “Angel” Drobnica to the North Pacific Fishery Management Council (NPFMC).

Unlike in 2022 and 2019, there was no formal announcement of governor Dunleavy’s nominations made last month to the US Commerce Department. But Alaska Department of Fish and Game commissioner Doug Vincent-Lang made the names public in a Wednesday speech here.

APR 165:36 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
ADF&G head lambasts Marine Stewardship Council, vows to find alternatives

Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G) commissioner Doug Vincent-Lang said the US state is looking for an “alternative” to the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) that allows certified “sustainable” seafood to be marketed with a blue label recognized by consumers.

“I understand how important MSC certification is to our fisheries, but it’s not a fair, metricable field,” Vincent-Lang told the ComFish audience, “and I’m just tired of dealing with being held accountable to a greater extent than anybody else that holds that little blue label that they have on their fisheries.”

APR 164:48 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Alaska rep Nick Begich supports relaxing observer requirements in federal fishing fleet

During his first ComFish appearance as a member of the US Congress member, representative Nick Begich told the audience that he supports modifying the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS)’s human observer requirements in the Gulf of Alaska, Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands in groundfish and halibut fisheries. 

“While the intent is sound, the execution has created real burdens,” Begich, an Alaska Republican, said in prepared remarks. “Observation can cost fishermen up to $2,000 a day.” 

APR 162:03 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
NOAA’s Alaska science director prevented from traveling to Kodiak

One of the top US government fisheries scientists in Alaska apologized for being unable to deliver his remarks in person in Kodiak.

“I was very much looking forward to another ComFish, another presentation with the community,” said Bob Foy, science and research director of the Alaska Fisheries Science Center in Juneau, Alaska. “Unfortunately, NOAA has some travel restrictions right now so I wasn’t able to be there in person.”

APR 168:57 AM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Murkowski: Trump can’t reorganize NMFS without Congress

US senator Lisa Murkowski delivered a message to the president Donald Trump administration’s rumored shakeup of the federal government’s major regulator for commercial fisheries: Not so fast.

CNN and other outlets have reported on internal documents that suggest that Trump plans to move the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) out of the Department of Commerce and into the US Fish and Wildlife Service, an agency that resides inside the Department of the Interior (DOI).

APR 158:12 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Alaska US senator Dan Sullivan pledges to support fishing industry amid Trump trade war’s uncertainty

The US senator beamed in virtually from his Washington DC office to the room full of seafood industry figures in Kodiak.

A political ally of US president Donald Trump, he spoke optimistically of the executive’s desire to tap into Alaska’s energy resources. He said he’d work to ensure the federal government would support the commercial fisheries.

APR 157:38 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Alaska seafood producers are vulnerable to US tariffs on China

The top valued US seafood products exported to China are from Alaska, so the reciprocal tariffs imposed by Beijing in response to Washington’s 140% tariff are especially dire to the already struggling industry.

The top three on the list are: H&G flatfish ($184m); H&G wild salmon ($168m); fishmeal ($161m), making the US state’s fishing sector especially exposed to US president Trump’s second trade war with Beijing.

APR 157:22 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Murkowski pushes US Congress to reclaim tariff powers

US senator Lisa Murkowski said she’s working on a bipartisan bill to claw back Congress’ authority to set tariffs away from president Donald Trump.

“Congress needs to reclaim some of our authority when it comes to tariffs, because it is our constituents, it’s our people that are feeling it,” she told scores of Alaskans gathered for the first day of the event.

Contact the author jacob.resneck@undercurrentnews.com
