title: Blue Food Summit: ‘A lot of retailers don’t know where their seafood comes from’
content:
LONDON, UK -- Undercurrent News reported from the Blue Food Innovation Summit, where some 300 delegates discussed the landscape for investment in innovative seafood solutions.

The two-day event covered food security, alternative aquaculture feed ingredients, AI, seaweed, burgeoning "hotspots" for fish farming, smallholder farmers, start-up pitches, and much more.

Recap all the updates below.

Auto updates: On
APR 911:55 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Icelandic salmon project close to securing next fundraise

Iceland land-based salmon company Laxey is close to having its fundraise for the second development phase secured, said chairman Larus Asgeirsson.

He declined to give details before anything was official, but told Undercurrent that the upending of the global trade and economic pictures by the US’ new tariffs did not seem to have hurt its fundraising.

READ MORE
APR 98:28 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Raw material access a bottleneck for seafood byproduct startups

Limited access to viable raw materials is a significant bottleneck for new companies looking to enter the seafood byproduct market, according to byproduct makers.

Using the whole fish is attractive for fish producers from a commercial and sustainability perspective. But James Berger, chief commercial officer at Hofseth Biocare, said securing raw material supply is challenging, not least because good quality fresh fish raw material oxidizes extremely quickly.

READ MORE
APR 97:51 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
‘A lot of Europe’s retailers don’t know where their seafood comes from’

A lot of retailers in Europe don’t know where the fish they purchase is coming from, warned fisheries economist Sebastien Metz, development manager for the Global Seafood Alliance’s Prism platform.

A lot of the seafood sector are “dinosaurs” who need to be pushed before making any traceability moves, he said.

READ MORE
APR 96:43 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
UK mussel farmer hopes gov’t can better incentivize restorative business

The UK government could be doing more to incentivize restorative/ regenerative aquaculture operations, said Offshore Shellfish managing director John Holmyard.

His business has just finished its 2024-2025 harvesting season, with 3,100 metric tons produced, he said.

READ MORE
APR 96:21 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Cuna del Mar interested in, but unconvinced by, seaweed as investment opportunity

The Walton family’s Cuna del Mar fund is interested in, but unconvinced by, seaweed as an investment opportunity thus far, said vice president Donald Grant.

Of interest to the fund is a definition of what “regenerative” aquaculture means, particularly when it comes to a commercial scale.

READ MORE
APR 94:44 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Tariffs make investors much more cautious, but opportunities will come

A panel of investment-sector speakers agreed that the new global tariff landscape would make investors much more cautious, but some felt M&A and fundraising opportunities would still present themselves.

“Aquaculture and aquatech are nascent industries, really, and the huge uncertainty is only going to make people more risk-averse,” said Maria Velkova, chief portfolio officer at Aqua-Spark. While it’s a more difficult environment, it’s the role of investors like Aqua-Spark to try and continue sector developments, she said.

READ MORE
APR 94:39 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
DOGE cuts threaten US bluetech startup funding

US ocean technology startups may struggle for public funding amid sweeping cuts to federal government programs by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), investors warned.

“Public-private partnerships were the great hope for the sector,” said Monica Jain, partner at Fish 2.0 Ventures, a global accelerator for seafood startups. “Now do we have to say goodbye to that, at least for a couple of years?”

READ MORE
APR 93:58 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Kenya’s Victory Farms doubled in size in 2024 through small-scale egg partnerships

Kenyan tilapia farming operation doubled in size in 2024 through its adoption of smallholder “pond partners” who supply it with eggs, revealed founder and CEO Joseph Rehmann.

The supply of eggs for its hatchery was a bottleneck for the company’s growth, so several years ago it decided to partner with local small-scale farmers to see if they could supply it.

READ MORE
APR 93:35 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Urchinomics, Restorae co-founder given blue carbon credit role by Japan

Brian Tsuyoshi Takeda — founder of ocean restorative businesses Urchinomics and Restorae — has been appointed as secretariat of international affairs by the Japan Blue Economy Association (JBE).

JBE is a research cooperative authorized by the Japanese government responsible for advancing the nation’s marine decarbonization and restoration efforts through the foundation, improvement, and management of the blue carbon credit scheme called J-Blue Credit.

READ MORE
APR 93:29 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Non-profit spending philanthropic capital on seaweed R&D

Seaweed non-profit GreenWave has begun spending the “philanthropic capital” it raises on downstream R&D in a bid to create more market pull for the small-scale farmers it supports, said director of market development Samantha Garwin.

“To make a value chain work, a farmer can’t be successful unless they have buyers who are buying at the right volumes and price,” she noted.

READ MORE
APR 812:38 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
eFishery situation has changed investment environment

The fallout from the eFishery debacle has changed the investment environment, said Claire Pribula, managing director and co-founder of the Yield Lab Asia-Pacific.

As reported, Indonesian aquatech unicorn eFishery is facing significant financial challenges, and recent investigations into alleged fraud have revealed investors face heavy losses.

READ MORE
APR 812:12 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Africa needs 10x aquaculture growth to maintain current per capita consumption

Sub-Saharan Africa must increase its seafood production tenfold over the next 25 years just to maintain current consumption levels, according to industry experts.

Francisco Murillo, CEO of Ghana-based Tropo Farms, cited recent FAO data showing Africa produces only 7% of global seafood despite representing 19% of the world’s population. The disparity is even greater in sub-Saharan Africa, which accounts for 16% of global population but just 2% of seafood production.

READ MORE
APR 812:00 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
New Zealand’s ‘precision harvesting’ tech seeks UK partner, approvals

New Zealand’s FloMo — previously called the Modular Harvesting System, and which has had wide uptake by major companies in its home country — is looking for partners to invest and help it reach the UK, said general commercial manager Andre Pinkert.

The firm provides the net technology to fishermen free of charge under a lease model and is paid a volume-based fee based on catches. It has been achieving a price premium of NZD 0.23/kg on average on deepwater catches and NZD 1.00.kg for inshore fisheries, he claimed.

READ MORE
APR 811:28 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Aquatech doubles down on cybersecurity 

The aquatech industry is taking seriously the risk of cyber attacks amid the rapid rollout of digital technology, according to industry leaders.

The stakes are particularly high for companies interfacing directly with production systems. “We integrate into systems within land-based environments,” explained Mathew Zimola, founder and CEO of ReelData AI. “If somebody can breach our technology to access their systems, it could be very dangerous.”

READ MORE
APR 810:14 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
More funding options needed for seaweed to boom outside of Asia

A lack of available investment is holding back the nascent seaweed cultivation sector from booming outside of Asia, where it’s already a huge industry, panelists said.

“There’s a lot of opportunities for early grants, capital of $1 million, $2m, even $5m. A lot of people are looking at this industry with that sort of cheque size,” said Sowmya Balendiran, co-founder of India’s Sea6 Energy.

READ MORE
APR 89:24 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Investing sector’s reaction to US tariffs mixed

The immediate reaction to the US’ new tariffs from the investor sector has been mixed, but nobody’s happy about the sheer unpredictability that has ensued, one source told Undercurrent.

“Some people aren’t taking it very seriously and think everything could change again; some have gone the other way and said they will just avoid doing business in the US for four years,” he said.

READ MORE
APR 88:02 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
No new US demands on Ecuador’s shrimp industry after gov’t slashes import tariffs to zero

Ecuador’s shrimp industry has not been asked for additional concessions from the US after eliminating import tariffs on US shrimp, Jose Camposano, the head of Ecuador’s National Chamber of Aquaculture told Undercurrent News.

Ecuador moved quickly to remove its 30% import tax shrimp imports ahead of the Trump administration’s imposition of a 10% tariff on Ecuadorian shrimp exports. The US tariff, part of broader trade actions targeting countries with trade surpluses, is the lowest among those imposed on major shrimp exporters. 

READ MORE
APR 87:26 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Farmer feedback creates positive growth cycle in maturing aquatech sector

Early skepticism that posed challenges for technology providers is turning into enthusiasm and productive relationships as the aquatech sector matures, according to aquatech founders.

Mathew Zimola, founder and CEO of ReelData AI, conceded that in the early phase of aquatech “a lot of technology had been overpromised to the market.” But as the technology matures aquatech is now solving real-world problems. 

READ MORE
APR 86:41 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
‘GM’ needs reframing for consumer mindset

Norway may have painted itself into a corner years ago when it celebrated its farmed salmon as “non-GM” (genetically modified), suggested Evy Vikene, Aquaterra aquaculture lead for Norway and the EU within Nuseed Nutritional.

“There’s a feeling now from consumers that GM isn’t ‘natural’ — how do we start to define ‘natural’? This technology has been around for more than 40 years, there’s been thousands of risk assessments on health and the environment. Nothing negative has been proven.”

READ MORE
APR 85:35 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Calysta co-founder: ‘75% of shrimp farmers don’t give a damn about sustainability’

The majority of shrimp farmers globally are not interested in how sustainable their aquaculture feed is; price is still the sole concern, said Alan Shaw, co-founder, president and CEO of Calysta.

But scaling uptake is possible, as his firm has found.

READ MORE
APR 85:08 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
ASC chief: Lower trophic species key to global food security

Lower trophic species like carp and bivalves and not shrimp will be crucial for addressing global food security challenges, according to the CEO of the Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC).

“Shrimp is not for food security – it’s valuable as a sector and for scale and access to markets. But you have to look at lower trophic species,” said ASC chief Christ Ninnes during the summit’s first panel discussion.

READ MORE
APR 85:06 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Cermaq boss confident salmon sector can cope with tariff landscape

The salmon aquaculture sector globally can adapt to the new trade picture the US has created with new tariffs on essentially all major trading partners, said Cermaq Group CEO Steven Rafferty.

Responding to a question from Undercurrent, he said quite simply that he couldn’t not say yet how the tariff landscape might impact on the salmon sector’s investment in growth and innovation. 

READ MORE
APR 84:48 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
‘Sustainability requirements cannot outpace feasible innovation’ for salmon sector

The environmental sustainability of salmon farming is, of course, vital to its future, but the regulatory demands on the sector will outpace feasible development if governments are not careful, said Cermaq Group CEO Steven Rafferty.

Specifically talking about closed containment pens, he expressed confidence that they would form part of the future of salmon farming — and other species too, potentially — but that currently, they are not feasible as a sole method of aquaculture business.

READ MORE
APR 712:09 PM GMT
Indonesia, UK start-ups to pitch for potential investors

The summit will see five startups from around the world showcase their seafood solutions to experts and investors looking to explore potential collaborations and scale-ups.

The seed-stage companies include:

READ MORE

title: Trump tariffs fallout: US drops duty on Switzerland to 15%
content:
US president Donald Trump came into office in January 2025 vowing to use tariffs to rebalance his country's trade deficit and to revitalize America's domestic manufacturing sector.

He has followed through on his threat. After imposing a temporary 10% tariff on most imported goods through the summer, Trump announced individualized tariff rates for 69 nations identified on a list known as "Annex I" in a Aug. 1 presidential order. The tariffs came into effect on Aug. 7, with a two-month shipping window at previous rates that runs until Oct. 5. 

Major seafood-exporting nations hit with higher tariffs include a few that agreed to the higher rates as part of a trade deal. Among the nations for whom sourcing seafood has become more expensive are: Thailand (19%), Indonesia (19%), Japan (15%), The Philippines (20%), South Korea (15%), the European Union (15%), the United Kingdom (10%), Norway (15%), Ecuador (15%), Argentina (10%), Chile (10%), New Zealand (15%) and Iceland (15%). 

Countries not listed in Annex I and now subject to a 10% tariff include: Peru, Faroe Islands, Colombia, Australia, Honduras, Bahamas, Morocco, Panama, Senegal, Suriname, Sri Lanka, Reunion, Egypt, Burma, Portugal, China-Hong Kong and Greenland.

Most Canadian and Mexican goods remain untariffed thanks to the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement signed in late 2020 during Trump's previous stay in the White House. However, the three neighboring North American nations remain engaged in negotiations on an updated trade deal that may eventually include tariffs.

Brazil was hit with a special 50% tariff imposed by Trump on July 30 and India is dealing with a 50% tariff that came into effect on Aug. 27.

On Aug. 11, Trump issued a 90-day extension of a reduction in combined tariffs on Chinese goods from 170% to 55%. Then, on Aug. 28,Trump extended the deal so that it would not expire until Nov. 29. In November, China's baseline rate was lowered to 45% as part of a deal Trump made with Chinese president Xi Jinping.

Here's the latest news from Trump's tariff initiative:

Auto updates: On
NOV 1410:35 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US drops tariff on Switzerland to 15%

Switzerland, which had been reeling from a 39% US tariff rate since August, won a major diplomatic concession on Friday (Nov. 14), with the administration of US president Donald Trump dropping its rate to 15%.

The lower tariff comes following a trip by a group of high-level Swiss business executives to visit Trump in the White House last week, and negotiations between US and Swiss government officials on Thursday (Nov. 13), Bloomberg reported.

READ MORE
NOV 139:21 AM GMT
By Cliff White
India trade delegation visits Moscow in diversification bid

A sizeable delegation of Indian exporters is in the midst of a four-day visit to Russia, in a move described as a response to US tariffs.

India is working to diversify its exports after US president Donald Trump hit it with a 50% tariff in August, blaming the high rate in part on India’s imports of Russian oil and gas.

READ MORE
NOV 129:48 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US ethnic grocery stores hit hard by tariffs

Ethnic grocery stores are taking an outsized hit from tariffs implemented by US president Donald Trump.

Stores serving immigrant, refugee and diaspora communities across the US are facing higher prices for specialty food items, including seafood, that can’t be easily sourced from places with lower tariffs.

READ MORE
NOV 1112:44 PM GMT
By Cliff White
Trump claims US will owe $3 trillion if forced to repay tariffs

US president Donald Trump warned on Tuesday (Nov. 11) that the Treasury Department will be forced to repay $3 trillion if the Supreme Court rules against him in a case that challenges his authority to implement tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA).

The oral arguments in the case were presented last week, and it did not appear to go well for Trump, Undercurrent News reported.

READ MORE
NOV 109:28 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US container entrances fell 7.5% in October

US tariffs continued to impact imports, with inbound container traffic falling 7.5% year-on-year in October.

US seaports handled a total of 2.3 million 20-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in the month, down 0.1% from September 2025 and below the 2.4 million to 2.6 million TEU range that typically signals peak trade activity, according to data from supply chain technology provider Descartes.

READ MORE
NOV 712:35 PM GMT

Cliff White

US shrimpers hope Trump’s tariff powers aren’t curtailed

The US domestic shrimp industry is hoping the president’s ability to implement tariffs on foreign product aren’t curtailed.

READ MORE
NOV 611:29 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Trade attorney: Seafood industry should file protests to ensure reimbursement if tariffs ruled illegal

The US Supreme Court on Wednesday (Nov. 5) heard heated oral arguments in a case that will decide the legality of US president Donald Trump’s tariff agenda.

The case, Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, is the first of at least seven legal challenges to Trump’s tariffs to reach the top US judicial body.

READ MORE
NOV 512:25 PM GMT
By Cliff White
Oral arguments ongoing at US Supreme Court

The US Supreme Court is hearing arguments in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, the first case to reach the top US judicial body to challenge tariffs imposed by US president Donald Trump earlier this year.

The case involves tariffs imposed in February on Canada, China and Mexico and in April on most other US trading partners. Trump justified these by declaring separate national emergencies under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). 

READ MORE
NOV 412:15 PM GMT
By Cliff White
US Supreme Court to set to hear tariff case on Nov. 5

The US Supreme Court will hear arguments in a case that will decide the future of US president Donald Trump’s tariff agenda.

Experts are not sure how the court will rule as to whether Trump has the ability to implement tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), as he has claimed.

READ MORE
NOV 310:04 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US still hasn’t imposed promised 10% tariff on Canada

US president Donald Trump promised to deliver an additional 10% tariff on Canadian goods on Oct. 25.

But that has not yet happened, as Trump has not yet signed an executive order to finalize the action.

READ MORE
OCT 3112:02 PM GMT
Shipping rates from Asia surge amid easing US–China tensions

Rates from Asia to the US and Europe have jumped by double digits in recent weeks as shipping lines curb capacity and traders respond to signs of a thaw in the US-China trade relationship, reports FreightWaves.

The Freightos Baltic Index showed trans-Pacific and Asia-North Europe rates rising 15-20% in late October, reaching about $2,000 per 40-foot container to the US West Coast, $3,500 to the East Coast and $2,270 to Europe, according to the shipping-related news service. Asia-Mediterranean rates climbed around 6% to $2,278 per unit.

READ MORE
OCT 3012:15 PM GMT
By Cliff White
US drops baseline Chinese tariff rate to 47%

A meeting between US president Donald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping resulted in an agreement for the US to lower its baseline tariff rate.

Trump agreed to lower a 20% tariff rate implemented earlier this year as punishment for China’s selling of chemicals used to make fentanyl.

READ MORE
OCT 2911:03 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Outline of US-China deal could keep tilapia duty at 55%

A framework agreement that removes the US threat of additional 100% tariffs on Chinese goods is in place, with likely confirmation coming Thursday (Oct. 30).

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday (Oct. 26) the additional tariffs on China are “effectively off the table” after a “very good two-day meeting” with Beijing’s top trade negotiator in Malaysia, according to CBS.

READ MORE
OCT 2811:02 AM GMT
By Cliff White
No India-US trade deal announced at ASEAN Summit

A trade deal dropping India’s US tariff rate to 15-16% was supposed to be announced at the ASEAN Summit in Malaysia, but it ended Tuesday (Oct. 28) without fanfare.

Currently, India faces a 50% US tariff, imposed in August as punishment for India’s purchases of Russian oil, as Undercurrent reported.

READ MORE
OCT 2712:29 PM GMT
By Cliff White
US Trade Representative releases framework of trade agreements with Thailand, Vietnam

US trade representative Jamieson Greer is touting deals struck with four Southeast Asian nations at the start of US president Donald Trump’s trip through the region beginning Sunday (Oct. 26).

Greer released details of the previously announced deals with Malaysia and Cambodia, as well as the frameworks of agreements on Thailand and Vietnam.

READ MORE
OCT 249:53 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Trump ends trade talks with Canada

US president Donald Trump late on Thursday night (Oct. 23) said he was ending trade discussions with Canada, threatening a seafood trade relationship that’s worth $5 billion a year.

Trump accused Canada of spending CAD 75 million ($53.5m) on an advertisement using comments attributed to former US president Ronald Reagan that were negative about tariffs in order to “interfere” with an upcoming decision by the US Supreme Court regarding the constitutionality of Trump’s tariffs.

READ MORE
OCT 239:52 AM GMT
By Cliff White
EU lawmaker pushes for US concessions in tariff deal

A top European Union elected official has called for the conditioning of any concessions the bloc makes to the US to secure a baseline 15% tariff rate.

The deal, agreed to in broad terms in July, as Undercurrent News reported, still requires approval of the European Parliament and EU governments.

READ MORE
OCT 229:28 AM GMT
By Cliff White
India nears deal to lower US tariffs to 15-16%

The US and India are nearing a trade deal that will lower the US tariff rate on Indian goods to 15-16%, Indian business and financial news outlet Mint reported on Tuesday (Oct. 21).

The current rate is 50%, which US president Donald Trump imposed in August as a punishment for India importing Russian oil, as reported by Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 179:15 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Harvard study finds tariffs push up inflation on goods not produced in US

US tariffs are pushing up prices, and the impact is being most acutely felt on goods not produced in the country, including some types of seafood.

The study, “Tracking the Short-Run Price Impact of US Tariffs,” was released via the Harvard Business School, found imported goods have risen 4% in price since early March, when US president Donald Trump began imposing tariffs on much of the rest of the world. The price of domestic good rose 2% in that time, according to the study, which tracked the prices of 359,148 goods at major online and brick-and-mortar retailers.

READ MORE
OCT 169:22 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Trump says India has stopped buying Russian oil, a key factor in 50% tariff

US president Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday (Oct. 15) India has pledged to stop buying Russian oil, a key factor in Trump’s imposition of an extra 25% US tariff on Indian goods in August.

India, the top supplier of shrimp to the US for the past decade, now faces 50% baseline tariffs on goods shipped to the US, plus additional taxes for shrimp.

READ MORE
OCT 1510:57 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Trump threatens Spain with more tariffs over NATO defense spending

US president Donald Trump is threatening Spain with additional tariffs over its refusal to hit his 5% defense spending target for North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) members

Spain is the only member of the 32-nation alliance not to commit to raise its military spending to 5% of gross domestic product, according to Reuters.

READ MORE
OCT 1412:41 PM GMT
By Cliff White
US growth outlook gets upgrade on positive tariff report

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) upgraded its US growth prediction to 2% for 2025, saying tariffs imposed by US president Donald Trump had proved less disruptive than expected.

Its semi-annual forecast was up from its 1.9% forecast in July and 1.8% growth prediction issued in April, the Associated Press reported.

READ MORE
OCT 1310:03 AM GMT
By Cliff White
China hits US with reciprocal shipping fees

China has placed new fees on US container ships entering its ports, after US president Donald Trump threatened the country with 100% tariffs.

The shipping fees mirror the levies set by the US Trade Representative in April, down to the rates and the dates.

READ MORE
OCT 127:24 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China vows retaliation after Trump’s 100% tariff threat

China’s Ministry of Commerce on Sunday (Oct. 12) criticized US president Donald Trump’s declaration of a new 100% tariff on Chinese imports, warning that Beijing “will take corresponding measures” if Washington proceeds.

The ministry issued a statement through its spokesperson in response to a series of US moves following China’s Oct. 9 decision to impose export controls on rare earths and related materials.

READ MORE
OCT 109:23 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Trump threatens new 100% tariff on China ‘over and above’ 

US president Donald Trump said Friday (Oct. 10) that his administration will impose a 100% tariff on Chinese imports starting Nov. 1, in response to what he described as an “extraordinarily aggressive” trade move by Beijing.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said China had sent a “hostile letter to the world,” declaring plans to impose large-scale export controls on virtually all products it manufactures — and even on some not made by them — starting the same date.

READ MORE
OCT 1010:48 AM GMT
By Cliff White
WTO forecast: Global trade to slow in 2026 due to tariffs

Global trade is expected to slow in 2026 due to US tariffs, the World Trade Organization predicted in a report issued Tuesday (Oct. 7).

The WTO had originally forecast a 1.8% expansion next year but reduced its prediction to 0.5% growth in its latest revision, blaming tariffs.

READ MORE
OCT 99:30 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US container imports drop in September, except from Southeast Asia

US container cargo imports dropped 8.4% in September year over year, though traffic from major seafood-producing nations in Southeast Asia increased.

Shipments from China dropped 22.9%, and imports from South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Germany and Italy were also down compared to September 2024, according to a report from supply chain technology and data provider Descartes.

READ MORE
OCT 811:21 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Carney returns to Canada from Washington without tariff deal

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney met with US president Donald Trump in Washington on Tuesday (Oct. 7), but didn’t get his desired trade deal, according to the Canadian Press.

Many Canadian goods (those qualifying under the CUSMA/USMCA trade deal) continue to enter the US tariff-free, but Trump has repeatedly threatened Canada with an across-the-board 25-35% duty. And Trump has implemented 25-50% tariffs on steel, lumber, automobiles, copper, furniture and energy.

READ MORE
OCT 711:37 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Iconic US grocery store chain raises seafood prices due to tariffs

Stew Leonard’s, an iconic grocery store franchise based in the state of Connecticut, is being forced to raise seafood prices because of US tariffs imposed on producing countries.

Due to a new 15% tariff on Greece, the chain raised the price of fresh branzino to $12.99 per pound, CEO Stew Leonard Jr. told the Wall Street Journal.

READ MORE
OCT 611:20 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US Democratic Party unites behind opposition to Trump’s tariffs

Years ago, the US Democratic Party was split on tariffs, with some national leaders arguing they could help protect domestic industries and rebuild the country’s middle class, which they said had been built upon union jobs that have disappeared due to free trade.

But today, the party has largely united in opposition to tariffs, according to Politico.

READ MORE
OCT 311:25 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Trump floats plan to issue tariff dividend checks to US citizens

US president Donald Trump wants to issue dividend checks to Americans using money generated from his global tariffs.

The US has collected around $214 billion since Trump imposed tariffs on most of the world’s countries in April.

READ MORE
OCT 211:48 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Retaliatory Chinese tariffs on US soybeans impact global aquafeed prices

Soybeans are an unheralded but critically important ingredient to the global seafood industry due to their role as a key ingredient in aquafeed.

But US tariffs on China — and China’s retaliatory tariffs on US soy — are collapsing bilateral trade vital to aquafeed production.

READ MORE
OCT 111:54 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Trump tariffs spur global trade deals as EU seeks to offset losses in US market

US president Donald Trump’s import tariffs have jolted free trade talks worldwide, spurring a wave of new alliances as the European Union (EU) and other economies look to offset lost access to the American market, reports Reuters.

Since Trump’s re-election in November 2024, the EU has sealed agreements with Mercosur, Mexico and Indonesia, and it aims to finalize a deal with India by year-end.

READ MORE
SEP 3010:29 AM GMT
By Cliff White
New Zealand trade minister worried about US tariff impact

New US tariffs on timber and furniture, and a threatened 100% tariff on films, has New Zealand’s trade minister increasingly worried about the future of bilateral trade between the antipodal nations.

A 25% tariff on upholstered furniture, kitchen cabinets and vanities came into effect on Tuesday (Sept. 30), with a scheduled increase to 30% for furniture and 50% for cabinets and vanities beginning in 2026. A 10% tariff on timber was also implemented Tuesday.

READ MORE
SEP 2910:11 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US grocery chain warns of rising seafood prices

A grocery chain in the US Northeast is warning customers that seafood prices are rising due to tariffs imposed by US president Donald Trump.

Tops Friendly Markets, headquartered in Buffalo, New York, operates 160 locations in New York, Pennsylvania and Vermont.

READ MORE
SEP 2611:38 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Venezuelan president wants direct talks with Trump administration

Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro has asked for direct talks with Rick Grenell, US president Donald Trump’s senior envoy for special missions, to work on resolving several issues that have heightened tensions between the two countries.

The US has increased its military presence near Venezuelan waters and has destroyed three boats Trump alleged were carrying drug traffickers to the US, killing at least 15 people. The US has also deported more than 8,000 Venezuelans since Trump took office.

READ MORE
SEP 259:42 AM GMT
By Cliff White
As US tariffs bite, other countries embrace free trade

US tariffs of between 15% and 50% hit countries worldwide in August. In response, the rest of the world is embracing free trade as a defensive strategy.

The dawn of the age of US tariffs has spawned an era of trade deals. The European Union has completed an agreement with Indonesia that reduces tariffs to zero on 80% of imports and is in negotiations with India, Australia and South America’s Mercosur bloc on deals, as Time has reported.

READ MORE
SEP 2410:35 AM GMT
By Cliff White
South Korean president questions feasibility of promised US investments

In July, South Korea signed a trade deal with the US that locked its tariff rate in at 15%. Part of what it promised in exchange was $350 billion in direct investments in the United States.

But new South Korean president Lee Jae Myung said following through on that promise in the manner being demanded by the US would be catastrophic for his country’s economy.

READ MORE
SEP 239:46 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Rift over H-1B visas further endangers US-India relationship

A move by US president Donald Trump to charge $100,000 for new H-1B visa applications has further damaged ties with India.

Historically, more than 70% of H-1B applicants come from India. The visa allows skilled workers to enter the US for jobs.

READ MORE
SEP 2210:06 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Vietnam could see US exports drop by $25bn in worst-case tariff scenario, tops in Southeast Asia

Vietnam could see $25 billion shaved off its annual US export total due to the 20% tariff imposed on it by US president Donald Trump in August.

Vietnam exported $136.5 million worth of goods to the US in 2024, including $1.71bn in seafood exports.

READ MORE
SEP 1911:57 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Consumer impact of tariffs now being felt, in US and abroad

US shoppers are facing rising grocery bills, while citizens of countries hit by tariffs are getting a break as more locally products goods are sold domestically.

Tariffs imposed on most countries globally by US president Donald Trump are now inflating prices for foodstuffs like organic sugar, coffee, bananas and avocados. Seafood is also taking a hit, with fish vendors in Houston, Texas raising prices 10-15% in line with rising wholesale prices.

READ MORE
SEP 1810:08 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Canada’s PM, Mexican president meet to talk trade, security

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney is expected to sign a strategic partnership agreement with Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum during two days of meetings in Mexico that begin Thursday (Sept. 18), reports Canadian Press (CP).

“Canada and Mexico have a strong relationship, built on more than three decades of free trade. In the face of a shifting global landscape, we are focused on elevating our partnerships in trade, commerce, security, and energy,” Carney said in a statement ahead of the meetings.

READ MORE
SEP 189:42 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Will US seafood industry benefit from tariff bailout for farmers

The US seafood industry spent at least $673.0 million in tariffs between early April and the end of July as a result of president Donald Trump global trade war, based on a review by Undercurrent News of seafood trade data maintained by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). 

The numbers can be expected to rise much higher when August trade data is reported, as the administration raised tariff rates that month for many countries. 

READ MORE
SEP 1711:00 AM GMT
Big toothfish supplier South Korea’s trade deal with US not yet settled

South Korea and the US are struggling to finalize the terms of their trade deal announced two months ago, as Seoul resists pressure to allow US president Donald Trump to decide where billions of dollars of its capital should be invested in the US, the Financial Times reports.

South Korea is the US’ 17th-most valuable source of seafood, sending it 27,731 metric tons worth $265.9 million in 2024. Among the most valuable seafood-related products imported from South Korea by the US are toothfish, seaweed and oysters.

READ MORE
SEP 161:10 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Indian politician says trade war has resulted in $2.8m loss for aquaculture industry

The tariffs introduced by US president Donald Trump earlier this year have resulted in losses upwards of $2.8 million for India’s aquaculture industry, according to Indian politician N. Chandrababu Naidu, the chief minister of Andhra Pradesh.

“The taxes imposed by America majorly hit shrimp exports,” Naidu wrote in a letter to union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, commerce minister Piyush Goyal and fisheries minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh.

READ MORE
SEP 151:02 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle 
US, China trade negotiations ‘deferred’
The US and China resumed trade negotiations in Madrid, Spain, on Monday (Sept. 15), with treasury secretary Scott Bessent and trade representative Jamieson Greer leading the talks. 


While advancements were made regarding a deal for social media platform TikTok, trade negotiations were ultimately “deferred,” Greer told CNBC.


US president Donald Trump currently has a 55% tariff rate in place on Chinese goods.


China was the seventh largest source of seafood for the US in 2024, accounting for 353,413 metric tons worth $1.5 billion, as reported by Undercurrent News. The US relies heavily on China for tilapia, red swimming crab, bay scallops, shrimp and numerous other seafood products, including whitefish landed in the US and sent to China for processing.


The trade negotiations between the two countries started up about a week after Trump called for the European Union to place tariffs of up to 100% on China and India as a means of forcing Russian president Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine.
SEP 121:27 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
US trade war costing jobs in Indian seafood sector, says politician

The US trade war has resulted in “significant job losses” in the seafood sector, according to Shashi Tharoor, an Indian politician and member of the Indian National Congress.

Tharoor, speaking at a conference for real estate developers in India, said, “I don’t want anyone to have any illusions that we can just wash it up,” according to The Federal.

READ MORE
SEP 119:52 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Trump reopens trade negotiations with India

US president Donald Trump used his Truth Social platform on Tuesday (Sept. 9) to share that he has reopened trade negotiations with India after slapping the country with a 50% tariff, which has been a massive blow for US importers of shrimp.

“I am pleased to announce that India, and the United States of America, are continuing negotiations to address the Trade Barriers between our two Nations,” Trump posted. “I look forward to speaking with my very good friend, Prime Minister Modi, in the upcoming weeks. I feel certain that there will be no difficulty in coming to a successful conclusion for both of our Great Countries!”

READ MORE
SEP 109:27 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US Supreme Court to hear tariff case in November

The US Supreme Court said Tuesday (Sept. 9) it will review a challenge to US president Donald Trump’s authority to impose tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) this fall.

In an order released Tuesday, the US’ highest court set a schedule to hear oral arguments in early November, placing it in line to deliver a decision before the end of the year.

READ MORE
SEP 109:14 AM GMT
By Cliff White
Trump pushes EU to impose 100% tariffs on China, India

US president Donald Trump called for the European Union to place tariffs of up to 100% on China and India as a means of forcing Russian president Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine.

Russia has continued to attack Ukraine despite Trump urging Putin to agree to a cease-fire during their meeting in the US state of Alaska last month.

READ MORE
SEP 911:17 AM GMT
By Cliff White
US domestic crabmeat industry calls for tariffs on Venezuelan product

The head of the Chesapeake Bay Seafood Industries Association is calling on the administration of US president Donald Trump to tariff Venezuelan crabmeat at a higher level than the 15% rate it currently faces.

The association’s executive director, Bill Sieling, said the industry in the US states of Maryland and Virginia is struggling due to lower-priced competition from blue crab imported from Venezuela, WBAL-11 reported.

READ MORE
SEP 89:41 AM GMT
By Cliff White

National Restaurant Association pans Trump tariffs

The National Restaurant Association (NRA), representing companies collectively operating more than a million US restaurant and foodservice outlets, has issued a statement condemning the Trump tariffs.

“Applying new tariffs at this scale will create change and disruption that restaurant operators will have to navigate to keep their restaurants open. The biggest concerns for restaurant operators — from community restaurants to national brands — are that tariffs will hike food and packaging costs and add uncertainty to managing availability while pushing prices up for consumers,” NRA President and CEO Michelle Korsmo said in a statement issued Wednesday, April 2, soon after the tariffs were announced.

READ MORE
APR 28:25 PM GMT
By Cliff White
Major US tuna exporters all face big tariff rates

All of the top 10 tuna exporters to the US will face tariff rates of at least 10%, with some confronting rates of near or beyond 40%.

The US imported more than 300,000 metric tons of tuna across a range of product types in 2024, with a total value of over $2 billion.

READ MORE
APR 28:24 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
US tariffs could trigger market crash for Japan’s scallops amid record prices

Japan’s frozen scallop market, which has been trading at record-high levels, may soon experience a downturn following the Trump administration’s announcement of new reciprocal tariffs targeting Japanese goods, sources told Undercurrent News early Thursday morning (March 24 local time).

The US is set to impose a 24% tariff on all Japanese products, including seafood such as scallops. Japan was the leading exporter of scallops to the US in 2024, shipping 9,365 metric tons worth $172.6 million — a 26% increase in volume and a 19% rise in value compared with 2023, as Undercurrent reported.

READ MORE
APR 26:40 PM GMT
By Cliff White
Chinese seafood gets slammed by new tariffs

Chinese seafood is now facing a 54% tariff coming into the US — at the minimum.

In addition to the base reciprocal rate of 34% announced Wednesday (April 2), Chinese goods now face two different 10% tariffs imposed by US president Donald Trump for what he has deemed a failure to help stem fentanyl trafficking into the US. 

READ MORE
APR 25:52 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chile, Scottish salmon get 5% edge on Norway

Chile, the largest US salmon supplier, will be subject to a 10% tariff, while Norway will be hit with 15%.

“It’s a small win for Chile but a loss for the industry,” one Chilean salmon executive told Undercurrent News of the 5% edge over its main competitor. 

READ MORE
APR 25:42 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Ecuador gets off light as Asian shrimp suppliers hit hard

Ecuador, the second largest shrimp supplier to the US, is being hit with a 10% tariff, while Asian suppliers will be impacted much more seriously.

India, the largest source of shrimp for the US, will have 26%.

READ MORE
APR 25:36 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Tariff list in full 

Below, you can see the full list of tariffs, which is more extensive than the one Trump presented on April 2. 

The average tariff level Trump claims is applied to US goods is shown on the right, and the left figure shows what Trump will retaliate with. 

READ MORE

Contact the authors tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, masahiko.takeuchi@undercurrentnews.com, neil.ramsden@undercurrentnews.com, Cliff.White@undercurrentnews.com, barb.simmons@undercurrentnews.com, jason.huffman@undercurrentnews.com, amanda.buckle@undercurrentnews.com

title: Untitled
content:
BOSTON, Massachusetts, US -- The Undercurrent News team reported live from Seafood Expo North America (SENA), held March 16-18 in Boston, Massachusetts.

Eleven of UCN's editorial team covered the show floor at SENA, with eight journalists and three price reporters. 

The show also marked the debut of UCN's new US wholesale pricing and trade platforms.

If you'd like to learn how the US wholesale and trade platforms can provide your business with more data, get in touch here.

To learn more about the US wholesale platform, click here. For more on the trade platform, click here.

Auto updates: On
MAR 1810:49 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Investor behind Fathom Seafood’s planned West Coast plant ID’ed

The lead investor behind US shellfish processor Fathom Seafood’s planned $280 million West Coast processor and cold storage facility has been revealed to be a New Jersey-based private equity real estate firm specializing in cold storage.

Saxum Real Estate and Development has about $3.5 billion in assets under management and has pledged at least $180m toward the total cost of the 550,000-square-foot facility.

“This would be the first of, hopefully, several projects with Fathom in terms of their broader vision and kind of fixing what is a fragmented seafood supply chain,” Saxum principal Matt Wassel told Undercurrent from the Seafood Expo floor.

READ MORE
MAR 1810:02 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Ecuador’s Omarsa seeks to ‘reduce dependence on China’ 

Ecuadorian shrimp farmer and processor Omarsa is seeking to increase sales to Europe and the US and cut its reliance on China, its CEO told Undercurrent News.

“We’re targeting to reduce our dependence on China down to 50%” of sales, Sandro Coglitore told Undercurrent at SENA.

READ MORE
MAR 184:53 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Weak EU market means prices for lower pollock surimi grades not rising with higher 

US pollock surimi producers are struggling to get higher prices for the lower grades of surimi sold to Europe, having got an increase for the premium grades to Japan for A season, sources told Undercurrent News at SENA.

As previously reported by Undercurrent, prices to Japan, the main market for pollock surimi, have increased by around 10-15% for A season.

READ MORE
MAR 182:25 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Dock prices still unsettled for Canada’s snow crabbers

Snow crab season has started for at least one crab fishing zone in Atlantic Canada, with boats from the Cape Breton area of Nova Scotia landing the first crab of the season this week, as previously reported by Undercurrent News.

However, dock prices for the start of the season remain a mystery and may not be settled until later this month, a source told Undercurrent at SENA 2025 in Boston this week.

READ MORE
MAR 181:46 PM GMT
By Cliff White
Tampa Maid Foods debuts new Margaritaville brand frozen shrimp products

Tampa Maid Foods is adding two new products to its Margaritaville line of frozen shrimp products.

Its crunch-coated cheese- and jalapeno-stuffed Volcano Shrimp and its tabasco-seasoned, crispy-coated Singin’ Spicy Breaded Shrimp will be available to ship across the US in May 2025, according to Michael Rhoads, Tampa Maid’s retail sales director.

READ MORE
MAR 181:40 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Canada’s geoduck industry halts ahead of Chinese tariffs

The geoduck industry in the Canadian province of British Columbia (BC) is one of the first casualties of China’s decision to impose 25% tariffs on seafood from the country.

“We went gangbusters up to yesterday (March 16) to land as much product as we could and, as of today, the fishery is shut down for at least five to seven days, and maybe longer,” Grant Dovey, executive director of the Underwater Harvesters Association (UHA) in BC, told Undercurrent News at SENA on March 17.

READ MORE
MAR 1811:52 AM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Fear and loathing among US Pacific halibut producers

Uncertainty continues among US Pacific halibut producers and processors with delays in permits, threats of Canadian tariffs and constrained supply buoying up potentially record prices making more questions than answers as the March 20 opening date approaches.

Dana Besecker is a medium-sized wholesaler that for nearly 30 years enjoyed a joint venture with a Canadian processor with a plant outside of Vancouver, British Columbia.

READ MORE
MAR 1811:51 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
US lobster processors would gain advantage over Canadians if tariffs imposed

No surprise. The potential of US tariffs on seafood from multiple source nations is the talk of the Boston seafood show this year.

At least one US company at the conference, however, believes it may gain an advantage if 25% tariffs go into effect on Canadian and Mexican goods as of April 2, as threatened by US president Donald Trump. 

READ MORE
MAR 187:09 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
US scallop leaders see 2025 dominated again by imports, small sizes

Despite the rare overestimation by the New England Fishery Management Council’s scallop staff of landings in open areas during the 2024-25 season, Peter Handy, the CEO of Bristol Seafood, in Portland, Maine, believes its projections for the upcoming 2025-26 season are most likely correct. 

The staff’s annual projected yield (APY) for the new season, which begins April 1, is 19.75 million pounds based on the rules included in Framework 39. 

READ MORE
MAR 175:53 PM GMT
By Cliff White
China’s seafood buffets are closing, impacting niche product pricing

A downturn in the Chinese economy has squeezed the country’s foodservice sector, forcing the closure of hundreds of seafood buffet restaurants, according to Yen and Brothers (YENS) chief operating officer Dennis Yen.

Taiwanese trader YENS, which has an annual turnover surpassing $170 million, is a specialist in importing, exporting, processing and distributing a wide range of frozen seafood products including Greenland halibut, vannamei shrimp, squid, toothfish, salmon and whelk, as well as the catch of Taiwan’s local and distant-water fleet such as tuna and mackerel.

READ MORE
MAR 175:03 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Social justice campaigners picket Seafood Expo entrance

A coalition of migrant fishermen held a vigil outside the Summer Street entrance at the convention center to raise awareness for human rights abuses in the seafood industry.

Adrian Basar, a 28-year-old former crewman from Indonesia, was aboard the Longbow 7 when his crewmate fell seriously ill, but the captain of the Taiwan-based vessel refused to return to shore.

READ MORE
MAR 173:19 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
South Korea’s Namdo Soban turns to Netflix show ‘Squid Game’ to sell new seafood snack

Namdo Soban a seafood company based in Gwangju, South Korea, is turning to the hit Netflix series “Squid Game” to help sell its new squid snacks in the US.

Jacob Choi, CEO, told Undercurrent News that the company is looking to introduce its crunchy snack to US retailers, with the goal of landing their products on the shelves of wholesale giant Costco.

READ MORE
MAR 172:52 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Pacific Seafood debuts new look for retail offerings

US West Coast processor, importer and distributor Pacific Seafood Group has rebranded its retail offerings with a first look offered at Seafood Expo North America in Boston.

“It’s been about seven years since we had a brand refresh and really did a deep dive on our packaging,” Kady Freeze, the Oregon-based company’s marketing brand manager told Undercurrent News. “We wanted to make sure that it was aligning with consumer market trends as well as our retailer’s needs.”

READ MORE
MAR 172:01 PM GMT
By Cliff White
BoA’s Jason Brantley: ‘Sea change’ underway in Alaska’s M&A outlook

Alaska’s seafood processing industry has been rocked by cataclysmic changes over the past year, with Trident Seafoods scaling back its holdings, Peter Pan Seafoods going bankrupt and Silver BaySeafoods snapping up plants across the US state, which accounts for up to 60% of the country’s total seafood production by volume.

Speaking to Undercurrent News at SENA, Bank of America senior vice president and senior relationship manager Jason Brantley said there has been a “sea change” in how industry players are looking at their Alaska holdings.

READ MORE
MAR 171:13 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
‘I don’t think it’s a panacea’ – tuna industry talks electronic monitoring on vessels

Electronic monitoring across the world’s tuna fleet is gaining traction as more major buyers require safeguards in their supply chain, as demanded by advocacy groups and some consumers.

But harvesters say the market needs to incentivize best practices, and retailers say they must be able to continue to deliver quality canned tuna to consumers who are very price-conscious.

READ MORE
MAR 1712:13 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Norwegian whitefish landings slump over start of year despite sizeable rollover

Painfully tight whitefish landings have been the story of the year so far in Norway, with volumes even lower than feared over the first two months of the year, according to Morten Jensen, managing director of Insula’s Nordic Group.

This drop has been particularly striking for saithe, where Jensen confirmed that a significant 40,000 metric tons was uncaught last year and has been added to this year’s quota.

READ MORE
MAR 1711:44 AM GMT
By Ben Fisher
CoolJapan seeks US distributor for frozen sushi product

Japanese firm CoolJapan is seeking a distribution channel to launch its frozen sushi product Midori Sushi in the United States later this year, CEO Hiroyuki Kakinuma told Undercurrent News. 

The company hopes to eventually launch direct to consumer sales, but plans to begin selling B2B, aiming initially for hotels, cruise lines, and offices, Kakinuma said.

READ MORE
MAR 1711:04 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
National Fisheries Institute hits refresh as industry faces rough storm

National Fisheries Institute (NFI) CEO and president Lisa Wallenda Picard took some time off the show floor with Catch the Current hosts Amanda Buckle and Lorin Castiglione to talk about the trade association’s big refresh of aboutseafood.com.

With tariffs a topic of conversation that can’t be ignored, Lisa explains why the redesign came at the perfect time for its members.

READ MORE
MAR 1711:00 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman 
NOAA cancels presentation at Boston seafood show

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration was scheduled to have three of its top executives, including Emily Menashes, the acting head of the National Marine Fisheries Service, speak at SENA 2025, but it wasn’t meant to be.

The one-hour presentation, which was scheduled for 2 p.m. EST on Sunday (March 16), was canceled, conference staff told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAR 1710:58 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons 
Ocean Choice to add more cold storage space for snow crab

As snow crab processors in Atlantic Canada wait to see whether US president Donald Trump will proceed with a 25% tariff on Canadian imports on April 2, they’re also contemplating how to store thousands of metric tons of snow crab on the Canadian side of the border awaiting final sale to US wholesalers.

Canadian crab usually winds up in cold storage on the US side of the border, but the tariff threat has at least one snow crab producer considering another option.

READ MORE
MAR 1710:54 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons 
World’s largest snow crab fishery not likely to start until April

The expectation that the world’s largest snow crab fishery might start a little earlier in 2025 is growing dimmer as the days of March tick away.

Don’t expect Canada’s Department of Fisheries and Oceans to make a formal announcement on the quota for the world’s largest snow crab fishery in the province of Newfoundland and Labrador for at least another week, one industry source told Undercurrent News at SENA in Boston on Sunday (March 17).

READ MORE
MAR 1710:50 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Thistle, Aquamar team up to bring UK value-added seafood to US retail

UK processing firm Thistle Seafoods has formed a new US sales partnership with surimi processing specialist Aquamar, it announced at SENA. 

Under the new arrangement, Scotland’s Thistle, which operates two value-added processing factories in Scotland, will sell new product lines to the US exclusively to Aquamar for further distribution, Thistle CEO Ryan Scatterty told Undercurrent News at the show.

READ MORE
MAR 1710:31 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
$500m Norway salmon processor sets up US operation with former Boston Sword exec

Norwegian salmon processor Vikenco has established a US entity with a former Boston Sword and Tuna (BST) executive to “get deeper into the market,” CEO Per Olav Mevold told Undercurrent News at SENA. 

Vikenco, which is 51% owned by farmer and processor SalMar and generates around NOK 5 billion (close to $500 million) in revenue annually, has hired former BST executive Chris Marchese to head its newly created US entity, Mevold told Undercurrent.

READ MORE
MAR 1710:24 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Possible tariffs on Canada could benefit Beaver Street’s spiny lobster

If US president Donald Trump goes ahead with the proposed 25% tariffs on imports from Canada, it would create an opening for spiny lobster tails from the Bahamas.

The current season is wrapping up in the Bahamas at the end of March, with volume committed, but there could be an opening for the new season if Canadian lobster and other seafood is hit with a 25% tariff, said Mark Frisch of Beaver Street Fisheries.

READ MORE
MAR 179:39 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
JETRO expands Japan pavilion, highlighting scallops, yellowtail 

The Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) has expanded its Japan Pavilion at Seafood Expo North America (SENA) as part of the government’s initiative to support the country’s fisheries industry. 

This year, 19 companies and organizations are exhibiting, up from 17 last year, showcasing products such as scallops and yellowtail.

READ MORE
MAR 177:03 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan’s surimi manufacturer aims to double offshore sales by tapping US demand

Yamasa Kamaboko, a major Japanese manufacturer of surimi-based products, is looking to tap into the growing demand for imitation crab in the US, aiming to double its overseas export revenue to JPY 3 billion ($20 million), Homare Nada, an executive director at the company, told Undercurrent News.

The Himeji, Hyogo-based manufacturer has launched its tempura-style Alaskan pollock imitation crab sticks in the US under the brand “BOCO’S.” 

READ MORE
MAR 177:03 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Owner of Peru’s Oceano strikes again in US squid with deal for Town Dock

A company majority controlled by the owner of Peru’s Oceano Corp. has acquired another US East Coast squid company, having snapped up Rhode Island’s Sea Fresh U.S.A. in 2023.

The Oceano-linked entity has just acquired The Town Dock, a squid processor also based in Rhode Island, sources at Seafood Expo North America told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAR 176:20 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japanese scallop exporters wary of high-price fatigue in US market

Japanese scallop exporters are increasingly concerned about weakening demand in the US market as record-high prices driven by strong demand show signs of fatigue.

“The main production area in the Sea of Okhotsk is currently in the off-season, and there isn’t enough inventory in Japan to supply the US market,” a source told Undercurrent News. However, he added, “There is a sense that demand for Japanese scallops in the US is softening due to high prices, and a significant market downturn could occur.”

READ MORE
MAR 175:41 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Alaskan pollock producers see firm roe prices at Seattle auction 

Alaskan pollock producers secured firm prices for standard-grade roe at the first auction of the 2025 A season in Seattle, Washington, despite an increase in listed volume, sources told Undercurrent News.

The increase in volume resulted from the auction being held one week later than last year, adding an extra week’s supply. Larger fish sizes this season also contributed to improved roe yields, producers said.

READ MORE
MAR 164:46 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Chilean coho farmer Salmones Aysen doubles US portion sales 

Salmones Aysen, a leading Chilean coho salmon farmer, has doubled its portion product sales in the US to 2,000 metric tons in the 2024-25 season compared to the previous year, Jorge Guzman, the company’s chief commercial officer, told Undercurrent News.

“We are like the Robin Hood of the salmon industry,” said Guzman. “Our mission is to continue offering US consumers the best quality salmon at attractive prices.”

READ MORE
MAR 163:52 PM GMT
By Cliff White
Two Fish expands into Walmart, H-E-B, eyes Costco deal

Two Fish Distribution’s seafood boil bags have been picked up by Walmart and H-E-B.

Founded by Yasmin Curtis in 2020, the Chicago, Illinois-based Two Fish manufactures frozen 1 lb bags featuring corn, whole red potatoes, a proprietary sauce, and either shrimp, snow crab legs or a shrimp and crab combination.

READ MORE
MAR 163:31 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Pacific Seafood in talks to acquire Florida skin-pack plant NovoMar

US West Coast distributor, importer and processor Pacific Seafood Group is in talks to acquire a Doral, Florida skin-pack plant that ran into financial difficulty last year, sources told Undercurrent News at SENA.

Clackamas, Oregon-based Pacific, the largest player on the US West Coast and one of the biggest seafood companies in the country, is in well-advanced discussions about buying the NovoMar plant in Doral, Florida, sources told Undercurrent.

READ MORE
MAR 162:59 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Norwegian trader First Seafood doubles US volume share in spite of tariff fears

Norwegian salmon processor First Seafood, part of  Insula Group, has sharply increased its sales to the US this year, echoing the broader trend across the country.

The firm produced 18,000 metric tons of salmon across its pair of factories in Norway last year, and intends to ramp up to 40,000t following the acquisition of a factory in Denmark, Insula Hvide Sande, in September last year.

READ MORE
MAR 162:23 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Trident Seafoods debuts ‘Essentials’ line of minced Alaska pollock products 

Trident Seafoods debuted a new line of products at SENA in Boston: Trident Seafoods Essentials.

In addition to the company’s Ultimate Fish Stick line, made from whole fillets, Trident has introduced its new Essentials line, to allow its products to better compete with other lower-value seafood products in the freezer section.

READ MORE
MAR 161:51 PM GMT
By Cliff White
CNA’s Camposano: Ecuador shrimp exports ‘will not be growing at a 15% rate anymore’

Over the past several years, Ecuador has become the world’s largest shrimp exporter, spurred by a doubling of its shrimp sales to China over the past 48 months.

Despite a sluggish 2024, the country’s shrimp industry still expects to grow, but at a more sustainable level, according to Jose Antonio Camposano, executive president of Ecuador’s National Chamber of Aquaculture (CNA).

READ MORE
MAR 161:34 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Fathom in ‘deal-making mode’ at SENA as expansion plans revealed

Fathon Seafood’s ambitious new $280 million automated processing line, cold storage and distribution center is planned in the US Port of Tacoma with scheduled completion for late 2026, Undercurrent News has been told.

It will be a 550,500-square foot third-party processor (3PP) attached to a third-party logistics (3PL) facility that will be available to use – for a fee – to retailers, distributors, suppliers and others including restaurant chains.

READ MORE
MAR 161:02 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Boston 2025 in 5: ‘March Madness’ with Alaskan Leader’s miso black cod

Five minutes are on the clock as Catch the Current welcomes Alaskan Leader president Keith Singleton and vice president of value-added sales Scott Sandvig to the podcast live on the SENA show floor in Boston, Massachusetts.

Keith and Scott share Alaskan Leader’s big success with Costco and the introduction of its new deli kit.

READ MORE
MAR 1612:47 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japanese surimi buyers accept 10-15% price hike for 2025 A season Alaska pollock

Japanese surimi buyers have largely accepted a 10-15% price increase for Alaska pollock surimi in the 2025 A season compared to the previous season, Japanese and US sources at the Seafood Expo North Americas told Undercurrent News.

In late February, Undercurrent reported that prices for Japanese-bound Alaska pollock surimi were expected to rise by 10-15%, driven by higher production costs, including rising labor costs in Alaska and the Japanese yen depreciation. 

READ MORE
MAR 1612:31 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
First Canadian snow crab of year lands March 17

The first Canadian snow crab of 2025 will be landed as soon as Monday (March 17) in the Cape Breton part of the province Nova Scotia, which opened its season Friday night (March 14).

Weather conditions were favorable on the weekend for the fleets that fish zones 23 and 24 off the east coast of Cape Breton, Allan MacLean, president of the Nova Scotia Seafood Alliance, the trade organization that represents most of the province’s seafood processors, told Undercurrent News on Sunday (March 16) at the Boston seafood show.

READ MORE
MAR 1612:20 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Mexican tuna farmers shift focus to Japan amid US tariff threats

Mexican bluefin tuna farmers are increasing their shipments to Japan in response to US President Donald Trump’s proposed 25% tariff on Mexican imports, sources told Undercurrent News at the SENA.

“Aquaculture producers in Mexico are offering to sell at lower prices to secure deals in Japan,” said a Japanese tuna buyer. Another Japanese tuna distributor noted a rise in inquiries from Mexican suppliers eager to find buyers.

READ MORE
MAR 1612:06 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Iceland on track for 60,000t salmon harvest in 2025

Bjorn Hembre, CEO of Icelandic salmon farmer Arnarlax, told Undercurrent that the country’s sea-based farming industry should produce roughly 60,000 metric tons of Atlantic salmon this year if all companies meet their guided targets.

The sector was beset by lice problems in 2023, forcing early harvests of fish and reducing the biomass available for harvest in 2024.

READ MORE
MAR 166:11 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Candor’s Bemiller offers seafood investor diligence service after eFishery debacle

Marcy Bemiller, whose company Candor Seafood was representing scandal-ridden seafood unicorn eFishery in the US market, said she hopes to offer a due diligence service to would-be investors to avoid the same happening again.

Candor was acting on the US sales side for eFishery — which was valued at over $1.2 billion in a 2023 fundraising round — in a tilapia project. When Bemiller made a trip to Indonesia last year, she said it was evident something was very wrong, she told Undercurrent News just before SENA.

READ MORE
MAR 154:46 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman 
Goldberg to join Aqua Star as shrimp, farmed fish buyer

Jeff Goldberg, one of the US seafood industry’s best-known and most-traveled executives, will be leading shrimp and farmed fish procurement efforts for Seattle, Washington-based Aqua Star, he announced Friday (March 14) on LinkedIn.

“I’m excited to announce that I have accepted a position with Aqua Star as vice president of procurement for shrimp and farmed fish,” he reported on his profile page, adding: “See you in Boston this weekend! Looking forward to this new adventure.”

READ MORE
MAR 154:24 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Catch the Current episode 8: Pregame with us for Seafood Expo North America 2025 in Boston!

The long, cold, dark days of February are behind us. And right smack in front of us is SENA 2025. 

So, break out those Dr. Scholl’s inserts, charge those backup phone batteries, and, for the love of sweet and crispy coconut-fried shrimp, make sure you have your QR code handy to get your badge! But most importantly — download the new episode of Catch the Current!

READ MORE
MAR 154:16 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chile’s largest salmon farmer opens US plant

AquaChile, the largest salmon farmer in Chile, has opened a new US operation in Miami, Florida, the company unveiled before SENA. 

The new branch includes a processing plant, distribution center, and offices, Sady Delgado, CEO of AquaChile, announced on LinkedIn. 

READ MORE
MAR 154:05 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
UCN debuts new US wholesale prices, trade platforms at Boston

Undercurrent News‘ team is at the SENA show to discuss our new US wholesale pricing and trade platforms.

If you’d like to meet at SENA to learn how the US wholesale and trade platforms can provide your business with more data, get in touch here.

READ MORE
