title: Untitled
content:
BERGEN, Norway -- Undercurrent News reported live from the North Atlantic Seafood Forum (NASF),  held March 4-6.

The annual three-day NASF event sees the town of Bergen play host to many of Norway's largest salmon farmers, as well as representatives of the international whitefish, pelagics, and aquaculture feed sectors.

Auto updates: On
MAR 74:12 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
High Liner woos young North Americans to replace red meat, poultry with seafood

“The children are our future” could be High Liner Foods’ new motto as it targets increased seafood consumption by drawing younger North American consumers to the category.

The Canadian seafood giant is partnering with colleges and student halls to put seafood on the menu, with the aim being to “establish those seafood eating habits among Gen Zs when they’re young,” said CEO Paul Jewer.

READ MORE
MAR 610:04 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Leroy backs embrace of shielding tech to turn around fortunes at south Norway ops

Leroy Seafood Group CEO Henning Beltestad showcased some of the initial benefits his firm has made from its widespread embrace of shielding technology.

Leroy, which operates a sizeable operation in the south of Norway under its Leroy Sjotroll division, has suffered more than most from sea lice and related issues in the relatively warmer waters near Bergen and Stavanger.

READ MORE
MAR 69:52 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
European salmon feed sector warns of ‘complexities, costs’ ahead of blue whiting sustainability deadline

Europe’s salmon aquaculture feed sector faces a period of planning in the face of added complexities and costs to the fishmeal supply chain as northeast Atlantic blue whiting nears a deadline for coastal states to agree on a quota-sharing deal.

There are 18 months and just two coastal state meetings left before blue whiting, which is an ingredient for some 50% of Norway salmon’s feed, fails its fishery improvement project (FIP) because no such quota-sharing deal can be agreed by politicians.

READ MORE
MAR 69:20 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Arnarlax hopes changes to Icelandic aquaculture law will allow growth, tax profits

Icelandic salmon farmer Arnarlax, which is controlled by Norway’s SalMar, hopes changes to the country’s aquaculture law will allow it to grow beyond its current estimates.

At the moment it holds biomass licenses worth 26,000 metric tons, and it has applications in the system that it hopes can grant another 14,500t, said CEO Bjorn Hembre.

READ MORE
MAR 69:13 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Salmon farming’s paradox: Poor public image despite sustainability credentials

Norway’s salmon farming industry faces a dispiriting disconnect between its environmental credentials and public perception, industry leaders warned.

“We’re producing food in salt water — we’re not using freshwater and there are low carbon emissions. What is the problem? It should be the most popular industry,” said Anne Hvistendahl, global head of seafood at Norway’s DNB Bank.

READ MORE
MAR 68:43 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Salmon Evolution nears cost, CAPEX parity with conventional farming

Land-based salmon producer Salmon Evolution is approaching capital expenditure and cost parity with conventional sea-based farming while targeting an additional 20% cost reduction, according to chairman Tore Tonseth.

“Our CAPEX is currently close to the conventional industry. And we can absolutely go down. Internally we want to go down 20%,” Tonseth said at NASF.

READ MORE
MAR 68:34 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Cargill relocates risk, sourcing manager to Europe amid downsizing

Cargill’s regional director for risk management and sourcing in Southeast Asia and India, Tom Windscheffel, is relocating from Bangkok, Thailand to Europe and assuming responsibility for some regions there, including Norway, he said during a presentation at NASF.

That comes as Cargill announced at the end of 2024 that it would reduce its global workforce by 5%. Its website states it employs some 160,000 in total.

READ MORE
MAR 67:35 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Atlantic Sapphire aims to be back at target harvest weight by Q3

Presenting for the first time at NASF, the new management team at Atlantic Sapphire detailed the Florida, US-based RAS salmon farmer’s plans to get back on track in 2025.

As previously reported by Undercurrent News, Atlantic Sapphire has been steadily raising its harvest weights, after the new managers found the firm had “too many fish per batch” when they took over last year.

READ MORE
MAR 66:56 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Nordic Aqua Partners up to 1,000t quarterly harvest rate as it resolves geosmin fears

Chinese recirculating aquaculture system project Nordic Aqua Partners (NAP) should now be consistently producing 1,000 metric tons per quarter from its first phase facility, which held its first commercial harvest last year.

The company had subsequently paused harvests after it identified a geosmin filter issue impacting the flavor of its salmon but began commercial production again earlier this year.

READ MORE
MAR 66:56 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
‘Lot of people looking at their books’ after Norway’s extra tax on ASC salmon

With the Norwegian government proposing what amounts to an additional tax on Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC)-certified salmon, farmers will be assessing the value of the certification, believes one sector source.

The wording of the Norwegian Price Council for Aquaculture’s setup imposes an additional charge of NOK 1.50 ($0.13) per kilogram on ASC-certified fish — a move the ASC has slammed, and which prompted farmer Bremnes Seashore to discontinue its use of the certification. 

READ MORE
MAR 66:31 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Salmon Evolution details latest construction, tank capacity aligned to grow-out plans

Salmon Evolution, the world’s largest land-based aquaculture firm by volume, is well on track with its “phase two” construction — a development which should be a “game-changer,” said CEO Trond Hakon Schaug-Pettersen.

Phase two will bring the Indre Haroy site to 18,000 metric tons head-on, gutted weight, and allow for weekly harvests, he noted.

READ MORE
MAR 66:19 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Seafood dominates global protein consumption, outpacing terrestrial sources

Seafood consumption is four times that of beef and exceeds the combined total of pork and poultry, according to global consultancy group McKinsey.

The striking statistic underlines seafood’s huge potential and availability, particularly outside the US and northwestern European markets, such as in Asia and southern Europe, where seafood is more in demand.

READ MORE
MAR 66:05 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
High Liner’s stake in Andfjord now up to 8.1%, latter confirms

Bjarne Martinsen, CFO of land-based flow-through farmer Andfjord Salmon Group, confirmed the new shareholder percentages after the conclusion of its recent private placement.

Notably, Canadian processor and distributor High Liner Foods has increased its ownership share after the subsequent offering to 8.1%, up from 5.3% before the latest share issue, he said.

READ MORE
MAR 64:00 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Norwegian seafood sector’s market cap surges 20-fold in two decades

The market capitalization of Norway’s seafood companies listed on the Oslo stock exchange has increased 20-fold since the first NASF two decades ago, according to Pareto Securities analysts.

The sector grew 13% in 2024 alone, with transactions totaling NOK 30 billion ($2.76bn) in the Norwegian market, according to Carl-Emil Kjolas Johannessen of Pareto. There were 10 transactions over NOK 1bn in value.

READ MORE
MAR 63:57 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Mowi CEO: Limited synergy with farm division prompted feed sale plan 

In the morning session of day three, Mowi CEO Ivan Vindheim addressed the “strategic review” (namely, a plan to sell) of the firm’s feed division, announced on March 4.

“The question of the hour is why did we do that?” he began. “The short answer is that the synergies between farming and feed are not always as easy to catch hold of in real life as in theory.”

READ MORE
MAR 63:40 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Analyst projects NOK 6/kg price hit if US tariffs all salmon imports

US tariffs on salmon imports could reshape global trade flows and significantly impact producer earnings, according to Pareto Securities equity analyst Sander Lie.

Lie projects that a 25% US tariff affecting all producing countries could force a dramatic supply shift toward European and Asian markets, potentially triggering a 3% supply shock and NOK 6 ($0.55) per kilogram price dip. However, the 25% tariff solely on Canadian imports should have minimal impact, reducing salmon prices by NOK 0.6/kg.

READ MORE
MAR 51:41 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Cod farmer Kime Akva conducts third stocking on five-year march to 24,000t

Yngve Myhre, formerly CEO of SalMar and current chair of Kime Akva, was on hand to detail the nascent cod farmer’s five-year growth plan to listeners at NASF.

The farmer, which has access to nine farm sites in the north of Norway, had stocked its third generation of fish the previous day, March 4, he said.

READ MORE
MAR 51:29 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Uncertain year ahead for whitefish 

The global whitefish sector is in for an uncertain and tough year, with supply down, prices high for key species like cod, and trade wars on the horizon, was the general conclusion of the NASF whitefish panel.

“I used to think things could change by the week, then by the day, now it’s by the hour,” said Paul Jewer, CEO of Canada’s High Liner Foods, which is based in Canada but has two plants in the US and generates two-thirds of its revenue from its southern neighbor.

READ MORE
MAR 51:27 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Pollock appears in European products where cod used to be

The record high prices for Atlantic cod mean it’s no longer being used in fish fingers and other breaded and battered products as much, said Finn-Arne Egeness, the head seafood analyst with Nordic lender Nordea.

“You are finding pollock in the places cod used to be,” he told the audience of the whitefish summit at NASF.

READ MORE
MAR 512:14 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Salmon farmers feel the fear as blue whiting deadline looms

Between March 2024 and March 2025, the number of Norwegian salmon farmers in the North Atlantic Pelagic Advocacy Group, which is campaigning to secure a quota-sharing agreement between coastal states for mackerel, herring, and blue whiting, rose from one to eight.

Now, with 18 months and two coastal state meetings left before blue whiting — the ingredient for some 50% of Norway salmon’s feed — fails its fishery improvement project (FIP), the reality of that looms large for a sector already concerned about its “social license to operate.”

READ MORE
MAR 510:46 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Fisk’s PVC closed containment sea pen ‘the future of targeted salmon growth’

Fisk’s closed containment PVC pen is being used by farmers to halve the amount of time post-smolt fish spend in open sea cages, the company said, offering a pathway for future production growth.

Developed over nine years, the company’s closed containment pens have completed over 80 production cycles producing 30 million post-smolt salmon. 

READ MORE
MAR 59:41 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Mowi: Precision aquaculture in ‘new phase’ of utilizing data

“Precision aquaculture” has entered a new phase of digitization, with Mowi able to now use its database to take decisions, said chief technology and sustainability officer Catarina Martins.

“Before, we were collecting data, not being certain that there were no human errors or that the sensors were always giving the right quality,” she said.

READ MORE
MAR 59:23 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Profitable land-based salmon pilot bodes well for Bue’s 50,000t project

For any land-based salmon farmer, future profitability is what draws investors. On the money then is Norwegian salmon farmer Bue, which has a license for a 50,000-metric-ton plant in Lutelandet, western Norway.

Since 2023, the company has reported positive earnings before interest, tax, deductions and amortization (EBITDA) at its pilot facility in Butelandet, Vestland county.

READ MORE
MAR 59:05 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Cargill models show 3% more fish oil needed per year

The aquaculture feed supply division of Cargill is modeling that an additional 3% of fish oil will be needed per year in the near future to avoid feed price hikes, said Tom Windscheffel, the company’s senior director for risk management and sourcing.

Cargill, using Kontali data too, estimates salmon supply growth at an annual compound growth rate of 3% over the coming years. That means the same amount of fish oil will be needed to keep up, he said.

READ MORE
MAR 58:37 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Potential for up to 800,000t of salmon from three assessed offshore zones, says Utror

Lars Konrad Johnsen, head of business development at offshore salmon project Utror said that impact assessments recently conducted at three sites off the coast of Norway showcase the huge possible production volumes from offshore salmon farming.

The company, owned by conventional farmer Lovundlaks, is waiting on the government to establish a regulatory framework for the nascent industry, expected to take place this year (see below).

READ MORE
MAR 58:19 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Regulatory breakthroughs on offshore aquaculture in Norway expected imminently

While land-based salmon farming comes on leaps and bounds, the sector is waiting for the government to set up its regulatory framework for offshore aquaculture.

Speaking at a lunch session hosted by DNV, Marius Dalen of Norway’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries said decisions on which areas it will launch the first phase of offshore aquaculture are due “very shortly.”

READ MORE
MAR 58:04 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Thai Union: Transactional nature of supply deals hurts sustainability

The transactional nature of seafood supply relationships is undermining industry sustainability initiatives, according to Thai Union Group’s European sustainability director Chris Shearlock.

“You can put in lots of work on sustainability for a customer and then they don’t renew the contract,” Shearlock said. “For long-term sustainability planning this is problematic.”

READ MORE
MAR 58:03 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Norway’s salmon sector not sharing knowledge as they try to rush innovations through

Opinions differed during the second panel on salmon welfare and sustainable growth. 

Kristine Hartmann, CEO of SalMar’s Salmon Living Lab, and Sondre Eide, CEO of Eide Fjordbruk, felt information sharing was key to the industry moving forward and that innovations were restrained, not incentivized, by Norway’s regulatory framework.

READ MORE
MAR 57:49 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Mowi can ‘maneuver’ US trade barriers with global salmon footprint

Mowi has the global footprint to “maneuver” the 25% tariffs Donald Trump has applied to Canada, with much speculation at NASF that Norway could be included when the US president focuses on the European Union (EU).

The 25% tariffs came into play on Canada on March 4, with Trump having stated he intends to hit the EU with the same level, which could include Norway.

READ MORE
MAR 57:46 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Mowi touts nationwide US skin-pack coverage, sees e-commerce as future driver

Mowi’s head sales executive touted the company’s strong position in US skin-pack distribution during a salmon-focused event at NASF on Tuesday.

From its plants in Miami, Florida, Arlington, Texas and Belfast, Maine, the company can sell fresh, pre-packaged salmon to the whole of the country, he said.

READ MORE
MAR 56:51 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
UK consumers aware of negative salmon stories reduce consumption

Nearly one-fifth of UK consumers who are aware of negative publicity around salmon farming say they reduce their consumption, according to industry data shared by Sofina Europe executive William Davies.

Salmon is the UK’s highest-value seafood category, worth £1.1 billion annually with 60,000 metric tons in sales volumes. However, headlines about sea lice and animal welfare are denting salmon’s reputation among the UK public.

READ MORE
MAR 55:48 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Hard truths highlighted for ‘immature’ salmon industry by Norwegian vet director

Edgar Brun, director of fish health at Norway’s veterinary institute, did not mince his words reflecting on a poor year for the country’s salmon industry that saw record mortalities and volumes of impaired, wounded fish.

“We hit rock bottom, production-grade fish exploded,” said Brun. “We had this brilliant product, and now the media was full of the opposite.”

READ MORE
MAR 55:24 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China’s seafood trade deficit could reach $10bn by 2030

China’s seafood trade deficit could reach $10 billion by 2030 as demographic changes and urbanization drive consumption growth, according to Rabobank analyst Gorjan Nikolik.

The shift is being fueled by an aging population, with those over 60 expected to reach 509 million by 2050, combined with increasing urbanization and rising disposable incomes, said Nikolik.

READ MORE
MAR 55:08 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Aquaculture should exploit advantages over terrestrial animal protein producers

Aquaculture should recognize and exploit its inherent advantages over terrestrial animal protein producers to capitalize on long-term potential, said Bastiaan van Tilburg, CEO of Skretting.

Tilburg — previously at Nutreco, Skretting’s parent company — noted how beef farmers in the Netherlands are scattered and rely on government subsidies “because they can’t get a fair price.”

READ MORE
MAR 54:22 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Fight for survival inspired turnaround at Norway’s greenest poultry producer

Just 10 years ago, Norwegian poultry producer Norsk Kylling was “in the shit”, CEO Hilde Talseth told audience members during the morning session on day two. Mired in an environmental scandal and NOK 240 million ($21.7m) in annual losses, the company needed a turnaround.

“Local salmon fishermen used to joke it was easier to catch chicken than fish in the river near our facilities,” said Talseth.

READ MORE
MAR 412:24 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Trade agreements gain importance as uncertainties sweep globe

Trade agreements are set to become even more important in 2025, with the US likely to cause big shifts in the flow of goods, said Arne Melcior, professor emeritus at the Norsk Utenrikspolitisk Institutt’s Centre for International Economics and Trade.

“Looking at free trade agreements with countries outside the EU and Europe, this graph [below] shows where EFTA [the European Free Trade Association, including Iceland and Norway] and the EU have negotiated deals.”

READ MORE
MAR 411:57 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Peru bounceback to see global pelagics supply for fishmeal, oil near 15m metric tons

A post-El Nino bounceback in Peru should take global pelagic supplies of whole fish caught for fishmeal and oil near to 15 million metric tons in 2025, according to estimates presented by IFFO’s Enrico Bachis.

Supplies of fishmeal should reach between 5.3m and 5.4m metric tons — up from a previously estimated 5.12m in 2024 — and fish oil is expected to inch up from 1.18m metric tons to between 1.2m and 1.3m, he said.

READ MORE
MAR 411:00 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Mackerel undergoing ‘second big price shift’

Mackerel is going through its second big price shift, said Nordea analyst Finn-Arne Egeness.

The first big shift took place in the 90s, as the product became more global and stimulated more widespread competition for a limited resource.

READ MORE
MAR 410:50 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Rabobank: Global fishmeal shortage, sharp price volatility likely to come ‘sooner than expected’

Global fishmeal demand is rapidly on track to becoming inelastic as supplies are stretched thinner with each passing year, according to Rabobank analyst Novel Sharma.

With fishmeal supplies roughly flat from year to year, around 75% of the total volume was used by aquaculture back in 2013.

READ MORE
MAR 410:43 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Kontali: Supply of export-grade Norwegian salmon could be up 25% in first half 

Although Norway’s Kontali Analyse is forecasting a 7% increase in the harvest volume of Norwegian Atlantic salmon in the first half of 2025, the quantity of export-grade whole fish could increase much more dramatically, said Ragnar Nystoyl, its managing director.

In 2024, the quantity of “production grade” Norwegian fish — which can’t be exported whole and has to be processed — was just under 20% of the total, the “worst year in history,” said Nystoyl.

READ MORE
MAR 49:34 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
US soybean prices expected to tank in tariff frenzy

While the circumstances of the global tariff conflict between the US and China changes with each passing day, Carlos Mera, head of agri-commodities research at Rabobank, is confident that US soybeans are likely to fall in value still further.

Earlier on March 4, China imposed additional retaliatory tariffs of 10% on US soybeans, and 15% tariffs on imports of US wheat and corn.

READ MORE
MAR 48:58 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Aker Qrill sees krill feed as solution to salmon sector’s winter wound problems

Sigve Nordrum, the chief commercial officer at Aker QRILL Company, was the new entity’s representative at its first NASF since the feed arm was officially spun off from parent company Aker Biomarine last September.

As previously reported by Undercurrent, the divestment means that significantly more krill should be made available for aquafeed purposes than before, with the salmon sector a priority.

READ MORE
MAR 48:57 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Skretting, Thai Union warn there is a ‘gun to your heads’ over pelagics sharing

During a panel discussion on the topic of northeast Atlantic pelagics quota sharing, representatives from feed firm Skretting and major processor Thai Union Group warned the fishing sector that “the age of consequences” for overfishing is near.

“I’ve heard fishermen say they don’t think an agreement will be made until they’re ‘punched in the face’ because there’s no ‘gun to our heads.’ But there is a gun,” said Skretting’s sustainability manager, Leif Kjetil Skjaeveland.

READ MORE
MAR 48:02 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Outlook for northeast Atlantic pelagics uncertain, especially if overfishing continues

The prognosis for stocks of mackerel, Norwegian spring-spawning herring, and blue whiting is highly uncertain, especially if the current overfishing continues, said Erling Kare Stenevik of Norway’s Insitute of Marine Research.

For herring, the spawning stock biomass (SSB) has dipped below the maximum sustainable yield Btrigger — the parameter in the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea’s management framework that triggers advice on reduced fishing mortality.

READ MORE
MAR 47:53 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Trump’s 25% tariffs on Canada will hit US salmon processing, says Cermaq CEO

US president Donald Trump’s 25% tariffs on Canada will hit its domestic salmon processors hard, especially those on the West Coast, Steven Rafferty, CEO of Cermaq Group, told Undercurrent News on the sidelines of NASF.

“They [West Coast US processors] are very dependent on the Canadian fish coming in, so Trump is causing a lot of stress to that sector.”

READ MORE
MAR 47:35 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Cargill warns fishermen suffer when feed firms stop buying blue whiting

Northeast Atlantic blue whiting lost its Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) in 2021, and the world’s aquaculture feed firms stopped sourcing it. 

“It wasn’t our intention, of course, but we know that hurt fishermen, before the FIP [fishery improvement project] started up [and buying recommenced],” said Dave Robb, group sustainability lead with Cargill.

READ MORE
MAR 47:35 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Lasers, submerged pens, zone-approach headline SalMar’s 2025 capex plans

Hakon Husby, head of investor relations at SalMar, said the firm’s two biggest investment focuses for 2025 are firmly rooted in the eternal battle against parasites: sea lice lasers and submerged pens.

“20% of our sites in Norway at the end of 2024 had preventative technology; at the end of 2025 we will be at 40%,” he said.

READ MORE
MAR 47:28 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
NEAFC coastal state meetings on pelagics sharing labeled ‘superficial’

Heidrun Lind Marteinsdottir, CEO of Fisheries Iceland, took the opportunity of her presentation at NASF to warn that meetings of the North East Atlantic Fisheries Commission (NEAFC) have, in her experience, been “superficial” at best.

She noted her experience, prior to the seafood industry, as a lawyer working extensively in dispute negotiations and said the NEAFC meetings in London, the UK — at which coastal states have been tasked with establishing a comprehensive sharing agreement for mackerel, Norwegian spring-spawning herring, and blue whiting quotas — lack the indicators of successful talks.

READ MORE
MAR 47:13 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Cermaq: Norway still clear center of salmon investment as sector faces key election year

Three years on from an NASF presentation by Cermaq Group CEO Steven Rafferty bemoaning growth-restricting measures taken by Chilean and Canadian politicians, head of strategy Harald Takle stressed once again that the international group’s investments remain firmly focused in Norway, despite the resource tax and additional regulations introduced since then.

“Norway still has national growth ambitions — that is very important,” he said. “I’m very hopeful and believe that in a couple of years we will be back on track when it comes to reasonable regulations and predictability.”

READ MORE

Contact the authors neil.ramsden@undercurrentnews.com, dan.gibson@undercurrentnews.com, tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com

title: 2025 Norway-UK Seafood Summit: UK adapts to record cod prices; Norway salmon biomass spike worth watching
content:
Undercurrent News was reporting live from the 2025 Norway-UK Seafood Summit in London, UK, on Feb. 25.

The Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC)-organized event is held annually, and this year, the latest "megatrends," supply, and trade outlooks for salmon, whitefish and coldwater shrimp were on the itinerary.

Recap all the updates below.

Auto updates: On
FEB 251:58 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Ode believes farmed cod volumes will offset wild supply decline in long-term

Increasing volumes of farmed cod can offset declines in wild supply over the coming couple of decades, Norwegian aquaculture firm Ode estimates.

Cathrin Rabben, sales manager with Ode, presented the slide below, which looks ahead to cod supply in 2050.

READ MORE
FEB 251:09 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Barents Sea shrimp MSC should be safe for another year

The Barents Sea coldwater shrimp Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) certificate should be safe in place until next year, said Tor Bjorklund Larsen, senior adviser with the Norwegian Fishermen’s Organisation.

“There have been rumors that the fishery’s certificate could be lost due to delays in achieving MSC conditions about harvest control rules,” said Larsen. 

READ MORE
FEB 2511:42 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Norwegian cod exports show resilience as UK market adapts to high prices

The UK’s fish and chip shops are adapting their business models amid rising cod prices, with higher Norwegian exports in January suggesting resilient demand.

During an afternoon panel, Johan Oksholen, sales manager at Nor Seafoods, said Norway’s frozen cod and haddock exports to the UK were up in January by 14-15% compared with last year, suggesting the sector is absorbing higher fish prices.

READ MORE
FEB 2510:39 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Hilton seeing increased sales of coldwater shrimp, but ‘premiumization’

Hilton Foods Seachill — part of Hilton Food Group — has seen UK sales of coldwater shrimp growing, “certainly in the past five years,” but with the segment also experiencing “premiumization,” said the firm’s head of seafood purchasing and strategic sourcing, Nicola Hunter.

That premiumization means the UK retail market is leaning towards older generations of buyers with a preference for single-frozen shrimp, she said; “a supply that’s coming under increasing pressure.”

READ MORE
FEB 2510:08 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Trade deal timing set to benefit Norway’s shrimp sales

The timing of the EEA EFTA-UK free trade agreement has proved a great opportunity for Norway’s sales of cooked and peeled coldwater shrimp, noted Josefine Voraa, seafood analyst with the Norwegian Seafood Council.

The UK gained free trade with the groups — collecting Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland and Norway — in 2023. It meant the UK could import tariff-free cooked and peeled shrimp from those countries from that year, and can import shell-on shrimp duty-free from this year.

READ MORE
FEB 259:27 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Cod recruitment in Barents Sea ‘not a complete failure’

Cod recruitment in the Barents Sea “isn’t a complete failure”, meaning stocks should stabilize and possibly recover in the future, according to Daniel Howell, a researcher at the Institute of Marine Research.

“Recruitment for cod and haddock has been lowish, but not disastrous. You do see recruitment failure in some fisheries and stocks go way down, but that’s not what we’re seeing,” said the researcher.

READ MORE
FEB 258:57 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
‘Salmon’ could broaden as a category as demand outstrips supply

The term “salmon” could broaden to cover additional salmonids as global market demand continues to outstrip supply, suggested DNB’s Dag Sletmo, asked for a forward-looking prediction. 

“We’re not going to see new countries enter the field of salmon farming in the sea — of course, it’s dictated by seawater temperatures,” he said. “However, I think we could see the term ‘salmon’ widening to allow more flexibility and adaptation in supply and demand.”

READ MORE
FEB 258:22 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Analyst: Norway spike in salmon biomass won’t mean supply surge, but worth watching

Norway saw a year-on-year leap in farmed salmon biomass in January, which is worth keeping an eye on, said Dag Sletmo of DNB Seafood.

“That 9% increase is significant,” he said. “Will it mean a wall of salmon hitting the market imminently? No, because we’re talking young fish, and they remain subject to the restraints of licenses. But it’s worth watching — it’s a data point I thought was very interesting.”

READ MORE
FEB 258:07 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Cod industry facing ‘historic’ supply challenge

It’s a well-known fact that the cod industry is in peril, with prices soaring amid a drop in quotas. But that doesn’t stop analysts from taking every opportunity to explain how dire the situation truly is.

According to Eivind Hestvik Braekkan, seafood analyst at the Norwegian Seafood Council, this year’s cod supply will be “the lowest since records began.” That takes the industry back to 1950, according to Braekkan, when fishing vessels were primarily wooden.

READ MORE
FEB 257:49 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Norwegian ambassador feels bilateral relationship with UK ‘stronger than ever’

Norway and the UK’s bilateral relationship has never been stronger, according to Tore Hattrem, ambassador of Norway to the United Kingdom, welcoming delegates to the summit.

Going “off script” at the end of his speech, he said the strength of Norway’s relations with the UK were important given the uncertainty around the US’ relationship with Europe.

READ MORE
FEB 257:35 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
NSC ‘megatrends’ report to guide through ‘challenging times’

The fifth ‘Megatrends’ report from the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC) debuted at this year’s Norway-UK Seafood Summit, offering guidance for seafood industry navigation through “challenging times.”

The report highlights the top megatrends “underlying the noticeable trends we can identify day-to-day, but we don’t understand the cause of,” said NSC consumer analyst Lars Moksness.

READ MORE

title: GSMC 2025: Stable-priced pollock offers best value against other proteins; Santa Monica CEO: Tariff impact ‘overblown’
content:
PALM SPRINGS, California, US – Undercurrent News is reporting live from the Global Seafood Market Conference (GSMC), held annually in the US in January and organized by the National Fisheries Institute (NFI).

NFI's 2025 GSMC is in Palm Springs, California, in the JW Marriott Desert Springs Resort & Spa (pictured above) – with the inauguration of Donald Trump in his second term as US president set to be a big talking point.

Six of Undercurrent's reporting team are at the conference to give you live coverage over the week.  

Keep clicking back for all the news from GSMC from Undercurrent. Also, if you'd also like to learn more about Undercurrent's new US wholesale pricing and trade platforms, get in touch here.

In addition, Undercurrent has just launched a new weekly podcast, "Catch the Current," which you can read more about here.

Auto updates: On
JAN 2411:04 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Santa Monica CEO feels possible tariff impact ‘overblown,’ backs Trump to improve US economy

Santa Monica Seafood’s CEO Roger O’Brien backs new US president Donald Trump to improve the country’s economy, with his only “worry” the possible tariffs on key trading partners Canada, China and Mexico.

“I think Trump’s going to improve the economy. I truly do,” O’Brien told Undercurrent News on the sidelines of the GSMC.

READ MORE
JAN 2311:13 PM GMT
By Lorin Castiglione
Need for sourcing flexibility emphasized on salmon, scallop sessions 

Across both the shellfish and salmon panels at GSMC, a clear message emerged: in a market facing tight supplies, strong consumer demand, and ongoing tariff uncertainties, flexibility is key. 

Members from the shellfish panel introduced and drove home the word ‘optionality’ and the need for buyers to be flexible on sizing and origins as the markets face some headwinds in availability.

READ MORE
JAN 239:29 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
More US tariffs on China tilapia could drive demand for Vietnamese pangasius

The possibility of US president Donald Trump adding additional tariffs to Chinese tilapia, on top of the 25% in place already, could be a driver for demand for Vietnamese pangasius fillets.

Tilapia prices have been rising anyway, due to higher feed costs in China, said Ron Risher of Grobest Seafood Global on the GSMC whitefish panel.

READ MORE
JAN 238:59 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
High Liner sees ‘challenges’ coming on US cod demand as higher prices hit market

The rapid increase in raw material prices seen on cod, especially Atlantic, are just hitting the market, said Paul Jewer, CEO of Canada-based processor High Liner Foods.

“With these price increases, it’s economics 101; there will be some challenges on the demand side. The increases are now making their way to the market. We will see what happens,” said Jewer, on the GSMC whitefish panel on Thursday, Jan. 23.

READ MORE
JAN 238:47 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Whitefish panel predicts stable PBO pollock prices as surimi struggles continue

Demand for US pin-bone out (PBO) pollock fillets looks set to remain strong in 2025, with prices likely to be stable, according to executives on the GSMC whitefish panel.

“There has been a lift in PBO demand in Europe and the US, driven by Ukraine situation,” said one executive with a large supplier on the GSMC whitefish panel. Direct and indirect imports of Russian pollock are now both banned in the US. 

READ MORE
JAN 2312:37 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Pollock offers best value competing against other proteins

Significant increases in PBO fillets of pollock could provide growth opportunities at retail, the species panel on whitefish told GSMC attendees Thursday (Jan. 23) morning. 

Pollock production in the US has been steady overall. However, when you break down the production by product, 2024 saw a decline of 12.6% for surimi. Deep-skinned fillet production also declined in 2024, down 23.4% year-on-year. However, when it comes to PBO filllets, production increased by 27.4%, reaching 270.3 million pounds in 2024.

READ MORE
JAN 2312:12 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Tilapia loses ground in US markets as global production rises

Global producers of farm-raised tilapia are producing higher volumes but the US market is becoming weaker for major exporters, particularly China.

“We’re producing more tilapia in the world, but the US is taking less and less tilapia overall,” said Urner Barry price analyst Angel Rubio.

READ MORE
JAN 239:18 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
US whitefish buyers keep eye on possible Russian return with H&G prices set high

US whitefish buyers are keeping at least one eye on the possible return of Russian fish to the market in 2025, which would relieve the record-high prices for cod and haddock, sources at GSMC told Undercurrent News.

What moves US president Donald Trump will make on trade is a major talking point at the GSMC conference. 

READ MORE
JAN 239:09 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Blumar adds two new US salmon skin-pack customers, sees demand growing on frozen for re-fresh

Chile’s Blumar has added two new retailers to its US salmon skin-pack program, the company’s Daniel Montoya told Undercurrent News during the GSMC conference.

The two new skin-pack customers are additional to the two the company already services from its BluGlacier plant in Miami, Florida, which is a joint venture with Productos del Mar Ventisquero, he said.

READ MORE
JAN 232:36 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Norway’s Ode to start sales of fresh pre-rigor farmed cod fillets for global sushi markets

Norwegian cod farmer Ode is installing equipment in its processing plant to produce and deliver pre-rigor fresh fillets in Q1 this year, said Cathrin Rabben, a sales manager who has been part of the company since its establishment.

“We are running tests and starting up the line at the moment. Pre-rigor fillets will hit the market in Q1, and live chilling functionality will follow in Q2. We plan to target the Asian, EU and US sushi and sashimi markets with the fillets,” she told Undercurrent News on the sidelines of the GSMC.

READ MORE
JAN 228:36 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
C-Store exec shares what the seafood industry needs to do to penetrate the convenience store category

GSMC panelist Michael Seidel of Performance Food Group asked attendees the following question during the day’s final panel on Wednesday (Jan. 22): “Can we sell seafood to the C-store?” 

Convenience stores are not necessarily the first place you think of going when you want to eat seafood, but then again, convenience stores have greatly evolved over the years. While C-stores used to be a place for just gasoline and a soda, today’s convenience stores have started to develop physical restaurant spaces to attract even more customers.

READ MORE
JAN 227:16 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
‘It’s hard to catch lightning in a bottle’ — seafood competes in crowded field to meet US consumers’ demand for healthy protein

The global seafood market is aligned with trends seen in the food industry where consumer demand is focused on increasing protein consumption in convenient settings such as fast-food restaurants or ready-made meals.

“Protein is the number one nutrient the American consumer says they want to add more of in their diet — bar none,” said David Portalatin, Circana’s industry advisor for food and foodservice. 

READ MORE
JAN 226:40 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
US supply of North American lobster stable despite volatile appearance, panel stresses

It’s easy to get the impression that the US’ supply of North American lobster is shrinking and volatile if you look at any one of the charts used to measure each of the Canadian and US sources separately, advised the NFI shellfish panel during a session on Tuesday (Jan. 21).

For example, the harvest in Maine peaked at 130 million pounds in 2016 but it hasn’t reached that level since and shrunk to about 90m lbs in 2022. In 2023, Maine – which accounts for roughly 90% of US lobster landings – saw a harvest of 93.7m lbs worth $464.4m.

READ MORE
JAN 225:48 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Riverence Provisions founder David E. Kelley talks importance of passion in the industry 

GSMC keynote speaker David E. Kelley, the founder of Riverence Provisions, the largest producer of trout in North America, took the stage Wednesday (Jan. 22) afternoon to share the importance of having passion.

“Passion is not something you can substitute in any job,” Kelley told GSMC attendees.

READ MORE
JAN 221:07 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Canadian salmon supplier warns US consumer will pay if Trump tariff threat materializes 

Like the GSMC panels before it, the species panel on salmon could not ignore the elephant in the room—US president Donald Trump’s looming tariff threats.

Recall that Trump, leading up to his inauguration on Monday (Jan. 20), called for a 25% tariff on imports from Canada and Mexico, and additional tariffs for other countries. 

READ MORE
JAN 2212:03 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Norwegian salmon makes inroads into US with small sizing, competitive prices

More Norwegian salmon will likely be exported to the US in 2025 as early harvesting continues to avoid biological issues, said GSMC panelists on Tuesday, Jan. 22.

Norway is making more inroads into the US market, based on smaller sizing and comparable pricing to Chile, said executives on the salmon panel.

READ MORE
JAN 2211:49 AM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
Global salmon supply down 12% largely driven by declines in wild fish

The planet’s salmon supply shrank in 2024 largely due to crashing pink and chum salmon from wild fisheries in Alaska and elsewhere.

“Pink salmon was down 25% globally, and 44% in Alaska for the last even year,” Richard Barry of the National Fisheries Institute said Wednesday. 

READ MORE
JAN 2211:41 AM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
GSMC salmon panel sees opportunity for Chilean coho in 2025

The species panel on salmon at GSMC believes there are opportunities for Chilean coho in 2025.

A panelist with a large US processor told conference attendees Wednesday (Jan. 22) morning that Chilean coho’s popularity has been rising in recent years. 

READ MORE
JAN 2211:34 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
‘Upward pressure’ on Canadian snow crab prices amid supply, trade uncertainty

There is “upward pressure” on snow crab pricing ahead of the Canadian harvesting seasons, where supply is expected to come down, said Roman Tkachenko, CEO of US importer Direct Source Seafood.

“We’re into the $8s [$8/lb] on 5-8s [oz clusters], and it remains to be seen where it goes,” but the signs are there of increases, said Tkachenko on the GSMC shellfish panel on Tuesday (Jan. 21).

READ MORE
JAN 2111:44 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Key to 2025 scallop market is ‘flexibility,’ ‘optionality,’ panel agrees

The challenges that confronted the US scallop sector in 2024 look to continue and even escalate in the new year, advised the shellfish panel at GSMC 2025 on Tuesday (Jan. 21). The key for suppliers and buyers will be both “flexibility” and “optionality,” panel members agreed.

They need to be flexible in considering smaller sizes and practice optionality in considering imported scallops.

READ MORE
JAN 218:39 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
ASMI’s Jeremy Woodrow tells GSMC to get your ‘tariff-free crab while you can’

Alaska is back to fishing crab again … “finally,” Jeremy Woodrow, executive director of the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute (ASMI), told GSMC attendees during the species panel on shellfish.

Panel moderator Janice Schreiber, editor at Urner Barry by Expana, “phoned a friend” when the conversation turned to king crab. Woodrow took the microphone to share an update out of Alaska.

READ MORE
JAN 218:02 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Opportunity for diversification of blue swimming crab meat as tariff threat looms

The pricing gap between blue swimming crab and red swimming crab is shortening, Troy Turkin, chief operating officer at Supreme Crab & Seafood, told the GSMC audience during the species panel on shellfish.

According to Turkin, the price of crab meat continues to be expensive, but the gap in price between red and blue swimming crab is closer to historical levels. Of course, the looming threat of tariffs will still play an impact, Turkin noted.

READ MORE
JAN 217:33 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Major US retailer Publix says Ecuador shrimp has edge over Asia

Guy Pizzuti, seafood director with US retailer Publix Super Markets, sees Ecuador shrimp as the preferable option over Asian.

“I do personally feel they produce a better shrimp,” said Pizzuti of Ecuador.

READ MORE
JAN 217:31 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
GSMC Ecuador shrimp panelist disagrees 2025 output will drop

GSMC’s shrimp panel presented a slight increase in 2025 vannamei production to 5.06 million metric tons but a drop in Ecuador to 1.35m metric tons.

The production forecast is based on numbers supplied by Robins McIntosh of Charoen Pokphand Foods, which Undercurrent News also covered on Monday. McIntosh gave Undercurrent a revised number for China down to 1.14m metric tons, taking the total below 5m metric tons.

READ MORE
JAN 217:21 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
USDA’s $25m contract for gulf shrimp will impact price of domestic product

Patrick Kraver, vice president and general manager of Fortune Fish & Gourmet, told attendees during the GSMC species panel on shrimp that domestic shrimp prices will likely continue to go up as a result of the US Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) latest purchase contract for gulf shrimp.

Recall that earlier this month, a Section 32 purchase was announced by the USDA for $25 million in gulf shrimp for distribution to various nutrition assistance programs, as well as charitable institutions. 

READ MORE
JAN 216:24 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Ecuador shrimp expert says industry needs time to grow into value-added products

Gabriel Luna, founder of Gluna Shrimp and the co-founder of the Global Shrimp Council, told GSMC attendees Tuesday (Jan. 21) afternoon that Ecuador’s shrimp industry needs more time to grow into value-added products.

Luna was part of a GSMC species panel on shrimp, sharing the stage with NFI’s Richard Barry, Jamie Marshall of AZ Gems, Patrick Kraver of Fortune Fish, and Guy Pizzuti of Publix grocery store. 

READ MORE
JAN 216:24 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
NFI panel: Tariffs among Trump’s tools as ‘a good negotiator’

How serious is newly re-elected US president Donald Trump about the tariffs of up to 25% that he’s threatened to levy against imports, including seafood, from Canada and Mexico? 

That was the question burning in the minds of many attendees of an afternoon panel session Tuesday and asked by Ian Smith, the CEO of Canada’s Clearwater Seafoods, during the Q&A part of the discussion. 

READ MORE
JAN 212:34 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Rabobank: Trump’s tariffs can make sense ‘in some instances’

Ahead of a GSMC panel titled “Trump 2.0: Trade, Tax & Investment Policy in The New Administration,” Rabobank senior market strategist Christian Lawrence previewed how tariffs will impact the US economy and seafood industry.

“Tariffs can, in some instances, make sense,” Lawrence told GSMC attendees. “They can be good for the economy.”

READ MORE
JAN 212:25 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
FMI survey: 44% of US consumers prefer wild seafood over farm-raised products

Nearly half of the 2,000 consumers surveyed by FMI – The Food Market Institute, said they preferred wild-caught seafood, while 22% preferred farm-raised products and 37% had no preference.

Of those who prefer wild-caught, 70% said they buy wild seafood exclusively and avoid farm-raised products.

READ MORE
JAN 212:04 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
US consumers: Seafood still seen as more expensive meal option

US shoppers continue to see seafood as a “luxury indulgence” and regular consumers feel it’s a more expensive option for the protein in their diet. But that’s not scaring them away as it’s seen as a healthy option.

“Even among those who are frequent seafood consumers, 73% there feel that it is expensive,” said Steve Markenson, vice president of research for FMI – The Food Industry Association. 

READ MORE
JAN 211:55 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Seafood sees win in prepared foods with deli sushi

It’s all about convenience, Chris DuBois, executive vice president at data and research company Circana, told GSMC attendees during his presentation on finding new directions for growth in seafood. 

As noted by DuBois, the US economy has continued to grow, but the seafood industry still has challenges ahead as 94% of all households are concerned about food cost inflation. However, a place for growth in the seafood category can be found when looking at convenience and prepared foods. 

READ MORE
JAN 211:31 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Opportunity for canned seafood in the premium space

Canned shelf-stable seafood is down 14.3% in volume sales when compared to four years ago, according to Chris DuBois, executive vice president at data and research company Circana. But that doesn’t necessarily mean that canned seafood sales will continue to keep going down.

DuBois told NFI GSMC attendees in his presentation on finding new directions for growth in seafood that high-end products are increasing in sales thanks to keto diets and the willingness to experiment with food thanks to viral videos on social media. He gave the example of canned sardines, which saw a growth of 9% versus four years ago.

READ MORE
JAN 211:22 PM GMT
By Jacob Resneck
US retail market cases: Refrigerated finfish is rising while shellfish struggles

Refrigerated cod, pollock and salmon and prepared sushi have been the major growth drivers in the US retail seafood market that’s seen a 3% decrease over the past four years.

That’s according to Chris DuBois, protein practice leader at Circana, delivering his 2024 State of the Industry.

READ MORE
JAN 211:22 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Alaskan Leader’s miso black cod ‘selling off the charts,’ says Circana’s DeBois

Alaskan Leader Seafoods’ miso black cod launch in US club store giant has seemingly been a great success.

Chris DuBois, executive vice president for protein with consumer sales data firm Circana, highlighted the product from the Pacific cod longline operator and sales company in his GSMC presentation.

READ MORE
JAN 211:08 PM GMT
By Amanda Buckle
Seafood sees growth at foodservice despite consumer concerns about food cost

Seafood did see growth in foodservice despite 94% of consumers being concerned about food cost inflation, according to Chris DuBois, executive vice president at data and research company Circana.

DuBois, while presenting on the 2024 state of the seafood industry at NFI’s GSMC on Tuesday, told attendees that while food sales remain shifted to food at home, seafood has seen some wins in the foodservice space.

READ MORE
JAN 2110:59 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chris Maze leaves Pescanova USA

Chris Maze has left the US arm of Spain’s Grupo Nueva Pescanova, sources told Undercurrent News during the GSMC.

Maze, who joined Miami, Florida-based Pescanova USA as CEO at the start of 2019, did not respond to a request for comment from Undercurrent.

READ MORE
JAN 2110:58 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Southwind adds another food sector big hitter to exec team

California, US-based Southwind Foods has added a food sector veteran to its team as chief operating officer (COO).

Southwind, which trades as Great American Seafood Imports Co. and has a turnover of around $600 million, appointed Jim Caltabiano as COO in December.

READ MORE
JAN 2012:49 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
UCN team in Palm Springs to talk new US wholesale pricing platform, podcast

Six of Undercurrent‘s reporting team are in Palm Springs this week to cover GSMC, but also work on and discuss our new US wholesale pricing platform and podcast.

In the past week, UCN has announced plans to initiate US wholesale pricing coverage of fresh and frozen Chilean salmon, as well as various crab species. Next up will be live lobster.

READ MORE
JAN 2012:44 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Major US seafood conference kicks off as Trump takes office

Much of the discussion at GSMC will be about the impact of Donald Trump’s second presidency on seafood trade.

Trump has promised to slap tariffs on trade with Canada and Mexico, two major US seafood suppliers, and increase the levels already in place on China.

READ MORE

Contact the authors tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, jason.huffman@undercurrentnews.com, amanda.buckle@undercurrentnews.com, jacob.resneck@undercurrentnews.com, gary.morrison@undercurrentnews.com, Lorin.Castiglione@undercurrentnews.com

title: ASMI meeting: Recap all the news out of Alaska
content:
ANCHORAGE, Alaska -- The annual Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute (ASMI) All Hands on Deck meeting is taking place, Dec. 3-5. 

To recap Undercurrent News' coverage of the ASMI All Hands from last year, click here.

Auto updates: On
DEC 58:18 AM GMT
Alaska Glacier Seafoods exec extolls virtues of ‘wonderfish’

ASMI’s halibut and sablefish producers are bullish on growing market potential for black cod but see rough waters ahead as Pacific halibut’s biomass continues due to poor recruitment.

Rock-bottom prices in Asia for black cod/sablefish have led to an expanding domestic market in both North America and Europe.

READ MORE
DEC 42:52 PM GMT
ASMI salmon committee braces for glut of pinks in 2025, eyes pollock playbook for mass-market appeal

Alaska’s seafood producers need to gear up for a potential glut of pink salmon in 2025. That was the message delivered by ASMI’s salmon committee at the Hotel Captain Cook on Wednesday.

“We’ve got a big run of pinks coming up, and we need to be proactive in how we handle those,” said veteran Bristol Bay fisherman Michael Jackson, also known as “MJ,” who chairs the committee.

READ MORE
DEC 42:14 PM GMT
Alaska’s whitefish producers eye new opportunities, traditional threats

Alaska’s whitefish producers say they see opportunities to sell more Pacific seafood in European markets ahead but warn that tariffs threatened by a second Trump administration and competition from Russia could mean headwinds for the troubled sector.

“We’re seeing in all the news articles the reduction in Atlantic cod,” said Frank O’Hara III, marketing manager of the O’Hara Corporation, a family-owned seafood producer that owns catcher/processor vessels that trawl in Alaska.

READ MORE
DEC 47:45 AM GMT
Strong demand for Alaska’s salmon roe in former Soviet, Eastern bloc nations

“Demand for Alaska salmon roe remains very high in Eastern Europe,” Nicole Alba, ASMI’s international marketing director, reported in a session on Tuesday.

A record high 2,300 metric tons (5.07 million pounds) valued at $27.4 million were exported to former Eastern bloc countries during the 2023-24 season, she said. That’s a 227% increase in volume and 146% increase in value year-over-year, she said.

READ MORE
DEC 36:29 PM GMT
Alaska fisheries ex-vessel values continued their slide in 2024

Ex-vessel values – the amounts paid to harvesters at the docks – have been slow to recover from 2023’s precipitous drop, a fisheries analyst told the ASMI conference on Monday.

“We can see 2024 prices haven’t recovered to 2022 levels, but also aren’t down across the board like in 2023,” Sam Friedman, a consultant with the McKinley Research Group, an Alaska-based firm that’s contracted to crunch fisheries price and volume data for ASMI told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
DEC 33:46 PM GMT
Panel: Alaska seafood markets slowly rebounding thanks to reputation

An industry panel on the state of the Alaska seafood market agreed that trends are improving this year but cautioned it’ll be a slow road to recovery after a disastrous downturn.

The outlook for the seafood retail sector is not as dire in late 2024 as it was a year ago, they said.

READ MORE
DEC 31:28 PM GMT
Analyst: Alaska seafood attractive to next generation of consumers

Alaska seafood is well-positioned to capitalize on the tastes of younger generation consumers, Circana vice president Chris DuBois, a fresh food analyst, said during a market overview at ASMI on Monday.

Pre-packaged seafood products like deli-case sushi are seeing growth. The Chicago-based analyst said his firm Circana‘s research finds Gen Z and Millennials eat at twice the rate of the average US household.

READ MORE
DEC 31:01 PM GMT
US senators Murkowski, Sullivan talk tough on buoying Alaska seafood sector

Lisa Murkowski, a frequent critic of president-elect Donald Trump, said she’s committed to getting to work with her colleagues in increasing support for Alaska’s seafood industry.

“It’s easy to get kind of caught up in the political rhetoric, but I’m just letting you know I’m ready to get to work,” she said via a recorded video address. 

READ MORE
DEC 312:29 PM GMT
ASMI chair: Increasing the value of Alaska seafood must be our ‘call to action’

ASMI board chair Allen Kimball says the US state’s beleaguered seafood industry’s “call to action” is to “increase the value and the demand for Alaska seafood globally.”

The industry is weathering a number of storms akin to the famed cold weather blast of a Williwaw-like storm that combined natural and human-caused events that’s seen an estimated $1.8 billion loss in direct revenue between 2022 and 2023, he said.

READ MORE
DEC 39:48 AM GMT
Alaska must fill $450m ‘hole’ in US market left by Russian ban, or others will

Jeremy Woodrow, executive director of ASMI, issued a rallying call for the US state’s seafood companies to fill the large market hole left by the Russian ban or others will.

“As challenging as the current market is, we do have opportunities that we must capitalize on,” wrote Woodrow in a welcome letter for the ASMI All Hands on Deck conference, held Dec. 3-5 in Anchorage, Alaska. Click here for the letter in full.

READ MORE

Contact the author jacob.resneck@undercurrentnews.com

title: ICWPF 2024: Bornstein to focus on US market expansion after election outcome
content:
AMSTERDAM, Netherlands -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the International Coldwater Prawn Forum 2024.

As usual, the packed single-day event will encompass presentations ranging the full length of the value chain, from stock and fishing outlooks, sustainability issues, and AI in fisheries through to markets and marketing.

Undercurrent is the official media partner for the event. Keep checking back for our live coverage, below.

Auto updates: On
NOV 1411:28 AM GMT
Bornstein to focus on US market expansion after election outcome

The US election result has prompted Washington-based Bornstein Seafoods to address the fact that it has allowed the domestic market to go under-utilized, said vice president of sales Kevin Larsen.

“The election result is going to mean challenges, we think, and most of all, uncertainty. Tariffs look likely to be the main change.”

READ MORE
NOV 148:29 AM GMT
Norway’s Stella Polaris pushing to study nuclear-powered fishing vessels

Norwegian shrimp processor and exporter Stella Polaris is pushing to pave the way for a feasibility study into nuclear power for fishing vessels, said the firm’s Jaran Rauo.

“We’ve been asking the government and some research institutions to allow for a study on this — it’s not as radical as it sounds,” he promised.

READ MORE
NOV 148:17 AM GMT
Bluewild opens marketing division, aims to create new coldwater shrimp category

Norwegian fishing firm Bluewild — most famous these days for its groundbreaking vessel Ecofive — has opened a sales and marketing department and aims to change how the coldwater shrimp category operates.

“We are just two guys, so be patient with us,” joked Carl Johan Pettersen, who joined Bluewild as sales director in the summer of 2024. “But we can say Bluewild is now a seafood company, not just a fishing company.”

READ MORE
NOV 147:36 AM GMT
World grows increasingly reliant on China to take cooked, shell-on shrimp

Global coldwater shrimp exporters are becoming increasingly reliant on China to purchase frozen, cooked, shell-on products, said the Norwegian Seafood Council’s Josefine Voraa.

China’s imports of coldwater shrimp jumped towards 70,000 metric tons in 2022 and barely eased in 2023, mostly supplied by Denmark/ Greenland and Canada.

READ MORE
NOV 146:20 AM GMT
Global Shrimp Council extends invitation to coldwater prawn sector

Marketing group the Global Shrimp Council has extended an open invitation to the coldwater prawn sector for a representative to join its board, said Melanie Siggs, a director of the Global Seafood Alliance.

You can read more about this here, when Miguel Barcenas — a veteran marketing consultant and the creator of the well-known “Avocados from Mexico” campaign — spoke about this at the Global Shrimp Forum in September. 

READ MORE
NOV 146:00 AM GMT
Argentine offshore shrimp fishery to enter MSC assessment early in 2025

Argentina’s offshore fishery for shrimp (Pleoticus muelleri) should enter full assessment for Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) certification early in 2025, said Federico Angeleri, CEO of Grupo Veraz.

“We began two FIPs [fishery improvement projects] in 2015, one for the inshore future and the other for the offshore future. I was one of the leaders of the project, so I suffered a lot, to be honest,” said Angeleri.

READ MORE
NOV 145:02 AM GMT
NMFS to sunset US West Coast jordani observer program

The National Marine Fishery Service (NMFS) is set to sunset the observer program on vessels catching pandalus jordani on the US West Coast, said Nick Edwards of the Shrimp Producers Marketing Cooperative.

Until now, Oregon and Washington have had observer coverage under which each vessel carries an observer for one month of the season to record by-catch and separate species by category.

READ MORE
NOV 144:25 AM GMT
2024 estimates suggest Norway has landed more shrimp than Canada for first time since 2010

The booming Barents Sea coldwater shrimp fishery has seen Norwegian landings roughly double since 2020, according to the ICWPF’s 2024 estimate.

Norwegian ladings have risen from 16,000 metric tons in 2014 to 36,000t in 2020 and an estimated 72,000t in 2024.

READ MORE
NOV 144:07 AM GMT
Still 40,000t catch decline to come in western Atlantic

Based on modeling, fisheries scientist Carsten Hvingel — now of DTU Aqua in Denmark — believes the western Atlantic coldwater shrimp fisheries are still to see a decline in catches of around 40,000 metric tons.

Canada’s fisheries have been trending down over the past years, and currently, Greenland’s are too. Greenland looks set to bear the brunt of a predicted further 20% dip in shrimp catches as we move towards 2030, said Hvingel.

READ MORE
NOV 143:19 AM GMT
‘Don’t let coldwater prawns drown in the sea of shrimp’

Talks continue around how to differentiate coldwater shrimp in the vast global market for various shrimp species, said Christian Nordahl — CEO of Norwegian processor Stella Polaris and chair of the ICWPF.

In 2020, global shrimp production reached 8 million metric tons — 7.5m of which was farmed vannamei.

READ MORE

title: 2025 Shrimp Summit: Loc Tran aims for 100,000t from ambitious eco-farm project; India will comply with new EU antibiotic rules
content:
BALI, Indonesia -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the 2025 Shrimp Summit, held at the Grand Hyatt Bali hotel in Nusa Dua, Indonesia.

The summit, which runs June 23-25, is hosted by non-profit The Center for Responsible Seafood, led by former Global Seafood Alliance president and founder George Chamberlain. 

The annual event brings together many of Asia's most important shrimp sector representatives from production, market and conservation in a year that has seen the industry rocked by the threat of heavy new trade tariffs to the US.

Check back regularly for updates from the event.

Auto updates: On
JUN 252:26 AM GMT
Veteran scientist Akiyama presented with Lifetime Achievement award

Dean Akiyama, one of the shrimp industry’s longest-serving experts, was presented with the third Lifetime Achievement award from the Shrimp Summit.

Originally from Hawaii, Akiyama acted as the first aquaculture technical representative of the American Soybean Association in Singapore, providing newsletters, technical reports and workshops.

READ MORE
JUN 2411:48 PM GMT
Vietnam’s ShrimpVet chief aims for 100,000t from ambitious eco-farm project

Loc Tran, a well-known face in the shrimp sector as the founder and director of veterinary consultancy ShrimpVet, has big plans after branching out into running his own farm.

The project, EcoSeafood Group, is based in Vietnam’s Ca Mau province in the Mekong delta, where shrimp farms extend as far as the eye can see.

READ MORE
JUN 2411:28 PM GMT
Still room to easily double technified farm areas in Ecuador

The steady transformation of Ecuador from a low-density, extensive farming hub into the single biggest producer of shrimp by a significant distance is still far from over, according to representatives from the country.

Allan Cooper, director of strategy at service company Vitapro, said that as of the end of 2024, around 30-40% of the country’s available farmland has been ‘technified,’ using aerators, automated feeders and other digital management tools to increase stocking densities while mitigating stress on the shrimp to keep mortality rates low.

READ MORE
JUN 2410:27 PM GMT
India will comply with new EU antibiotic rules, but repeats call for lower sampling rate

Shanmuganathan Kandan, aquaculture director at India’s Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA), spoke on behalf of the country regarding its response to the new EU rules on antibiotic use.

“We are very positive that we will comply with the EU standards,” he said. “Our minister of farmers has taken up steps with the commission, and this list (see below), how it can be addressed, and we can assure that India will definitely comply.”

READ MORE
JUN 2410:10 PM GMT
Looming antibiotic health crisis underscores need for latest EU crackdown

While not as publicly visible as climate change or rising global conflict, antibiotic resistance is a looming health crisis that at current rates will kill more people than cancer globally by 2050, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

Speaking on the Shrimp Summit’s antibiotic residue panel, Matthew Mitchell, cofounder and CTO of US bacteriocin startup Organicin Scientific, noted the role aquaculture plays in the crisis.

READ MORE
JUN 249:49 PM GMT
EU residue approval list will be renewed before September 2026 deadline

Hans Joostens, the head of the trade and economic section at the EU’s Indonesian delegation, confirmed to the summit that the existing list for countries approved to export to the EU from Sept. 3, 2026, will be revised before this deadline.

The EU’s current list of countries whose governments have provided “sufficient evidence and guarantees” regarding antibiotic prevention was released earlier this year. India and Indonesia were notably absent, and if not changed they will be unable to export shrimp to the EU after next year’s deadline.

READ MORE
JUN 2412:13 AM GMT
Yen depreciation starts to weigh on shrimp consumption in Japan, says Maruha Nichiro

While Japan was one of the faster growing shrimp consumption markets last year — up 11% y-o-y according to Kontali — crippling exchange rates are starting to weigh heavily on demand this year, according to Maruha Nichiro’s Kotaro Mori.

“There was a 40% depreciation in the exchange rate between Japanese yen and USD in the past few years,” Mori told listeners. “Last year, the offer when we buy from Southeast Asian suppliers in USD was pretty reasonable, but since our own currency depreciated so much, we had to consider that into our price strategy.”

READ MORE
JUN 2311:26 PM GMT
Innovation award winner Dalan aims to bring white spot vaccine to farmers by 2028

Dalan Animal Health, a US company that gained international recognition for creating the world’s first insect vaccine with honeybees is now looking to make a splash in the shrimp industry, CEO Annette Kleiser announced.

The company is currently conducting clinical trials on its fist vaccine against white spot syndrome, one of the chief menaces of Asian shrimp production — especially in India — and hopes to bring a commercial product to market for 2028, Kleiser said.

READ MORE
JUN 2310:34 PM GMT
Antibiotic alternative promises to ‘pop vibrio like a balloon’

At a time when the EU is cracking down hard on antibiotic residues in farmed shrimp exports, the US startup Organicin Scientific has chosen an auspicious time to enter the shrimp sector.

Matthew Mitchell, co-founder and CTO of Organicin, explained that the company offers what’s known as a bacteriocin to combat pathogens on shrimp farms.

READ MORE
JUN 239:51 PM GMT
Nutrition key to removing link between fast growth and high mortality

As is tradition, Robins McIntosh, executive vice president at Thailand’s Charoen Pokphand Foods, was on hand to answer some of the biggest questions surrounding broodstock.

“Why does the fast growth die, but the slower growth doesn’t?” he posed, referring to CP Foods’ two signature vannamei broodstock lines, the fast growing CP Turbo and the more robust CP Kong (see below).

READ MORE
JUN 232:07 PM GMT
Shrimp now far from ‘endless’ at Red Lobster

Over at US foodservice chain Red Lobster Management, days of bottomless shrimp offerings are fast becoming a thing of the past.

Indeed, ever since the Liberaton Day tariff announcement, discussion at the firm has turned to focus squarely on mitigating its shrimp exposure as much as possible.

READ MORE
JUN 231:51 PM GMT
Don’t expect final reciprocal tariffs to be aimed solely at China, NFI counsel warns

Addressing the room full of Indonesian shrimp sector representatives, US National Fisheries Institute general counsel and executive vice president Robert DeHaan poured cold water on any hopes that reciprocal tariff threats from the Trump government are merely a negotiating tactic.

“It’s important for Indonesians and the Pacific Rim to understand that in a lot of the documents from the [US] administration, they talk about allies as much as they talk about our strategic rivals and enemies,” he said. 

READ MORE
JUN 231:30 PM GMT
US shrimp retail demand yet to drop but first tariff-impacted products starting to hit market

Eric Bloom, president of US wholesaler and trader Eastern Fish Company, outlined the industry’s fears that the new tariff rates will hit seafood consumption in the country, and hard.

To date, under the new 10% baseline tariff rate, this hasn’t really been felt yet, with seafood retail sales “stable” and in some cases growing compared to foodservice.

READ MORE
JUN 231:18 PM GMT
‘My job now is to watch Newsmax’ – US shrimp buyers stuck in tariff limbo

If responding to every shift in the new US tariff regime each day for three months has been a challenge for Undercurrent, it’s nothing compared to the living hell faced by the country’s seafood importers.

“Every single business day of my life since April 2 has been involved with this and the complexity of conversations just with customers to figure out how to make this work has been ridiculously disruptive,” said Travis Larkin, president and CEO of importer and wholesaler Seafood Exchange on this year’s one-note US market panel. 

READ MORE
JUN 2312:19 PM GMT
Average tariff rate on US shrimp imports to jump to 25% come July 9

Emphasizing the scale of the tariff threat posed to shrimp exporters, Ragnar Nystoyl, chief analyst at Kontali, said that just over 70% of all imported shrimp to the US will face a hike in tariffs if no extensions are agreed by the end of the 90-day ‘freeze’ on July 9.

Such is the burden faced by the biggest Asian producers, the effective average tariff rate across all imported shrimp into the country will become slightly over 25% overnight, he said.

READ MORE
JUN 2311:49 AM GMT
Indonesia looks to Japan, EU trade in move away from US dependence

Speaking on the Indonesian shrimp sector at the summit’s production panel, Hendi Efendy, head of international business development at aquaculture service company CP Prima, said the country has begun looking in earnest at diversifying shrimp sales away from the US.

More than any other producing nation save perhaps India, Indonesia relies heavily on US exports to absorb the roughly 360,000 metric tons of vannamei shrimp it produces annually.

READ MORE
JUN 2311:39 AM GMT
Domestic market ‘black box’, stocking spread behind Indian volume growth

Ravi Yellanki, managing director of Indian hatchery operator Vaisakhi Bio-Marine, said the growth of the country’s domestic market is going some way to explaining why Indian shrimp production estimates seem to differ from source to source these days.

“Every year we do a corporate review,” he told listeners. “In 2024 we expected 970,000 [metric] tons, whereas Erwin [Termaat from Kontali] showed 1.1 million [mt].”

READ MORE
JUN 233:38 AM GMT
US opening means 2025 could be first year that HOSO is less than half Ecuador’s shrimp exports

While Ecuador is looking at another year of double-digit volume growth in 2025 (below), this only tells half the story of what’s happening in the country, according to Omarsa CEO Sandro Coglitore.

As it stands, only 44% of Ecuador’s total vannamei exports year to date have been raw, head-on shell-on (HOSO), traditionally the mainstay product of the country, which means it’s on track to be under 50% for the first time on record.

READ MORE
JUN 232:46 AM GMT
Global shrimp production to grow another 6% in 2025 despite tariff headwinds

With the world’s single largest shrimp purchasing nation imposing sweeping reciprocal tariffs on four of the five largest producing countries in the world, you could be forgiven for thinking that farmed vannamei production would suffer this year.

The reality, according to analyst Erwin Termaat with Kontali, could not be further from the truth, as every major shrimp producer is expecting significant year-on-year volume growth.

READ MORE
JUN 231:39 AM GMT
NFI legal counsel believes US must grant tariff extension to countries ‘talking in good faith’

Robert DeHaan, executive vice president and general counsel of the US National Fisheries Institute (NFI), gave his outlook on the upcoming tariff deadline of July 9, when the high reciprocal tariffs first introduced by the US government on April 2 are due to kick back in again following a 90-day pause.

Many international governments have been in negotiation with the US since then, but very few formal deals have been made, especially between the US and Asia’s largest shrimp producers in India, China, Vietnam and Indonesia.

READ MORE
JUN 229:59 PM GMT
Indonesian fishery exports grew to nearly $6bn last year

Opening the summit, Tornanda Syaifullah, the Indonesian fisheries ministry’s director general of product competitiveness, detailed how the country’s fisheries exports increased in value by 5.7% last year, to $5.95 billion.

This exceeded Indonesia’s total annual export growth rate of just 3.7% on average since 2020.

READ MORE
JUN 229:28 PM GMT
2025 event to feature first-ever antibiotic residue session as EU ban approaches

Opening the 2025 Shrimp Summit, George Chamberlain noted that the third day will feature a first-ever session on managing antibiotic residues on farms.

While it has always been a bone of contention between the EU and Asian farmed shrimp producers, new regulations set to come into force next year have pushed residues to the top of the agenda.

READ MORE
