title: IISS 2025: Full impact of US tariff on Indian shrimp prices won’t hit until December
content:
DELHI, India -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the biennial India International Seafood Show (IISS), held this year at the Bharat Mandapam center in the country's capital, New Delhi.

This year's edition of the trade show has been organized by the Seafood Export Association of India (SEAI) as part of the larger World Food India show taking place at the same venue.

The event comes at a challenging time for the country's seafood sector, reeling from the imposition one month ago of additional 50% trade tariffs on goods shipped to its largest single trading partner, the US.

Check back each day for updates from the show floor.

Auto updates: On
SEP 2912:32 AM GMT
Full impact of US tariffs not likely to hit Indian farmgate prices until December

While there was an initial downturn in Andhra Pradesh vannamei shrimp farmgate prices after the imposition of the initial 25% tariff at the start of August, eagle-eyed users of Undercurrent‘s prices portal will have noticed that prices out of India have been steadily creeping up since then.

The market is currently in an offseason, with most of the second crop of the year to be harvested in October and early November, according to a source with an integrated processor, who spoke to Undercurrent under conditions of anonymity.

READ MORE
SEP 2811:53 PM GMT
Choice Canning chases new markets to reduce US reliance

After opening its new processing factory in Bapatla, Andhra Pradesh, in May last year, Choice Canning Company now faces the challenge of ramping up production at the 200,000 square foot plant amid the most serious market crisis Indian shrimp exporters have seen in many years.

The firm is more exposed than most processors to the US tariffs, conducting nearly 88% of its trade to the country, according to factory manager James Joseph.

READ MORE
SEP 275:05 AM GMT
Indian gov’t project working with Hendrix to add indicus to farmed shrimp basket

India’s Central Institute for Brackish Aquaculture (ICAR-CIBA) is working with Hendrix Genetics on a selective breeding program for the indigenous Pennaeus indicus farmed shrimp, Undercurrent learned at the show. 

CIBA principal scientist KP Kumaraguru Vasagam said the breeding program has been in the works since February 2023, and will likely take another couple of years to come to fruition.

READ MORE
SEP 2611:37 AM GMT
Indian exporters looking to wait out US tariffs only able to hold shipments up to a month

When the full 50% additional tariff on Indian shrimp exports to the US first took effect on Aug. 26, many North American importers requested that Indian shipments be slowed down, according to an executive with a major processor who spoke to Undercurrent under condition of anonymity.

However, the maximum time that even the largest Indian firms are able to keep shrimp shipments in storage is around a month, he said.

READ MORE
SEP 2611:18 AM GMT
UK FTA driving demand for more certified shrimp farms in India, says Fedora

Having only begun processing operations in 2021, Nellore-based integrated shrimp processor Fedora Seafoods has thus far avoided the US, where the market is dominated by a handful of veteran players.

In contrast, the company, which exported 6,500 metric tons of finished products last year, has been focusing primarily on the UK, Japan and EU — incidentally now the most promising markets for Indian companies looking to diversify away from the US.

READ MORE
SEP 264:53 AM GMT
EU response to Indian gov’ts antibiotic paperwork expected shortly

A response from the EU to documents submitted by the Indian government to fulfil the bloc’s latest antibiotic requirements is expected within the next fortnight, according to SEAI president Pawan Kumar.

India is currently not on the list of permitted exporters to the EU under new regulations introduced this year demanding tighter enforcement of antibiotic bans from countries looking to sell to the continent.

READ MORE
SEP 2612:44 AM GMT
‘Good chance’ CVD relief could come before end of year, says SEAI chief

Speaking with Rajesh Agrawal, India’s chief tariff negotiator with the US, SEAI president Pawan Kumar said there was reason to believe that India’s current countervailing duties (CVD) to the US will be cut when the first review comes in December.

“There is a good chance the present countrvailing duty, which is 5.77%, can be brought down drastically to below 2%, which will help us in the future,” Kumar said.

READ MORE
SEP 2511:39 AM GMT
India needs national aquaculture land use policy to reach lofty targets

While the Indian government retains its goal of doubling seafood export values to $15 billion by 2030, the reality on the ground is that production of vannamei shrimp — by far its largest export product by value — has plateaued since COVID.

As is well-documented, 75% of India’s total shrimp output comes from private farms in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh.

READ MORE
SEP 2511:12 AM GMT
Indian shrimp industry at mercy of US trade deal

The bottom line of the aquaculture outlook panel at the show was that ultimately, India’s shrimp sector has little to no immediate recourse away from the US.

“With these tariffs, we face real trouble like never before,” said D. Ramraj, director of Chennai-based consultancy Padmanabha Labs. “There is talk about diversification and selling more to the domestic market, but that’s not going to happen overnight.”

READ MORE
SEP 2510:59 AM GMT
Avanti warns many farmers taking crop holidays with second harvest

It may come as a surprise to see farmgate shrimp prices out of India rising steadily since the full 50% tariff to the US came into effect, but the sector, which is between crops, is now facing a much weaker autumn harvest than had been expected.

“The impact of the tariff has been massive, and the farmers are the most impacted,” Avanti Frozen Foods sales manager Srikar Kodali told Undercurrent at the show.

READ MORE
SEP 253:20 AM GMT
Extra 25% is ‘too much’ for US shrimp importers to absorb as Indian trade grinds to standstill

While the initial import tariffs could to some degree be absorbed by US importers, the additional 25% duty on Indian exports added by president Trump on Aug. 26 have had a more severe impact on demand, according to SA Exports CEO Pervez Ahmed Khan.

Speaking to Undercurrent at the New Delhi show, West Bengal-based Khan said that since the new tariffs were introduced, shrimp trade to the US has “stalled.”

READ MORE
SEP 251:02 AM GMT
SEAI confirms US buyers among 15 countries attending show

In a release sent ahead of the trade show, the SEAI noted that buyers from 15 different countries had registered and would be present — including the US.

Representatives from the US were conspicuously absent from the list of buyers present at the Seafood Expo Bharat show organized by MPEDA earlier this year.

READ MORE
SEP 2512:45 AM GMT
Latest show result of SEAI split with MPEDA, sources say

While the India International Seafood Show is usually run as a combined effort by the country’s seafood industry, represented by the Seafood Exporters Association of India (SEAI) and the government’s Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA), this year has marked a split between the two bodies.

MPEDA held its own event in Chennai back in July, Seafood Expo Bharat, which it hopes will become an annual gathering of seafood sector members.

READ MORE

Contact the author dan.gibson@undercurrentnews.com

title: RASTECH 2025: Why small-scale RAS is gaining ground in a post-hype market
content:
SAN DIEGO, California, USA -- RASTECH, an international, two-day recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) conference and trade fair, kicked off Monday (June 9), and Undercurrent News is here to cover it live. 

The event, which brings together RAS producers, engineers, consultants, fish biologists and investors to explore the latest challenges and innovations in operations, science and technology, comes at a pivotal time for the industry. After years of headline-making announcements and investor enthusiasm, the sector is shifting into what insiders are calling a more disciplined second phase.

Undercurrent News recently reported that fewer than 25 land-based salmon farms remain active worldwide -- down from over 50 proposed projects just a few years ago. Still, new capital is flowing into ventures that can demonstrate credible scaling plans and cost discipline, sources say.

Follow this space for updates, interviews, and insights.

Auto updates: On
JUN 119:20 AM GMT
Why small-scale RAS is gaining ground in a post-hype market

Large-scale land-based salmon farms no longer dominated the conversation at RASTECH 2025, which concluded here on Tuesday (June 10).

Speakers and attendees pointed to a growing focus on smaller, modular RAS operations- newly launched and already in production- designed for local markets, varied species and financial viability at lower volumes.

READ MORE
JUN 101:51 PM GMT
Asia will remain aquaculture’s powerhouse, while Africa is rising, says land-based shrimp innovator

Farshad Shishehchian, a pioneer in the land-based shrimp farming sector, said India and Africa are shaping up to be the most promising regions for growth, while North America remains premature for meaningful development.

Shishehchian told Undercurrent News his outlook is informed by ongoing investments in emerging markets where conditions are favorable for scaling intensive shrimp production systems. 

READ MORE
JUN 1010:15 AM GMT
Tariff threats rekindle push for US-based salmon egg supply

The US market for Atlantic salmon eggs was considered too small to justify local production for years, but that assumption is starting to shift as the threat of tariffs and persistent biosecurity concerns prompt a fresh look at building domestic capacity.

That was the consensus among panelists at a day one session moderated by Yonathan Zohar of the University of Maryland’s Institute of Marine and Environmental Technology (IMET). 

READ MORE
JUN 93:49 PM GMT
SalmoGen hopes to break ground this fall on Maine-based Atlantic salmon egg facility for RAS market

SalmoGen, backed by Walton-family impact fund Cuna del Mar, hopes to break ground this fall on a 61,200-suare-foot Atlantic salmon egg production facility in Indian Island, Maine, general manager Nick King told attendees5.

King explained that SalmoGen’s breeding program is based on the St. John River strain of North American Atlantic salmon and uses genetic material from the USDA’s National Cold Water Marine Aquaculture Center.

READ MORE
JUN 92:15 PM GMT
American Unagi to expand production, launch kabayaki processing facility in Maine

Sarah Rademaker, CEO and founder of American Unagi (pictured below), is planning a major expansion that would boost production and add a dedicated kabayaki processing facility in Maine. 

The move is part of a broader push to capture a larger share of the US eel market and keep more of the supply chain domestic.

READ MORE
JUN 912:21 PM GMT
Fish farmer opens sushi bar to prove RAS model works

As many land-based aquaculture ventures chase scale, one startup is going in the opposite direction.

The UK- and Japan-based company ARK is betting on small, modular RAS units — and opened its own sushi restaurant to prove the model can work in high-end urban markets.

READ MORE
JUN 99:02 AM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Tracking the next chapter of land-based aquaculture at RASTECH 2025

The RAS sector is grappling with a new reality as RASTECH 2025 begins here today. Investors say they want to see working farms, not just working theories.

After a string of high-profile setbacks and missed production targets, the land-based salmon industry faces heightened scrutiny over whether RAS can deliver on its economic promises. Recent Undercurrent News reporting shows venture capital flowing to the sector has become more selective, with funders demanding clearer paths to profitability.

READ MORE

Contact the author liza.mayer@undercurrentnews.com

title: Aquaculture Canada 2025: Aquaculture industry sees need for smarter public engagement
content:
FREDERICTON, New Brunswick, Canada -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the Aquaculture Canada conference, hosted here by the Aquaculture Association of Canada, June 8-11.

The theme for this year's conference is 'Aquaculture is Agriculture.'

With aquaculture leaders from across Canada, the three-day event will feature presentations on developments in aquaculture science and technology, discussions on climate impacts on aquaculture, and regulatory challenges for the industry.

Check back regularly for updates from the conference.

Auto updates: On
JUN 1310:38 AM GMT
Aquaculture industry stresses need for smarter public engagement

Among the challenges faced by Canada’s fish farmers, the public perception of fish farming has been one of the most frustrating for the aquaculture industry to tackle.

At a panel discussion and question period moderated by Kaitlin Guitard, co-director of the Young Salmon Farmers of BC (YSFBC), industry leaders agreed that they need to rethink how they engage with the public.

READ MORE
JUN 1211:55 AM GMT
Atlantic Aqua Farms pursues solutions to MSX problem

As the oyster industry in Atlantic Canada continues to grapple with the challenge of the parasitic disease multinuclear sphere X (MSX), one Prince Edward Island-based company is hopeful federal agencies will give their blessing to use US seeds to build a stronger breed of oysters.

Atlantic Aqua Farms (AAF), which is among North America’s largest oyster and mussel producer, wants to use disease-resistant oysters developed by the Haskin Shellfish Research Laboratory at Rutgers University, in New Jersey, as brood stock to cross with native PEI oysters for a more resilient generation of animals.

READ MORE
JUN 121:14 AM GMT
Cooke CEO mum on whether Grieg acquisition on company radar

The Cooke family didn’t grow its single-pen, 5,000-fish salmon farm in New Brunswick, Canada, to the world’s largest privately-owned seafood business without some key acquisitions along the way.

Since 2010, the Canadian company, headed by CEO Glenn Cooke, has acquired at least one company every year, including major acquisitions like the purchase of US seafood processor Slade Gorton in 2023, and a $1.1 billion deal to acquire Australia’s largest salmon producer, Tassal Group, in 2022.

READ MORE
JUN 1212:40 AM GMT
Oyster seed bank growing at Prince Edward Island hatchery

A shellfish hatchery in the Canadian province of Prince Edward Island says it will have about 30 million oyster seeds available this year, to ensure farmers on the island can start new crops.

Oyster farmers on PEI would usually source their seed from the wild. However, the discovery of the oyster-killing parasitic disease multinuclear sphere X (MSX) in July, 2024, had brought rigid controls to prevent the spread of the disease. That means no wild seed is allowed at aquaculture sites.

READ MORE
JUN 1112:19 PM GMT
Cooke mulls cod farming again

Glenn Cooke admits he’s been watching with interest the recent developments in cod aquaculture in Norway, and he’s not ruling out the possibility that his company might add cod farming to its list of operations at some point.

“I’m very enthused with what we’re seeing in Norway as far as the growth of the cod farming industry,” the CEO of New Brunswick-based Cooke, the world’s largest privately-owned seafood company, told Undercurrent News on Tuesday (June 10).

READ MORE
JUN 116:34 AM GMT
Science built the industry, and science will save it, Cooke tells aquaculture convention

Science and innovation have helped propel the world’s largest privately held aquaculture company through its 40-year history, Cooke CEO Glenn Cooke told delegates at the Aquaculture Canada conference here on Tuesday (June 10).

“It’s incredible where technology has come, and we have embraced technology,” Cooke said during a fireside chat with Aquaculture Association of Canada president Cyr Courtuier, in front of about 350 conference delegates.

READ MORE
JUN 1011:18 AM GMT
Ocean science research needs more aquaculture-focused data, conference hears

Although scientists have a decade-long set of data about the ocean environment around Atlantic Canada, more research is needed to fill data gaps to determine how climate change in the region is impacting the aquaculture industry.

Canada’s Department of Fisheries and Oceans (DFO) has collected most of the historical ocean temperature data in Atlantic Canada. Still, most of that data is taken from offshore areas, Gregor Reid, director at the Center for Applied Marine Research (CAMR) in the province of Nova Scotia, told delegates during a Tuesday morning session on climate change.

READ MORE
JUN 93:47 PM GMT
Canadian company aims to prove algae, aquaculture can be good mix

Stan Pankratz believes he’s found a solution for a costly problem for recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). 

The president of Rainforest Algae, based in the Canadian province of Alberta, said algae could be the answer to filtering solid waste and nitrates, purifying water and adding oxygen to RAS systems.

READ MORE
JUN 91:12 PM GMT
Artificial Intelligence, deep learning solutions pitched

The themes of innovation and technology are featuring prominently on day one of this year’s event. In one of the first sessions, delegates learned how Artificial Intelligence (AI) and deep learning can enable fish farmers to monitor the fish they manage in land-based facilities.

Typically, especially in small and medium-sized fish farming operations, fish sampling is a hands-on, labor-intensive process. Manual sampling to collect information on health and weight takes time, and can caught stress for the fish, said Adam Bird, chief financial officer for Halifax, Nova Scotia-based Reel Data.

READ MORE

title: IAOF 2025: ‘Party over’ for US salmon sales within a year; Atlantic Sapphire concerns less of a threat to investor interest
content:
REYKJAVIK, Iceland -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the third annual Icelandic Aquaculture and Oceans Forum in the capital Reykjavik from May 26-27.

The show, hosted by Arion Bank, has been created to represent the growing aquaculture sector in Iceland, covering both conventional sea-based farms as well as several innovative land-based projects.

It platforms several of the largest aquaculture firms in both Iceland and Norway, alongside Icelandic banks and international investors. Check back regularly for updates from the forum.

Auto updates: On
MAY 284:15 AM GMT
Investors have ploughed €650m into Iceland’s five biggest land-based projects to date

Iceland’s five major hybrid flow-through salmon farming systems have already collectively raised €650 million in capex, according to a presentation from the largest, First Water.

With Norway’s Salmon Evolution one of the only proof of concepts so far established for the farming model, investors have already spent heavily in First Water’s planned €853m farm at Thorlakshofn, and Samherji’s €800m Ice Fresh Seafood project.

READ MORE
MAY 272:42 PM GMT
‘Party’s over’ for US salmon sales within a year, warns analyst

Angel Rubio, lead forecast analyst at Expana, drew on experience of what happened the last time Donald Trump sat in the Oval Office to suggest what may lie in store for the salmon sector.

During Trump’s first term, a 25% tariff imposed on imports of Chinese tilapia was passed on almost entirely to consumers.

READ MORE
MAY 272:20 PM GMT
Atlantic Sapphire concerns now less of a threat to land-based investor interest

Speaking on the investor panel, Kristoffer Jordheim — formerly an investment banker with Pareto Securities, now investment director at Blue Future Holding — remembered the days when US recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) salmon farmer Atlantic Sapphire was the industry darling.

“We invested in Atlantic Sapphire, and we had a very good return and sold out at a very high share price,” he told listeners. 

READ MORE
MAY 272:00 PM GMT
Lack of salmon demand should prompt investor caution, says Summa advisor

Jon Hindar, an industry expert with Swedish investor Summa Equity — owners of Polish salmon processor Milarex — sounded a word of caution at what had previously been a heavily bullish investor session.

Many land-based projects are built on the long-term assumption that salmon demand will continue to outpace supply, supporting the raised raw material prices necessary to make flow-through or recirculating aquaculture systems viable.

READ MORE
MAY 279:07 AM GMT
Skretting chief advises sector to take cost pain of alternative feed now, not later

Skretting CEO Bastiaan van Tilburg addressed the elephant in the room for aquafeed, as a global shortage of fishmeal and fish oil looms in the years ahead.

“We’ve been investing a lot of time and research in testing hundreds of alternatives,” he admitted. “The conclusion we came to is a bit sobering: there aren’t too many.”

READ MORE
MAY 278:31 AM GMT
Gigante Salmon receives first invoice after Norwegian event

Norwegian flow-through salmon farmer Gigante Salmon sold the first salmon from its facility this month, according to chief financial officer Rune Johansen.

“Last week at a conference in Norway, that was the first serving of our fish,” he told listeners. “We started this project in 2016, it took five years to get through government regulations, then in 2021 we started construction work.”

READ MORE
MAY 278:18 AM GMT
Morgan Stanley: Europe, Asian economies should be able to navigate US slowdown

Giving an assessment of the current global trade environment, Rajeev Sibal, a senior global economist at Morgan Stanley, told listeners to expect volatility in the months ahead with the full impacts of the US’ new tariff regime unlikely to be fully felt until much later this summer.

“The big challenge in the investment environment is now that Trump has finished negotiations with China, they think the worst is behind us,” he said. “That may be true for tariffs but not for growth and inflation; usually that doesn’t hit the US until three to four months after the tariffs are implemented.”

READ MORE
MAY 276:53 AM GMT
Andfjord reaches major milestone as it blasts through outlet tunnel

Norwegian flow-through farmer Andfjord Salmon reached a major milestone last Thursday (May 22), according to chief operational officer Christian Torgersen, as it successfully blasted the last layer of rock linking the outlet tunnel from its farm to the ocean.

The farm, based on the island of Andoya, uses a series of inlet tunnels 50 meters below sea level to fill a series of concrete pools on land, before wastewater is filtered then released through a single, large outlet tunnel.

READ MORE
MAY 275:39 AM GMT
Skretting waits for ‘right moment’ to make Iceland factory investment

Last year, Skretting’s salmon director, Harvard Walde, was beset by questions about when the Norwegian feed giant would build or partner with its first feed factory in Iceland.

This year, to address those questions more directly, the firm’s CEO Bastiaan van Tilburg was in attendance.

READ MORE
MAY 274:33 AM GMT
Laxey on track to add another 4,500t of capacity, hold first harvest this year

Laxey, the hybrid flow-through salmon farmer located on the island of Vestmannaeyjar, off Iceland’s southern coast, said that it was bringing another six tanks on line this year as it looks to conclude phase two by the end of 2025.

Chairman Larus Asgeirsson told listeners that each phase of construction at the farm adds another 4,500 metric tons of capacity, with the first completed last year.

READ MORE
MAY 2611:45 AM GMT
First Water to start production of 5kg salmon by autumn

First Water, currently the largest land-based salmon farmer based on the southern coast of Iceland’s Reykjanes peninsula, is expected to bring its next set of larger grow-out pools online later this year, according to CEO Eggert Thor Kristofferson.

Last year, the farmer produced 1,274 metric tons of head-on gutted fish, at an average weight of 2.6kg.

READ MORE
MAY 2610:39 AM GMT
High Liner sees big future prospects for Icelandic seafood in US

Fresh from buying minority stakes in Norwegian cod farmer Norcod and flow-through salmon farmer Andfjord Salmon earlier this year, Paul Jewer, CEO of Canadian processor High Liner Foods, has come to Reykjavik in search of more raw material.

“We will make more investments like these in cod and salmon,” Jewer confirmed. “And we think Iceland will tap into a significantly growing North American market.”

READ MORE
MAY 2610:11 AM GMT
AKVA: ‘Nobody moving as fast on land as Iceland’

Knut Nesse, CEO of Norwegian aquatech manufacturing giant AKVA group, noted the rapid gains being made in land-based farms in Iceland.

The company supplies land-based farming technology along with sea-based pens and digital software products, each of which it sells in markets all over the world. 

READ MORE
MAY 269:50 AM GMT
Icelandic salmon could be more valuable than cod by decade’s end, says minister  

Icelandic minister of industries, Hanna Fridriksson, emphasized the huge scale of the industry under consideration by the government in her keynote speech.

A new regulatory framework for the sector in Iceland is currently under discussion, and Fridriksson said she would be bringing legislation to the Icelandic parliament by “next autumn.”

READ MORE
MAY 269:26 AM GMT
Iceland expects 50,000t from aquaculture this year

Opening the third annual Iceland Aquaculture and Oceans Forum, event chair Kjartan Olafsson gave an update on production expectations this year.

After enduring a tough second half of 2023 and start to 2024, salmon farmers in the country have once again been building up biomass in 2025, with growth expected to return to the sector’s production output by the year’s end.

READ MORE
MAY 269:18 AM GMT
BioMar becomes first major aquafeed producer with Iceland presence

Denmark’s BioMar Group announced that it had formed a partnership with Iceland’s Fodurblandan to begin the manufacture and distribution of aquafeed in Iceland for the very first time.

According to BioMar, it is now the only global feed manufacturer with an aquafeed presence in Iceland.

READ MORE

Contact the author dan.gibson@undercurrentnews.com

title: Aquaculture America 2025: Animal rights activists ‘well-funded, strategic,’ says NAA
content:
NEW ORLEANS, Louisiana, US -- Undercurrent News is blogging live from Aquaculture America, which is being held March 6-10, in New Orleans, Louisiana. 

The event, which is expected to dive deep into heated debates on policy changes, sustainability challenges and innovative breakthroughs, anticipates 2,000 delegates, including 150 exhibitors and participants from nearly 60 countries.

Auto updates: On
MAR 123:33 AM GMT
Animal rights activists: Well-funded and strategic, says NAA

Animal rights organizations are creating detailed stories and using strategic laws to influence how people view aquaculture practices negatively, according to the National Aquaculture Association (NAA).

Speaking at Aquaculture America over the weekend, Paul Zajicek, NAA executive director, detailed a coordinated effort by animal rights groups to undermine the aquaculture industry through legislative maneuvers and attempts to shape public opinion.

READ MORE
MAR 1110:09 AM GMT
Seafood campaign chief: Political storm will pass

The campaign manager of the seafood industry coalition Stronger America Through Seafood acknowledged the pressing challenges and opportunities facing the US aquaculture sector amidst federal budget cuts and potential US tariffs on its trading partners, in an interview with Undercurrent News on Monday (Mar. 10).

Drue Banta Winters, campaign manager of SATS, expressed serious concerns regarding the reported potential plan by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to lay off more than 1,000 additional staff members as part of the Trump administration-mandated reduction in workforce.

READ MORE
MAR 1010:05 AM GMT
Details emerge on what led to Pacifico Aquaculture’s closure

The closure of Pacifico Aquaculture at the end of January has left many questions unanswered. As Undercurrent News reported, the Baja, California-based operation seemed poised for success due to its strategic location near the US-Mexico border, financial backing, growing international sales and approval to export to China.

At Aquaculture America, a source familiar with the situation shared that Pacifico was beleaguered by systematic extortion from local drug cartels, which demanded “fuel donations” and created an unpredictable business environment.

READ MORE
MAR 85:24 PM GMT
US salmonid industry reels in $379m for economy, says study

An economic analysis shared at the conference reveals the impact of the US salmonid industry, which contributed $379 million to the national economy in 2022 and created 2,250 jobs across various sectors, according to research supported by the US Department of Agriculture.

Shraddha Hegde, assistant professor at Texas A&M University, highlighted in her presentation that every dollar invested in the salmonid industry generates an additional 91 cents in economic activity.

READ MORE
MAR 84:34 PM GMT
Mexican shrimp feed supplier awaits clarity on potential US tariffs

A Mexican shrimp feed ingredient manufacturer exhibiting at Aquaculture America is preparing for possible US tariffs on its products, which could range from 10% to 25%.

Promaharin, located in Los Mochis, Sinaloa, derives about 15% of its revenue from the US market. While the company’s organic fertilizer line is exempt from these tariffs, the status of its shrimp feed products remains uncertain. 

READ MORE
MAR 810:30 AM GMT
Washington state aquaculture industry seeks $250,000 to fund lawsuit challenging net-pen ban

The Northwest Aquaculture Alliance (NWAA) is launching a fundraising effort to support a lawsuit challenging the US state of Washington’s Department of Natural Resources (DNR) ban on commercial net pen aquaculture. The projected legal costs are estimated at $250,000.

The complaint, filed on Feb. 27 in Thurston County Superior Court, charges that DNR exceeded its authority by imposing the ban without necessary legislative approval in violation of the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) and the State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA), as Undercurrent News reported.

READ MORE
MAR 78:26 PM GMT
Trump’s budget cuts, firings muzzle fed staff

The chilling effect of US president Donald Trump’s federal travel restrictions, recent firings of federal employees, and funding cost-cuts was palpable at the conference, where multiple sources expressed fear of repercussions for speaking to the media.

Undercurrent News spoke with employees at several federal agencies on the sidelines of the conference, one of whom had recently been fired and is now attending as a civilian and another who is the sole representative from his agency officially sent to the event. Both requested anonymity, citing concerns about potential fallout from speaking publicly.

READ MORE
MAR 711:17 AM GMT
Retiring NOAA aquaculture champion Michael Rubino honored with lifetime achievement award

Michael Rubino, a top executive at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) who worked to advance aquaculture in the US, is retiring after 20 years at the agency.

Rubino, who is receiving a lifetime achievement award, carries the title of senior advisor for seafood strategy at NOAA. But he is attending as a civilian due to federal travel restrictions imposed by the president Donald Trump administration. 

READ MORE
MAR 710:14 AM GMT
F3 krill replacement challenge crowns two winners

The F3 initiative continues to drive sustainability in aquaculture by challenging companies to develop alternatives to marine ingredients. 

At this year’s conference, the F3 Krill Replacement Challenge celebrated two winners who demonstrated innovation in replacing krill-based ingredients in fish feed.

READ MORE
MAR 69:30 AM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Organizers reshape agenda to adjust for NOAA absence

The agenda at Aquaculture America 2025 has been re-arranged to adjust for the absence of National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) staff.

A planned “town hall” session, which was set to focus on NOAA’s newly finalized “National Aquaculture Development Plan” on Friday (March 7) — the first day with sessions on the program — at 1:30 p.m., has been replaced with a new session aimed at addressing industry challenges at national, state and local levels.

READ MORE
MAR 512:11 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Turmoil at NOAA casts shadow over event

Aquaculture America 2025, which kicks off here on Thursday (March 6), has been overshadowed by recent decisions by US president Donald Trump that have disrupted the participation of federal agencies.

Mass firings last week at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and executive orders restricting federally funded travel have resulted in the federal agency pulling its participation from this year’s conference.

READ MORE

Contact the author liza.mayer@undercurrentnews.com

title: Arctic Securities conference: Akvafuture looks to Canada due to lack of Norwegian backing; Veramaris to double capacity in US
content:
OSLO, Norway -- Undercurrent News was reporting live from the Arctic Securities Seafood Investor Conference on Nov. 21, which brings together many of Norway's largest seafood companies in the capital, Oslo, at the Hotel Continental.

This year, the third year of the show's existence, the event took particular focus on the current productivity challenges in Norwegian salmon farming, as high lice levels, policy red tape and inclement weather have continued to stymie growth in 2024.

Check back regularly for updates from the show.

Auto updates: On
NOV 224:25 AM GMT
Veramaris looks to double capacity as it makes value argument

Dutch algal oil producer Veramaris is in talks to double the capacity of its factory in the US state of Nebraska, global business development director Ian Carr told listeners at the show.

The company has been at the forefront of the spreading use of algal oil as a fish oil replacement for fish farmers, and last year reported a 50% increase in production volumes.

READ MORE
NOV 224:02 AM GMT
Pelagia to open new mackerel filleting factory next year

Norwegian pelagics giant Pelagia is set to open a new filleting factory in Egersund for single-frozen mackerel next year, according to CEO Emil Haugstad.

As owners of roughly a third of Norway’s pelagic market share, Pelagia has a responsibility to drive the industry forward in terms of adding value to its fish, Haugstad said, and the new factory was designed with this in mind.

READ MORE
NOV 223:46 AM GMT
Akvafuture looks to Canada due to lack of Norwegian backing

Akvafuture, the Norwegian manufacturer of closed-containment salmon farms, was forced to turn to Canada to explore growth prospects due to a lack of available sites in Norway and backing from the Norwegian government, CEO Thomas Myrholt explained.

“Right now, there’s no room for us in Norway,” said Myrholt, whose business currently operates three farming sites in northern Norway. 

READ MORE
NOV 218:33 AM GMT
BioMar’s possible IPO at very early stage, confirms parent VP

“I can tell you when you announce you have intentions to float a company, you get a lot of friends,” Kasper Okkels, vice president of business development at Denmark’s Schouw & Co. told listeners. “It’s not often that Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, and the Bank of America call me on the same day.”

Just over a week ago, Schouw announced that it was looking into listing its feed subsidiary, BioMar Group — the world’s third-largest producer of aquafeed — as a separate independent company, and the phones have barely stopped ringing since, he said.

READ MORE
NOV 217:36 AM GMT
Andfjord to release up to 2m smolt into new pools next summer

With four new pools coming online next year, 2025 promises to be a milestone period for Andoya, Norway-based flow-through farmer Andfjord Salmon.

The company has spent 2024 constructing the infrastructure and blasting out the tunnels that it needs to connect its land-based pools to the sea, a process that is due to complete this winter, according to CEO Martin Rasmussen.

READ MORE
NOV 217:02 AM GMT
Land-based sector at inflection point, says Salmon Evo chief

Trond Schaug-Pettersen, CEO of Norwegian hybrid land-based farmer Salmon Evolution gave a bullish outlook on the future of the sector at a time when volume growth from sea-based farms is stalling.

“I really believe that were now at an inflection point for the land-based industry where you can see parity compared to conventional farming,” he said. 

READ MORE
NOV 215:15 AM GMT
Mowi: 50% of south, mid-Norwegian harvest to come from post-smolt next year

Kristian Ellingsen, chief financial officer of Mowi, the world’s largest salmon farmer by volume, noted the company was on track for a major post-smolt milestone in 2025.

Excluding the north of Norway, where sea lice is less of an issue, roughly 20% of Mowi’s Norwegian salmon production in 2023 was grown in land-based post-smolt facilities, up to an average weight of 250g.

READ MORE
NOV 214:26 AM GMT
Pharmaq: More widespread vaccine use should reduce wounds this winter

The spreading use of a new vaccine developed by Pharamaq is likely to cut the number of fish affected by winter ulcers, and thereby the volume of salmon being classified as ‘production fish’ next year, according to sales manager Lars Jorgensen.

Winter ulcers, caused by the bacteria Moritella viscosa, have been a growing issue for the sector since 2020. 

READ MORE
NOV 214:08 AM GMT
Next Norwegian gov’t likely to cut salmon tax, scrap price council

With the next Norwegian government likely to be some combination of center-right and right-wing parties if the latest polls are to be believed, Linda Helleland, a spokesperson for the Conservative party, Hoyre, said the sector could expect current tax burdens to be lightened under a new administration.

“The salmon tax is expected to remain, but with substantial changes,” Helleland told listeners. “Initially proposed at 40%, it has now been cut to 25%, with potential for a further reduction to 15%.”

READ MORE
NOV 213:53 AM GMT
More than NOK 20bn in EBIT growth possible for Norway’s salmon sector

In a keynote speech, Arctic Securities analyst Christian Olsen Nordby addressed the question that’s front and center of the sector’s thoughts this year: why, when prices are so consistently high, have margins stayed flat?

The answer, he said, is a combination of raised feed raw material prices, reduced smolt yields, and an increased share of low-value production fish hitting the market.

READ MORE

title: CFSE 2024: European smokers seek Chilean coho supplies for first time
content:
QINGDAO, China -- Undercurrent News reported live from this year's China Fisheries and Seafood Exhibition (CFSE) held at the Hongdao International Convention and Exhibition Center in Qingdao, China, from Oct. 30-Nov. 1.

Undercurrent also reported from the Norway-China Seafood Summit, held at the Haitian Center on Oct. 29, one day before the main show's opening.

CFSE is China's largest seafood trade show and is central to international seafood companies' marketing calendar in China. Domestic Chinese seafood companies are also expected to turn out in force.

Auto updates: On
NOV 38:28 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Turkish trout prices soar as Russian demand clears stock

The price of Turkish frozen farmed trout salmon has risen this season to $7.80–$8.00 per kilogram, a noticeable increase from the lower $7.00/kg range recorded last season.

The main buyers are in the Russian market, where high demand has cleared previously unsold stocks. “It was estimated that around 1,000 metric tons remained unsold, but all of it has now been allocated to Russia during the show,” an industry executive from a major Turkish producer told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
NOV 14:41 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
European smokers seek Chilean coho for first time amid Pacific wild salmon decline

Eastern European salmon smokers are seeking to procure Chilean coho salmon on a large scale for the first time, following a decline in Pacific wild salmon harvests, a marketing executive from a Chilean farmer told Undercurrent News.

In recent years, Chilean farmers have been eager to tap into markets in China, South Korea, and Southeast Asia to reduce their dependence on Japan. “Unexpectedly, this year, we have seen a rapid increase in inquiries from Europe and the US,” stated Jorge Guzman, the commercial manager of Salmones Aysen.

READ MORE
NOV 13:51 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Peru’s jumbo squid prices reach all-time high, hitting local processors

Peru’s jumbo squid prices have reached an all-time high this season, placing “considerable pressure” on local primary processors, an executive from a major exporting company told Undercurrent News.

Since early September, no squid has been landed in Paita, Peru’s primary fishing port for squid. As a result, ex-vessel prices in southern Lima have surged to a historic PEN 14.00 ($3.72) per kilogram, a dramatic increase from PEN 3.0/kg) in January.

READ MORE
NOV 112:46 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Ecuadorian shrimp price rises not mirrored in China, says importer

Ecuadorian exporters have increased their offer prices for farmed shrimp to Chinese buyers at the Qingdao show, causing buyers to become more cautious, said an executive with Quanlian Jicai, the largest shrimp import platform.

“The domestic prices have already fallen below the import costs,” said Liu Min, CEO of Quanlian.

READ MORE
NOV 112:14 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Vietnamese pangasius prices in China expected to rise further

Vietnamese pangasius export prices to China are expected to continue rising, according to an industry veteran.

“In the first three quarters of this year, Vietnam’s pangasius exports have increased, and recent prices have been on the rise,” Chen Xindong, general manager of Octogone, China’s largest pangasius distributor, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 3110:07 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Vietnamese surimi producers seeing ‘better’ sales despite challenges in India

Vietnamese surimi producers are currently experiencing “better” sales to China and South Korea following the price collapse in 2023, while their Indian counterparts are struggling with stagnant prices.

“The market had encountered challenges this past year due to an influx of inexpensive Russian products,” a major Vietnamese surimi manufacturer sales executive told Undercurrent News. “However, prices have risen by 10% since the beginning of the year, indicating a positive trend.”

READ MORE
OCT 319:23 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
India’s Jeelani Marine invests $13m in value-added shrimp plant in Maharashtra

Indian seafood processor Jeelani Marine will invest $13 million in a new value-added shrimp processing facility in Maharashtra, India.

The new plant, which will be built adjacent to the company’s existing five-year-old facility, will feature breading lines, cooking facilities, and IQF freezing capabilities, chief operating officer Muhammed Thanveer told Undercurrent News. The facility will primarily process black tiger shrimp and squid for export to Europe, North America, China and the Middle East.

READ MORE
OCT 319:10 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
India’s Zeal Aqua invests in brine freezing equipment for black tiger exports to China

Indian shrimp producer Zeal Aqua has invested €400,000 ($435,502) in French-made brine freezing equipment to target China’s growing demand for head-on black tiger shrimp.

The Gujarat-based company, which also sells to European markets through a partnership with Lenk Frozen Foods, installed the brine freezer this summer. The investment follows Zeal Aqua’s strategic shift to black tiger shrimp production, having harvested 1,800t at its own farms in the past year with plans to reach 2,500t in 2025.

READ MORE
OCT 318:47 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Russian pink salmon prices double on harvest shortfall

Russian pink salmon prices have surged to $4.20-$4.50 per kilogram for headed and gutted (H&G) product, more than double last year’s levels, as catches have fallen to about two-thirds of the pace of 2023’s record harvest, industry sources said.

The price spike comes as harvests drop even lower than scientists’ already bearish forecasts, forcing Chinese processors to scramble for supply across multiple vendors.

READ MORE
OCT 318:13 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japanese surimi processor markets US-made crab sticks in China

In response to the Chinese government’s ban on Japanese seafood products last September, Sugiyo, a major Japanese surimi processor, is pivoting by marketing its crab stick, manufactured at its US plant, to the Chinese market.

“Previously, we sold mostly Japanese-made products to the Chinese market,” Chunmei Meng, Sugiyo’s overseas department chief, told Undercurrent News. “Since the embargo, we have produced US-made options at our Sugiyo USA subsidiary to meet market demands.”

READ MORE
OCT 317:29 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
JETRO returns to Qingdao Show amid Chinese ban on Japanese seafood

Amidst China’s continued comprehensive import ban on Japanese seafood products, the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) returned to the Qingdao Seafood Show for the first time since 2021. 

“The timeline for the Chinese government to lift the ban remains uncertain,” Yohei Akazawa, JETRO Qingdao’s director, told Undercurrent News. As a result, the organization “has been showcasing Japanese companies manufacturing products outside Japan.”

READ MORE
OCT 3112:37 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
‘Best China show ever,’ says Omarsa’s CEO 

The 2024 Qingdao show is a celebration for Ecuadorians, as their largest market—China—is on the rise.

Sandro Coglitore, CEO of Omarsa, Ecuador’s second-largest shrimp exporter, told Undercurrent News that his company received many orders from China in the first two days of the exhibition.

READ MORE
OCT 317:10 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Indian shrimp packers target Vietnam before China as prices firm

Indian vannamei shrimp exporters are targeting Vietnamese buyers who are currently offering higher prices over Chinese importers, according to industry sources.

“Vietnam prices are $0.20-$0.30 higher than China at present,” Suryaprakash Rao Voodi, president of operations at Mekworld Marines and Exports, told Undercurrent News. “Vietnamese processors are currently focused on reprocessing for US and European markets.”

READ MORE
OCT 316:47 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Demand for Atlantic capelin roe remains stagnant despite zero TAC outlook

International buyers are maintaining a cautious stance regarding Atlantic capelin roe, despite forecasts predicting a zero fishing quota for the 2025 season, a sales executive from a major Icelandic pelagic harvester told Undercurrent News.

“There are no indications of buyers, including those from the Chinese market, eager to secure capelin roe during the trade show, primarily due to a significant stockpile left over from the 2023 season,” the executive stated.

READ MORE
OCT 311:57 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Chilean mussel farmer poised to enter lucrative Chinese market

Manuelita Acuicultura, a major Chilean mussel farmer, is making strides in its plans to enter the lucrative Chinese market, Jose Ignacio Lopez Anwadter, the company’s sales manager, told Undercurrent News.

In August, the company obtained an export permit for its processing plant in Puerto Montt, setting the stage to enter one of the world’s largest seafood markets.

READ MORE
OCT 311:24 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Mowi aims for 20% sales growth in the Chinese market next year

Mowi, the world’s largest salmon farmer and a pioneer with processing plants in Asia, is targeting a 10-20% year-on-year growth in sales volumes in the Chinese market, the top executive of its China operation told Undercurrent News.

“After the pandemic, we’ve observed a notable expansion in Chinese salmon consumption, which has grown by 7% year-on-year this year alone,” Xu Wannong, Mowi China’s country manager, said. He emphasized that the market’s potential for further salmon consumption remains substantial.

READ MORE
OCT 308:56 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Honduras shrimp producers pool resources in China market bid

Honduran shrimp producers have launched a unified marketing strategy to crack the competitive Chinese market, following the Central American nation’s diplomatic switch from Taiwan to China last year.

Under the “HonduMei” brand initiative, fourteen Honduran shrimp producers are coordinating their market approach rather than competing individually, industry executives told Undercurrent News at the Qingdao show.

READ MORE
OCT 308:42 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Clearwater launches frozen-at-sea quahogs in Asian markets

Canadian seafood giant Clearwater Seafoods has launched frozen-at-sea quahogs in Asian markets, targeting premium sushi and sashimi segments after securing increased harvesting capacity, company executives said.

The clams, traditionally used in North American chowders, are processed and frozen aboard vessels, distinguishing them from conventional quahogs and enabling high-end culinary applications, according to Diana Hanus, Clearwater’s marketing director.

READ MORE
OCT 308:35 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Chinese tilapia prices may remain firm until May 2025

The price of farmed tilapia in China is expected to remain firm until the first half of next year, as fingerling production in October has not yet recovered from Typhoon Mojie, which made landfall in Hainan in September, source said.

“In October, there were not many fingerlings available in China, as 90% of the production comes from Hainan,” Yunfeng Zhou, general manager of Hainan Qinfu, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 308:01 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Irish shellfish makes inroads into China’s high-end market

Irish shellfish, such as brown crab and langoustine, have entered China’s high-end dining and retail markets, achieving strong sales performance, according to an executive of Bord Bia, the Irish Food Board.

“We are now exporting live brown crab to China, which has a higher premium compared to frozen crab during COVID,” Conor O’Sullivan, China manager of Bord Bia, told Undercurrent.

READ MORE
OCT 307:16 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Irish seafood sales to China surge

From January to August 2024, Irish seafood exports to China rose by 35.6% year-on-year to €26.52 million, driven by increased shellfish sales, according to Conor O’Sullivan, China manager of Bord Bia, the Irish Food Board.

Speaking at the 2024 Irish Seafood Trade Seminar in Qingdao, O’Sullivan emphasized that Irish seafood exports to China have surged post-COVID-19, positioning China as Ireland’s sixth-largest trading partner in 2023.

READ MORE
OCT 306:52 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Aussie rock lobster firm to maintain frozen sales after China lifts ban on live

Australian rock lobster company Ferguson Australia will keep selling frozen product to Europe and domestic markets even as China lifts its four-year ban on live imports from the country.

“We won’t be losing what we’ve developed,” managing director Andrew Ferguson told Undercurrent News. “We had all our eggs in one basket before, and we won’t be doing that again.”

READ MORE
OCT 305:38 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Indian surimi producers face market challenges as prices remain stagnant 

Indian surimi producers are facing significant challenges in the market, as tropical surimi prices have remained static, industry executives told Undercurrent News.

“Our business continues to face considerable headwinds,” noted a sales executive from a leading surimi producer. “Although there have been price hikes for Russian and Alaskan pollock products this year, the increase in Indian surimi prices is quite limited.”

READ MORE
OCT 303:56 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
China’s Guoxin developing branded products for its giant aquaculture ship

Chinese state-owned company Guoxin Group has cultivated high-end demand for fish farmed in its giant farming vessel, Guoxin 1, according to a company executive.

After three years of operation, Guoxin 1 has reached technological maturity, harvesting 2,600 metric tons of yellow croaker in the first three quarters of this year and successfully marketing the fish to both domestic and international markets, said Wang Xiangyu, the marketing director of Guoxin.

READ MORE
OCT 303:16 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Maltese bluefin tuna sold to China under JV

Farmed Maltese bluefin tuna is making its consumer debut at the CFSE show through a joint venture between Malta and China.

Mediterranean Bluefin Industry Development (Hainan) Co. (MFF Limited) is a joint venture established in June 2024. Malta Fish Farming (MFF) holds a 60% stake, while China’s Shandong Far-sea Development holds 40%.

READ MORE
OCT 303:01 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Atlantic mackerel prices expected to soar even higher in 2025

Prices for Atlantic mackerel are expected to exceed this year’s record levels next year, a sales executive from one of Norway’s leading pelagic species producers told Undercurrent News.

“When demand remains high and supply decreases, it stands to reason that prices will rise,” he explained. “However, it is currently challenging to determine the exact extent of this increase.”

READ MORE
OCT 302:43 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese farmed abalone pressures prices for Aussie wild-caught

Australian wild-caught abalone prices have dropped AUD 20 per kilogram ($13/kg) since the start of the year as expanding Chinese aquaculture production intensifies competition in the premium seafood market.

The price pressure particularly affects smaller wild-caught abalone from Tasmania, Australia’s main producing region, where annual quotas have already been cut by more than half over the past 15 years to ensure sustainability, Simon Leonard, factory manager at Aussie seafood company Hai Loong Export told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 302:27 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Russian pollock producers explore new roe markets in China

Russian pollock producers are exploring the roe product line in the Chinese market as part of their strategy to diversify exports. 

With an annual output of approximately 35,000 metric tons, the demand for Russian pollock roe has traditionally been concentrated in Japan and South Korea. 

READ MORE
OCT 302:04 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese fish trader in Senegal starts value-added amid drop in pelagic catches

Tamou Fishing International, one of Senegal’s largest seafood trading companies, is expanding its value-added processing operations as local pelagic fish catches decline, a senior executive told Undercurrent News.

The Chinese family-owned business, which sells several hundred containers of seafood annually, has begun focusing on products like cleaned cuttlefish alongside its traditional trading operations.

READ MORE
OCT 301:47 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Newfoundland’s Greenland halibut prices remain firm in China

The Chinese market for Greenland halibut has shown resilience, with prices remaining steady, a sales executive from a major processor in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada told Undercurrent News.

“Chinese processors faced a stockpile of Greenland halibut from 2023 during March-April,” he said. “They opted to purchase raw materials at high rates to prevent a drop in inventory prices.”

READ MORE
OCT 301:30 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Vietnam gains mackerel processing market share from China aided by Japan trade deal

Vietnam’s seafood processors are capturing an increasing share of the mackerel reprocessing market from China, leveraging zero-tariff access to Japan through a long-standing free trade agreement, according to industry experts.

Chinese imports of Norwegian mackerel have plummeted from 130,000 metric tons in 2019 to a projected maximum of 50,000t for 2024, based on January-September import figures of 30,000t, according to Joe Qiao of Qingdao Meichu Foods, a major Chinese seafood importer and distributor.

READ MORE
OCT 301:17 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese salmon sales grow through e-commerce but traditional retail still dominates

E-commerce platforms are capturing an increasing portion of China’s salmon sales, though traditional retail channels continue to dominate, according to a senior executive at Mowi, the world’s largest salmon company.

Online sales now account for 19% of salmon purchases in China, up from 16%, as major platforms like JD.com and Alibaba’s T-Mall aggressively expand their fresh food offerings, said Emily Zhang, commercial manager at Mowi China.

READ MORE
OCT 298:30 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
China overtakes South Korea to become Norway’s third-largest mackerel market

Norway has exported 150,000 metric tons of frozen mackerel in the first nine months of 2024, a decrease from the 161,000t recorded during the same period in 2023. However, the export value has increased by 16%, driven by a 19.5% rise in average prices.

During the first three quarters of 2024, Norwegian mackerel exports to China saw a 36% year-on-year increase, allowing China to surpass South Korea and become Norway’s third-largest export market, according to Jan Eirik Johnsen, key account manager for pelagic species with the Norwegian Seafood Council.

READ MORE
OCT 295:39 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Pretty pictures ‘not enough’ for Chinese seafood e-commerce

Attractive product photos are “not enough” to sell salmon in China’s competitive e-commerce market, as platforms increasingly pivot toward livestreaming and interactive content, according to Emily Zhang, commercial manager at Mowi China. 

Zhang said the seafood industry must adapt to rapidly evolving digital marketing trends. “Beautiful pictures and well-designed pages are no longer sufficient,” Zhang said. “Today’s success depends on attracting traffic through compelling storytelling and livestreaming.”

READ MORE
OCT 295:36 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Norwegian mackerel market sees 10% growth in China, says importer

The Norwegian mackerel market in China continues to flourish, recording a 10% year-on-year growth, as Jason Wu, executive director of Yantai Xintown Foodstuff Co., revealed during the Norway-China Seafood Summit 2024.

Wu reported that Yantai Xintown Foodstuff has effectively introduced Norwegian mackerel into the domestic Chinese market, offering the fish in whole and fillet forms.  A portion of these products is targeted at the vibrant Japanese restaurant sector in China.

READ MORE
OCT 295:08 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Norwegian seafood exports to China surge amidst market resilience

At the Norway-China Seafood Summit 2024, Sigmund Bjorgo, China Director for the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC), highlighted an impressive growth trend in seafood exports to China, despite broader economic challenges.

Bjorgo reported that last year, Norway achieved an extraordinary 43% increase in seafood exports to China, making it the fastest-growing salmon market in the world. 

READ MORE
OCT 295:02 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Freshness ranks above sustainability, brand for Chinese salmon consumers

Chinese consumers prioritize freshness over brand name and sustainability certification when purchasing salmon, according to new market research from Hi-Chain, highlighting opportunities for suppliers with efficient logistics networks.

Henny Li, founder and general manager of Hi-Chain, a Shanghai-based salmon processor, said that big data analysis of online reviews shows freshness dominates positive consumer feedback about salmon products in China.

READ MORE
OCT 294:54 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese restaurant chain ‘North Salmon’ launches in Shenzhen

A new restaurant chain specializing in salmon dishes has launched in Shenzhen, marking the latest sign of China’s growing appetite for premium seafood and new distribution channels for salmon producers.

North Salmon, which focuses exclusively on salmon-based cuisine, represents an emerging trend in China’s food service sector, according to Henny Li, founder and general manager at Hi-Chain, a Shanghai-based salmon processor. The chain’s launch comes amid rising salmon consumption across Chinese urban centers.

READ MORE
OCT 294:13 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China has ‘greatest potential’ for salmon consumption growth 

Chinese consumers ate more salmon than ever in 2023, but industry experts say the market is just getting started.

The country’s salmon consumption — fresh and frozen — jumped 43% last year to 100,000 metric tons, marking a 30,000t increase from 2022, Henny Li, founder and general manager of Hi-Chain, said at the Norway-China Seafood Summit.

READ MORE

Contact the authors louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com, lewis.hu@undercurrentnews.com, masahiko.takeuchi@undercurrentnews.com

title: GSA summit 2024: Recap all the news and market forecasts from Scotland
content:
ST. ANDREWS, Scotland -- Undercurrent News was reporting live from St. Andrews for the 2024 Responsible Seafood Summit.

It was a packed two days running Oct. 22 and 23, featuring a focus on technology as well as the usual supply outlooks from Rabobank's Gorjan Nikolik and Kontali's Ragnar Nystoyl.

Auto updates: On
OCT 244:54 AM GMT
Walmart looking into alternative salmon feeds, smallholder shrimp farm collaborations

Across different panel discussions during this week’s summit, representatives from US retail giant Walmart have given some insight into their work in sustainable seafood sourcing.

“By the end of next year, our aspiration is that all of our salmon feed is sourced more responsibly — deforestation, conversion-free, and certified from a feed standpoint,” said one. “Along with that, we’re still continuing to look at other viable options such as insect meal, algae oil.”

READ MORE
OCT 243:59 AM GMT
German RAS secures €35m funding to scale up to 2,000t

Germany-based recirculation aquaculture system (RAS) technology firm Oceanloop secured a loan of €35 million from the European Investment Bank (EIB) this month to scale up, revealed chief technology officer Bert Wecker.

The company operates RASs for shrimp in Munich and Kiel, and Wecker said its “Oceanloop 2.0” technology is ready to be scaled up.

READ MORE
OCT 243:24 AM GMT
Sandhya CEO: Rise of farming tech means smallholder shrimp farms no longer ‘invisible’

The rise of Indian shrimp farming digitization technology over the last few years means smallholder farms are no longer “invisible,” said Kunam Kotaiah Chowdary, CEO of Sandhya Aqua.

From being essentially hidden and not caring about certification schemes, many farmers with just a few hectares of ponds are now interested in the market access they bring.

READ MORE
OCT 2311:05 AM GMT
Seafood Exchange’s Larkin hopeful of US demand improvements in 2025

After some tough years since the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, US retail demand for frozen shrimp should pick up in 2025, hopes Travis Larkin, president and owner of Seafood Exchange.

Retail sales have steadily slumped since the boom experienced during the pandemic, influenced by inflation and the mindset that shrimp is something of a luxury, he said.

READ MORE
OCT 239:36 AM GMT
Kontali expects minor recovery in China’s shrimp imports by Q4

China should see a minor recovery in shrimp imports by the final quarter of 2024, said Ida Skancke of Kontali.

For the first eight months of the year, China’s market supply has been down slightly at somewhere close to 1.2 million metric tons, using Kontali’s measure of “live shrimp equivalents.” That market supply is made up of domestic production and imports, minus exports.

READ MORE
OCT 239:18 AM GMT
Norway’s share of world coldwater shrimp trade up to 10% in 2024, Greenland’s exports slide

The Norwegian share of the global trade in coldwater shrimp has climbed from 1.7% in 2019 to 10.1% in the first eight months of 2024, according to data presented by Fabienne O’Donoghue of Expana.

In those months of 2024, the total volumes exported by all players was 152,000 metric tons — down 11% versus the same period of 2019.

READ MORE
OCT 238:11 AM GMT
2025 GSA summit heads to Colombia

Next year’s Responsible Seafood Summit will be held in the coastal city of Cartagena, Colombia, revealed Carlos Ramirez — the Global Seafood Alliance’s coordinator for Latin America.

It is scheduled to take place at the InterContinental, Cartagena de Indias, during the week of Sept. 29, 2025.

READ MORE
OCT 237:57 AM GMT
Scotland’s Lunar achieves MarinTrust certification for salmon feed ingredients

Scottish pelagics and whitefish company Lunar has this year achieved the MarinTrust factory standard certification for sidestream products made at its processing division, said the certifier’s Libby Woodhatch.

Lunar supplies UK retailer Marks and Spencer (M&S) with pelagics and whitefish and now has the certification for the “by-products” it turns into fishmeal and oil.

READ MORE
OCT 237:29 AM GMT
Tesco: Past 12 months saw good volume sales growth

Despite the difficulties posed to all by inflation and the cost of living crisis, Tesco — the UK’s largest retailer — has seen good volume sales growth, said the group’s head of sustainable agriculture and fisheries, Natalie Smith.

“It’s actually looking pretty positive. It’s been a difficult couple of years with a lot of inflation coming through, but that’s across all proteins. Actually, over the last year, we’ve seen really good volume growth, both in fresh and frozen.”

READ MORE
OCT 237:17 AM GMT
Hilton tests Seafish carbon emissions profiling tool

UK seafood and meat firm Hilton Food Group has been helping to develop and test a new carbon emissions profiling tool alongside public body Seafish.

The image below shows the outcome of the profiling tool for a retail pack of pangasius from Vietnam. 

READ MORE
OCT 236:27 AM GMT
Ecuador shrimp supply growth changes to lower gear, unlike Brazil

Ecuador’s vannamei shrimp farming — “the fastest-growing major aquaculture industry in the world” — is changing to a lower gear this year and next, according to the forecast presented by Rabobank’s Gorjan Nikolik.

After a compound annual growth rate of 14.3% between 2010 and 2022, production is estimated to have leaped 14% in 2023 alone. But then, 2024 is expected to see only a 4% output growth, and 3% in 2025. 

READ MORE
OCT 236:14 AM GMT
Global farmed shrimp supply growth slows but remains positive

The global supply of farmed vannamei shrimp has slowed in 2023 and 2024 but remains positive and should do so again in 2025, according to the forecast presented by Rabobank’s Gorjan Nikolik.

After a compound annual growth rate between 2010 and 2022 of 6.7%, 2023 saw a lift of 4%. A lift of just 1% is expected for 2024 and 2% for 2025, according to respondents to the Global Seafood Alliance’s surveys.

READ MORE
OCT 234:57 AM GMT
M&S buyer: Fish stunning becoming so widespread that some workers won’t work without it

In-water electrical fish stunning is becoming so normal that some seafood factory or vessel workers will now refuse to work without the technology, said UK retailer Marks and Spencer’s fisheries and aquaculture manager Linda Wood.

This sums up the gist of several of the morning’s talks: that “once workers are shown good animal welfare, and are ‘un-desensitized,’ they can’t look past poor welfare.”

READ MORE
OCT 234:33 AM GMT
Shift to non-ablation in shrimp may not mean hike in production costs

A move from farmed shrimp eyestalk ablation to alternative, non-ablation methods may not bring the increase in production costs that may have been expected, according to research by Simao Zacarias of Scotland’s University of Stirling.

2024 has seen a growing movement from retailers and the supply chain in Europe and the UK to require non-ablation, and there are a number of alternative methods that can be implemented in shrimp hatcheries, said Zacarias.

READ MORE
OCT 233:37 AM GMT
Cargill expects to see more ‘policy FIPs’ as climate change impacts fisheries

We are likely to see more “policy FIPs” (fishery improvement projects) globally as climate change alters the distribution and patterns of stocks, said Benjamin Weis of Cargill.

A “policy FIP” is a concept designed first by the North Atlantic Pelagics Advocacy group to drive sustainability in blue whiting fisheries. 

READ MORE
OCT 233:22 AM GMT
Scotland’s spatial planning needs greater clarity

Scotland’s marine strategy needs greater clarity of direction and some decisions needed, according to a panel of three representing the fisheries, offshore wind, and aquaculture sectors.

Fingal Mckiernan, commercial fisheries manager with wind energy business SSE Renewables, was clear that the process needed to be a triangular one between the energy sector, marine food production, and the government. 

READ MORE
OCT 229:33 AM GMT
Green shoots of recovery for UK seafood industry after trade value drops £1bn

Marcus Coleman, CEO of UK public body Seafish, is confident there are signs the industry is on the road to recovery following an extremely challenging five years.

The UK sector continues to adapt to life outside the EU and recover from disruption caused by COVID-19, the impacts of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the UK’s cost of living crisis and more recent supply chain difficulties caused by the war in Gaza.

READ MORE
OCT 227:02 AM GMT
Marine finfish aquaculture in China has ‘huge potential’

The farming of marine finfish has ‘huge potential’ in China as consumers look for new and premium species away from carp, noted Rabobank’s Gorjan Nikolik.

Carp production growth has stalled, and the real question is, “When will that begin to trend down,” said Nikolic. “The other question is, what will their new favorite be?”

READ MORE
OCT 226:37 AM GMT
Tilapia output to ‘crack 7m metric tons’ in 2025

Global tilapia production is set to exceed 7 million metric tons in 2025, according to estimates by Rabobank based on survey respondents in key aquaculture countries.

After growth in China stalled between 2018 and 2021, increases of 2.9% and 2.6% are forecast again for 2023 and 2025, either side of a dip this year. Chinese output is expected to just tick over 1.8m metric tons in 2025.

READ MORE
OCT 226:19 AM GMT
Kontali: Low salmon supply in first half of year likely once again in 2025

The last two years have seen the supply of farmed Atlantic salmon somewhat limited in the first half, and that pattern looks set to continue again in 2025, said Ragnar Nystoyl of Kontali.

Even with the analyst’s forecast of a 4-5% global supply growth year-on-year, it’s “really a story of no growth, still,” he said.

READ MORE
OCT 224:56 AM GMT
Minecraft co-creator says he’ll look to put aquaculture in next game

Chris van der Kuyl — Scottish entrepreneur and co-founder and chairman of 4J Studios, the videogame studio behind Minecraft — has promised he’ll look to include aquaculture in the studio’s new game, Reforj.

“It already has detailed agricultural models, and faithful models of ocean ecosystems with currents, shallows, deep waters, and creatures therein,” he said. 

READ MORE
OCT 224:42 AM GMT
AI can ‘prove aquaculture’s sustainability’ 

At its most basic usage, AI can work to prove to the public that the aquaculture industry can be run sustainably, suggested John Goodlad of Sustainable Ocean Fund.

He noted that aquaculture will be crucial to feeding a growing population, but at the moment, we’re at a point where perhaps a majority of people don’t think it can be a sustainable industry.

READ MORE
OCT 224:22 AM GMT
Minecraft co-creator: AI about to revolutionize seafood sector

Artificial intelligence is on the verge of revolutionizing the seafood sector, said Chris van der Kuyl, Scottish entrepreneur and co-founder and chairman of 4J Studios, the videogame studio behind Minecraft.

Already, AI is involved in aquaculture for health monitoring, biomass estimation, feed optimization, and more. 

READ MORE
OCT 223:57 AM GMT
Mairi Gougeon stresses international collaboration for innovation

Fresh off a year of visiting international seafood events, Mairi Gougeon — Scotland’s cabinet secretary for rural affairs, land reform and islands — stressed collaboration across borders as key to advancing the sector.

This year, Gougeon has been to shows in Barcelona, the Faroe Islands, Norway, Chile and more, she said. 

READ MORE
