title: IFFO 2024: Recap all the news from annual marine ingredients summit
content:
LISBON, Portugal -- Undercurrent News was reporting live from the annual conference of the Marine Ingredients Organisation held in Lisbon over Oct. 21-23.

The event brought together experts from across the fishmeal and fish oil industry to share analysis, production and consumption data, and trade statistics.

This year's conference took place against a backdrop of a recovery in Peru's critical anchovy fishery, after last year's El Nino conditions severely hampered catches, fueling a surge in fishmeal and fish oil prices. This year's improved supply has helped drive fishmeal prices back down.

Auto updates: On
OCT 2311:24 AM GMT
Cautious industry optimism on Peru’s bumper second season anchovy quota

Peru’s recently announced anchovy quota of 2.51 million metric tons for the first fishing season has drawn cautious optimism from industry, according to IFFO market research director Enrico Bachis.

The substantial quota, which reflects a healthy biomass following last year’s El Nino disruption, represents a maximum allowable 30-35% of biomass. However, Bachis told Undercurrent News that actual catch volumes remain uncertain.

READ MORE
OCT 2311:13 AM GMT
EU relaxes proposals on MOAH regulation in fish oil products

The EU has significantly relaxed its proposed limits on mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons (MOAH) in fish oil products, following industry concerns about testing capabilities and implementation challenges.

The European Commission now proposes a limit of 10 milligrams per kilogram starting in 2026, with a reduction to 5 mg/kg by 2030, Ellen Schutt, managing director of the Global Organization for EPA and DHA Omega-3s (GOED), told Undercurrent News. This represents a major shift from the initial proposal of 2mg/kg, which industry representatives argued was technically unfeasible.

READ MORE
OCT 2310:56 AM GMT
Tokyo to host IFFO’s annual conference in 2025

IFFO announced Tokyo as the host city for its 2025 annual conference.

IFFO president Egil Magne Haugstad also indicated the 2026 conference will return to the Americas, though the location remains undisclosed. 

READ MORE
OCT 2310:35 AM GMT
Dearth of certified fish oil fuelled price rise despite global surplus

Global fish oil markets continue to face elevated prices despite increased supply, largely due to a severe shortage of certified omega-3 sources, according to a veteran trader.

Christian Meinich, senior partner at Chr.Holtermann, explained that while overall fish oil production has risen, particularly following Peru’s improved fishing season, the critical divide between certified and non-certified oils is maintaining price pressure in key market segments (see prices below).

READ MORE
OCT 2310:11 AM GMT
Omega-3 consumption growth slows amid record prices

Global omega-3 ingredient demand grew by just 1.4% in 2023, marking a significant slowdown from historical growth rates of 2-4%, according to Aldo Bernasconi, vice president of data science at the Global Organization for EPA and DHA Omega-3s (GOED). 

The market reached 122,764 metric tons in 2023, with growth expected to recover to 4.7% annually through 2026, potentially reaching 142,723t. However, this forecast depends heavily on resolving current supply challenges.

READ MORE
OCT 239:53 AM GMT
‘Remarkable’ increase in Chinese fishmeal production in 2023

China’s fishmeal production surged to 623,000 metric tons in 2023, with whole fish accounting for 83% of the output, marking a significant increase in domestic production despite overall declining marine catch trends since 2016, according to IFFO.

The “remarkable” growth in production was largely attributed to rising prices incentivizing producers and substantial sardine imports from Russia, said Maggie Xu, China director at IFFO.

READ MORE
OCT 234:58 AM GMT
Global fish oil supply, consumption down in 2023

Global fish oil production and consumption fell markedly in 2023, driven by aquaculture reducing inclusion rates, said Enrico Bachis, market research director at IFFO.

“Exports were down. China also exported a lot though,” Bachis noted. Peru saw the largest decline among top exporting countries, with its global export share plunging from 12% to 3%.

READ MORE
OCT 234:36 AM GMT
Global fishmeal production, use fell in 2023 

Global production and use of fishmeal fell “across the board” in 2023, according to Enrico Bachis, market research director at IFFO.

“Global fishmeal exports declined, no surprise there. But there are interesting dynamics,” Bachis said. “Peru saw a decrease, half of production so half exports. India saw an increase.”

READ MORE
OCT 229:42 AM GMT
Norwegian harvester deploys unmanned drones to find Antarctic krill

Norwegian Antarctic krill harvesting company Aker BioMarine is utilizing unmanned naval drones to locate krill swarms and direct its fishing vessels, increasing efficiency and sustainability.

The drones are deployed to scout ahead of the fleet and use sensors to detect potential signs of krill. The data is transmitted back to the fishing vessels, allowing the captains to pinpoint more productive fishing areas. (The more productive areas identified by the drone are marked below in red.)

READ MORE
OCT 229:22 AM GMT
Veramaris CEO: High fish oil prices ‘fantastic’ for algal oil

Soaring fish oil prices were “fantastic” for the algal oil industry and created new opportunities for alternative omega-3 fatty acid sources like algae, said the CEO of algal oil company Veramaris.

Gertjan de Koning said the world faces a supply gap in fish oil sources of omega-3s EPA and DHA if aquaculture continues to rely solely on wild catch fisheries. He warned another bad fishing season in the biggest fisheries could cause supply problems.

READ MORE
OCT 229:10 AM GMT
‘Overwhelming’ soybean surplus sinks prices

Rapid expansion of soybean production in Brazil and sluggish demand growth in China have combined to create an overwhelming global soybean surplus this year, sending prices plunging, according to a Rabobank analyst.

“We have the largest surplus ever. No surprise prices are coming down. I would argue that they still have more downside to go,” said Carlos Mera, head of agri commodities market research at Rabobank in the Netherlands.

READ MORE
OCT 224:38 AM GMT
Scientists lose sway in uptake of novel feed ingredients

Nutritionists and scientists will have decreasing influence over aquaculture feed formulations in coming years despite their deep knowledge, according to Einar Wathne, assistant professor at NMBU Norway.

Wathne predicted nutritionists and scientists will struggle to keep pace with emerging sustainability demands from other stakeholders, with their traditional gatekeeper role eroding.

READ MORE
OCT 224:06 AM GMT
Climate change makes fisheries management ‘much harder’

Managing fisheries will become “much harder” because of climate change, said Jim Cannon, CEO of Sustainable Fisheries Partnership.

Warming waters are causing fish to migrate from historical habitats, ocean acidification and deoxygenation threaten species health, and altered current mixing impacts nutrients that support marine life, he said.

READ MORE
OCT 211:51 PM GMT
Less public money for sustainability programs post-COVID, inflation

Less public funding will be available for fisheries sustainability programs due to budget tightening from COVID-19 and inflation, warns Jim Cannon, CEO of nonprofit Sustainable Fisheries Partnership.

Cannon pointed to a multi-million Mexican government shrimp vessel buyback program in the 1990s and early 2000s as an example of substantial public investment that initially improved sustainability, but gains were not sustained long-term without consistent stock assessments and data collection.

READ MORE
OCT 211:31 PM GMT
Marine ingredients trade ‘not the priority’ amid rising global tensions

Food security is a growing concern for nations amid a rise in global tensions, though it remains secondary behind priorities like semiconductors, automotives, and other critical industries, according to a journalist at the Financial Times.

“Food is somewhere in the middle of the list,” said Gideon Rachman, an FT columnist who covers international affairs. “It’s really only when you start think apocalypically that you start thinking, ‘Could an enemy blockade us?'”

READ MORE
OCT 2111:23 AM GMT
Attendees quizzed on fishmeal inclusion range in aquafeed

The conference started with a pop quiz gauging attendees’ grasp of the current role fishmeal plays in global aquaculture feeds.

When polled, just under half of the audience estimated average inclusion sat between 5-10%. Approximately one quarter believed rates had dipped below 5%, potentially factoring the proliferation of vegetarian species like tilapia or carp. Another quarter placed estimates between 10-20%, more consistent with feeds used in shrimp or marine fish production.

READ MORE
OCT 2111:21 AM GMT
Record attendance at IFFO annual conference

The annual conference has drawn a record attendance this year in Lisbon, evidence of the “continued and growing importance” of the industry, said Egil Magne Haugstad, CEO of Pelagia in Norway and president of IFFO.

He spoke to the more than 500 delegates at the event. The conference comes as fishmeal and fish oil production is holding steady at about 7 million metric tons annually amid growing demand, according to IFFO data.

READ MORE

title: Untitled
content:
COPENHAGEN, Denmark -- Undercurrent News reported live from the 2024 Groundfish Forum, being held Oct. 15-17 in Copenhagen, Denmark. 

Although members of the media are not permitted to attend the event, Undercurrent's team brought readers updates based on conversations with key market players over the forum.

Auto updates: On
OCT 1711:49 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Full Cape hake quota likely to be caught for 2024, next year’s TACs to come

Although difficult winter weather in 2023 left South Africa’s Cape hake haul some way short of the full quota, this year is likely to see the full total allowable catch (TAC) taken, according to Sea Harvest Group’s chief operating officer Konrad Geldenhuys.

While the official government statistics for 2023 landings of Cape hake are due to be published soon, the Groundfish Forum’s own supply data put last year’s figure at 103,000 metric tons, well down on 132,000t in 2022.

READ MORE
OCT 1711:31 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Early end to US Pacific hake fishery will ‘leave shortfall’ on fillets, surimi

US vessels have stopped harvesting Pacific hake (also known as whiting) early, which will leave a shortfall of fillets and surimi, the CEO of American Seafoods Company (ASG) told Undercurrent News.

Harvesting on Pacific hake in the Fall fishery has finished in mid-October when it would normally end a month later. 

READ MORE
OCT 177:30 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Post-war lifting of Russian sanctions would benefit all pollock producers, says American Seafoods CEO

A normalization of global pollock trade with the lifting of sanctions and trade barriers on Russia would benefit all producers, said the CEO of American Seafoods Group (ASG), the largest US at-sea Alaska pollock processor.

In an ideal world, the war in Ukraine would end peacefully, then sanctions put in place on Russia in Europe and the total ban in the US could be lifted for the benefit of the industry as a whole, Einar Gustafsson, CEO of ASG, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 174:16 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Norway’s cod sector forced to turn to saithe, alternatives

The following years are going to test Norway’s cod processing sector to the limits of its resilience, with the focus now on utilizing every commercial species on offer, according to Nordic Group managing director Morten Jensen.

“We’re going to try and process more of the fish that’s landed in Norway, and we’re going to try and process more saithe; that’s the most stable whitefish quota we have.”

READ MORE
OCT 174:01 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Barents Sea cod harvesters unlikely to see quota recovery until 2028

A forecast of the future of the Barents Sea cod stock presented by Johanna Fall, a researcher from Norway’s Institute of Marine Research, makes for grim reading.

“It was especially two years in 2019 and 2020 that we had extremely low recruitment, much less than expected given the size of the spawning stock,” she told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
OCT 173:18 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Farmed ‘snow’ cod can only supplement wild-caught, not replace it

With wild-caught cod volumes out Norway set to plummet next year (see below), cod farmers would seem to be in a place to capitalize on the deficit.

But the reality is that what cod farmers are capable of producing now remains a niche product aiming to supplement off-season cod supplies rather than fill the industry’s glaring shortage in a significant way, according to Christian Riber, CEO of Norcod.

READ MORE
OCT 168:33 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Current prices for Russian H&G pollock ‘not workable’ given fillet levels

The current prices for headed and gutted (H&G) Russian pollock are way too high given the levels for finished products in the market, said an executive with a Chinese processing company who wished to remain unnamed at the 2024 Groundfish Forum. 

Between week 24 and week 30 of 2024, Russian H&G pollock prices in the 25cm-plus size were stable at around $1,010 per metric ton, cost and freight (CFR) China. 

READ MORE
OCT 165:18 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Farmed whitefish supplies to see another growth hike in 2025

As well as wild catch species, the Groundfish Forum’s annual supply projections also cover those for major farmed whitefish species such as pangasius and other catfish species, and tilapia.

Both global catfish and tilapia supply volumes are looking at significant increases of 5.6% and 4.6% y-o-y respectively in 2025, according to the forum.

READ MORE
OCT 165:14 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Hake volumes to bounce back next year

Global supplies of hake are expected to recover next year following a disappointing 2024, driven by supply improvements in the Americas, the forum predicts.

In its annual supply outlook, the forum gives a catch projection of 1.04 million metric tons of hake for 2025, back in line with the rough 1.06m metric tons landings estimate from last year after a low predicted 2024 output of 961,000t.

READ MORE
OCT 164:52 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Huge 20% cut in global Atlantic cod supply projected for 2025

The annual supply handout from the 2024 Groundfish Forum showed, as expected, that the industry is looking at an unprecedented shortage of Atlantic cod next year.

The forum’s outlook suggests that the global market can expect only a scant 656,000 metric tons of Atlantic cod catches next year, down from 816,000t this year, and 1.08 million metric tons as recently as 2022.

READ MORE
OCT 164:30 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
US pollock focus on fillets over surimi is about picking ‘lesser evil’

While US pollock sellers at the forum noted the market for fillets is more positive than surimi, it’s very much a case of picking the “lesser of two evils,” sources told Undercurrent News.  

Due to the rapid increase in Russia’s surimi production, US companies have dropped their output by 14% year-on-year to 167,906 metric tons, according to production data through Sept. 28, 2024.

READ MORE
OCT 164:24 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Will Norwegian trawlers suffer larger cod cut than coastal catchers?

There’s some speculation at the Groundfish Forum that Norway could end up reducing its quota more percentage wise to the trawl fleet.

Scientists are recommending a 31% reduction in the Barents Sea cod quota for Norway and Russia to 311,587 metric tons. The Russians and Norwegians will set the quota in the coming weeks.

READ MORE
OCT 1511:59 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Rocketing H&G saithe prices hamper European product development plans

Some European processing companies were looking at headed and gutted (H&G) Norwegian saithe as a cheap raw material option to counteract the rocketing prices for H&G cod (read more on this below), one source who asked not to be quoted by name told Undercurrent News.

Back in June, the price was NOK 18/kg ($1.67/kg) for 1-2.3kg H&G frozen saithe on the Norges Rafisklag auction in Norway. In week 40, frozen H&G saithe in the 1-2.3kg size was NOK 26.19/kg on the auction, an increase of 45% on the June level.

READ MORE
OCT 159:22 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
High Liner CEO doesn’t expect price relief on Norwegian cod anytime soon

As finished products cut from Norwegian frozen cod raw material that has risen 70% since the end of last year hit the North American market, demand will drop, Paul Jewer, the CEO of High Liner Foods, told Undercurrent News.

However, the likely decline in demand will be offset by a further reduction in supply in 2025, with scientists recommending a 31% cut, which would take the level to 311,587 metric tons. The Russians and Norwegians will set the quota in the coming weeks.

READ MORE

title: Untitled
content:
BARCELONA, Spain -- Undercurrent News is reporting from the Surimi School Europe in Barcelona, Spain, held on Oct. 8, 2024.

During the conference, coldwater and warmwater surimi production and the markets are covered.

Auto updates: On
OCT 93:44 AM GMT
Survey of world’s surimi seafood processors gives bleak outlook for sector

A survey of surimi seafood processors globally shows the sector has a long way to go to recover from the current tough climate.

The short market survey, based on 25 responses from surimi seafood processors in China, Europe, Southeast Asia, Russia and the US, was included in a presentation from industry veteran Pascal Guenneugues.

READ MORE
OCT 93:41 AM GMT
Tropical surimi set to drop for second year to 618,000t amid reduced demand, Russian competition

The production of tropical surimi is set to decline by some 20,000 metric tons in 2024 to around 618,000t, according to figures put together by global sector veteran Pascal Guenneugues.

Tropical surimi production in Asia decreased by 60,000t since the peak of 2022 of 693,000t “due to reduced demand by the Asian market and new competition from Russian pollock surimi,” wrote Guenneugues, whose presentation was delivered by Surimi School organizer Jae Park.

READ MORE
OCT 93:25 AM GMT
Japan could up import quota on Russian pollock surimi in ‘coming years’

It’s conceivable that Japan could increase the relatively small import quota for Russian pollock surimi in the future, given the dramatic increase in production of the latter, said an executive with a Maruha Nichiro subsidiary.

“Japan has an import quota on pollock surimi, and a big part of it is specific to the US,” said Caroline Hanako Felus of Seafood Connection, a subsidiary of Japan’s Maruha Nichiro based in the Netherlands.

READ MORE
OCT 811:35 AM GMT
French, Spanish surimi giants seek to stem dropping sales

Executives with two of the largest surimi finished product producers in Europe noted sales in France and Spain continue to decline in 2024.

In the first half, surimi imports by France, the largest market in Europe, are down 15% to 6,327 metric tons, with the bulk Alaska pollock and Pacific whiting, said Marine Laplace of Alliance Oceane, which owns the number two brand, Coraya.

READ MORE
OCT 810:49 AM GMT
US pollock stock could support TAC hike in 2025

An increase in the 2025 Alaska pollock total allowable catch (TAC) at least looks possible from the current data, but it remains to be seen if that will happen, said a leading industry figure.

The North Pacific Fishery Management Council (NPFMC) will meet in December to recommend the US TACs for pollock and other species in Alaskan waters.

READ MORE
OCT 810:47 AM GMT
Despite possible Russian pollock TAC hike, catch likely to be stable

The Russian government is considering a 7% increase in the 2025 total allowable catch (TAC) for pollock to 2.46 million metric tons, but a senior industry figure said the catch will likely be stable.

In 2024, the forecast is that Russia will catch 2.04m metric tons of a 2.29m TAC due to slow fishing in the west Bering Sea fishery, which have been previously reported by Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 810:45 AM GMT
Russian Fishery forecasts 14% surimi growth in 2025, then two years of ‘spikes’

Russian Fishery Company (RFC) is anticipating countrywide production growth of 14% in 2025 to 80,000 metric tons, before two years of rapid growth as new vessels start operating.

With two new RFC super-trawlers arriving at the end of 2025 with surimi capacity, country-wide production should be 100,000t in 2026 and then 120,000t in 2027, said Oleg Moskvin, RFC sales director. 

READ MORE
OCT 810:39 AM GMT
Kyokuyo’s new plant will take North American total to 10

The addition of a new surimi seafood plant in the US from Japan’s Kyokuyo will take the total in North America to 10.

John Henderschedt, CEO, Phoenix Processor Limited Partnership (PPLP), a US mothership operator, presented a slide from forum organizer Jae Park that estimates the North American production is 115,000 metric tons across the current nine plants, with 15,000t of imports.

READ MORE
OCT 810:38 AM GMT
Despite drop in volume, Pacific whiting surimi prices ‘not hit bottom’

Prices for Pacific whiting surimi have been diving and “do not yet show a bottom,” said John Henderschedt, CEO, Phoenix Processor Limited Partnership (PPLP), a US mothership operator.

A chart presented by Henderschedt illustrates that declared import prices for Pacific whiting to France, Japan, Lithuania, and fell sharply from a peak in mid-2022 to the lows of Q2, the latest data available.

READ MORE
OCT 810:36 AM GMT
US pollock, Pacific whiting surimi production dives in 2024 amid rock-bottom prices

The US production of Alaska pollock and Pacific hake/whiting surimi has dived in 2024, with the former being market-driven and the latter supply-driven.

According to the latest B season catch data presented by John Henderschedt, CEO of Phoenix Processor Limited Partnership (PPLP), US pollock surimi production for 2024 is down 21% year-on-year to 154,128 metric tons.

READ MORE

Contact the author tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com

title: TSSS 2024: Indonesian tuna volumes forecast to drop 30% by 2050
content:
TOKYO, Japan – Undercurrent News is reporting live from the tenth edition of the Tokyo Sustainable Seafood Summit, taking place from Oct. 8 for three days at the Tokyo International Forum.

Co-hosted annually by Seafood Legacy, a leading Japanese consultancy specializing in seafood sustainability, the summit aims to enhance sustainable practices amid rising seafood demand and increasing environmental pressures on the world’s oceans and fish stocks.

With over 1,300 pre-registered participants from various industries, the event is expected to facilitate important discussions that could influence the future of seafood sustainability both in Asia and globally.

Keep checking back below for updates on the summit.

Auto updates: On
OCT 102:45 AM GMT
Maruha Nichiro launches enhanced procurement policy to ensure ethical seafood sourcing

Japanese seafood giant Maruha Nichiro Corp. has strengthened its commitment to sustainability with a comprehensive seafood procurement policy, aimed at promoting responsible sourcing and transparency across its supply chain.

The company’s “Marine Products Procurement Policy,” which took effect last month, underscores Maruha Nichiro’s dedication to aligning its operations with global standards for environmental protection and human rights practices, according to Yusuke Sato, the company’s Sustainable Group Manager, during his speech.

READ MORE
OCT 101:35 AM GMT
Thai Union aims for 100% blue finance portfolio by 2030

Thai Union has set a target to shift its entire long-term financing portfolio to Blue Finance by 2030, according to Yongyut Setthawiwat, Managing Director and Group Treasurer of Thai Union Group.

“Our target for long-term financing is $1.4 billion or THB 45bn, and Blue Finance is essential for us to achieve this,” Setthawiwat noted during his speech.

READ MORE
OCT 911:57 PM GMT
Climate change to cut Indonesia’s tuna revenue by 30% by 2050, says Planet Tracker rep

François Mosnier, Head of the Ocean team at Planet Tracker, highlighted the looming challenges facing Indonesia’s tuna industry due to climate change.

Mosnier projected a staggering 30% revenue decline by 2050 if immediate action is not taken. However, he stressed that investing in sustainability measures—such as reducing overfishing and improving traceability—could help offset these predicted losses.

READ MORE
OCT 98:00 PM GMT
Japan’s MEL sees potential growth in sustainable seafood certification

Naoya Kakizoe, Chairman of the Marine Eco-Label Japan (MEL) Council, emphasized in his speech that there is significant room for further growth in the certification of sustainable seafood.

Kakizoe pointed out that bottom trawling in fisheries is currently at zero, and foodservice in the distribution sector is non-existent.

READ MORE
OCT 97:37 PM GMT
By-products are key to sustainable marine ingredients, says Marine Trust CEO

Francisco Aldon, CEO of Marine Trust, emphasized the critical role of byproducts in the production of marine ingredients, a sector poised for growth in sustainability and responsible sourcing, during his speech.

Aldon noted that while whole fish are a primary source for producing marine ingredients, byproducts—specifically the heads, guts, and fish frames—are equally important.

READ MORE
OCT 97:13 PM GMT
China’s fisheries sector embraces greener practices amid growing demand, says domestic NGO leader

China has increasingly embraced greener practices in the past decade, particularly influenced by developments in its fisheries and agriculture sectors, Songlin Wang, founder and president of the Qingdao Marine Conservation Society, said in an interview with Undercurrent News.

Wang told Undercurrent that while consumer awareness is slowly rising, the primary driving force behind these foundational changes is government policy and initiative.

READ MORE
OCT 96:28 PM GMT
Japan’s role in sustainable aquaculture growing, says ASC CEO

Chris Ninnes, CEO of the Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC), touched upon the ASC’s alignment with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the growing certification in Japan, and the future of responsible seafood production during his speech.

Ninnes emphasized that Japan, though ranked 13th in global aquaculture production, imports more farmed seafood than it produces, making it a crucial player in the international seafood market.

READ MORE
OCT 98:27 AM GMT
Seafood Legacy, DIWA partner to enhance labor rights in Japan’s seafood industry

Japanese seafood sustainability consultancy Seafood Legacy and Dignity in Work for All (DIWA) inked a memorandum of understanding on Oct. 9 to address the growing public concern regarding human and labor rights within the seafood industry.

The partnership is expected to offer stakeholders crucial technical support, helping them better understand, identify, and mitigate human rights risks and impacts within their operations and supply chains.

READ MORE
OCT 97:25 AM GMT
US to-go sushi market set for explosive growth to exceed $4bn, says a leading seafood importer

The US sushi market is on the brink of substantial growth, driven by increasing health consciousness and shifting consumer preferences, Michael McNicholas, Managing Director and CEO of New York-based seafood importer Culinary Collaborations, told Undercurrent News.

Current estimates place the US sushi market value at approximately $2.4 billion including foodservice sector, but McNicholas believes the actual worth exceeds $4bn annually for the to-go sushi segment alone.

READ MORE
OCT 92:42 AM GMT
Japanese tuna longliner urges tougher penalties on distributors to combat illegal fishing

Sotaro Usui, CEO of Japanese tuna longline fishery operator Usufuku Honten Co., urged expanded penalties for illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing.


Usui pointed to a recent incident in Miyagi Prefecture, where unreported tuna catches were uncovered. He said that while the fishermen faced penalties, distributors avoided consequences by claiming ignorance.

READ MORE
OCT 92:00 AM GMT
Over 68% of seafood-producing countries face human rights abuses, says Packard Foundation rep

Japan’s seafood industry, along with 68% of seafood-producing countries worldwide, has come under scrutiny for evidence of forced labor, human trafficking, and child labor in its supply chains, according to Sarah Hogan, Ocean Director for The David and Lucile Packard Foundation.

“Japan has demonstrated leadership by addressing illegal fishing and human rights abuses,” she said. “Here again, Japan has a tremendous opportunity to lead by example.”

READ MORE
OCT 91:24 AM GMT
SFP calls for industry-led collaboration to overhaul fisheries management in developing nations

Jim Cannon, CEO and founder of the Sustainable Fisheries Partnership (SFP), stressed the urgent need for a major overhaul in global fisheries management, particularly in developing nations, during his speech.

“The future of fisheries management isn’t in Alaska,” he remarked. “Alaska [and the US] is a rich country that can afford central taxation, fund scientists, conduct independent research cruises, and maintain a robust Coast Guard and fisheries inspectors.”

READ MORE
OCT 91:19 AM GMT
Taiwan implements first-ever individual quota for Mackerel to boost sustainable fisheries

Taiwan has introduced its first-ever Individual Fishing Quota (IQ) this year, targeting the coastal mackerel fishery, Wei-Hsiang Chang, section chief of Taiwan’s Fisheries Agency, told Undercurrent News.

“We applied the IQ to mackerel because it accounts for the largest catch volume of any single species,” he explained. In the future, Taiwan plans to extend the IQ system to other species, such as hairtail, primarily exported to China, South Korea, and Japan.

READ MORE
OCT 89:35 PM GMT
South Korea leads Asia’s fight against IUU fishery with advanced technology, says policy analyst

South Korea stands as the only Asian country within the global IUU Fishing Action Alliance, underscoring its pivotal role in leading efforts against the global illegal, unreported, and unregulated issue, Jooyoun Lee, policy analyst of South Korea’s Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries told the audience.

“Korea has made encouraging progress in combating IUU fishing, supported by robust legal frameworks and international cooperation,” Lee stated.

READ MORE
OCT 89:19 PM GMT
Japan aims for 200% growth in seafood exports to $8bn by 2030, says Fisheries Agency head

Takeshi Mori, director-general of Japan’s Fisheries Agency, underscored Japan’s ambitious target of increasing fishery product exports to JPY 1.2 trillion ($8.1 billion) by 2030 during his speech.

The targeted export value for 2030 represents more than a 200% increase compared to 2023’s figure of JPY 390bn.

READ MORE
OCT 82:49 AM GMT
South Korean seafood traceability system covers only 0.5% of total imports

South Korea’s seafood traceability system covered only 0.5% of total imports in 2023, according to Woojin Chung, senior campaigner at the Environmental Justice Foundation.

Chung emphasized the importance of traceability in combating illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and highlighted the need for better coverage of both domestically caught and imported seafood.

READ MORE
OCT 82:22 AM GMT
Only 2% of tuna longliners equipped with electronic monitoring, says Nature Conservancy advisor

The Nature Conservancy (TNC) is advocating for the global adoption of electronic monitoring (EM) in industrial tuna fishing, emphasizing its crucial role in combating illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing while promoting sustainability.

Rob Johnson, TNC’s senior corporate engagement advisor, stressed the importance of transparency at sea to ensure sustainable and responsible seafood practices.

READ MORE
OCT 81:34 AM GMT
Nissui reports 83% of seafood sourced from ‘well-managed’ fisheries

Japanese seafood giant Nissui Corp. has made strides in sustainable seafood procurement, with 83% of its seafood now sourced from well-managed fisheries in 2023, according to Shigeo Morii, deputy general manager of the company’s sustainability division.

This represents an increase of 4% since the 2020 survey, as previously reported by Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 81:12 AM GMT
Japan’s consumers org reports 200% rise in shrimp survival rates from sustainable project

Satoshi Matsumoto of the Japanese Consumers’ Co-operative Union (JCCU), Japan’s largest consumers’ organization, showcased the success of the Indonesia Shrimp Aquaculture Improvement Project (AIP), which has led to a 200% increase in the survival rate of farmed shrimp, rising from 7-13% to 25-27% during his speech.

According to Matsumoto, the AIP, launched in July 2018, is a key initiative aimed at improving shrimp farming practices in Indonesia while ensuring ecological preservation and sustainable livelihoods for local communities.

READ MORE
OCT 812:08 AM GMT
Walton Family officer highlights Japan’s role in shaping global sustainable seafood

Theresa Ish, senior program officer at the Walton Family Foundation, emphasized that Japan has a unique role to drive sustainability efforts domestically and globally, during her speech.

“Even as seafood remains central to Japanese diets, Japan increasingly relies on imports to meet demand,” said Ish. She stressed that the reliance on imports places Japan at the center of efforts to improve sustainability throughout global seafood supply chains.

READ MORE
OCT 711:37 PM GMT
Japanese retail giant targets 100% certified seafood by 2050

Seven & i Holdings, the Japanese retail giant, is aiming to expand its lineup of certified seafood, with plans to source 50% of its original products by 2030 and reach 100% by 2050, according to a presentation by Junro Ito, representative director and vice president of the company.

With a global network of 85,800 stores, including Seven-Eleven Japan and Ito-Yokado, the retail group pushes its sustainable procurement efforts even further. 

READ MORE
OCT 711:32 PM GMT
MSC aims to engage one-third of global fish landings by 2030

Rupert Howes, CEO of the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC), announced the organization’s goal either to certify or engage over one-third of global fish landings by 2030, aligning with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals.

In his speech, Howes acknowledged the significant challenges facing the world’s oceans but remained optimistic about the future.

READ MORE

title: Conxemar 2024: Iberconsa launches vessel in Namibia, plans new one in South Africa
content:
VIGO, Spain -- Undercurrent News was reporting live the week of Sept. 30 - Oct. 4 from the Conxemar trade show in Vigo, Spain.

The main event, which ran from Oct. 1-3, was preceded by a conference on global seafood supply, organized by the Spanish industry association Conxemar and the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization.

You can recap all the news from both events below:

Auto updates: On
OCT 45:00 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Iberconsa launches vessel in Namibia, plans new one in South Africa

Spanish firm Grupo Iberica de Congelados (Iberconsa) is advancing its fleet renewal plans in Namibia and South Africa. 

Following the recent deployment of the vessel Oukaume in Namibia, the company, which is owned by US-based investor Platinum Equity, is now setting its sights on expanding its South African operations with the acquisition of a new vessel to replace Umzabalazo.

READ MORE
OCT 42:23 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Argentina’s inshore red shrimp fishery moves closer to achieving MSC certification

Argentina’s inshore red shrimp fishery is making significant strides towards achieving certification from the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC).

MSC representatives provided an update on the ongoing evaluation process during the trade show, noting that the fishery anticipates receiving its pre-assessment report in November.

READ MORE
OCT 39:01 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti 
Nueva Pescanova sees 2024 sales volume surge

Fernando Zaldivar Kunz, Grupo Nueva Pescanova’s commercial, marketing, and innovation director, said he remains optimistic about the company’s performance this year.

Zaldivar told Undercurrent News that 2024 has been a strong year for the group so far. He emphasized that the company has seen a significant recovery in volume, not just in value. This is a crucial shift, indicating that consumers are purchasing larger quantities of seafood products, not merely seeing an increase due to pricing adjustments.

READ MORE
OCT 38:23 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Conxemar’s economic impact soars despite space shortage

Conxemar occupies 37,000 square meters and generates around €750 million ($827.8m) over three days. Of that, approximately €185m stay in Vigo, contributing to the local economy, said president Eloy Garcia. 

The trade show also supports around 6,500 jobs per edition. 

READ MORE
OCT 32:41 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
ABANCA launches executive master in seafood management

ABANCA’s business school has launched a new executive master in seafood management, a specialized program designed for professionals in the seafood industry. 

This master’s program aims to prepare participants for high-level executive positions within the seafood sector by providing deep knowledge and hands-on experience in key areas of the entire value chain, from the most advanced educational perspective, Javier Fraga Diaz, ABANCA MAR’s director, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 212:15 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Spanish body urges EU to prioritize processing industry in fisheries policy update

As the EU embarks on a review of its Common Fisheries Policy (CFP) for the first time in a decade, stakeholders from the fishing industry are voicing their perspectives on necessary changes to enhance sustainability and competitiveness.

Roberto Alonso, the secretary of the Spanish canning industry association ANFACO-CECOPESCA, showed optimism about the CFP evaluation process, which he believes is long overdue. 

READ MORE
OCT 28:00 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Grupo Pereira set to launch new squid fishing vessel in November

Grupo Pereira is poised to enhance its fishing fleet with the upcoming launch of the “Argos Berbes,” the firm’s new 85-meter-long squid fishing vessel.

The vessel, currently under construction at the Nodosa shipyard in Marin, in Vigo, is scheduled to be launched on Nov. 28, marking a significant milestone for the company.

READ MORE
OCT 27:26 AM GMT
By María Feijóo 
Peruvian squid prices triple as market faces unprecedented shortage

The Peruvian market is grappling with a severe squid shortage, causing prices to triple and leaving consumers struggling to access this once-affordable staple. 

Current prices have surged past PEN 20 (approximately $5.40) per kilogram, with some firms reporting prices as high as PEN 22 for frozen squid in the domestic market, sources told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 26:35 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Declining wild groundfish landings in EU could be an opportunity for farmed products

Recent trends in the EU groundfish market reveal a significant decline in groundfish landings, which dropped by 35% from 2018 to 2022, while import reliance has increased, according to Kontali’s senior analyst Jan Erik Oksenvag. 

This shift presents both challenges and opportunities for the market, particularly in the context of rising prices and shifting consumer preferences.

READ MORE
OCT 19:15 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Spain’s Marfrio takes full control of Portuguese tuna processing plant, previously shared with Atunlo

Marfrio has acquired full control of Central Lomera Portuguesa, a factory in Vilanova de Cerveira that was previously co-owned with the Vigo-based tuna processor Atunes y Lomos, commonly known as Atunlo.

This strategic acquisition follows the “swift judicial dismissal” of three Atunlo administrators on July 15, a decision prompted by their involvement in creating a financial deficit exceeding €3 million ($3.32m).

READ MORE
OCT 18:03 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Pescapuerta launches new freezer trawler for Falklands fleet

Petrel Fishing Company, owned by Galicia, Spain-based group Pescapuerta, has launched the ‘Prion,’ a new freezer vessel to operate in the Falkland Islands.

The vessel is set to become the largest and most advanced freezer trawler constructed in recent years, with 85 meters in length, 14 meters in width and a 2,500 gross tonnage.

READ MORE
OCT 17:32 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Ecuadorian shrimp industry faces ‘mixed fortunes’ ahead of Christmas, eyes European demand

As the holiday season approaches, Ecuadorian shrimp companies are gearing up for a surge in demand, especially from European markets known for their seasonal spikes in consumption.

Fabricio Mogrovejo, customer service and planning head of Bilbosa, an Ecuadorian shrimp processor and exporter based in Manta, in the Manabi province, has already observed an increase in shrimp prices attributed to a shortage of certain sizes.

READ MORE
OCT 15:56 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Argentina’s shrimp catches could reach a new record this year

Argentina’s deputy secretary of aquatic resources and fisheries, Juan Antonio Lopez Cazorla, told Undercurrent News the country’s shrimp production is poised for a potentially record-breaking year.

“Argentina’s shrimp catches are increasing. This year, they could harvest 200,000t, which would be a record,” he said. “Despite issues with the unions, we have already caught 170,000t and the season in provincial waters hasn’t started yet,” he noted.

READ MORE
OCT 15:18 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Spain’s Wofco to process whitefish from Norway’s Bluewild, moves headquarters to Fandicosta’s plant

Spanish firm Worldwide Fishing Company, also known as WOFCO, and Norwegian frozen cod and haddock supplier Bluewild have entered into a strategic partnership, they announced. 

They aim to “provide consumers with a new quality benchmark in seafood products from the North Atlantic,” they said. 

READ MORE
SEP 301:46 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Viciunai anticipates record 30% growth in 2024 amid rising consumer demand

Lithuanian firm Viciunai Group is poised to achieve a 30% growth in sales this year, driven by an increasing consumer demand for high-quality, innovative food products. 

This anticipated surge would mark “a significant milestone” for the company, following a consistent five-year average growth of 15%, it announced. 

READ MORE
SEP 301:00 PM GMT
By María Feijóo
Spanish minister wants priority on sustainability, economic viability in fisheries management

At the closing of the 12th Conxemar-FAO Congress in Vigo, in northern Spain, the country’s fisheries minister, Luis Planas, addressed “a pivotal challenge” facing the global fishing sector: the need for the EU to adopt “a more balanced approach to fisheries management that prioritizes both sustainability and economic viability.”

This call to action came amid increasing concerns about the future of marine resources and the livelihoods of fishing communities.

READ MORE
SEP 304:43 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Global fisheries and aquaculture reach record high output, aquaculture surpasses capture

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has announced that global fisheries and aquaculture production hit an all-time high in 2022, with animal aquaculture volumes surpassing capture fisheries for the first time.

Audun Lem, FAO’s deputy director of fisheries and aquaculture, presented at the Conxemar congress the 2024 edition of the state of world fisheries and aquaculture report, also known as SOFIA, which analyzes the world’s official seafood production data.

READ MORE

title: GAPP meeting: Trident sees crab stick sales grow amid Japan’s seafood declining consumption; Global H1 surimi output estimated down 10.5%
content:
SEATTLE, Washington, US -- Undercurrent News blogged live from the annual meeting of the Genuine Alaska Pollock Producers (GAPP), held in Seattle, Washington. 

The GAPP meeting, which took place in the W Seattle hotel, comes amid a time of unprecedented turmoil for the US sector, which is engaged in a market battle with Russia on fillets and surimi.

Auto updates: On
SEP 267:40 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Trident sees crab stick sales grow amid Japan’s declining seafood consumption

Japan’s seafood consumption has hit a record low, driven by rising prices and a reduction in domestic catches, Japanese panelists told the audience.

Trident Seafoods, however, has experienced significant growth in its crab stick product sales in the country, according to Toshihiro Tsunetaka of Trident Seafoods Japan.

READ MORE
SEP 267:22 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan consumes 40,000t of pollock roe per year

The global output of pollock roe was estimated at 50,000 metric tons in 2023, according to the presentation by Tatsuya Gake, representing Japanese seafood giant Nissui Corp.

Japan emerged as the dominant consumer, accounting for 40,000t, while South Korea consumed the remaining 10,000t, he said,.

READ MORE
SEP 265:37 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Global H1 surimi output estimated down 10.5% to 383,600t 

Global surimi production is projected to reach 383,600 metric tons in the first half of 2024, a decline of 10.5% compared to the previous year, according to a presentation by Angel Rubio of Expana.

Alaska’s pollock surimi production up to statistical week 37 remains steady at 162,700t but has been downward since 2017.

READ MORE
SEP 265:23 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Angulas Aguinaga launches Japanese-themed surimi products to stem consumption slide

Spain’s Angulas Aguinaga has launched surimi products with a Japanese theme to stem dropping consumption in the country.

The company is offering surimi noodles and sticks with a teriyaki flavor to gain more “younger consumers,” said the company’s Yaiza Donaire.

READ MORE
SEP 264:30 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
US pollock fillet exports surge 26% while surimi remains flat

Alaska pollock fillet exports surged to 59,570 metric tons in the first seven months of this year, marking a 26% year-on-year increase, with production up by 11% as of Sept. 7, according to the presentation by Ron Rogness of GAPP.

Surimi exports through July were relatively stable compared to last year, although production has decreased by 3,000t through Sept. 14.

READ MORE
SEP 264:19 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Pollock fishery in Bering Sea approaches quota, with closure in central Gulf of Alaska

Ron Rogness, representing GAPP, described the Alaskan pollock fishery in the Bering Sea as more “deliberate” during the 2024 B season, particularly for the catcher-processor sector.

According to the National Marine Fisheries Service figures, the region’s total catches reached 93.6% of the quota through Sept. 14.

READ MORE
SEP 262:52 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Alaska pollock closes awareness gap with cod, tilapia

Alaska pollock has pulled ahead of haddock in terms of consumer awareness and is closing the gap with cod and tilapia, said Lauren Hasse of Ketchum Analytics.

Pollock “continues to outpace haddock on familiarity, positive opinion and intent to eat,” said Hasse.

READ MORE
SEP 261:47 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Alaskan pollock industry drives global expansion with $9.5m partnership program, says GAPP CEO

Craig Morris, CEO of the Association of Genuine Alaska Pollock Producers (GAPP), emphasized the pivotal role of the GAPP partnership program in driving the growth of the Alaskan pollock industry during his speech.

Morris said that since marking its five-year milestone earlier this year, the partnership program had invested $9.5 million across nearly 100 collaborations, which have helped introduce Alaska pollock into new products and menus worldwide.

READ MORE
SEP 261:30 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Sullivan ‘making progress’ on stopping EU using ‘Alaska’ on Russian pollock

US lawmakers are making headway on changing the labeling of Russian pollock as “Alaska” in Europe, said senator Dan Sullivan.

Even before the full ban on Russian seafood, even when processed in third countries, only US pollock could be called “Alaskan.”

READ MORE
SEP 261:28 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
US senator Sullivan: Canada ‘very interested’ in Russian seafood ban

Canada is “very interested” in banning Russian seafood, according to US senator Dan Sullivan.

Sullivan told the audience at the GAPP conference that a recent meeting with Justin Trudeau, the prime minister of Canada, was fruitful.

READ MORE
SEP 261:06 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Global Seas’ Desautel laments costs of vessel building in US

Bob Desautel, the CEO of pollock catcher boat operator Global Seas and the current chairman of GAPP, said the US sector “needs some help” when it comes to building new vessels in the country.

The cost of building a factory trawler in the US is $300 million, while the same vessel would be $100m in Turkey, for example, said Desautel.

READ MORE
SEP 2612:09 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
‘Shocking’ Europe still purchasing Russian pollock, says Alaska senator Murkowski

A priority of Alaskan senator Lisa Murkowski is to get its allies to stop buying Russian pollock, she told the GAPP conference. 

Europe, “shockingly,” continues to do so, she said.

READ MORE

Contact the author tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com

title: Icefish/Fish Waste for Profit blog: Iceland cluster plans own fund; Aurora Abalone plans harvests by 2027
content:
REYKJAVIK, ICELAND -- Undercurrent News was live from the Icefish expo and the Fish Waste for Profit conference, running Sept. 18-20 in Reykjavik, Iceland.

The Icelandic Fisheries, Seafood & Aqua Exhibition (to give it its full title) is the longest-running international fishing exhibition in Iceland. First held in 1984, the expo has developed into a "showcase of every aspect of the commercial fishing industry and seafood sector," said its organizers.

Then the Fish Waste for Profit event, which began Sept. 19, provided attendees with knowledge on how to maximize their return on investment from potentially discarded parts of the catch that can be turned into high-value products for non-food sectors.

Auto updates: On
SEP 201:05 PM GMT
UK’s Ace Aquatec wins by-product innovation award for role in harvesting ‘too-small’ salmon

UK aquaculture technology firm Ace Aquatec has been recognized in the 2024 Icelandic Fisheries Awards — on its first trip to Icefish — for its role in developing harvests of farmed salmon “too small” for conventional markets.

Perhaps 10% of salmon raised from each batch of eggs are never going to catch up in size to the rest and will be too small for conventional harvesting, Ace’s head of sales, Ben Perry, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
SEP 2012:45 PM GMT
Delayed but not defeated: Aurora Abalone plans harvests by 2027

Icelandic aquaculture firm Aurora Abalone is still operating in the town of Grindavik, despite the ongoing volcanic eruption that began in November 2023, said CEO Vala Valthorsdottir.

“It’s like a ghost town, but thanks to a very quick and agile government, the water and power were restored, and it has only delayed us,” she said.

READ MORE
SEP 2012:19 PM GMT
Canadian by-product upcycling business wants to merge with or buy seafood processor to scale up

Newfoundland, Canada-based by-product upcycler 3F Waste Recovery is planning to merge with or purchase a seafood processor in order to scale up its business, said Ben Wiper, founder and CEO.

The company takes the traditional waste sidestreams from cod processing and turns them into valuable products, with its chief technology a “plug and play” system that allows processors to turn their skins into 99% marine collagen, branded CleanCollagen.

READ MORE
SEP 2012:02 PM GMT
With cash for start-ups hard to come by, Iceland seafood cluster plans fund

Seafood sector start-ups often find that cash and investors for businesses that are only on the cusp of realization is hard to come by.

That’s why the Iceland Ocean Cluster (IOC) intends to establish an investment fund of its own, revealed Kristinn Thor Sigurdsson, project manager at the cluster.

READ MORE
SEP 207:19 AM GMT
Processing ‘wastewater’ one of the ‘high-hanging fruits’ of the 100% fish proposal

One project being worked on by Icelandic research body Matis is a particularly challenging one — utilizing the wastewater from fish processing, said project manager Hildur Inga Sveinsdottir.

For Iceland’s catch of Atlantic cod (which came to 220,000 metric tons in 2023), the “sidestream” of potentially useful materials is around 6,600t wet weight or 1,000t dry, diluted in “at least 3 million [metric] tons of water,” she said.

READ MORE
SEP 206:40 AM GMT
Danish seafood cluster to launch this month

The Danish Ocean Cluster is finally due to officially open next week after first being announced in the summer of 2022.

It has been launched as a collaboration between the Port of Hirtshals and the North Sea Science Park, and will have 30 participants at opening with a further 20 interested, said a representative at the Fish Waste for Profit conference, Mette Roussis.

READ MORE
SEP 206:32 AM GMT
Latest ‘100% fish’ proposals include Pacific Islands tuna, Royal Greenland-linked shrimp effort

Icelandic cod has become the figurehead for the “100% fish” movement — thanks in large part to the work of Thor Sigfusson and the Iceland Ocean Cluster he founded — but various other projects are now in the works worldwide.

Clara Jegousse, a research project manager at the Iceland cluster, revealed that just this morning (Sept. 20), a proposal was submitted for the valorization of sidestreams from coldwater shrimp. That’s been done in conjunction with Royal Greenland and Icelandic chitosan producer Primex.

READ MORE
SEP 206:19 AM GMT
‘Pulled salmon’ can be processors’ most affordable, most profitable product offering

As reported earlier this month, Finnish biotechnology firm Hailia launched its first salmonid product at retail earlier this year; initial sales and feedback have been good, said Michaela Lindstrom, managing director and founding partner at the start-up.

Its patent-pending technology takes trout frames — bones, fins, muscle tissue and any meat left on those — and via a chemical-free “novel reforming,” creates a “pulled trout” that is ready-to-eat. The reforming gives the final product the texture of fillets, the firm says.

READ MORE
SEP 1912:18 PM GMT
Scotland needs its own seafood cluster

Scotland would benefit from its own seafood hub or cluster to work on maximizing the value of its sector, said Donna Fordyce, chief executive of Seafood Scotland.

The industry body is involved in talks to drill down into establishing exactly what is landed in Scotland, in what volumes, auditing what companies do with their by-products and where opportunities lie, she said.

READ MORE
SEP 1911:24 AM GMT
There remains a profitability case for an Atlantic Canada chitin plant

In Atlantic Canada, despite ample resources, there are no crustacean waste processing plants remaining.

If we look at coldwater shrimp catches, the fishery is in decline, and thus, so are the volumes of shells. But if crab and lobster shells are factored in, volumes are plentiful, noted Francis Desilets-Mayer, a researcher with research group Merinov.

READ MORE
SEP 1910:13 AM GMT
‘Our fish skins are worth more than $2,000 each — they’re not waste’

Iceland’s first “unicorn” — a start-up business valued at over $1 billion — is living proof that 100% fish utilization has some gems waiting to be uncovered.

The company, which created fish skin grafts for human healthcare, was bought by Danish multinational Coloplast in 2023 for up to $1.3bn, of which $1.2bn was an upfront cash payment.

READ MORE
SEP 199:41 AM GMT
PBS documentary ‘Hope in the Water’ to raise awareness of full fish utilization

A documentary first shown on US television channel PBS is set to bring the notion of 100% fish utilization to a wider audience, said Thor Sigfusson, founder and chairman of the Iceland Ocean Cluster.

The show — “from Emmy Award producer Andrew Zimmern, in collaboration with multi-award-winner and storytelling visionary David E. Kelley” — showcases a number of sustainable seafood case studies. The seafood industry will recognize some featured, such as Simply Shrimp in Minnesota, the Cultured Abalone Farm, and the work of Dr Loc Tran in Vietnam.

READ MORE
SEP 199:24 AM GMT
Turning ‘troublemaking’ zooplankton into valuable aquafeed

Zooplankton looks like it could be a useful and more sustainable alternative to fishmeal and oil in feeding farmed fish, but there are concerns over the harvesting of species that form an important part of the ocean’s food chains, noted Stefan Thor Eysteinsson, research group leader at Iceland’s Matis.

One answer to that could also prove a boon to the pelagics sector: removing zooplankton (in this case, calanus finmarchicus) from commercial mackerel hauls before it impacts the quality of that fish.

READ MORE
SEP 198:02 AM GMT
Norwegian startup invests in plant for whitefish-derived collagen, protein

Norwegian company Pretio has invested in and is now constructing a commercial-scale plant in Alesund to produce collagen and proteins derived from waste from the whitefish sector, said CEO Rune Frostad.

The factory will require some 10,000 metric tons of raw materials, chiefly fish bones, and Pretio is looking for fishing partners both in Norway and worldwide, said Frostad.

READ MORE
SEP 197:35 AM GMT
After Leroy investment, Salmonics plans to launch salmon blood-derived healthcare products

Maine, US-based Salmonics is looking to launch more human and animal healthcare products derived from the blood of farmed salmon, having taken investment from Norway’s Leroy Seafood Group this summer.

Of 2.7 million metric tons of farmed salmon globally, there are around 50,000t of blood produced, and largely wasted now, said Salmonics CEO Cem Giray.

READ MORE
SEP 196:45 AM GMT
Royal Greenland seeks strategic partnerships to utilize more of its raw materials

North Atlantic seafood firm Royal Greenland is keen to make more use of its raw materials, but the logistics of Greenland make it tricky, noted director Kristian Ottesen.

With essentially no safe roads between townships, and it neither practical nor green to fly “secondary” materials around the country, the best route for the company is to find specialized strategic partners, he said.

READ MORE
SEP 196:01 AM GMT
Namibia’s ocean cluster eyes collagen, gelatin from hake skins

The Namibian Ocean Cluster — the most recent of the “100% fish” centers to open, earlier this year — has embarked on a project to utilize every aspect of the huge volumes of hake caught in the country, said Iceland Ocean Cluster’s CEO, Alexandra Leeper.

“Namibia catches huge volumes of hake, but a lot of that is lost at the processing and even the fishing stage,” she said.

READ MORE
SEP 195:50 AM GMT
Iceland ‘100% fish’ cluster working with under-development land-based salmon sector

Reykjavik’s Iceland Ocean Cluster is keen to ensure the country’s growing salmon aquaculture sector embraces the “100% fish” circular economy potential of seafood “waste.”

Its CEO, Alexandra Leeper, told attendees at the Fish Waste for Profit conference that conversations have begun with the sector, highlighting work to utilize “sludge” — uneaten feed and fish feces. 

READ MORE
SEP 182:39 PM GMT
Barents Sea cod catch cuts push up production costs for Iceland’s saltfish

The impact of reductions in cod catching in the Barents Sea has certainly been felt by Iceland’s salted fish industry, according to Vinnslustodin (VSV)’s head of groundfish, Sverrir Haraldsson.

“There have been several cuts in the quotas, so the pressure has been there on all markets. Raw material prices that we pay are definitely up.”

READ MORE
SEP 1812:24 PM GMT
VSV aims to start using new building early in 2025

Icelandic fishing and processing firm Vinnslustodin (VSV) is aiming to move into and begin using a new building at its main site early in 2025, head of groundfish Sverrir Haraldsson told Undercurrent News.

The new — almost 6,000-square-meter, two-story — addition to VSV’s base in Vestmannaeyjabaer, on the island of Vestmannaeyjar, will house and consolidate some of its whitefish and pelagic processing operations. 

READ MORE
SEP 189:18 AM GMT
Scotland’s Gael Force seeks export manager, new markets

Scottish aquaculture equipment and technology supplier Gael Force Group is looking for a new export sales manager, among other roles, as it continues to look to expand its markets, group sales director Jamie Young told Undercurrent News.

The company is at Icefish for the first time, doing some market research into Iceland’s salmon-farming sector, he said, noting it was one place where said business is growing rather than becoming a little stagnant, as elsewhere. 

READ MORE
SEP 187:55 AM GMT
New Canadian redfish quota prompts demand for processing tech

The May 2024 announcement from Fisheries and Oceans Canada for a new 2024-2025 quota and management plan for redfish has sparked a high interest in new processing equipment on the east coast, Camille Gagne — sales manager for Carsoe in Canada and the US — told Undercurrent News.

The government has announced a total allowable catch of 60,000 metric tons, increased from an initial 25,000t, in a move which came as something of a surprise, she said.

READ MORE
SEP 187:47 AM GMT
‘Ship of the year’ Ecofive conducts pilot fishing

New vessel Ecofive — operated by Norway’s Bluewild, designed by Ulstein Design & Solution, and initially built by Norse Shipyard in Turkey — will continue to conduct trial fishing later this year, Ahmet Colak, shipyard manager with Norse, told Undercurrent News.

The vessel was the first fishing new-build to be awarded “ship of the year” by the Nor-Shipping exhibition in 2023, with the awarding jury stating the ship offers “ground-breaking technology with several innovations for a greener fishing fleet.”

READ MORE
SEP 185:15 AM GMT
AKVA-supplied Laxey hatchery takes in third egg batch

Land-based salmon farming project Laxey’s hatchery facility on the archipelago of Vestmannaeyjar is operating well, having taken its third batch of eggs in July, executives told Undercurrent News.

AKVA group constructed the turnkey system within an interior-designed, 8,500-square-meter system in the harbor of Vestmannaeyjabaer. 

READ MORE
SEP 184:49 AM GMT
Fishing association angry as gov’t discusses higher taxes

Iceland’s association of fishing companies, which goes by SFS, has slammed talk by the government of increasing the taxes faced by the country’s seafood companies.

A recently commissioned report found that when the current fishing fees are added to income tax and a capital income tax on dividends, the effective income tax due on fishing firms is 58% of the profit.

READ MORE

title: Recap GSF: Indian shrimp farm area drops, volume could remain stable, says Aqua Exchange CEO
content:
UTRECHT, the Netherlands -- Undercurrent News was reporting live from the Global Shrimp Forum (GSF), held Sept. 3-5 in Utrecht, the Netherlands. 

See all GSF coverage below. To recap last year's GSF coverage from Undercurrent, click here. 

Auto updates: On
SEP 64:04 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Indian shrimp fragmentation compared to Ecuador laid bare

There are 150 Indian shrimp firms exporting over 1,000 metric tons, compared to only 50 in Ecuador, where the sector is consolidated into the hands of a small number of very large players, according to data presented at GSF.

The top three players in India only make up 10% of exports, whereas they are 39% in Ecuador, according to data from Shrimp Insights and Gluna Shrimp, the consulting companies owned by Willem van der Pijl, managing director of the Global Shrimp Forum Foundation, the GSF organizer, and Gabriel Luna, a sector veteran.

READ MORE
SEP 63:46 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Indian shrimp farm area drops, volume could remain stable, says AquaExchange CEO

The quantity of Indian shrimp farms is dropping, and post-larvae (PL) sales are down, but this does not mean output will decline, said the founder of a hardware and software supplier to the sector.

Pavan Kosaraju, CEO and founder of India’s AquaExchange Agritech, told Undercurrent News on the GSF sidelines that his forecast is based on data collected from the industry. AquaExchange has a good overview derived from working with 18% of the market.

READ MORE
SEP 510:47 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Exporters to China need downstream foothold, advises consultant

The future of China’s growing shrimp import trade lies downstream, according to independent consultant Fang Qing.

The downstream processes of the Chinese market are currently something of a black box, he explained.

READ MORE
SEP 510:39 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
China’s 2024 shrimp production from greenhouses alone could be 700,000t

Chinese shrimp production from “greenhouses,” which enable farming in the colder northeast, could be as much as 700,000 metric tons in 2024, said one sector expert at GSF.

Luca Micciche, aquaculture technical director and global business development manager with US-based Verdesian Life Sciences, estimates greenhouse account for 28% of China’s total production, which he pins at 2.5 million metric tons.

READ MORE
SEP 59:13 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
New US tariffs to rapidly follow if Trump wins election, analyst warns

Brought in to provide a broader roundup of current economic trends, Jan Lambregts, head of RaboResearch global economics and markets at Dutch bank Rabobank, noted that if the shrimp sector should keep its eyes on anything this year, it’s the US election.

“For most of you, the US election will be very important,” he described. “If [Donald] Trump wins, he will do some of these tariffs.”

READ MORE
SEP 58:48 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Walmart supplier Fishin’ hires veteran buyer from King & Prince

Walmart-focused US importer The Fishin’ Company has hired a seafood sector veteran, Jay Jayendran Muthushankar, as its global director of procurement.

Muthushankar, who was involved in a panel at GSF giving feedback to seafood sector startups, joined Fishin’ from Nissui Corp.-owned King & Prince Seafood in August, according to his LinkedIn profile.

READ MORE
SEP 58:42 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
CenSea’s Torch notes low shrimp prices haven’t stopped decline in US consumption

Even with a prolonged period of low prices, US shrimp imports are set to fall for the third successive year, according to a forecast from the GSF presented on Wednesday.

“We are not selling enough shrimp. Even with record-low prices, it hasn’t done anything to drive consumption,” said Nate Torch, co-president of Central Seaway Company (CenSea), a $350-million-turnover US shrimp importer snapped up by India’s Captain Fresh earlier this year.

READ MORE
SEP 57:42 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Shrimp tech, genetics investments up sharply since pandemic

Presenting data sourced from Undercurrent News’ extensive M&A database, Rabobank analyst Gorjan Nikolik noted that deals for tech companies in the shrimp sector have risen significantly since the pandemic.

While downstream transactions remain the main target sector — accounting for 24 of the 41 M&A deals and investments recorded in 2023 — 15 of the remainder came in the tech and genetics, or “peripheral,” sectors.

READ MORE
SEP 53:05 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Biggest soybean surplus ever expected in next 12 months

Excellent harvests and insufficient demand are set to produce the biggest soybean surplus ever recorded in the next financial year, according to Carlos Mera, managing director of Rabobank’s agri-commodity research division.

“Conditions are excellent in the US,” he said. “Especially when we look at the maximization of the soybean areas in the US, we are expecting a record crop. We passed the peak of the corn weather risk in July, and the peak of soybean risk in August, so so far, so good.”

READ MORE
SEP 52:49 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
India shrimp leader: I wish production was going down, but it isn’t

While Robins McIntosh, senior vice president of Thailand’s Charoen Pokphand Foods, predicts a drop in Indian production, the sentiment from GSF is that output will be up (see blog post here).

“I wish production would drop,” said Balasubramaniam V, general secretary of the Prawn Farmers Federation of India, a farmers’ association, on a panel at GSF.

READ MORE
SEP 52:35 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Indonesian shrimp price crisis means only most efficient can survive

The low global shrimp prices and disease issues in Indonesia are seeing some farmers lose large sums of money and look for a way out, said one operator whose company is performing well in these tough times.

There are “two sides” to the current situation, said Rizky Darmawan, founder and president of PMI, the Indonesian young farmers’ association, and CEO of trader Delta Marine Group.

READ MORE
SEP 43:23 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
European shrimp customers move from Asia to ‘more sustainable’ Latam

More end buyers in Europe are requesting suppliers move from Asia shrimp to Latin America due to sustainability concerns, said the commercial director of a large Dutch processor.

“There is stable demand in Europe for shrimp. What we see on supply is [imports from] Latin America going up, Asia going down,” said Jan Bootsman of Klaas Puul, which is part of the UK’s Sykes Seafood Group.

READ MORE
SEP 412:04 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Startup seeks to solve shrimp’s ‘black box’ biomass problem

Minnowtech Technologies is seeking to solve the “biomass problem” that impacts all shrimp farmers, Suzan Shahrestani, its co-founder, told the audience at a GSF breakout session on technology in the sector.

“Shrimp farming is a black box, as farmers do not know how much they have in their ponds,” Shahrestani told a panel about technological innovations in the sector.

READ MORE
SEP 412:02 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Former aerospace engineer uses satellites to map shrimp ponds

Suyash Singh, an Indian entrepreneur who is an aerospace engineer by background, has mapped 300,000 shrimp ponds across India using satellites with his GalaxEye startup, he told the audience at GSF.

Singh, whose company announced at the start of August that $6.5 million had been raised in an ongoing series A, said his GalaxEye Blue product could give users analytics on a country down to the village level and more visibility on supply availability forecasting.

READ MORE
SEP 48:45 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Are Chinese shrimp farmers being impacted by imported volumes?

Chinese shrimp farmers face a challenging year ahead, with panelists at GSF citing increased imports of vannamei from Ecuador, India and Vietnam as a headwind.

Another, however, said the market for locally farmed live shrimp is not competing with the imports.

READ MORE
SEP 48:40 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
US-focused Indonesia’s shrimp export drop set to get deeper, Vietnam to grow again

Indonesian shrimp exports, which are mainly focused on the US, are set to drop by an even bigger margin than predicted at the GSF, said Aris Utama, a director of Bumi Menara Internusa (BMI), a large processor.

Meanwhile, Vietnamese exports are set to increase in the second half after stability in H1, said Nguyen Hoang Liem, vice general director of Minh Phu Seafood Group, on the import and export panel at GSF on Wednesday morning.

READ MORE
SEP 46:01 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China’s import market enters new ‘cautious era’

China’s shrimp imports declined for the fourth consecutive quarter in 2024, marking a new era of cautious purchasing in the vast market, according to a panel of experts.

Despite importing a record 1 million metric tons of shrimp in 2023, imports declined in the 12 months to the end of June, according to Willem van der Pijl, managing director of the Global Shrimp Forum Foundation.

READ MORE
SEP 44:47 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
US duties likely to reduce Ecuador trade volumes, but buyers will adjust, says Luna

Ecuador’s shrimp exports to the US are being impacted by the preliminary US antidumping and countervailing (CVD) duties, said Gabriel Luna, an Ecuadorian shrimp procurement specialist. 

US imports of shrimp from Ecuador have a preliminary CVD rate of 2.89% on top of an antidumping rate of 10.58%, and the duties have certainly impacted exports to the market. 

READ MORE
SEP 44:20 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Ecuador production slowing, but 10% growth still forecast for H2

According to data collected by the Global Shrimp Forum Foundation and presented by Willem van der Pijl, Ecuador is still on track for further volume growth in H2, even as its export boom finally slows down.

Van der Pijl showed how first half export volumes from the country increased just 2% year-on-year, even as Q2 sales from Ecuador hit an all time quarterly record of 344,000 metric tons.

READ MORE
SEP 44:05 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
New players, Chinese demand prop up Indian shrimp exports

Sarabpreet Singh, general manager at one of India’s largest shrimp exporters, Devi Seafoods, gave his take on why shrimp exports continued to keep pace with 2023 through H1 in spite of rock-bottom prices and farmer apathy.

“Last year, new players came into the market and existing players went for capacity expansions, then since this year that new capacity became operational,” Singh explained.

READ MORE
SEP 43:53 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Indian H2 production expected to follow usual curve

Despite sentiment within the industry that Indian vannamei production will drop off in the second half of the year, satellite and export data suggests that 2024’s harvest volumes are likely to be in line with those of last year, according to Global Shrimp Forum Foundation managing director Willem van der Pijl.

The forum’s co-founder believes that another 5% year-on-year increase in shrimp exports is expected from India this year, giving a loose volume estimate of 734,000 metric tons — in line with the previous peak of 2021.

READ MORE
SEP 41:26 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
BioMar CEO: Farmed shrimp has potential for lower carbon footprint than salmon

Ecuadorian farmed shrimp currently has a marginally higher carbon footprint than Norwegian salmon, said Carlos Diaz, CEO of feed producer BioMar Group.

Delivering a presentation on what the shrimp farming sector can learn from salmon, Diaz said the former has a lot of potential.

READ MORE
SEP 312:03 PM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Global Shrimp Council ad campaign to hit US in ‘early 2025,’ urges industry to join

Kicking off the plenary session on the first day of the forum, Global Shrimp Council co-founders Gabriel Luna and David Castro presented the current status of the council.

“The very first thing is we are going to start a jumpstart campaign in early 2025, but we don’t know yet if it’s Q1 or Q2,” said Luna. “Start a campaign with jumpstart funding, which won’t be our long-term funding, but will be a funding which we are discussing at the moment.”

READ MORE
SEP 311:20 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
eFishery, Monterey Bay working to tackle shrimp’s ‘financial apartheid’

It’s a well-known issue of South Asia’s shrimp sector that there are a handful of major farmers and thousands upon thousands of small-scale operators who account for well over 90% of production.

And while larger farmers have the necessary capital to pursue certifications, most don’t. According to Cameron Maclean, head of shrimp supply chains at Indonesia’s eFishery, only about 63 of Indonesia’s total shrimp farmers have internationally recognized certification.

READ MORE
SEP 38:56 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Cooke, Krustagroup execs eagerly anticipate upcoming MSC approval for Argentine shrimp

The European shellfish supply arm of Canadian seafood giant Cooke hopes the in-shore red shrimp fishery in Argentina will be Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) certified by the end of 2024.

Ralph Sanders (below), purchase and trade manager with Cooke-Morubel, added the offshore fishery is expected to be certified by mid-2025, said during the GSF wild catch panel.

READ MORE
SEP 37:32 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Global Shrimp Council looks for first wild member, aims to be on Super Bowl in five years

The Global Shrimp Council (GSC) is looking for its first wild-catch member for a campaign that will hit the market next year, said Miguel Barcenas, a veteran marketing consultant who is the creator of the well-known “Avocados from Mexico” campaign.

So far, the group has 43 members, mostly farmers from Ecuador, India, Indonesia, Mexico and Vietnam, but “no wild-caught members.” In avocados, where genetic marketing has seen volume and value rocket, 90 packing houses and 36,000 growers are investing.

READ MORE
SEP 36:58 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Coldwater shrimp production shifts fast to shell-on, but prices under pressure in China

The coldwater shrimp sector is moving fast toward more shell-on production at the expense of cooked and peeled, but prices are under pressure in China, the main market, said Joanna Hutchins of Royal Greenland during the GSF.

Looking at the sales split to Asia and Europe, the percentage has shifted to 70/30 in favor of Asia, compared to 45/55 in only 2021. “This is happening fast. You’re looking at a three-year chart here,” said Hutchins, executive vice president of marketing, innovation and sustainability for Royal Greenland.

READ MORE
SEP 36:13 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Bangladesh’s move to vannamei threatens black tiger ops, says Lenk

Asked on whether the future of shrimp farming in Asia was an inevitable move to intensive production, Heiko Lenk, managing director of Bangladesh-based Lenk Frozen Foods, believes the country’s efforts to add vannamei to its output is misguided.

“As far as Bangladesh is concerned, it’s the ideal environment for extensive farming near the Sundarbans,” he said, referring to Lenk’s black tiger shrimp production clusters in the region. “I don’t see that there is any scope for doing any intensive farming in Bangladesh.”

READ MORE
SEP 34:31 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
McIntosh adjusts 2024 global shrimp production forecast down with outlook for next year uncertain

Drops in production from the three largest shrimp farming countries in the world will see global output of black tiger and vannamei come down around 5% year-on-year to 4.89 million metric tons, according to the latest forecast from an industry expert.

With four months left of the year, Robins McIntosh, senior vice president of Thailand’s Charoen Pokphand Group, is predicting output from China, Ecuador and India will all be down this year, seeing global output drop some 260,000t.

READ MORE
