title: Untitled
content:
SHANGHAI, China — Undercurrent News reported live from the 18th edition of the Shanghai International Fisheries and Seafood Exhibition (SIFSE), held at the Shanghai New International Expo Center from Aug. 28 to 30.

This year's event spanned 180,000 square meters, featuring over 4,000 exhibitors and 40 industry-related activities. The exhibition, also known as World Seafood Shanghai, showcases a wide array of aquatic and marine products from around the globe.

Last year, SIFSE drew 106,635 professionals from 67 countries and regions.

Check below to recap all the updates.

Auto updates: On
AUG 304:37 AM GMT
Ecuadorian vannamei production expected to remain flat or ‘even lower’ in 2024, says Omarsa CEO

The Ecuadorian vannamei shrimp production in 2024 is expected to remain “stable” compared to a previous year, or potentially “even lower,” Sandro Coglitore, CEO of Omarsa, the country’s second-largest shrimp producer, told Undercurrent News.

“Production in 2024 will never go up,” said Coglitore. He attributed the stagnation to a combination of factors, including cold weather and declining prices in major markets, which have led to decreased investment in harvesting efforts.

READ MORE
AUG 303:28 AM GMT
Japan’s Kibun Foods shifts sourcing to Thai surimi products for Chinese market amid seafood ban

Japan’s Kibun Foods, the world’s leading finished surimi processor by revenue, has shifted its sourcing primarily to its Thai plants for the Chinese market, according to Tei Saya, CEO of Kibun China Co., who spoke with Undercurrent News.

The move comes in response to China’s comprehensive ban on Japanese seafood, including finished surimi products, following the release of treated water from the Fukushima nuclear plant.

READ MORE
AUG 302:26 AM GMT
Santa Priscila sees shift in shrimp exports from China to US 

Ecuador’s Industrial Pesquera Santa Priscila is shifting its export focus from China to the US, capitalizing on favorable pricing conditions, Nicole Mosquera, the export account coordinator for the company, told Undercurrent News.

“In July, we exported approximately 50-55% of our shrimp to China, but we’re now experiencing a shift, with over 50% of our shipments heading to the US,” she said.

READ MORE
AUG 301:56 AM GMT
China’s Atlantic salmon consumption expected to surge 35% by 2029, says NSC rep

The consumption of Atlantic salmon in China could potentially increase by 30-35% by 2029, Sigmund Bjorgo, the regional director for mainland China and Hong Kong at the Norwegian Seafood Council, told Undercurrent News.

His optimistic projections are supported by promising statistics revealing that from 2023 to 2029, the number of households capable of purchasing Atlantic salmon is expected to grow by 54 million.

READ MORE
AUG 301:14 AM GMT
Shanghai Xinjiangyang inks exclusive deal with Aussie Stehr Group for southern bluefin tuna in China

Shanghai Xinjiangyang has established a long-term contract with Australia’s Stehr Group to become the exclusive general agent for Australian southern bluefin tuna in China.

The announcement was officially made during the Shanghai International Fisheries and Seafood Exhibition, where Shanghai Xinjiangyang showcased fresh Australian southern bluefin tuna.

READ MORE
AUG 298:40 PM GMT
Norway’s Ode ventures into Eastern Asia with premium ‘snow cod’

Ode, a pioneering Norwegian cod farmer, is making inroads into the Eastern Asian market with its premium “snow cod” branding, Cathrin O. Rabben, a sales manager for the company, told Undercurrent News.

The company’s new target markets include the US and Eastern Asia, particularly China and Japan, alongside Southeast Asian nations like Thailand, Singapore, Vietnam and South Korea.

READ MORE
AUG 2910:05 AM GMT
Dani Group targets 20% sales growth in Chilean king crab in China

Spain’s Dani Group has been expanding its sales of Chilean king crab and toothfish in Asian markets, particularly in China, through its subsidiary, Pesquera Catalunya.

Victor Perez de Castro, managing director of Dani Foods—another subsidiary based in the UK—told Undercurrent News that the group aims to increase its sales volume of Chilean king crab to 700 metric tons this year, reflecting a 20% growth compared to 2023.

READ MORE
AUG 298:01 AM GMT
Ecuador dominates China’s vannamei imports with lowered prices 

At the Global Vannamei Shrimp Summit Forum, Jin Huang, CEO of DXD Supply Chain, showcased the remarkable surge in China’s vannamei shrimp imports over the past few years.

China’s total vannamei shrimp imports soared from 63,538 metric tons to 986,921t in 2023. This substantial growth is attributed to rising domestic demand and significant shifts within the global shrimp farming sector.

READ MORE
AUG 297:06 AM GMT
Greenhouse methods boost 23% of China’s vannamei production

At the Global Vannamei Shrimp Summit Forum, Li Yu, the founder and editor-in-chief of Farmed Shrimp World, shed light on the transformative impact of greenhouse farming within the Chinese vannamei shrimp industry despite the significant challenges. 

Greenhouse farming methods have resulted in increased production, becoming a vital element for a sector that is contending with a 30% decline in the availability of vannamei shrimp seedlings in 2024. 

READ MORE
AUG 2912:46 AM GMT
Chinese domestic canned tuna market grows to $87m

The Chinese domestic canned tuna product market is exhibiting potential for growth, despite recent fluctuations, Liu Yougan — chairperson of the China Canning Industry Association — said during his presentation at the International Tuna Industry (Shanghai) Summit Forum.

According to Liu, the canned tuna product market in China reached CNY 507 million ($71.1m) in 2015 and grew to CNY 565m in 2019, showing a steady but modest increase.

READ MORE
AUG 2811:31 PM GMT
China emerges as third largest tuna exporter, contributing 7% to global market

China is currently the third largest exporter of tuna products in the world, behind Thailand and Ecuador, as presented by Bill Holden, senior tuna fisheries outreach manager for the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC), at the International Tuna Industry (Shanghai) Summit Forum.

In 2022, China held a 7% share of the global tuna product export market, while Thailand dominated with 29% and Ecuador followed with 15%.

READ MORE
AUG 2811:05 PM GMT
China’s tuna catches hit 395,000t for 2023 

China’s tuna fishing industry reported a total catch of 395,000 metric tons in 2023, as highlighted by Xu Liuxiong, a professor at Shanghai Ocean University, during his presentation at the International Tuna Industry (Shanghai) Summit Forum.

Xu noted that last year’s harvest involved 49 fishing companies operating a total of 486 vessels. 

READ MORE
AUG 289:04 AM GMT
China’s Yantai Jinghai aims for 10,000t from offshore rainbow trout farming

Yantai Jinghai Marine Fishery, a prominent offshore rainbow trout farmer in China, is setting its sights on achieving a production capacity of 10,000 metric tons in the coming years. 

Ralph Zhang, the company’s assistant general manager, revealed the first “small” goal during his presentation at the Global Salmon Industry Development Summit.

READ MORE
AUG 286:52 AM GMT
Global land-based Atlantic salmon production expected to double to 40,000t in 2025

Global production of land-based Atlantic salmon farming is projected to double to approximately 40,000 metric tons in 2025, marking a 100% increase from an estimated 20,000t in 2024, Andreas Thourd, general manager of Nordic Aqua Partners, said during his presentation at the Global Salmon Industry Development Summit.

The 2025 anticipated production surge is driven by major land-based producers such as Andfjord Salmon, Nordic Aqua, and Gigante Salmon, all of whom are increasing their targeted harvests.

READ MORE
AUG 285:52 AM GMT
China drove record growth in AquaChile’s coho sales across Asia

The Chinese market for farmed Pacific or coho salmon is evolving rapidly, Rafa Tong, AquaChile’s sales director for Asia, said during his presentation at the Global Salmon Industry Development Summit.

As the world’s largest coho salmon producer, AquaChile reported an impressive 2,673 metric tons of coho salmon sold to the Chinese market during the 2022/23 season, a significant increase from just 929t for the previous year.

READ MORE
AUG 283:46 AM GMT
Chinese Atlantic market is largest in Asia, but per capita consumption remains low

Despite the Chinese Atlantic salmon market being the largest in Asia, its per capita consumption remains significantly low, said Sigmund Bjorgo, regional director for the Chinese mainland and Hong Kong at the Norwegian Seafood Council, during his presentation at the Global Salmon Industry Development Summit.

He added that it underscores a vast potential for future growth.

READ MORE
AUG 2711:51 PM GMT
Russia’s Antey expands Barents Sea live crab shipments to China with ‘reduced mortality rate’

Antey Group, Russia’s largest crab harvester, is ramping up its live crab shipments from the Barents Sea to the Chinese market, boasting a “reduced mortality rate,” Ivan Novikov, the company’s deputy CEO, told Undercurrent News.

The significant reduction in mortality rates can be attributed to advancements in technology, particularly the introduction of specialized boxes designed for air shipments, Novikov explained.

READ MORE
AUG 2711:49 PM GMT
China’s H1 seafood import hit second-highest despite price declines

China’s seafood imports for the first half of 2024 reached 2.17 million metric tons, valued at $8.63 billion, reflecting declines of 6.5% in quantity and 12.5% in value, according to trade statistics from the country’s customs.

This represents the second-highest level recorded for both volume and value.

READ MORE

title: Vietfish 2024: Pangasius business eyes Chinese demand for maws
content:
HO CHI MINH CITY, Vietnam -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, for the Vietfish trade show, held Aug. 21-23, 2024.

Keep checking back below for the latest updates.

Auto updates: On
AUG 231:46 AM GMT
Pangasius business eyes Chinese demand for maws as it widens byproduct usage

Vietnamese pangasius farmer and processor Nam Viet Joint Stock Company (more commonly known as Navico) is looking to commercialize fish maws in a quest to maximize its profits on as much of the fish as possible, assistant chairman Thien Doan told Undercurrent News.

“I see a lot of potential for the byproduct business, we have a lot of product that can still be used – the oil, the maws,” he said.

READ MORE
AUG 231:44 AM GMT
Fimex reports July shrimp export boom with lower supply expected

Vietnamese shrimp processor Sao Ta Foods (known as Fimex Vn) saw a boom in shrimp exports in July as customers sought to stock up ahead of what could be a period of lower supply, it said.

July saw the business surpass $30 million in export revenue, its highest single month for four years. Record months are to be expected, though, as it aims to double its 270 hectares of farming area by the end of 2025.

READ MORE
AUG 231:18 AM GMT
Tuna drives 2024 hike in Vietnam’s marine product exports to EU

Tuna has driven a 2024 hike in the sale of marine (non-aquaculture) products to the EU in the first seven months, according to data from the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers (VASEP).

Overall marine product exports dipped year-on-year in 2023 to just under $360 million. Some $176m of that was tuna.

READ MORE
AUG 2312:24 AM GMT
Trader eyes shift to domestic market for 2025

Ho Chi Minh City-based trader Tbesfood will be turning increased attention to the domestic Vietnamese market in 2025, managing director Hieu Kelly Nguyen told Undercurrent News.

The business was established in 2016 and trades in all of Vietnam’s seafood – though it has operated its own shrimp processor since 2020.

READ MORE
AUG 2312:19 AM GMT
Navico invests to automate pangasius production as far as possible

Vietnamese pangasius farmer and processor Nam Viet Joint Stock Company (more commonly known as Navico) is investing to modernize and automate as much of its supply chain as it can, assistant chairman Thien Doan told Undercurrent News.

Earlier this year, Navico increased its charter capital to more than VND 2.67 trillion ($104.7 million), surpassing the country’s largest pangasius exporter Vinh Hoan Seafood as the biggest such producer on the stock exchange in charter capital terms.

READ MORE
AUG 2210:20 PM GMT
VASEP: China, Middle East buying up large pangasius fillets

Chinese and Middle Eastern customers have been “aggressively” buying large-sized pangasius fillets since early July, driving up the farm-gate prices of the larger fish, according to the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers (VASEP).

For the fillets of 300 grams and above that these markets prefer, demand has been pushed up for pangasius harvest sizes of 1 kilogram and over, said VASEP communications director Le Hang. A 1kg fish can produce a 270g fillet.

READ MORE
AUG 2212:26 AM GMT
Vietnamese tuna supply to be squeezed in H2 2024, 2025

A government policy passed in 2024 has caused consternation among fishermen and parts of the Vietnamese seafood sector, with it seemingly putting a serious constraint on tuna supply.

Fishing representative Bui Thanh Ninh explained during the Vietfish conference program that new size restrictions on landings, including for tuna, meant fishermen faced being practically unable to catch skipjack during the key season of August and September.

READ MORE
AUG 2212:07 AM GMT
Crab sales to Japan buck trend as overall seafood consumption slips

Seafood consumption in Japan hit a record low of 22 kilograms per capita in 2022, and Vietnam has seen its marine products exports to the nearby nation slip in 2023 and so far in 2024.

Data from the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers (VASEP) showed a small dip in export value (for all non-aquacultured species) in 2023 after a strong growth to $1 billion in value in 2022.

READ MORE
AUG 2111:10 PM GMT
Gov’t strategy aims to rebalance Vietnam’s fisheries by 2030

Vietnam’s fisheries sector continues to steadily grow but with an imbalance between vessel capacity and resource availability, warned Le Trung Kien, chief of office at the country’s department of fisheries.

The Asian nation still has a “yellow card” warning from the EU over a perceived lack of action on illegal fishing — something the government aims to reverse under its current 2021-2030 “master plan.”

READ MORE
AUG 2110:40 PM GMT
Tomota data helped shape Minh Phu’s new shrimp farming strategy

The data gathered by tech firm Otanics Technology’s Tomota system directly helped to shape shrimp giant Minh Phu Seafood’s new aquaculture strategy, said CEO Vu Van Van.

The Vietnamese farmer’s chairman, Le Van Quang, is an outspoken proponent of adapting shrimp aquaculture to the best possible new practices and research. It has switched from a “2-3-4” model this year to what it calls “MPBio” – a policy that uses the large amounts of data gathered by Tomota, in which it has invested.

READ MORE
AUG 2110:31 PM GMT
Vietnam keen to explore marine farming growth

The Vietnamese government is keen to explore the potential for widening its aquaculture production from pangasius and shrimp to marine-farmed species, according to Dang Phuong Lien, a senior advisor with the commercial section of Norway’s Embassy in Hanoi.

The sector remains nascent, with only one industrial-scale business in the shape of Australis Aquaculture. Several other big businesses had gotten as far as applying for licenses before the COVID-19 pandemic put the dampers on development, Dang told Undercurrent News.


READ MORE
AUG 215:15 AM GMT
Retail policy shapes CP’s shrimp hatchery efforts

Charoen Pokphand Foods (CP)’s Vietnamese shrimp hatchery is investigating alternative sources for feed ingredients, with Nguyen Van Cong of subsidiary Advanced Aquaculture Vietnam Company (AAVN) citing sustainability policies set by UK retailer Tesco.

Tesco has said it will work with its supply base to “support the reduction of wild-sourced fishmeal and fish oil used in diets, to ensure that all of our suppliers obtain a forage fish and oil dependency ratios of less than one.”

READ MORE
AUG 214:24 AM GMT
Minh Phu-backed shrimp tech firm eyes $10m fundraise by Q1 2025

Otanics Technology — a shrimp technology firm backed by Minh Phu Seafood — remains in talks with investors to raise $10 million to finance further international expansion, the company’s Nguyen Hoang Liem told Undercurrent News.

Final decisions are expected “very soon,” he said — perhaps in the final quarter of 2024, or the first of 2025.

READ MORE
AUG 212:39 AM GMT
Norway’s Optimar meeting Vietnamese firms with electrical stunning on verge of being required practice

Norwegian processing system supplier Optimar is in Vietnam as part of a mission organized by Innovation Norway and the Norwegian Embassy in Hanoi, meeting shrimp and pangasius suppliers.

The meeting comes at an interesting time, with UK retailer Tesco on Monday announcing that “by 2026, 100% of [its] farmed Penaeus vannamei shrimp will be electrically stunned.”

READ MORE
AUG 205:09 AM GMT
Inspection firm backs Vietnam to reverse yellow card, sees increasing strictness on exports

OFCO Group – a French inspection and consulting firm based in Vietnam – sees increasing levels of adherence to regulations and best practices in seafood exports, especially when it comes to the tuna sector, director Jean-Charles Diener told Undercurrent News.

Vietnam has been slapped by the EU with a “yellow card” warning since 2017 over perceived failures in the Asian nation’s management and regulation. The government often communicates that it is striving to improve, and Diener feels this is not only rhetoric.

READ MORE
AUG 205:02 AM GMT
Can Tho university study aims to inform government policy on antibiotic use in pangasius farming

A study conducted by Can Tho University’s College of Aquaculture and Fisheries aims to inform government policy on the drastic overuse of antibiotics in pangasius farming, project leader Professor Tran Minh Phu told Undercurrent News.

The work is being funded by the International Centre for Antimicrobial Resistance Solutions and carried out in partnership with Pharmaq, part of the US livestock drug business Zoetis. Pharmaq is the only company thus far to have manufactured a vaccine for “bacillary necrosis of pangasius” and “motile aeromonas septicemia,” which between them kill a huge percentage of fingerlings.

READ MORE
AUG 201:54 AM GMT
Easing feed prices mean mooted pangasius shortage this year now unlikely

An easing in the price of soybean meal, in turn leading to more manageable feed prices for pangasius farmers, means a mooted shortage of raw material this year should now be unlikely, an industry source told Undercurrent News.

“The market remains bad; China has pushed down the [export] prices, in their position where they control the market. Supply is good enough for the lower demand — we won’t have oversupply, and I don’t think we’ll have any lack.”

READ MORE

Contact the author neil.ramsden@undercurrentnews.com

title: Untitled
content:
TOKYO, Japan – Undercurrent News is live at the 26th edition of the Japan International Seafood and Technology Expo (JISTE), taking place at Tokyo Big Sight in Koto Ward, Tokyo, from August 21 to 23.

Also known as the Seafood Show Tokyo, JISTE is one of Japan's largest seafood trade fairs, spotlighting the theme "Creating the future of fisheries through seafood business and technological innovation."

The expo features a diverse array of seafood products, processing equipment, and related technologies from Japan and around the globe. This year’s event is expected to draw over 25,000 visitors across the three days.

The Japan Fisheries Association, representing the nation’s entire fishing and seafood industry, organizes two major seafood exhibitions yearly: the Seafood and Technology Expo Osaka in February and JISTE in August.

Keep checking back below for the latest updates.

Auto updates: On
AUG 232:05 AM GMT
Nichimo eyes 800t of Kuji coho, trout salmon harvest in 2025

Japanese seafood giant Nichimo Co. is set to harvest a combined 800 metric tons of farmed coho and trout salmon in Kuji, Iwate Prefecture, next year.

The 2025 production target is expected to remain steady or slightly increase compared to the 2024 harvest, Shotaro Mizuno, a senior staff member at Nichimo, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
AUG 2211:47 PM GMT
Maruha Nichiro dominates Japanese canned seafood market 

Maruha Nichiro led the Japanese domestic seafood canned products market in fiscal year 2023, securing the top share of 35.2%.

By species, the Tokyo-based group captured 39.1% of the market for sardine canned products and 33% for mackerel.

READ MORE
AUG 2211:19 PM GMT
Atland to harvest 2,500t of Atlantic salmon in 2027

Atland Corp., a new land-based salmon farming joint venture of Japanese seafood giants Mitsubishi Corp. and Maruha Nichiro, is set to harvest 2,500 metric tons of Atlantic salmon in 2027.

The construction of land-based farming facilities is currently underway and scheduled to be completed by the fiscal year of 2025, a spokesperson for Maruha Nichiro told Undercurrent News at the Seafood Show Tokyo.

READ MORE
AUG 2211:01 PM GMT
Clearwater Seafoods expands Macduff products in Japan

Clearwater Seafoods, a global leader in wild-caught shellfish, is looking to expand the presence of its Scottish seafood products in the Japanese market.

According to Kondo Takeshi, the company’s business development manager for the Asia Pacific region, the Canadian shellfish harvester focuses on growing the market for its products produced by its subsidiary, Macduff Shellfish.

READ MORE
AUG 228:39 PM GMT
Indian suppliers seek $0.25/kg price hike for low-grade surimi blocks

Indian surimi raw material suppliers are seeking a price increase of $0.20-$0.25 per kilogram for low-grade products in the ongoing new season, industry sources at the Seafood Show Tokyo told Undercurrent News.

This targeted price hike is driven by a reduced inventory of low-grade surimi blocks in Japan, particularly those with a gel strength between 200 and 300.

READ MORE
AUG 228:10 PM GMT
Yen appreciation drives down Chilean Coho prices in Japan

The wholesale price of Chilean coho salmon in Japan has dropped to JPY 1,080 per kilogram for 4-6 pound headed-and-gutted (H&G) products, largely due to the recent sharp yen appreciation.

Industry sources at the Seafood Show Tokyo report that wholesale prices—where importers sell to primary wholesalers—have fallen by JPY 70/kg for 4/6 sizes and JPY 60-70/kg to JPY 1,050-1,070/kg for 6/9 sizes.

READ MORE
AUG 227:42 PM GMT
Marinet secures 300t of crab product for year-end sales amid rising prices

Marinet Co., a seafood importer and processor based in Fukuoka, has secured approximately 300 metric tons of crab products for the upcoming year-end sales, according to Yuuichi Takashima, the sub-manager of the company’s crab product division.

Takashima described this as a “significant decrease” compared to the previous year, largely driven by price increases in major crab species.

READ MORE
AUG 227:11 AM GMT
Canada’s ThisFish enters Japanese market with AI platform, targeting eel farming sector

ThisFish Inc., a Vancouver, Canada-based software and artificial intelligence (AI) company, is looking to expand its global footprint, with eyeing the Japanese seafood processing market.

The company entered into a partnership with EZO CREATE last year, to introduce its AI-powered management platform, Tally, in Japan.

READ MORE
AUG 226:13 AM GMT
Japan’s salmon market shifts with increased demand for fillets, says NSC rep

During a presentation to Undercurrent News, Johan Kvalheim, regional director for Japan and South Korea at the Norwegian Seafood Council, highlighted significant shifts in the global salmon market, largely driven by changing consumer habits.

In Japan, the retail sector has taken a commanding share of fresh salmon consumption, accounting for approximately 90% of the market between 2020 and 2022, as consumers shifted their dining preferences from restaurants to home during the COVID-19 pandemic.

READ MORE
AUG 225:43 AM GMT
Alaskan seafood industry faces challenges amid yen depreciation, rising competition, says ASMI rep

The Alaskan seafood industry, a long-standing supplier to Japan’s seafood market, is encountering significant hurdles as the depreciation of the yen and increasing competition from other countries threaten its market position, according to Yakata Akiko, trade representative for the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute (ASMI), in an interview with Undercurrent News.

ASMI’s analysis revealed that Japanese imports of Alaskan seafood, including products processed in third countries, amounted to 172,283 metric tons valued at $620 million in 2023. 

READ MORE
AUG 2111:56 PM GMT
Tokyo Seafoods leads Japanese market with 350t of wild Andalusian bluefin tuna

Tokyo Seafoods, one of Japan’s leading seafood importers, has secured 350 metric tons of wild-caught bluefin tuna from Spain this year, according to Takeshi Sugiura, the company’s general manager.

Bluefin tuna were caught using traditional large set nets, known as “almadraba,” along the southwestern coast of Spain. Tokyo Seafoods sources the fish from the regions of Conil, Barbate, and Tarifa.

READ MORE
AUG 2111:20 PM GMT
MSC Japan introduces new award to further promote sustainable seafood

The Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) Japan has launched the “MSC Japan Award,” a new initiative aimed at recognizing businesses that have played a key role in spreading the adoption of MSC-certified seafood across the county.

Since its establishment in 2007, MSC Japan has witnessed steady growth in the number of MSC Chain of Custody (CoC) certified businesses.

READ MORE
AUG 214:49 AM GMT
Kyokuyo to boost domestic crab stick production to 8,000t

Kyokuyo is aiming to expand its domestic crab stick production to between 7,000 and 8,000 metric tons annually in the coming years, Kazumasa Takahashi, deputy general manager of the company’s research and development department, told Undercurrent News.

The Tokyo-based seafood giant operates its crab stick production through its subsidiary, Kyokuyo Foods, which is celebrating its 40th anniversary this year.

READ MORE
AUG 212:38 AM GMT
Hanwa aims for 12,000t sales of Chilean coho H&G 

Japanese seafood trader Hanwa Co. plans to sell 12,000 metric tons of Chilean farmed coho salmon headed-and-gutted (H&G) products in Japan throughout the year 2024, according to a sales representative who spoke with Undercurrent News.

This sales target remains consistent with the previous salmon season, which ended in June 2024.

READ MORE
AUG 2010:52 PM GMT
Gadre launches Japan subsidiary to market finished surimi products

Indian surimi processor Gadre Marine Export launched its Japanese subsidiary this February, aiming at the sales expansion of its finished products including crab sticks, Arjun Gadre, managing director told Undercurrent News.

The launch of subsidiary came as the Indian surimi processor has seen the sales expansion of the value-added products in recent years in Japan.

READ MORE
AUG 2010:30 PM GMT
Japan’s top crab processor focuses on Barents Sea extra-large sized king crab

Tsukiji Kanisho Co., Japan’s leading crab trader and processor, is gearing up to promote Barents Sea-origin king and snow crab for the year-end sales in Japan.

The standout product for the upcoming year-end sale is the extra-large-sized king crab from the Barents Sea, according to CEO Noriaki Nakamura, who spoke to Undercurrent News at the Tokyo Seafood Show.

READ MORE
AUG 2010:28 PM GMT
Nissui expands bluefin tuna farming site to five locations in Japan

Nissui is expanding the short-term bluefin tuna ranching operation in Japan, with adding new two farming sites into the current three locations.

In addition to the previous farming locations in Ine, Oki, and Tsushima, the Tokyo-based giant is expanding to include Sasebo, Nagasaki and Koshikijima, in Kagoshima, a spokesperson for the group told Undercurrent News at the Tokyo Seafood Show.

READ MORE

title: Untitled
content:
BANGKOK, Thailand -- Undercurrent News is reporting from the Aquaculture Roundtable Series (TARS) 2024 in Bangkok, Thailand, on Aug. 14 and 15.

This year, TARS offers expert analysis, business models, technology, innovations, and state-of-the-art biotechnology along the entire supply chain – from genetics to production to markets. 

Keep checking back for Undercurrent's updates below.

Auto updates: On
AUG 158:40 AM GMT
Tilapia experts call for Asian countries to follow China’s stronger regulations

Tilapia sector experts stressed the urgent need for stronger and more cohesive regulations in Asian countries after the TARS breakout panel, which took place on the second day.

According to Krishna R Salin, aquaculture program chair at the Asian Institute of Technology, who summarized the breakout panel, the current regulatory framework was described as loosely structured, leading to inefficiencies and inconsistencies across the industry.

AUG 156:52 AM GMT
Call for unified market name for pangasius

A panel of executives in the pangasius sector called for a unified market name for the commodity whitefish, after a TARS breakout panel. 

To enhance pangasius’s global market presence, the group proposed a unified market name, “Panga,” to address consumer confusion and mislabeling issues. The group — led by Romi Novriadi, a lecturer at Jakarta Technical University of Fisheries –called for global collaboration, innovation, and commitment to sustainable practices. 

AUG 153:10 AM GMT
Indonesia’s eFishery aims to empower small-scale farmers through integration

Cameron Maclean, vice president for aquatech and financial services platform eFishery, is at the forefront of a project in Indonesia to empower small-scale farmers through an integrated system.

According to Maclean, Indonesia’s aquaculture industry has traditionally been highly fragmented, with each stage of the supply chain — from hatcheries to feed companies, farmers, aggregators, and processors — operating in isolation.

AUG 151:51 AM GMT
Singapore aims for 30% self-sufficiency in seafood, veg sectors by 2030

Rui Alexandre Goncalves, deputy director for Singapore’s Food Agency (SFA), addressed his country’s need to transform the current seafood and vegetable industry into a highly productive, resource-efficient and science-based sector.

This is in keeping with the nation’s vision for food security, where the SFA aims to meet 30% of the country’s nutritional needs domestically by 2030.

AUG 151:11 AM GMT
Global aquafeed production saw first decline in recent memory in 2023

Global aquafeed production declined 4.4% year-on-year to 52.09 million metric tons in 2023, representing the first decrease in recent memory, said Linda Chen of Hatch Blue, an aquaculture and seafood specialist firm.

The recent negative growth was driven by a 7% y-o-y drop in the Asia-Pacific region, according to her presentation.

AUG 1512:16 AM GMT
Protease enzymes lead charge for sustainable feed, cost efficiency, says Jefo’s expert

The aquaculture industry is on the cusp of significant transformation, driven by the need for innovations in feed efficiency and environmental sustainability, said Herve Lucien-Brun, an aquaculture consultant of Jefo Nutrition.

He said as the aquaculture industry expands, it faces the dual challenge of maintaining feed quality while cutting costs and minimizing ecological impact.

AUG 1411:52 PM GMT
Singaporean tech firm unveils biotechnological solutions for disease management

Rishita Changede, CEO of Teora, a Singapore-based technology firm, introduced biotechnological advancements to revolutionize disease management and growth enhancement in the aquaculture industry.

Teora’s innovative approach, which blends bioinformatics, precision fermentation, and oral vaccine delivery, addresses some of the most pressing challenges in aquaculture, particularly in tropical regions.

AUG 1411:06 PM GMT
Tilapia farming needs to transform to protected practices, says DSM-Firmenich

Tilapia farming is shifting from traditional, exposed methods to more protected, sustainable practices due to rising demand and production challenges, said Abung Simanjuntak, technical expert manager at DSM-Firmenich.

Tilapia face numerous stressors, including pathogens and environmental changes, leading to a higher risk of disease and mortality.

AUG 147:14 AM GMT
Southeast Asian tilapia farms face more unpredictable disease patterns

Southeast Asia’s tilapia farms face a future with increasingly unpredictable disease patterns, particularly at critical stages like the nursery phase, said Roberto Cascione of VIRBAC Asia and Middle East.

Cascione highlighted the alarming spread of pathogens like Streptococcus agalactiae, tilapia lake virus, and infectious spleen and kidney necrosis virus across the region, revealing that the landscape has changed dramatically over the last decade.

AUG 146:12 AM GMT
Leveraging feed taste preferences can boost aquaculture growth, says Spanish expert

Sofia Morais, an aqua team innovation leader at Spain-based feed additive firm Lucta, highlighted the critical role of taste in fish feeding and its impact on aquaculture productivity during her speech.

She explained that while fish need nutrients, they must also recognize these nutrients as food. The recognition is driven by their highly developed taste systems, which influence feeding behavior.

AUG 145:43 AM GMT
Carbon footprint reduction in fish feed becoming priority in EU, says IFFO director

The animal feed industry is undergoing a transformation, with sustainability and precision nutrition at the forefront, said Brett Glencross, technical director at the Marine Ingredients Organisation, known as IFFO.

He emphasized the growing importance of reducing the carbon footprint of animal feeds, particularly in Europe, where this is becoming a priority.

AUG 145:15 AM GMT
Marine fish fry production in EMEA expected to grow to 1.6bn by 2028, says Inve exec 

Marine fish fry production in Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) is expected to grow 1.7% year-on-year to 1.423 billion fish in 2024, with 77 hatcheries across 16 countries, according to the presentation by Young Chul Kim, R&D trial manager for Singapore-based INVE Aquaculture.

In 2022, 70% of 1.541bn fries were produced in Turkey and Greece, and seabass and seabream accounted for 95% of the total production.

AUG 144:34 AM GMT
Advanced genomic selection technology transforms breeding programs, says director for Norway’s Benchmark Genetics 

Morten Rye, a director for external services and international strategies at Norway’s Benchmark Genetics, stressed the importance of balancing new technologies with solid breeding practices while aquaculture genetics is progressing rapidly.

According to his presentation, 80% of global livestock meat currently comes from just three major species, while aquaculture relies on over 70 different species to achieve a similar level of global production.

AUG 142:26 AM GMT
Vietnamese pangasius production continues to grow with small margins for farmers, says ADM exec

Pangasius production has seen a continuous growth in Asian countries in 2023, with 3.33 million metric tons in the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region, according to Mai Chung, a regional manager for aquaculture feed additives with ADM Animal Nutrition.

The breakdown of pangasius production in APAC includes 1.71m metric tons in Vietnam, 756,000t in India, 463,000t in China, 398,000t in Indonesia, and 397,000t in Bangladesh.

AUG 141:04 AM GMT
Thai tilapia genetics sector faces climate change challenges

Thai farmed tilapia production amounted to over 200,000 metric tons in 2023 worth nearly THB 13 billion ($373 million), according to the presentation by Amorn Luengnaruemitchai, managing director, Manit Genetics Co. & Manit Intertrade Co.

The country’s tilapia farming differs from other regions, with many small-scale farmers using small cages. 

AUG 1412:23 AM GMT
Golden pompano is ‘prime example’ of China’s marine aquaculture growth

The golden pompano has become a prime example of rapid growth within China’s marine fish industry, said Yufan Zhang, China aqua business department manager at Alltech.

According to him, its production surged from 2020 to 2021 in the country, overtaking other species like the sea bass, which previously dominated the market.

AUG 1412:21 AM GMT
Tilapia popularity declines amid market shift in US

Tilapia, once a major player in the US seafood market, has experienced dramatic fluctuations in consumption over the years, said Francisco Murillo, CEO of Tropo Farms, the largest tilapia producer in Ghana.

The fish entered the top 10 most consumed seafood items in the US in 2001, with a remarkable growth of 144% over the next five years. US tilapia consumption peaked in 2012 and decreased by 35% from its peak by 2021.

title: 2024 Shrimp Summit: China shipment ban created 70,000t backlog in Ecuador
content:
CHENNAI, India -- Undercurrent News has been reporting live from the 2024 Shrimp Summit, held at the ITC Grand Chola hotel, in Chennai, India.

The summit, which ran from June 27 to 29, was hosted by non-profit The Center for Responsible Seafood, led by former Global Seafood Alliance president and founder George Chamberlain. 

The event aimed to reverse Asia's declining growth trend by bringing together key sector representatives from production, market and conservation.

Auto updates: On
JUL 15:48 AM GMT
China shipment ban has created 70,000t backlog in Ecuador

Kontali analyst Erwin Termaat told listeners that Chinese restrictions on shipments from nine Ecuadorian shrimp exporters imposed by China in the first quarter of this year has created a build-up of roughly 70,000 metric tons in the country’s storage facilities.

The East Asian country had allegedly detected metabisulfite levels above permitted levels in shrimp shipments sent from Ecuador between February and March this year, suspending imports from nine Ecuadorian companies in response.

READ MORE
JUL 15:26 AM GMT
Kontali: Global shrimp price index down 20% since 2019

Ragnar Nystoyl, senior analyst with Kontali, noted that since the firm had begun monitoring vannamei shrimp farmgate prices from January 2019, there has been an unprecedented worldwide drop in value.

The company gets global prices, and weighs them based on production volumes from different regions and count sizes to create a ‘global price index’, showing the average value of farmed shrimp.

READ MORE
JUL 15:08 AM GMT
Singapore’s Blue Aqua on track to build 3,000t trout RAS by end of year

Farhad Shishehchian, founder and CEO of Singapore land-based shrimp and trout farm manufacturer Blue Aqua International, told listeners that his company was currently constructing a major rainbow trout farm in the country.

Blue Aqua, which was founded in 2009 as a technical supplier to the aquaculture sector, aims to have a land-based 3,000 metric ton capacity rainbow trout facility completed by the end of the year.

READ MORE
JUL 14:37 AM GMT
Intensive farming no guarantee of risk-free yields, says Viet Uc

Lam Dinh, the director of business development at Vietnamese intensive farmer Viet Uc Seafood Corporation, described to listeners that even super-intensive farms are volatile investments.

Dinh, who comes from a background in finance, described that company valuations typically weigh up both the “low-risk, consistent part” alongside high-risk elements that are “unstable but with a huge potential for upside.”

READ MORE
JUN 298:46 AM GMT
Next year’s summit to be held in Bali, Indonesia

George Chamberlain, president of The Center for Responsible Seafood, confirmed that the third edition of The Shrimp Summit would take place in Bali, Indonesia, next year.

No further dates or information were provided.

READ MORE
JUN 296:27 AM GMT
Farm data now being used to insure Indian farmers against disease

Pavan Kosaraju, CEO of Indian aquatech firm AquaExchange, shared that insurance companies in the country have begun insuring farms against the loss of their crops from disease using newly available data.

Typically, he said, shrimp farms could only be insured against one-off macro-events such as heavy rain and flooding.

READ MORE
JUN 294:23 AM GMT
Vietnam’s Otanics already supplying to 20 countries

Having been one of the major faces of the 2023 edition of the Shrimp Summit, Vietnamese aquatech supplier Otanics Technology — owner of the Tomota brand — has grown rapidly over the past year, according to CEO Van Vu.

“Our products are in use by hatcheries and farms in Vietnam, India, Indonesia, Thailand, and many other countries,” he told listeners. “Yesterday we saw two new countries added that takes us to 20.”

READ MORE
JUN 294:00 AM GMT
Still no certainty on shrimp council’s funding model

Fittingly, the event poll on a preferred funding model for the Global Shrimp Council — choosing between a voluntary or mandatory duty scheme among exporters — ended in a rough tie.

For all the progress the council has made since its foundation at the tail-end of 2023, the thorny question of funding remains unanswered, but council founder Gabriel Luna is undaunted.

READ MORE
JUN 292:25 AM GMT
TCRS, Tomota, AquaExchange collaborate on smallholder improver program

“Smallholders are typically beyond the reach of certification,” said George Chamberlain, president of The Center for Responsible Seafood (TCRS). “You can imagine the cost of bringing in an external auditor, it’s impractical. But with the emergence of affordable technology, the irony is there’ll now be more information from the small farms than the medium and large farms.”

While aquatech firms like India’s AquaExchange are using the data they collect from shrimp farmers to help them access financing and insurance, Chamberlain said there are also boundless possibilities for improver programs and potentially, sustainability certifications.

READ MORE
JUN 291:48 AM GMT
India to be second focus of Global Shrimp Council

The Global Shrimp Council, founded last year by 13 of the largest shrimp producers and traders in the world in an effort to grow consumer demand for shrimp worldwide, may be starting with a focus on US advertising, but will make boosting Indian consumption its second target market.

“We’re going to start in the US, but of course it makes sense that the second place to go will be India,” confirmed Gabriel Luna, the council’s founder.

READ MORE
JUN 281:22 PM GMT
Chinese vannamei production to stagnate in 2024

There is expected to be minimal shrimp production growth in China for 2024, despite an impressive 8% increase in 2023, according to Kontali’s Erwin Termaat.

This year, numerous headwinds and ongoing struggles in the first quarter means the analyst has revised its expectations downwards, Termaat said.

READ MORE
JUN 286:30 AM GMT
Duties a headache for Chapter 11-hit Red Lobster’s ‘value’ shrimp offering

Matt Livesay, chief supply chain officer at US restaurant chain Red Lobster, admitted the new countervailing and antidumping duties being introduced by the US department of Commerce are running headfirst into the chain’s use of shrimp as a relatively lower-cost item on its menu.

“Shrimp in our space plays a critical role; it’s the value offering, it’s a very diverse offering, and will always comprise 65% of our volume purchases,” said Livesay, speaking while Red Lobster is in the midst of a Chapter 11 bankruptcy process in the US. 

READ MORE
JUN 286:19 AM GMT
Indonesian production set for 2025 turnaround

Indonesia has been very much the black sheep of vannamei producing nations in recent years, reporting year-on-year volume declines even as other countries grow relentlessly amid a demand crisis.

According to Kontali analyst Erwin Termaat, Indonesian production decreased by 7% last year, and this slide is expected to continue — albeit slower, by just 5% — in 2024.

READ MORE
JUN 286:14 AM GMT
India’s lower vannamei densities may help it pass 1m metric tons this year

Despite enduring rather than enjoying last year, Kontali analyst Erwin Termaat confirmed that the country is understood to have grown production volumes by 2% in 2023.

“Then we’re seeing in feed sales and export data quite strong numbers for India at the start of the year, making them up 6% in our production models for 2024 at the moment, going over 1 million metric tons,” he said.

READ MORE
JUN 283:59 AM GMT
Final determination on US duties likely to arrive in late October

Warren Connelly, senior counsel with Trade Pacific Law, has explained to attendees the remaining steps in the ongoing US countervailing duty and anti-dumping duty determination process.

Although preliminary figures have been released by the US Department of Commerce (DOC), these are still subject to change, he noted, until the final determination is made.

READ MORE
JUN 282:57 AM GMT
Rising costs responsible for yawning gap between farm-gate, retail price

A common bone of contention among shrimp producers, the vast chasm between the low farm-gate prices being offered to farmers and the relatively high retail price that these shrimp are then sold for, was addressed again at the show.

Ragnar Nystoyl, chief analyst at Kontali, expressed his belief that rising inventory and logistic costs play a greater role than suppliers realize.

READ MORE
JUN 281:49 AM GMT
US duties have created misleading supply shifts in first four months of 2024

Although imports of vannamei shrimp to the US and the EU have increased by 14% and 11% respectively in the first four months of the year, the former at least is misleading, according to Kontali analyst Erwin Termaat.

“In the US, there’s been some economic struggles, and we believe that this year’s increase to market is not necessarily corresponding to any improved demand, but about companies sending before the [countervailing] and [anti-dumping] duties were announced,” he told listeners.

READ MORE
JUN 281:30 AM GMT
Kontali: Ecuador, India expect single-digit volume growth in 2024

Norwegian seafood data analytics firm Kontali is expecting 5.7 million metric tons live shrimp equivalent (LSE) of farmed vanamei to be produced worldwide in 2024.

“Most producing countries are seeing numbers that are up; Indonesia is the only one seeing a decline,” said Kontali analyst Erwin Termaat.

READ MORE

title: Aquaculture Canada 2024: Canada’s aquaculture industry needs its own legislation, seaweed farmer suggests
content:
Undercurrent News reported live from Aquaculture Canada 2024, being held at the Delta Hotel & Prince Edward Island (PEI) Conference Center, in Charlottetown, PEI, June 16-19.

Auto updates: On
JUN 2012:24 AM GMT
Canada’s aquaculture industry needs its own legislation, seaweed farmer suggests

Canada’s aquaculture industry needs enabling regulations, not rules that create barriers for seafarmers, said Steve Backman, a seaweed farmer from the Canadian province of New Brunswick.

“From the very beginning, the regulations for aquaculture in Canada have been squeezed into everybody’s regulations, and every government department that oversees a regulation adds costs and a barrier to entry,” said Backman, one of the delegates at the Aquaculture Canada 2024 conference to present this week.

READ MORE
JUN 1911:11 PM GMT
Despite hiccups, Canadian oyster hatchery remains committed to seeding east coast

In the eight years since the Lennox Island Development Corporation (LIDC) in the Canadian province of Prince Edward Island (PEI) decided to start an oyster hatchery, there have been some hiccups, but the group is undaunted.

The Bideford Shellfish Hatchery has managed to increase production from 10 million seeds in 2017 to about 14m in 2021, reported LIDC executive Mike Randall.

READ MORE
JUN 198:12 AM GMT
Can oysters help bring a dead sea back to life?

Researchers in Canada and Spain aim to answer that question as they test a theory that bivalves could be used to filter toxins from lagoons polluted by industrial activity.

Laboratory tests have shown promising results, Dr. Ramon Filgueira, associate professor of Marine Affairs at Dalhousie University in Nova Scotia (NS), Canada, told delegates at the Aquaculture Canada 2024 convention, offering a time-lapse video to show how oysters helped clear algae from a tank of water.

READ MORE
JUN 182:47 PM GMT
Canadian sea farmers want Ottawa to establish insurance program for industry

They consider themselves farmers of the sea, managing underwater crops like their agricultural peers manage crops on land.

Unlike those who pull food from the dirt, however, Canada’s sea farmers don’t have a Business Risk Management (BRM) program like the one the federal government offers to the agricultural industry.

READ MORE
JUN 187:52 AM GMT
Young salmon farmers vow to keep advocating for British Columbia industry

Uncertainty has driven some people away from the salmon farming industry in the Canadian province of British Colombia (BC), but among the relative newcomers to aquaculture are those who say they won’t stay silent while others push to shut down net pens, creating uncertainty for the industry.

“I have met the people in coastal communities who depend on this industry,” said Kaitlin Guitard, laboratory manager for Mowi Canada West, noting that just a couple years after she joined the company, the Department of Fisheries and Oceans gave notice that it would be shutting down net pens in the Discovery Islands area of BC.

READ MORE
JUN 187:45 AM GMT
Activist groups should be stripped of charitable status for lying, says Cooke executive

Environmental activist organizations or any not-for-profit groups that lie to the public about the aquaculture industry and salmon farming should be stripped of their charitable status, a Cooke Aquaculture executive said during a panel discussion at the Aquaculture Canada 2024 convention on Monday (June 17).

“It’s reprehensible that governments continue to allow environmental organizations, you can name a million of them that are out there, that are lying right now. It’s terrible, and it’s putting people’s jobs at risk,” said Joel Richardson, vice president of communications with the New Brunswick-based global aquaculture giant.

READ MORE
JUN 187:34 AM GMT
Study shows Canadians prefer farmed Canadian salmon

A recent survey of Canadians shows that 79% prefer Canadian salmon over Chilean or Norwegian equivalents, and just over half believe aquaculture is a sustainable method of production. 

Those were among the conclusions of a survey by consumer research company Angus Reid for the Agrifood Analytics Lab at Dalhousie University (DAL) in the Canadian province of Nova Scotia.

READ MORE
JUN 172:09 PM GMT
Canadian aquaculture group surprised by leak about BC plan

The Canadian Aquaculture Industry Alliance would prefer to hear directly from the Canadian government before commenting on Monday’s (June 17) announcement that the industry has just five more years to phase out net pens in the province of British Columbia.

As reported by Undercurrent News, while the exact details of the plan have not been unveiled, the Globe and Mail reports that sources have said the government will give companies another five years to transition their operations to land-based. Current leases for farm sites in BC were set to expire on June 30.

READ MORE
JUN 1710:46 AM GMT
Canada needs consistent funding, marketing for aquaculture, seafood, says industry rep

Canada’s aquaculture, and seafood industry, in general, needs to be more prominent in the food discussion.

Specifically, the farmed fish and wild fish industries need a consistent, long-term marketing program to ensure it’s part of the food conversation, said Timothy Kennedy, executive director of the Canadian Aquaculture Industry Association (CAIA).

READ MORE

title: RASTech 2024: Audience gets insights into commissioning land-based systems
content:
CHARLOTTE, North Carolina, US -- Key players in the global recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) industry have converged in Charlotte, North Carolina, for the annual RASTech Conference and Trade Show, taking place Wednesday (June 5) and Thursday (June 6).

This year’s event features 75 exhibitors and over 70 speakers and has attracted 350 registered participants. Stay tuned for comprehensive coverage and updates on the latest industry developments.

Auto updates: On
JUN 610:37 PM GMT
Audience get insights into crucial role of commissioning land-based systems

James Tuller of Pure Salmon Technology gave attendees at RASTech some valuable food for thought around commissioning in his keynote on day two of the conference.

As a specialist in wastewater treatment for aquaculture with Pure Salmon Group, owned by private equity fund 8F Asset management, Tuller shared his experience getting complex recirculation systems up and running smoothly.

READ MORE
JUN 610:58 AM GMT
RAS isn’t ready for the stock market, says former Atlantic Sapphire CEO

Former CEO and co-founder of Atlantic Sapphire, Johan Andreassen, has had his fair share of ups and downs. 

In 2019, Atlantic Sapphire became a $1-billion company. On Dec. 4, its stock reached NOK 128.50, boosting its market cap to NOK 9.16bn. However, the tides have changed since then, pegging its trading value today to around NOK 10.60, approximately equivalent to $1 per share.

READ MORE
JUN 67:23 AM GMT
Salmon Evolution busts land-based cost myth

Salmon Evolution is overturning conventional wisdom in aquaculture by proving that land-based salmon production can be cost-competitive with traditional net pen farming methods, says Todd Deligan, the Norwegian company’s general manager for North America.

In Q1 2024, Salmon Evolution reported production costs of NOK 67/kg  ($6.34) of salmon produced, comparable to the range of 50 to 80 NOK/kg seen in net pen aquaculture, depending on various sea-based challenges.

READ MORE
JUN 54:12 PM GMT
Standardized RAS design will ease investor concerns, says BC-based expert

KC Hosler, who holds the dual roles of chief operating officer and chief technology officer at British Columbia-based aquaculture technology provider PR Aqua, said standardizing recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) design will significantly help address ongoing investor trepidation that is hindering growth in the land-based aquaculture industry.

At the RASTech conference on Wednesday, Hosler told attendees that by developing repeatable, proven module designs that can be deployed rapidly at scale, standardization builds confidence in technical and operational performance.

READ MORE
JUN 511:51 AM GMT
Megan Sorby: There’s huge potential for growth in the US seafood market

The US seafood market holds substantial potential for expansion, considering that seafood currently comprises only 2% of the average weekly grocery cart, said Megan Sorby, the founder and CEO of Pine Island Red Fish, a newly launched land-based RAS operation in Florida.

Speaking at the RASTech conference, Sorby provided valuable insights into the burgeoning opportunities and challenges within the US seafood industry.

READ MORE
JUN 59:40 AM GMT
Maiman, Holm highlight future of sustainable fish farming in keynote

Ohad Maiman, co-founder and former CEO of The Kingfish Company, and Thue Holm, co-founder and former CTO of Atlantic Sapphire, kicked off the RASTech conference on Wednesday with a keynote.

They emphasized that land-based fish farming is increasingly recognized as a crucial solution to meet the rising global demand for fish while alleviating pressure on wild fisheries.

READ MORE
JUN 59:05 AM GMT
Microsoft-backed, woman-led $81M fund invests in aquaculture tech

Amy Francetic, managing general partner and co-founder of Chicago-based Buoyant Ventures, sat down with Undercurrent News at the RASTech conference and tradeshow on Wednesday to discuss her firm’s focus on investing in digital climate solutions. 

Buoyant Ventures has raised $81 million from notable backers, including Microsoft, Xcel Energy, and family offices, to support technology companies working in areas like sustainable aquaculture.

READ MORE

Contact the author liza.mayer@undercurrentnews.com

title: Untitled
content:
BANGKOK, Thailand -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the Thaifex Anuga Asia food show, held at the IMPACT Muang Thong Thani events hall in Bangkok, Thailand, from May 28 to June 1.

This year's event is larger than last year's, featuring over 3,000 exhibitors from 50 countries and attracting an estimated 80,000 trade visitors from 133 countries.

Thaifex Anuga Asia covers a wide range of food and beverage segments, with a significant portion dedicated to seafood. Many of Thailand's largest seafood traders and processors are present, including major conglomerates Charoen Pokphand Foods and Thai Union Group.

Auto updates: On
MAY 313:11 AM GMT
Asian premium seafood brand ‘Ocean Gems’ to explore North American market

The premium seafood division of Southeast Asian protein conglomerate Foodservice APME intends to expand its “Ocean Gems” brand to markets beyond Asia, including North America and Europe.

The brand was originally created in 2003, aiming to diversify away from terrestrial meat during the Hong Kong SARS pandemic, Makiko Kurosawa, manager for Ocean Gems, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 312:40 AM GMT
Thai shrimp supplier Shing-fu launches giant freshwater prawn for China market

Thai shrimp supplier Shing-fu Seaproducts Development Company has launched “giant freshwater prawn” (Macrobrachium rosenbergii) products for Asian markets, especially China.

The release of the product comes as part of a bid to differentiate Thai shrimp from Ecuadorian, company director Isariya Issarawattanakul told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 3010:46 PM GMT
Thaifex features 209 seafood companies this year

The Thaifex Anuga Asia show 2024 has featured 3,133 exhibitors, including international exporters from 52 countries, more than the 3,034 at last year’s event.

A total of 209 companies from the seafood sector had stands, accounting for 6.67% of the exhibitors.

READ MORE
MAY 302:22 AM GMT
Vinh Hoan adds 5,000t pangasius surimi production line

Vietnam’s largest exporter of pangasius, Vinh Hoan Corporation, has invested in surimi production, including raw material blocks and crab sticks, Hoa Truong, chief sales officer, told Undercurrent News.

After adding a surimi raw material production line at its plant in Cao Lanh city, Dong Thap province, in 2023, the company has an annual processing capacity of 5,000 metric tons.

READ MORE
MAY 301:23 AM GMT
NSC names Ashild Nakken as new Southeast Asia region director

The Norwegian Seafood Council has named Ashild Nakken (below right) as the new director for its Southeast Asia region, effective on July 1.

She will be succeeding Asbjorn Warvik Rortveit (below, second from the left), who has served as the seafood envoy for the past five years.

READ MORE
MAY 298:53 PM GMT
Norwegian seafood exports to Southeast Asia grew 90%

Norwegian seafood exports to Southeast Asia have seen a 90% growth in value from 2020 to 2023, according to the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC).

The growth was largely due to the weakness of the Norwegian currency, but “the market has caught up with the higher prices,” said Asbjorn Warvik Rortveit, the NSC’s regional director for Southeast Asia, during his speech at the seminar, which took place at the NSC pavilion on May 29.

READ MORE
MAY 292:47 AM GMT
CP-Uoriki increases Japan-style fishmonger stores to 20 outlets this year

CP-Uoriki Co., a joint venture between CPF Global Food Solution — itself part of Thai protein conglomerate Charoen Pokphand Foods — and Japanese fishmonger Uoriki, plans to increase its seafood retail stores to 100 outlets within five years.

After opening the first outlet at Lotus Sukhumvit 50 in the Thai capital of Bangkok in October 2023, it has already expanded to 10 stores, Jatuphon Tantisuntharodom, managing director, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 292:23 AM GMT
Japanese seafood trader Kohyo aims to increase overseas sales ratio to 30%

Japanese seafood trading company Kohyo Co. is looking to increase its overseas sales ratio from the current 14% to 30% by 2030, Cao Guang Xiu (below left), deputy managing officer for the company, told Undercurrent News.

Its major products for Asian markets include Hokkaido scallops, salmon roe, and Hiroshima-origin oysters, according to Yui Nakashiba (below center).

READ MORE
MAY 291:33 AM GMT
Thai surimi supplier TVI launches crab stick, seaweed salad combo

Major Thai surimi finished product manufacturer Thaveevong Industry Co. (TVI) has just launched a new product that combines crab sticks and seaweed salad for the domestic retail market.

Starting May 23, the product named “Alaska Crab Flavoured Legs with Seasoned Seaweed Japanese Style” became widely available at Seven-Eleven stores across the country, Thamonwan Thawornthaweewong, assistant marketing manager for the manufacturer, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 289:38 PM GMT
Thai ‘Iron Chef’ offers Hokkaido scallop menu at Japan Pavilion

The Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) has established a Japan pavilion with a total of 40 exhibitors at this year’s Thaifex.

For the first time at the event, JETRO is running cooking demonstrations focusing on Japanese scallops, according to Hiroki Taniguchi, director for the organization in Bangkok.

READ MORE
MAY 289:36 PM GMT
Shrimp sales a ‘positive sign’ for demand at Thai Union

After a difficult year in 2023, Thanachote Boonmechote, managing director for shrimp at Thai Union Group, confirmed the seafood conglomerate is currently seeing a positive sign in demand from major markets.

“As we have seen slow demand from the US, but also Japan, Korea, Europe and other countries, our earnings in the first quarter of 2024 were slightly below [the results of 2023’s Q1],” he explained. “But starting this May, we are seeing demand recovery, even in quotations.”

READ MORE
MAY 288:12 PM GMT
Thai tuna product export up 19% during first four months of 2024

Thai exports of frozen tuna, including canned products, increased 19% year-on-year to 174,166 metric tons for the first four months of 2024, according to data supplied by the Thai Tuna Industry Association (TTIA).

In value terms, the growth is even more impressive, advancing from THB 22.7 billion to THB 27.5bn ($751.4 million), an improvement of 21% y-o-y.

READ MORE
MAY 2811:40 AM GMT
Chilean coho salmon harvest for 2024/25 will likely see reduction

The supply and demand structure for the 2024/25 season will likely be the complete opposite of what Chilean coho farmers have seen in the past year, Salmones Aysen commercial manager Jorge Guzman told Undercurrent News.

“The 2024/24 season will be the first year to see a year-on-year reduction in global salmon and trout supply, at least since I entered the industry over 15 years ago,” he said. “We are waiting to see what will happen next.”

READ MORE
MAY 2810:35 AM GMT
TTIA urges canners to support domestic fishery sector

With sustainability high on the agenda of international buyers, the Thai Tuna Industry Association (TTIA) has outlined sustainable development strategies for the entire supply chain, said TTIA president Chanintr Chalisarapong.

The new guideline follows Thamanat Prompow’s recent policy as Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives, which aims to raise the prices of domestic fishery products, increase fishermen’s income, and control illegal imports, as previously reported by Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAY 289:54 AM GMT
Lucky Union plans $50m surimi plant in Thailand

Thai surimi supplier Lucky Union plans to invest around $50 million to open a new surimi processing plant within three years, vice president DH Karl told Undercurrent News.

The move comes as the surimi processor has seen steady growth of surimi finished products in Thailand and its neighboring countries.

READ MORE
MAY 277:20 AM GMT
Thai authorities tighten aquatic product import procedures

The Thai Department of Fisheries has issued a new announcement regarding import procedures for aquatic products, which took effect on May 7.

The new announcement — called Regulations, Methods, and Conditions for Applying for and Granting Permits for the Import of Aquatic Animals or Aquatic Animal Products — revised parts of the existing notice, with an aim to tighten aquatic product import procedures.

READ MORE
MAY 277:16 AM GMT
Thai surimi, fish meat export grows 60% to 6,226t in Q1

Thai customs data shows that the country’s frozen surimi and fish meat exports for the first three months of 2024 totaled 6,226 metric tons, up 60% compared to the same period last year. 

The price averaged THB 103.5 ($2.82) per kilogram, down 22% year-on-year.

READ MORE

Contact the author masahiko.takeuchi@undercurrentnews.com

title: Untitled
content:
LONDON, UK -- Undercurrent News is reporting from the Blue Food Innovation Summit in London, UK, on May 21 and 22.

The event touts itself as an event for aquaculture producers, innovators and investors, discussing new technologies and "climate-resilient ocean solutions."

Keeping checking back for Undercurrent's updates, below.

Auto updates: On
MAY 2212:21 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Accelerators identify funding gap between seed, VC stages

Executives with several global technology accelerators and development organizations identified a gap during which young or novel companies are struggling to find the cash to survive.

Throughout the Blue Food summit, the need for investment in aquaculture technology and related fields has been echoed by many, with start-ups reportedly vying for a very limited pool.

READ MORE
MAY 229:42 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Indonesia’s Jala: Cultural resistance to change remains a barrier

Indonesian shrimp aquaculture data business Jala Tech has more than 10,000 farms using its mobile applications, but cultural barriers to change among smallholders continue to prevent wider uptake, said CEO Liris Maduningtyas.

Data collection at a farm level has spread widely across the country, and at a bigger scale, digitization has allowed Jala to offer farm credit scores and financing. 

READ MORE
MAY 228:30 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Luke’s Lobster warns about dark side of certifications

There can be grim unintended side-effects of regulations and certifications in fisheries that should be protected against, warned Ben Conniff, co-founder and CIO of US supplier Luke’s Lobster.

“A lot of these regulations and certifications and systems and tech solutions are expensive, and they’re onerous, and they’re really hard to manage for fishermen and for small and medium enterprises,” he said. 

READ MORE
MAY 228:16 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Data the ‘language we can coalesce around’ as biodiversity investments become vital

As biodiversity and environmental reporting becomes an increasing necessity, it is important not to get caught up in how and what to report and remain focused on changing things on the ground, warned Kat Bruce, founder of motoring data provider Naturemetrics.

Businesses are going to have to be reporting on their environmental impacts, and data can be a “common language” for cooperation that various stakeholders should be able to coalesce around, she said.

READ MORE
MAY 226:32 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
The ‘cynical’ view: Investing in biodiversity needs ‘business logic’

For corporate investments to flow into ocean biodiversity and restoration, there must be a long-term business logic to the project, noted Jan Erik Saugestad, CEO of Storebrand Asset Management, and Francois Mosnier, head of ocean for Planet Tracker.

“Investors need a long-term view, and there are plenty of those investors out there,” said Saugestad. “There needs to be a return — and it won’t be in the next quarter, it will be long-term. Again, there is plenty of awareness growing that there’s a business logic to these investments.”

READ MORE
MAY 225:34 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Intersection of biodiversity pilots, corporates needs policy backing

Ocean restoration is “moving from charity to being a business,” but pilot biodiversity schemes need the policy backing of governments and need “a corporate in the room,” according to one panel at the Blue Food summit.

Pet food business Nestle Purina took part in a “fireside chat” with two partners it is working with — Sea Ranger Service and Seaforester — to show how financial backing is beginning to yield larger-scale results when it comes to ocean restoration.

READ MORE
MAY 225:08 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Oceans ‘behind’ in Earthshot Prize award innovations

The field of ocean conservation is lagging behind when it comes to the UK’s Earthshot Prize, said the award scheme’s chief product and technology officer Hilary Roberts.

The Earthshot Prize is a global award given to five winners each year for their contributions towards environmentalism. It was first awarded in 2021 and is planned to run annually until 2030. Each winner receives a grant of £1 million to continue their environmental work.

READ MORE
MAY 224:26 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
France pushing for countries to ratify UN biodiversity treaty

After the United Nations (UN) launched a new treaty on marine biodiversity last year, France is pushing for more countries to ratify it ahead of the next UN Ocean Conference, in France, in June 2025.

The “Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction” has 90 signatories but only five ratifications thus far, said Liz Karan, director of ocean governance with NGO the Pew Charitable Trusts.

READ MORE
MAY 2112:58 PM GMT
Genetics has ‘huge potential’ given relative novelty of aquaculture

Genetics still has huge potential to boost productivity in aquaculture given farmed fish species are still relatively close to their wild ancestors, according to Ross Houston, director of genetics and innovation at Benchmark Genetics UK.

Houston noted terrestrial livestock animals are almost unrecognizable compared with wild pigs and cattle, underlining how livestock farmers have bred more productive animals. 

READ MORE
MAY 2112:11 PM GMT
Thai Union: ‘Blue finance’ drives sustainability buy-in at board level

Thai Union has achieved strong buy-in from management for its sustainability efforts thanks largely to an innovative use of “blue finance,” according to a company executive.

Chris Shearlock, Thai Union’s sustainability director for Europe, said that linking financial performance to environmental targets has been crucial for getting decision-makers on board.

READ MORE
MAY 2111:41 AM GMT
Aquaculture sector urged to share data to unlock power of AI

Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation could rapidly transform the aquaculture industry, especially if fish farmers are willing to share their data, according to a panel of experts at the Blue Food Innovation Summit.

Automation is being adopted on an “incredible scale” in aquaculture, said Christian Lim, managing director at venture capital firm SWEN Capital Partners. The real-time monitoring of aquaculture farms possible today — in fish health, predictive analytics around disease outbreaks, and optimized feeding — “we couldn’t have imagined five years ago,” he said.

READ MORE
MAY 2111:31 AM GMT
BioMar: GM crops could have big impact for aquafeed if regulators give go-ahead

Genetically modified crops designed to produce omega-3 fatty acids could have a significant impact on the aquaculture industry if regulators and consumers accept them, according to the vice president of feed supplier BioMar’s UK salmon division.

Speaking at the Blue Food event in London, Paddy Campbell said genetic modification is an available solution to concerns over the sustainability of fish oil and shortages of omega-3 fatty acids — a crucial ingredient in aquafeed for fish health, pharmaceuticals and supplements.

READ MORE
MAY 2111:29 AM GMT
Attendees met by protest from Ocean Rebellion 

Attendees to the Blue Food Innovation Summit in London were met by protesters from Ocean Rebellion, an offshoot of the climate change movement Extinction Rebellion.

The protesters stood dressed as fishermen for photographers from the UK press. Two members of the group also lay in a mock giant can of tuna from John West, a UK tuna brand.

READ MORE

Contact the authors louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com, neil.ramsden@undercurrentnews.com
