title: Infofish Tuna 2024: New canneries for Maldives, Oman; Ecuadorian canneries, software provider test ‘transformative potential’ of AI in tuna processing
content:
BANGKOK, Thailand -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the World Tuna Trade Conference & Exhibition, held in Bangkok, Thailand, from May 20-22. 

With over 500 participants expected this year, the conference will address market trends, technological advancements, stock management and sustainability initiatives. 

The full program for the conference can be viewed here. Keep checking back below for the latest updates.

Auto updates: On
MAY 236:13 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
MSC to publish revised standard in July

The Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) is amending its recently published version three certification standard due to implementation challenges. 

Bill Holden, MSC’s senior tuna fisheries outreach manager, provided an overview of the amendments.

READ MORE
MAY 235:05 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Ecuadorian canneries, software provider test ‘transformative potential’ of AI in tuna processing

According to Eric Enno Tamm, CEO and co-founder of software provider ThisFish, artificial intelligence (AI) will transform the tuna industry.

AI and machine learning excel at solving intricate problems by identifying patterns in large datasets., he said, providing examples illustrating AI’s capacity to handle complex variables, such as predicting outcomes in scenarios with multiple influencing factors. He also touched on the role of computer vision, a technology that converts images into numerical data, allowing AI to detect patterns and anomalies.

READ MORE
MAY 234:43 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Ecodesigned buoys supplier Zunibal integrates AI tools to increase fishing efficiency, sustainability

Zunibal, a supplier of eco-designed buoys, has transformed significantly over its nearly three-decade history from a provider of technological products for the fishing industry into a comprehensive service provider.

Angel Martinez, Zunibal’s commercial director, said that Zunibal’s tools and technologies are designed to enhance efficiency, profitability, and sustainability in fishing practices.

READ MORE
MAY 2312:28 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
FAO: Traceability landscape improves by expanding implementation of international instruments

Nada Bougouss, a fishery officer for Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), spoke on “Social Responsibility and Traceability in Aquatic Value Chains.”

The FAO’s social responsibility guidance in the global seafood industry — non-binding voluntary instrument addressed to the private sector — adopts a value chain approach with six sections such as industrial fishing, aquaculture production, and processing distribution.

READ MORE
MAY 224:41 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
WWF: Technology advancement is game-changer for crew welfare

Bubba Cook, Western and Central Pacific Tuna Program Manager, World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), spoke on “New Horizons: Ensuring Crew Welfare at the Nexus of Technology Advancement and Modern Media Exposure.”

“This issue is a matter of black and white,” he said. “There are no shades of gray when it comes to treating fisher with respect and dignity.”

READ MORE
MAY 224:00 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Maldives’ MIFCO to boost its capacity with three new canneries

The Maldives Industrial Fisheries Company (MIFCO) recently announced plans to build three new canneries across the country, a spokesperson with the company told Undercurrent News.

Each new cannery will boast a production capacity of 100 metric tons per day, equipped with cold storage facilities, freezing capabilities, fishmeal production, and fish oil extraction units, according to the firm.

READ MORE
MAY 219:17 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Oman’s new $80m cannery set to become largest in Middle East

Oman’s state-owned firm, International Sea Food Company (SAOC), has recently launched a new cannery. 

Speaking to Undercurrent News, SAOC’s CEO, Zakariya Al Hasni said the cannery’s development, which began in 2019, represents a significant investment of approximately $70 million to $80m. 

READ MORE
MAY 217:57 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
AI creates new quality standards for tuna traders worldwide

A new Japanese app is helping global tuna buyers instantly to determine the grade properties, such as taste and texture, through a cross-sectional tail scan.

The app, Tuna Scope, developed by Japanese advertising leader Dentsu, assesses database of quality assessments made by human connoisseurs and a huge amount of image data to render its quality judgments.

READ MORE
MAY 2110:38 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
IPNLF: Market access is key to better supporting small-scale tuna fisheries

Martin Purves, managing director at the International Pole and Line Foundation (IPNLF), stressed in his speech that the market could play a very important role in improving the support of small-scale tuna fisheries.

According to Purves, one-by-one fisheries represent 14% of the global tuna supply but are linked to more than 90% of employment in all fisheries worldwide.

READ MORE
MAY 219:25 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Thai Union’s collagen, peptide purification plants delve into co-product utilization

Thai Union Group started commercial collagen and peptide purification operations to utilize by-products from tuna processing at its new plants in Samut Sakhon, Thailand, in September 2023.

At “state-of-the-art” plants, the Thai tuna giant produces collagen peptides from tuna and freshwater fish co-products and fish protein hydrolytes from tuna by-products.

READ MORE
MAY 218:27 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Tri Marine: US canned tuna demand drops in volume, rises in value, as private labels gain market share in 2023

During his presentation, Matthew Owens, sustainability director at Tri Marine Group, US, highlighted some significant trends in the US tuna market in recent years, including market growth, private label trends, and the increasing emphasis on sustainability.

Owens noted that the US canned tuna market experienced noticeable growth between 2018 and 2022, partly driven by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, 2023 saw a slight decline in overall market volume and an increase in value, similar to the trend in the EU markets.

READ MORE
MAY 215:01 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
UK-based Princes commits to 100% MSC-labeled tuna products

Princes Group, the UK food-and-beverage brand owned by Japan’s Mitsubishi Corp., has set a target to offer only Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) ecolabel-certified canned products by the end of 2025.

The move comes after the UK cannery achieved 100% MSC-certified for tuna products sold in the Netherlands in 2022, Neil Bohannon, procurement director for Princes.

READ MORE
MAY 213:34 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Middle East tuna consumption declines

The current market value for the tuna industry in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region stands at approximately $800 million, despite facing significant challenges, according to Arnab Sengupta, deputy CEO at JMB International, Thailand.

The tuna market in the MENA region witnessed a downturn last year, the first in recent years (see slide below), primarily due to economic challenges and shifting consumer preferences, he said.

READ MORE
MAY 213:25 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Global tuna product exports slid 3% in 2023

Global tuna product export was estimated to experience a 2.5% year-on-year decline to 1.72 million metric tons in 2023, worth $8.23 billion, down 5.5%, according to Amornphan Aramwatananont, director of Thai Tuna Industry Association (TTIA).

Exports from Asia-Pacific regions accounted for 52% of the total global shipment volumes, an estimated 900,000t.

READ MORE
MAY 2112:44 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
GTA expands with new participation of Japanese, French firms

Daniel Suddaby, executive director for the Global Tuna Alliance (GTA) announced that the two new Japanese partners, Meihou and Usufuku Honten, has just joined in the GTA.

“We’re no longer a European focused organization,” stressed Suddaby. “We are not only spreading across the supply chain, but we are geographically spreading, represented all of the major regions.”

READ MORE
MAY 209:23 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Skipjack prices for delivery in Bangkok move upwards, as Manta prices drop amid record catches

The tuna market in Manta, Ecuador, has experienced a significant decline in prices over recent weeks, now standing at $1,350 per metric ton, down sharply from last month’s $1,400-$1,500/t range. Earlier this month, some deals were even struck in Manta for around a week at $1,300/t, highlighting the rapid decline, but now prices are back at around $1,350/t, according to Ecuadorian sources in Bangkok.

The primary driver behind this steep price drop is the continuous robust catches in both Ecuadorian and Peruvian waters. With storage facilities at full capacity and vessels lining up to unload their catches, the oversupply situation has exacerbated the price fall.

READ MORE
MAY 209:05 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Bolton merges food arm with Tri Marine, Corrales appointed senior VP of business development 

As of January 2024, Bolton Food and Tri Marine, both business units of Bolton, have merged to form a new integrated business unit. Luca Alemanno has taken on the dual role of CEO at both Bolton Food and Tri Marine. 

Bolton Group has announced that Juan Corrales, formerly CEO of Tri Marine, has taken on the role of senior vice president business development, reporting to the CEO.

READ MORE
MAY 2010:31 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Indonesia launches new strategy framework for quota-based tuna fishery management

As the largest archipelagic country, Indonesian authorities launched the tuna harvest strategy framework in 2023, in an effort to sustain the future of the fisheries.

The recommendation from the framework has been used as a reference for the implementation of government regulation, including quota-based fisheries managements, for yellowfin, bigeye, and skipjack tuna.

READ MORE
MAY 2010:23 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Maersk targets sustainability goals, despite challenges

Thue Barfod, global director of Maersk’s fish and seafood vertical, highlighted the complexities of implementing sustainable practices in a highly dynamic and often disrupted global marketplace.

“Sustainability is an interesting topic, but also a challenge to actually execute,” he stated. His presentation illustrated the extensive network of Maersk’s shipping routes worldwide, highlighting the logistical complexities and environmental considerations that come with managing such a vast operation.

READ MORE
MAY 209:38 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Pouches, ready-to-eat products gain popularity in Australia, New Zealand

The tuna market in Australia and New Zealand is evolving with a clear focus on innovation and sustainability, according to Tim Anastasopoulos, procurement senior category manager at Simplot Food Group in Australia.

He said the majority of tuna in the Australian and New Zealand markets is sourced from the Western and Central Pacific, with only a minor portion coming from the Indian Ocean. 

READ MORE
MAY 208:47 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Thai tuna industry establishes new guidelines for migrant worker recruitment

The Thai tuna industry is currently working to reduce the risks of human trafficking, especially for Burmese workers in the country, through its new recruitment guidelines in partnership with the International Labour Organization (ILO), according to Chanintr Chalisarapong, the president of Thai Tuna Industry Association (TTIA). 

The move has come with their buyers and stakeholders beginning to realize the importance of labor recruitment guidelines, according to ILO principles, he told Undercurrent News on the side of the conference. 

READ MORE
MAY 208:44 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
PNG approves preferential new vessel day rates to local processors

Jelta Wong, Papua New Guinea’s minister for fisheries and marine resources, said that the country’s fisheries sector is poised for a transformational policy shift aimed at developing a robust, diversified, and globally competitive industry. 

During his presentation, he observed that this transformation will require comprehensive legislative, policy, and regulatory interventions across the fishing and processing industry. According to Wong, the PNG’s National Fisheries Association is actively working on initiatives to expand commercial fishing capacity and enhance aquaculture productivity, with tuna fisheries being a primary focus.

READ MORE
MAY 204:17 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
FAO: Seafood accounts for half of global animal protein exports

Fishery and aquaculture are the key sources that provide 49% of all animal protein exports in value, including beef, poultry, and pork, according to Marcio Castro de Souza, senior fishery officer, international trade of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO).

“That’s quite significant in terms of exporting and international trade profile,” he said. “Fisheries is the only animal protein that is a shared good, and to deal with a shared good, we need conserved actions.”

READ MORE
MAY 202:49 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Fiji tuna catches account for nearly 90% of TAC

Rovereto Nayacalevu, acting permanent secretary for the ministry of fisheries for Fiji, said the country’s tuna catches, including albacore, bigeye and yellowfin, stood at 9,899 metric tons in 2022, accounting for nearly 90% of the total allowable catch of 10,109t.

“These underscore the paramount importance of tuna within our fishing sector, both in terms of volume and economic significance,” he said at the opening ceremony of the 18th Infofish World Tuna Trade Conference and Exhibition. “It is essential to note that tuna dominates our catch, with other tuna-like species contributing substantially to the remaining 10% of the TAC, approximately over 1,000t.”

READ MORE
MAY 202:29 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Maldives aims to increase domestic tuna processing

Ahmed Shiyam, Maldives’ minister for fisheries and agriculture, said the country aims to increase its domestic tuna processing. 

According to Shiyam, the country catches around 100,000 metric tons of skipjack, 60% of which is exported as raw material to be processed elsewhere in the world.

READ MORE
MAY 198:55 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Skipjack tuna prices expected to rise as sector executives convene in Bangkok

As tuna executives gather in Bangkok for the Infofish tuna conference, anticipation looms over a potential uptick in skipjack tuna prices in the coming days. 

In recent months, buyers worldwide have inked a flurry of contracts, capitalizing on the relatively subdued tuna prices. 

READ MORE
MAY 198:49 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Mixed views arise from recent IOTC meeting

The latest annual session of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC), held in Bangkok, Thailand, concluded on May 17, leaving a trail of mixed sentiments among stakeholders. While some hailed progress in modernized management for certain species, others expressed deep concerns over the measures approved.

European fishing industry bodies voiced strong opposition to the measures approved on the management of fish aggregation devices (FADs), warning of severe consequences for the EU fleet.

READ MORE

title: Barcelona 2024: Smaller sizes, low coho prices pressure Chilean salmon in US; JP Klausen to process Kiwi H&G in Peru for Europe
content:
BARCELONA, Spain -- The Undercurrent News team reported live from Seafood Expo Global (SEG), held here, April 23-25. 

Before that, on April 22, Undercurrent also attended the Fish Pool/DNB salmon aquaculture seminar.

Auto updates: On
APR 2610:22 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Nissui’s JP Klausen to process Kiwi H&G fish in Peru for Europe

Nissui Corp.-owned supplier J.P. Klausen & Co. has started shipping headed and gutted (H&G) fish from New Zealand to Peru to then be processed into fillets and portions for Europe, the Denmark-based company’s CEO told Undercurrent News.

Containers with New Zealand fish such as H&G southern blue whiting, orange roughy, dory and hoki are on the water to Peru, which has a free trade agreement (FTA) with the EU and where JP Klausen with partner plants, Jens Peter Klausen told Undercurrent.

READ MORE
APR 2610:05 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Smaller sizes, low coho prices pressure Chilean salmon in US

In recent months, Chilean salmon prices have been pressured by a complex interplay between available supply, demand, and international trade strategies.  

The high availability of coho salmon at relatively low prices compared to Atlantic salmon and the fact that there is a slower production of large salmon has pressured prices in recent months, industry sources in Barcelona said.

READ MORE
APR 269:08 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Venezuela’s largest shrimp exporter eyes US expansion with new value-added plant, upgrades

Venezuelan shrimp giant Grupo Lamar maintains a strong presence in Europe while setting its sights on expansion in the US.

At the firm’s busy stand during the Barcelona expo, Rincon highlighted Lamar’s consistent performance in Europe, emphasizing the company’s robust operations on the continent. “We remain strong in Europe,” he said, indicating Lamar’s stability and success in this key market.

READ MORE
APR 263:02 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Norway’s frozen whole cod exports to Vietnam soar in early 2024

How export markets for frozen cod would rearrange in the wake of the US government’s decision to ban all imports of Russian origin cod has been an open question in the early months of 2024.

But, according to data shared with Undercurrent News from the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC) at the show, the result has been a huge shift to Vietnam, which overnight became the largest single export market by volume for Norwegian frozen whole cod in Q1.

READ MORE
APR 262:56 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Scotland’s Organic Sea Harvest still pursuing two new sites

Scottish salmon farm Organic Sea Harvest (OSH) is still pursuing applications for licenses at two new sites in addition to the two it currently operates, Ove Thu – CEO of Blue Resource group and chair of OSH – told Undercurrent News.

“We have applications in for two new sites, which would allow us to operate much more efficiently and year-round,” he said. “Customers want organic salmon year-round, not just part of the year.”

READ MORE
APR 252:11 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Portuguese processor Brasmar achieves record turnover, profit

Portuguese seafood processor and trader Brasmar achieved its best results ever last year. Speaking to Undercurrent News during the Barcelona expo, CEO Sergio Couto Reis said Brasmar’s total sales reached €320 million in 2023, which was slightly below expectations due to market conditions in the latter half of the year. 

However, according to Couto, the company achieved the highest turnover and profit margin. “So everyone is happy,” he said.

READ MORE
APR 2510:20 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Kilic consolidates its position as Turkiye’s largest seafood exporter with Agromey acquisition

Turkish seabass and seabream producer Kilic Holding has solidified its position as the country’s largest seafood exporter following the acquisition of Agromey, another prominent seabass and seabream farmer, according to Sinan Kiziltan, the firm’s vice president.

The acquisition was announced last month.

READ MORE
APR 259:43 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
UK-Greenland FTA talks said to be back on, still pressure for higher coldwater shrimp ATQ

The UK’s talks with Greenland on a free trade agreement (FTA) are back on after stalling altogether in 2023, but any progress still looks to be a way off, a source familiar with the process told Undercurrent News.

Civil servants working within the UK government guess that a deal should be struck soon after a general election. Prime minister Rishi Sunak has said he expects that “in the second half” of 2024.

READ MORE
APR 259:08 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
US states tackling invasive species problem with marketing

An invasive fish that’s become a problem in rivers in two US states is also turning into a sales opportunity for fishermen and fishing companies.

Wild blue catfish—introduced to Virginia and Maryland in the 1970s for recreational fishing—have proliferated to the point that they now account for as much as 80% of all fish species in some river systems.

READ MORE
APR 258:08 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
US companies say lack of a trade agreement with the EU puts them at a disadvantage

American seafood companies have been busy at the Seafood Global Exhibition in Barcelona this week, pitching everything from wild Alaskan salmon and cod to Maine lobster, aiming to make more deals with potential customers.

However, many of them say the sales pitch is more challenging because the US does not have a trade deal with the EU.

READ MORE
APR 257:01 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Salmon trader hopes EU successful in ending Norway’s production fish ‘export ban’

One salmon trader, at least, is hopeful that the EU is able to work out a deal with Norway that will see the latter’s “production fish” sold to Europe on the open market.

The EU Commission (EC) has said it will open talks with Norway after finding the Scandinavian country’s policy of processing all downgraded salmon in-country should be considered a “barrier to trade.”

READ MORE
APR 256:26 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
New group to promote Japanese scallop exports sees positive reaction from visitors 

The Japan Scallop Export Promotion Association has had positive reactions from visitors at Seafood Expo Global (SEG), Ichiro Nomura, the chairperson of the association, told Undercurrent News.

The association was incorporated last October, coincidently after China, the main destination for Japanese scallops, banned Japanese seafood last August following the release of treated wastewater from the damaged Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant into the ocean.

READ MORE
APR 255:51 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Weather woes impact illex squid catch, prices rise in Argentina

The illex squid market in Argentina is witnessing a surge in prices as the 2024 fishing season progresses, sources in the industry told Undercurrent News. 

Recent data from Argentina’s ministry of agriculture, livestock and fisheries shows a substantial increase in landings compared to last year, with around 115,000 metric tons harvested in the first four months of the year. 

READ MORE
APR 255:43 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Barents supply stability allows big Norwegian coldwater shrimp exporter to begin expansion

The expected stability of supply in the Barents Sea coldwater shrimp supply has allowed major Norwegian exporter Stella Polaris to commit to its expansion plans, CEO Christian Nordahl told Undercurrent News.

The Norwegian total allowable catch is over 100,000 metric tons, but in 2022 and 2023, the fleet landed roughly 34,000t, he noted. This year that’s expected to rise, “but not by an amount that the market wouldn’t be able to handle,” he said.

READ MORE
APR 254:14 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takauchi
Sushi topping market gets back to normal after tough times 

Sushi topping product market is getting back to normal from “the disaster” in the last few years, Chien- Tin Lin, a president of New Cheng Corp, Taipei, Taiwan-based delicacy seafood processor told Undercurrent News.

Most of sushi topping products, including salted Capelin roe (Masago) and flying fish roe (Tobiko), had seen sharp ups and downs in prices, impacting the earnings of the delicacy seafood sectors in the past few years, Chien said.

READ MORE
APR 254:00 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
US lobster industry braces for impact of new minimum size rules

New minimum size requirements that will take effect in 2025 will have a significant short-term impact on the US east coast lobster fishery, one live lobster exporter told Undercurrent News at the Seafood Expo Global (SEG) show in Barcelona this week.

As previously reported by Undercurrent, the minimum and maximum catch sizes for lobster in certain parts of the Gulf of Maine will change gradually by fractions of an inch starting in January 2025, with additional changes to come in 2027 and 2028.

READ MORE
APR 253:22 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Norway’s new fisheries minister already ‘has the picture’ of production-fish clash with EU

Norway’s new minister for fisheries and oceans, Marianne Sivertsen Naess, was only appointed to the role a few days ago, but has rapidly been brought up to speed on the country’s “production fish” row with the EU, a source with an exporter told Undercurrent News.

The EU Commission (EC) is to open talks with Norway after finding the Scandinavian country’s policy of processing all downgraded salmon in-country should be considered a “barrier to trade.”

READ MORE
APR 252:15 AM GMT
European groups unite in lobbying, promotional alliance

The European Fish Processors Association (AIPCE CEP), European Association of Fish Producers Organisations (EAPO), fishing representative body Europeche, and the Federation of European Aquaculture Producers (FEAP) have announced their intent to launch a strategic alliance during SEG.

Through this alliance, they seek to “amplify their impact by forging common ground and promoting collaborative initiatives to reach out to a wider audience.”

READ MORE
APR 2512:48 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
​Vietnamese Ocean Gift plans to increase revenue to $40m in 2024

A Vietnamese value-added seafood producer, Ocean Gift Foods, is looking to increase its turnover to $40 million in 2024, a growth of $3m from the previous year, an executive told Undercurrent News at SEG.

“We intends to thrive further growth amid tough times, as our main market, Japan, has seen the depreciation of its currency against the dollar,’ said Troung Nguyen (right below), a sales representative for the company.

READ MORE
APR 241:30 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Giant squid catches in Peru remain scarce

The Peruvian fishing industry is facing a significant scarcity of giant squid catches.

Suppliers at the Barcelona Seafood Expo indicated that Peru has experienced a prolonged period, lasting approximately nine to ten months, without substantial giant squid catches. 

READ MORE
APR 2410:18 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Seaborn investing strongly to widen market for trout

Major Norwegian salmonid distributor Seaborn is investing to promote the sale of fjord trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss), chief sales and marketing officer Maria Barroso told Undercurrent News.

Traditionally, Norwegian trout is a seasonal product, requiring quite niche markets given that it was not supplied year-round. With the salmon sector booming over the past decade, trout has become the “little sister,” she said.

READ MORE
APR 248:59 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Norwegian salmon plant 1814 flies first fresh shipment to US

New Norwegian salmon processing plant 1814 Salmon flew its first shipment of fresh goods to the US in March, Alf-Goran Knutsen — general manager for Kvaroy Fiskeoppdrett, one of the factory’s owners — told Undercurrent News.

Also owned by Fram Seafood and investment company Nyhamn, 1814 was launched to add more value to salmon before the fish leave Norway, with a view to producing fillets to fly to Asia and the US and truck to Europe.

READ MORE
APR 248:48 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Land-based trout farmer’s design optimization means US sites will aim for 22,000t

Norwegian land-based trout farmer Hima Seafood is closing in on having all the preparations in place to break ground on its US expansion in the third quarter of 2025, chief investment officer Magnus Torp told Undercurrent News.

“The type of site needs to be quite specific to us — high-quality groundwater is key, with no salt. That’s not only for the trout but also so that the leftover feed and feces can be sold as organic fertilizer,” he explained.

READ MORE
APR 248:10 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Canadian cracks code to improve shelf life of sea urchin caviar

A company in the Canadian province of British Columbia (BC) has cracked open the door for sea urchin caviar exports to Europe with an innovative process to extend the shelf life of the urchin roe.

Unifresco is one of several companies from BC that supply the Asian markets with uni.

READ MORE
APR 247:46 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Taiwan looks to place quotas on coastal Pacific mackerel fishery

Taiwanese authorities are looking to introduce a catching quota on Pacific mackerel in the economy waters, an executive of the fishery sector told Undercurrent News.

Taiwanese coastal Pacific mackerel fishing takes places place on the coasts off northern Taipei throughout the year, except for February and June, said Eric Lin, general manager of JM Ocean Corp, which operates two purse seiners for pelagic fishery in the economy.

READ MORE
APR 247:28 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Siam Canadian’s Gulkin: US shrimp market slowly moving again, duties won’t be big factor

After a tough 2023, Siam Canadian Group’s Jim Gulkin is seeing the US shrimp market slowly return to buying.

As has been widely reported, 2023 was a terrible year in the US shrimp sector, as large inventories that had built up during the COVID pandemic met reduced demand as retail spending slowed. Retail demand was hit by travel starting up again and foodservice re-opening post-pandemic, but the stocks had already been accumulated.

READ MORE
APR 246:11 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Loch Duart celebrates green feed use on 25th anniversary

One year since introducing BioMar Group’s “blue impact feed,” Scottish salmon farmer Loch Duart is celebrating its 25th anniversary by announcing that the new, improved diet means its salmon is now “industry-leading in health, low impact farming and purity.”

The feed maintains a high level of omega-3 levels, reduces its carbon footprint, and gives Loch Duart “the lead in lowering its foraged fish dependency ratio [FFDR],” it claimed.

READ MORE
APR 246:02 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Gjogur joins Icelandic Pelagic group as it, Skinney await new vessels

Icelandic fishing company Gjogur has become part of the Iceland Pelagic group, joining Isfelag, Skinney-Thinganes, and Brim. 

It has also joined Stormar, which markets those same firms’ whitefish, mainly in the UK and France.  

READ MORE
APR 245:41 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Sales of fish to Ukraine still hampered by Polish border blockades

Polish farmers’ blockades of roads and rail links over perceived unfair competition in favor of Ukraine — which, as Undercurrent News previously reported, began in the fall of 2023 — continue to hamper the sale of fish in the region.

“The price to truck pelagics through Poland and into Ukraine now is insane,” an Icelandic source told Undercurrent. “It’s meant delays on shipments, it’s hurt some of the capelin sales this season.”

READ MORE
APR 243:49 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Aussie rock lobster co-op launches retail packs

The Geraldton Fishermen’s Cooperative is launching a range of raw frozen lobster packs for retail chains, representatives told Undercurrent News.

The range, to be launched under its established Brolos brand, has been a long-term project for the group as it continues to diversify beyond the Chinese market, after China banned imports of live Australian rock lobster in 2020.

READ MORE
APR 242:16 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Sea Harvest ‘weeks’ away from closing landmark deal, celebrates 60-year anniversary at SEG

South Africa’s Sea Harvest Group is closing in on finalizing a landmark deal for Terrasan Group’s pelagic business and a 60% stake in its abalone operations, CEO Felix Ratheb told Undercurrent News during the week of Seafood Expo Global (SEG) in Barcelona, Spain.

The approval on the deal “goes to competition authority tribunal this week, “so we probably two weeks away,” said Ratheb, as the company gears up to celebrate 60 years in business at SEG, he said.

READ MORE
APR 241:09 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan pavilion runs cooking demonstrations for first time at SEG

The Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) has established a Japan pavilion at Seafood Expo Global (SEG), with a total of 19 exhibitors this year.

The number of participants is an increase from 13 companies the previous year, with an exhibit space for each participant narrowing from the previous year’s nine square meters to six square meters.

READ MORE
APR 2311:44 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Kunihiro expands Pacific oyster sales via Nissui’s Nordic marketing channels

A Japanese seafood processor, Kunihiro, plans to increase its Pacific oyster (Crassostrea gigas) shipments to the EU market to 40 metric tons this year.

The Onomichi, Hiroshima-based firm is an “equity method affiliate” for Japanese seafood giant Nissui. Following a trial shipment of “Japanese frozen full shell oyster” last year, the company markets the oysters through Nissui’s Nordic Seafood supply chain, Hiroshi Kawasaki, a director and chief marketing executive for Kunihiro told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
APR 2311:04 PM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Japan’s Yamasa Kamaboko launches Tempura Alaskan pollock crab sticks 

A Japanese surimi finished product manufacturer, Yamasa Kamaboko, is marketing Tempura-style Alaskan pollock crab sticks in the EU market.

The name of the product “BOCO’S” comes from Kamaboko, which means surimi finished products in Japanese. BOCO’s has been available only at its own shop in Japan, but the manufacturer is now promoting it in the EU.

READ MORE
APR 2312:58 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Pescanova exec optimistic as first quarter 2024 sales surge

Seafood consumption in European markets such as Spain, France, and Italy is surging after challenging years, according to Fernando Zaldivar, Nueva Pescanova’s commercial, marketing and innovation director.

In Spain alone, Pescanova’s first-quarter volume sales have surged by 5.2%, marking a significant recovery, according to Zaldivar.

READ MORE
APR 2312:53 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
UK coldwater shrimp prices rising a little too quickly

The prices of cooked and peeled coldwater shrimp have risen in recent weeks and are expected to continue to do so, a source with an important UK importer told Undercurrent News.

The rise is being driven by rising demand and a lack of raw materials. 

READ MORE
APR 2312:38 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Poland’s Suempol ups ‘deli’ range of ready-to-eat products

Polish salmon processor Suempol had debuted several new products in the “ready-to-eat” category in time for its homeland’s May 1 vacations and to be nominated as finalists in SEG’s “seafood excellence” awards.

Its salmon kofta “kebabs,” baked flavored salmon, and salmon “meatballs” expands its “deli” range, an area it has been growing as it tries to tempt consumers who may not necessarily love salmon, but are looking for healthier alternatives to processed meat, said the firm’s Pawel Piech.

READ MORE
APR 2311:40 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Regal Springs launches new branch to harness tilapia by-products

Regal Springs has announced the launch of a new business branch, “Regal Springs Natural Additions,” to be headquartered in Hamburg, Germany.

The new business unit — under the leadership of Petra Weigl, general manager of Regal Springs Europe — marks a step towards maximizing the firm’s utilization of tilapia, aiming for 100% by 2030.

READ MORE
APR 239:54 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
French lobster supplier 5DO intends to increase offshore sales and VAP lineups

A French lobster processor 5DO (Cinq Degree Ouest) is expanding its sales to offshore markets, including Germany, Spain, the UK, China, and Japan.

5DO claims that it is a pioneer in high-pressure processing (HPP) in Europe, a method that extracts meat from shellfish and crustaceans. The products include Homard Bleu (Homarus gammarus) lobster tail, tail and claws, and half tail shell-on.

READ MORE
APR 238:49 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
High Liner continues diversification from China, eyes ‘near-shoring’

High Liner Foods is continuing to reduce its reliance on re-processing in China, with the large Canada-based processor also eyeing moving production back closer to home.

The company, which generates around two-thirds of its sales from the US market, has been moving processing out of China and into Indonesia and Vietnam in the past few years, CEO Paul Jewer told Undercurrent News at Seafood Expo Global.

READ MORE
APR 238:42 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Still business as usual at Turkish bass, bream firm Lucky Fish post-PE acquisition 

“Everything is the same,” assured an executive at Izmir, Turkey-based seabass and seabream farmer Lucky Fish, when asked about the acquisition last year by United Arab Emirates-based private equity firm E20 Investments. 

E20 Investments acquired a 70% stake from Turkey-focused private equity firm Mediterra Capital Partners in October of last year. Mediterra Capital, which acquired 100% of Lucky Fish in 2013, attempted to sell Lucky Fish back in 2017, as reported by Undercurrent News at the time. 

READ MORE
APR 238:26 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
French discount chain Noz doubles sales in 2023, expands global B2B operations

French discount retailer Noz doubled its sales to €800 million ($852m) in 2023. 

The company, which purchases surplus and clearance goods from seafood producers, has solidified its position within France and expanded its reach globally with a strategic B2B cross-trading business, according to its buyer for Southern Europe, Raffael Buenos Aires (in the photo below at the Seafood Expo Global in Barcelona this week).

READ MORE
APR 237:56 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
State-backed Omani company ready to welcome second tuna vessel, investing partners

Fisheries Development Oman (FDO) — founded by the government under its Oman Investment Authority — has taken delivery of its first new tuna purse seiner and expects the second by the end of May, group director for business development Badar Al Naabi told Undercurrent News.

Between them, the pair will have a fishing capacity of 20,000 metric tons. They will fish in the Indian Ocean. 

READ MORE
APR 237:46 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Acme’s Norlax launches new steamed salmon range in Oceania

Danish smoker Norlax, part of Acme Smoked Fish since 2021, has launched a new line of steamed products in Oceania as the group looks to bolster its ready-to-eat options.

Supplied to Australian distributor Ocean Blue and launched initially under that brand in retailer Cole’s, Acme and Norlax hope the format will also appeal in New Zealand and, ultimately, in Europe and the US.

READ MORE
APR 236:54 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Canada kills funding for seafood marketing campaign

Just two years after launching a program to encourage more Canadians to buy seafood, the Canadian government has halted funding for the Choose Canadian Seafood campaign.

The latest budget from the Government of Canada, which was revealed on April 16, did not provide any money to continue the campaign.

READ MORE
APR 236:49 AM GMT
By Masahiko Takeuchi
Mowi Japan looks to launch new brand for smaller-sized, three-year Atlantic salmon

Mowi Japan is looking to launch a new brand for its smaller-sized, three-year-old farmed Atlantic salmon from Norway.

The move comes as the Japanese sales arm of the Norwegian farmer has seen strong performances of “Emperor Salmon” in Japan. “Emperor Salmon” is the brand name for three-year-old Atlantic salmon, with fish weighing over nine kilograms per fish.

READ MORE
APR 236:44 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Spain’s Froxa eyes growth with new product developments, business line

Spanish frozen processor Froxa is poised to see growth in 2024 by venturing into new product developments and a new business line, the firm’s co-owner and CEO, Jose Javier Fernandez, told Undercurrent News.

The firm is aiming to elevate its brand to “a premium level” and will debut samples of its new product line during the show, with an official launch scheduled for October during Conxemar in Vigo.

READ MORE
APR 232:54 AM GMT
Iceland’s Skaginn 3X enters Chile with ‘seven-digit’ Friosur contract

Icelandic processing equipment manufacturer Skaginn 3X has announced its entry into the Chilean market via a “seven-digit” contract with Friosur.

The Chilean firm acquires a Skaginn 3X freezing and glazing system, the “multi-lane IQF freezer,” which can freeze 2,500 kilograms of salmon fillets per hour, cooled rapidly to below 21°C.

READ MORE
APR 2212:07 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
2025 a lively year for Norwegian aquaculture regulation

Next year is looking like a pivotal one for Norwegian aquaculture regulation, not least because a general election in the country could shift the political direction that has been in place for the last year or two, said Lisa Marie Opdahl of the Bergen Office of Law firm BAHR.

Firstly, regulation changes on sustainable new technologies in coastal aquaculture — which were due to be looked at by the government in 2025 but which industry pressure was able to bring forward — could end up coming into effect next year.

READ MORE
APR 2211:43 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
DNB expects no easing in salmon spot prices for foreseeable future

There was little surprise in the salmon spot price outlook given by DNB Markets analyst Alexander Aukner at the Fish Pool/ DNB seminar. Supply growth looks very limited, both in Norway and globally, and demand is not expected to change, meaning continued high prices, he said.

Aukner noted that in future, we might be talking about several different price outlooks, for different products — fillets, downgraded salmon, or new sizes, as well as the standard 3-6 kilogram superior fish. 

READ MORE
APR 2210:33 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Switching of salmon futures to euros means advantage for European buyers

As part of Fish Pool’s listing of salmon futures on Euronext (see previous blog post), trading in forward contracts will switch from Norwegian kroner to euros. 

This should hand the advantage to European buyers and could be a disadvantage to Norwegian farmers, said DNB Markets, with reduced currency risk for those in the EU.

READ MORE
APR 229:57 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Fish Pool lists salmon futures on Euronext Paris Commodity Derivatives market

Euronext will list new cash-settled Salmon Futures on its Euronext Paris Commodity Derivatives Market based on the Sitagri Salmon Spot Index. 

This contract will be available in the EUA test environment (Next EUA) from June 6, 2024. The first trading day in production is scheduled for July 22, 2024.

READ MORE
APR 225:23 AM GMT
By María Feijóo
Spain’s Cabomar launches updated brand identity

Spanish wholesaler Cabomar Congelados has unveiled its refreshed brand identity ahead of the show, the firm’s director of marketing, Tania Lage, confirmed to Undercurrent News. 

“Our journey over the past 18 years defines and inspires us for the future, urging us to grow and seek positive changes. We introduced one of these changes with a refreshed image that embodies our timeless values,” the firm said on LinkedIn. 

READ MORE
APR 224:50 AM GMT
Profand launches new Greek seabass, branded tapas lines in UK

Kefalonia Fisheries — a Greek aquaculture firm owned by Spain’s Grupo Profand — has selected the UK as its first market to launch a range of retail-ready seabass products, it announced.

The items will be launched by sister company Profand UK via its Cornwall-based retail co-packing partner Ocean Fish (Retail) — formerly S. Riddler, now part of the Ocean Fish group.

READ MORE

Contact the authors tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, neil.ramsden@undercurrentnews.com, matilde.mereghetti@undercurrentnews.com, Maria.Feijoo@undercurrentnews.com, dan.gibson@undercurrentnews.com, barb.simmons@undercurrentnews.com, masahiko.takeuchi@undercurrentnews.com

title: IFFO Miami: Initial Peruvian landings, yields offer fish oil price relief
content:
The International Marine Ingredients Organisation (IFFO) kicked off its first session of the year for the marine ingredients sector in Miami, Florida, on Monday (April 15).

The event, which is the smaller of two annual sessions and for members only, has drawn a joint record 220 delegates from 29 countries. Delegates include representatives from the fishmeal and fish oil industry, as well as experts in aquaculture, pharmaceuticals, and sustainability.

Check our live blog for the latest expert reports, opinions and analyses for this far-reaching global sector. 

Auto updates: On
APR 176:11 PM GMT
Peruvian trading firm tapped foreign fish oil suppliers during El Nino

Marex Global Sourcing, a major fish oil brokerage company based in Peru, managed to supply its clients with fish oil despite dramatically reduced supply from Peru over the past year.

Peru is normally the world’s top producer of fish oil from anchovy fisheries, with volumes reaching 300,000 metric tons in the 1990s. However, ocean warming effects from El Nino resulted in fish oil plummeting in 2023 to just 18,000t.

READ MORE
APR 175:50 PM GMT
Certifications alone not a ‘panacea’ for labor abuses

An executive with UK-based sustainability organization MarinTrust said certifications alone are not a “panacea” for preventing labor abuses in supply chains.

“You have to be realistic. An audit is a snapshot in time,” Libby Woodhatch, executive chair of the fishmeal and fish oil certification group, told Undercurrent News. “No one could ever say whatever standard they’ve got is going to be 100% foolproof.”

READ MORE
APR 173:56 PM GMT
Faroe Islands startup hooks industry on vessel tracking platform

Faroe Islands-based startup FishFacts is helping to digitalize the fishing industry with its vessel tracking platform, according to co-founder and sales manager Hanus Samro.

FishFacts, which was founded in 2018, uses a proprietary database that tracks all commercial fishing vessels globally using satellites, categorizing them by type and gear used. This allows fishermen to identify the most promising fishing locations based on other vessel activity in real-time.

READ MORE
APR 173:11 PM GMT
Good early fishing for Peruvian anchovy should temper fish oil prices

Initial reports from Peru’s first anchovy fishing season indicate good catching and oil yields, offering respite for an industry starved of supply.

On the sidelines of the IFFO Miami event, Enrico Bachis, chief market analyst at the host organization, told Undercurrent News that 86,000 metric tons of anchovy have been landed in the first two fishing days since fleets embarked to fish at midnight on April 16.

READ MORE
APR 1610:21 PM GMT
IFFO: Microplastics in fishmeal, fish oil ‘negligible’

Microplastics detected in fishmeal pose little risk of contaminating farmed fish, according to Brett Glencross, technical director at IFFO, the marine ingredients organization.

Glencross told Undercurrent News that when he first joined IFFO three years ago, “microplastics were all the rage.” At the time, only one published study had examined fishmeal samples globally and found microplastic contamination to be widespread though variable.

READ MORE
APR 165:28 PM GMT
China’s fishmeal consumption declined by 200,000t in 2023

China’s fishmeal consumption declined by an estimated 200,000 metric tons last year amid a weak aquaculture sector, high prices and oversupply in China’s pig industry.

The world’s largest fishmeal importer brought in 1.65 million metric tons of fishmeal in 2023, down 9% compared with the year prior. Although domestic fishmeal production increased to 450,000t from 390,000t in 2022, the increase was not enough to offset the drop in imports.

READ MORE
APR 163:06 PM GMT
Shrimp meal for pet food still niche but growing

Shrimp meal is being used in cat food in the US in small quantities, but not in amounts meaningful for shrimp producers, according to an industry expert.

“Some companies will mix shrimp and salmon, crab; a lot is going into blends for cat food,” said John Rodysill, trading unit manager at Omaha, Nebraska-based Scoular Company. “But it is still small.”

READ MORE
APR 161:12 PM GMT
‘Survival mode’ for makers of fish oil for dietary supplements

The fish oil industry that produces oils for dietary supplements continues to face major supply shortages, leaving companies in “survival mode,” according to an industry expert.

Aldo Bernasconi, vice president of data science at the Global Organization for EPA and DHA, or GOED, said makers of fish oil products for human consumption are reaching the bottom of the barrel when it comes to supply.

READ MORE
APR 1611:02 AM GMT
Salmon meal market buoyed by strong US pet food demand

After seeing skyrocketing growth coming out of the COVID-19 pandemic, US demand for premium high-protein pet foods has cooled off somewhat but remains strong, according to an executive at Omaha, Nebraska-based Scoular Company.

John Rodysill, trading unit manager at the $10 billion US grain and food ingredients giant, said pet food manufacturers ramped up production between 2020-2022 to meet demand spikes of as much as 10% annually. But purchasing slowed in 2023 as consumers balked at rising prices.

READ MORE

title: Alaska’s ComFish 2024: US senator to travel abroad in effort to expand ban on Russian seafood
content:
KODIAK, Alaska -- Undercurrent News reported live from ComFish, the commercial fishing trade show that took place in Kodiak, in the US state of Alaska, held Thursday-Saturday (April 11-13, 2024).

The event kicked off Thursday with legislative updates from Republican US senator Lisa Murkowski and Democratic US representative Mary Peltola. Industry panels, over the three days, are to include presentations by the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute and Pacific Seafood Processors Association, as well as an update on the Bristol Bay commercial sockeye fishery ahead of the summer season.

Auto updates: On
APR 138:07 PM GMT
US commerce secretary pledges support for Alaska’s fisheries

US secretary of commerce Gina Raimondo told ComFish attendees during pre-taped remarks Saturday morning (April 13) that the department is committed to Alaska’s seafood industry as it confronts a myriad global market challenges.

“I promise you to continue to work across federal agencies to improve coordination between initiatives and increase access to resources that can benefit the seafood sector, including grants, loans and workforce development programs,” she said.

READ MORE
APR 136:06 PM GMT
Industry groups push for more domestic marketing as Russia ban hits

The market conditions currently hitting Alaska’s seafood industry are at crisis levels, according to United Fishermen of Alaska (UFA) executive director Tracy Welch, but the impending ban on Russian seafood products entering the US presents a prime opportunity to reach more domestic consumers. 

Welch and Pacific Seafood Processors Association (PSPA) executive director Julie Decker made that case at a ComFish panel Saturday afternoon (April 13).

READ MORE
APR 135:41 PM GMT
Alaska Fish and Game commissioner decries possible endangered species protections for king salmon

Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADFG) commissioner Doug Vincent-Lang says he anticipates the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) will move forward with the next phase of its review process for a potential federal Endangered Species Act (ESA) listing for Alaskan king, or Chinook, salmon.

Vincent-Lang told ComFish attendees during a Saturday morning (April 13) ComFish panel that the department has not received official word from NOAA, although a petition for ESA protections from the Washington state based environmental group Wild Fish Conservancy (WFC) was submitted Jan. 11. 

READ MORE
APR 132:53 PM GMT
Sullivan to travel abroad in effort to expand ban on Russian seafood

US senator Dan Sullivan, a Republican from Alaska, will be heading to Europe later this month to make his case for an EU-wide ban on seafood products imported from Russia.

Sullivan told attendees at an in-person panel at Kodiak, Alaska’s ComFish trade show on Saturday (April 13) that he also plans to push EU trade representatives to crack down on seafood products from Russia and China being falsely labeled as Alaskan in retail settings.

READ MORE
APR 125:57 PM GMT
Mariculture industry continues to grow in Alaska

Mariculture, or the cultivation of shellfish and kelp, continues to be a bright spot on the horizon for Alaska. 

There’s currently 27 kelp farm permits and 25 active oysters farms in the state, according to data from the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) presented at a Friday morning (April 12) climate change resiliency panel at ComFish. And in 2022, kelp farmers harvested almost a million pounds of seaweed. That’s up from essentially nonexistent harvest levels that started in 2017.

READ MORE
APR 129:27 AM GMT
Alaskan seafood exports to Japan remain high despite economic struggles

The volume of exports of Alaskan seafood products to one of its biggest trade partners, Japan, neared pre-pandemic levels in 2023, according to McKinley Research Group consultant Sam Friedman, at a Thursday afternoon (April 11) panel.

That’s despite tough market conditions for both of the trade partners, including a weak Yen and a strong US dollar.

READ MORE
APR 129:25 AM GMT
Alaska’s seafood industry snapshot by the numbers in 2022

Alaska’s seafood industry cracked $5 billion in wholesale value in 2022, according to data presented by the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute (ASMI) on Thursday (April 11), with a harvest value of more than $2 billion that same year.

That year, almost 13,000 Alaskan fishermen harvested more than 5.8bn pounds of seafood on 6,000 resident-owned fishing vessels. Similarly, the 147 shoreside processors spread out amongst 40-plus communities in Alaska employed nearly 21,000 workers, according to ASMI data.
The state’s seafood sector had a $6bn in-state economic footprint that year, and a $15bn economic impact nationally.

READ MORE
APR 117:08 PM GMT
McKinley Research Group outlines nearly $500m impact from Russian seafood ban

As much as $452 million worth of pollock, cod and salmon products made from Russian raw materials were imported to the US from China in 2022, according to McKinley Research Group consultant Sam Friedman. 

Friedman told attendees at a joint ComFish panel with the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute (ASMI) that the data group estimates 70,000 metric tons of seafood products from those three species came into the US that year.

READ MORE
APR 113:13 PM GMT
Peltola outlines Russian ban, action on shrimp imports as industry wins 

Alaska’s lone US representative, Mary Peltola, a Democrat, told ComFish attendees in a pre-recorded video message that it’s been a busy time in the US capitol for seafood legislation. 

Specifically, Peltola said the Russian seafood ban represented progress for the state’s struggling seafood industry. Peltola also called out congressional action targeting imports of shrimp from India, and touted her work across the aisle with US representative Garret Graves, a Republican from Louisiana, on the issue.

READ MORE
APR 113:11 PM GMT
Murkowski highlights Alaska labeling, USDA support as legislative priorities

US Senator Lisa Murkowski said there have been wins for Alaska’s seafood industry this year, including the Russia seafood ban, a boost in purchases from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA), and $25 million in federal appropriations that will go towards the state’s fisheries.

But, she said, securing additional support from the USDA through a forthcoming farm bill reauthorization is still a top priority in the year ahead for both her and US representative Mary Peltola.

READ MORE
APR 113:10 PM GMT
Murkowski emphasizes support for Alaska seafood industry amidst tough times

US senator Lisa Murkowski kicked off her pre-recorded remarks to ComFish attendees on Thursday by addressing industry-wide struggles that have hit Alaskan fishermen and processors.

“When I spoke to you all a year ago, there was really no telling what 2023 had in store for us. We did not know the extent to which Russia’s predatory pricing would upset the global market,” she said. 

READ MORE
APR 1112:38 PM GMT
ComFish panels include Alaska’s congressional delegation, US commerce secretary

Kodiak, Alaska’s annual commercial fishing trade show will kick off Thursday (April 11) with Republican US senator Lisa Murkowski and Democratic US representative Mary Peltola. The two US lawmakers are expected to deliver joint remarks in an opening panel.

US senator Dan Sullivan, a fellow Alaska Republican, will also deliver remarks as part of an individual, in-person panel on Saturday morning (April 13). 

READ MORE

Contact the author kirsten.dobroth@undercurrentnews.com
