title: NASF 2024: NESI whitefish wins push revenue over £200m; Atlantic Sapphire’s bullish update
content:
BERGEN, Norway -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the North Atlantic Seafood Forum (NASF) in Bergen, Norway, held March 5-7, 2024.

NASF 2024 kicks off with "technology Tuesday," during which there will be more than 70 presentations on technology as a part of the solution towards a more sustainable industry, according to organizers.

Day two starts with a plenary session, followed by dedicated sessions for salmon, whitefish and pelagics. Sustainability, aquafeed and land-based investor seminars follow.

Then, day three is dedicated to the Pareto investor seminar, during which numerous major seafood firms will present their companies.

Keep checking back below for all the latest updates!

Auto updates: On
MAR 85:56 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Arctic faces ‘Atlanticisation’ as species migrate north

Global warming is causing the “Atlanticisation” of the Arctic, whereby fish and other marine life migrate northwards from warming waters in the northeast Atlantic, said a senior researcher at the Norwegian Polar Institute.

“We are seeing a phase shift between the Atlantic and the Arctic,” said Geir Wing Gabrielsen, who is also professor at University Centre in Svalbard. “In the last five-six summers, the Barents Sea has been completely surrounded by Atlantic water, which has big implications.”

READ MORE
MAR 85:20 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Markets alone won’t drive sustainable feed transition

Markets alone “will not solve” the challenges involved in transitioning to novel feed ingredients, said industry representatives during a seminar on aquafeed.

When asked if leaving the issue up to market forces alone would drive adoption of alternative feeds, Kristin Vibeke Hurum, head of HR for sustainability and quality at salmon farmer Cermaq Group, definitively responded it “will not happen.”

READ MORE
MAR 710:00 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Atlantic Sapphire sets 4,000t mid-year biomass target

Bidding to reclaim its title as the world’s largest land-based farmer by production volume, Atlantic Sapphire CFO Karl Oystein Oyehaug gave a bullish outlook to attendees on the company’s production prospects.

The firm is after a production biomass close to 4,000 metric tons by the mid-year he said, having ended 2023 with close to 3,000t of standing biomass at its farm in Florida, US.

READ MORE
MAR 79:40 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
‘No rush’ as Nordic Aqua discusses phase three financing with ‘keen’ banks

Nordic Aqua Partners, a Norwegian company working to build China’s first large-scale Atlantic salmon farming operation using land-based recirculating aquaculture system technology, is in no great hurry to get to its “phase three” target of 20,000 metric tons of output.

Stage two is now in progress; “the government property company began work at the end of January on the large building,” said chair Atle Eide.

READ MORE
MAR 78:59 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Marine heatwaves intensify, Barents Sea a ‘hotspot’

Oceanographer Marta Trodahl sounded the alarm on increasing marine heatwaves, and the impact on marine eco-systems and fisheries.

“The number, intensity and duration of marine heatwaves are increasing globally,” said Trodahl, a researcher at the Norwegian Meteorological Institute. Studies show the annual number of heatwave days has doubled globally since 1982.

READ MORE
MAR 78:05 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
New England Seafood’s revenues near £210m after big whitefish win

New England Seafood International (NESI) — owned by US-based Sealaska — saw its revenue take a “big step up” in 2023 as it took on close to £50 million in UK retail contract wins, said CEO Dan Aherne.

The wins — for chilled whitefish for J. Sainsbury and Marks and Spencer, as Undercurrent News reported at the time — mean that Sealaska’s global seafood operations are now approaching $350m in turnover, with the UK business, NESI, “probably $250m of that.”

READ MORE
MAR 77:08 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Arnarlax switches some sales to Asia as China demand booms

Icelandic Salmon, which trades as Arnarlax, saw a shift in its sales during the third and fourth quarters of 2023, with lower volumes to the US and greater sales to Asia, said CEO Bjorn Hembre.

Iceland enjoys a trade deal with China, which allows it to compete well with other producing countries, he said.

READ MORE
MAR 75:51 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Camanchaca boss: Huge room for salmon farming growth in Chile if relations with gov’t, public can improve

There is vast space for salmon farming to grow in Chilean waters, if the two major challenges facing the industry can be reckoned with, said Ricardo Garcia Holtz, CEO of Camanchaca.

At the moment, just 0.004% of Chile’s exclusive economic zone waters have been allocated for salmon farming — only a fourth of that is actually in use now, he said.

READ MORE
MAR 75:26 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Chile’s Multi X aims to begin vast post-smolt expansion by end of 2024

Chilean salmon farmer Multi X intends to begin the phase two and three expansions of its large land-based post-smolt joint venture Multisea by the end of 2024, said CEO Cristian Swett.

It already has the necessary land, water rights, and environmental permits, he said, so “this will happen.”

READ MORE
MAR 75:02 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Mowi: Hitting 500,000t of salmon production would be ‘major milestone’

Reaching 500,000 metric tons of salmon production in 2024 would be a “major milestone for Mowi,” said the company’s CEO Ivan Vindheim. 

The forecast production for 2024 represents a 33% increase in production over six years, he said, and a combined annual growth rate (CAGR) of 4.9% since 2018. The industry average CAGR over the period is 2.9%.

READ MORE
MAR 74:58 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
IFFO forecasts fishmeal production bounceback in 2024

Global fishmeal supply should bounce back by around 500,000 metric tons in 2024, according to forecasts by the Marine Ingredients Organisation (IFFO) shared by Austevoll.

With a normalization from the El Nino phenomenon that severely challenged Peru’s anchovy seasons in 2023, fishmeal output globally should reach 5.12 million metric tons.

READ MORE
MAR 74:25 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Oslo exchange’s Seafood Index back to pre-resource tax levels

The collective valuation of Norway’s largest seafood companies on Oslo’s Euronext stock exchange — known as the Seafood Index — has finally recovered from its huge value shock in late 2022.

“After the resource tax was announced in September 2022, we saw NOK 40 billion to NOK 50bn in market cap disappear overnight,” said Christian Jomaas, CEO of market analyst Pareto Securities.

READ MORE
MAR 74:19 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Leroy wants 35% of salmon ‘shielded’ in submerged or semi-closed pens by end of 2024

Leroy Seafood Group is aiming to have as much as 35% of its 175,000 metric tons of salmon output in Norway “shielded” — housed in submerged or semi-closed containment net pens — by the end of 2024, said CEO Henning Beltestad.

It has invested hundreds of millions of kroner in this field already and will put NOK 500 million ($47.4m) in this year, he said.

READ MORE
MAR 74:10 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Bakkafrost takes delivery of Faroes’ first cargo plane

Hogni Jacobsen, chief financial officer of Bakkafrost, announced that the farmer had taken delivery of the first cargo plane to be based out of the Faroe Islands.

“This week has been extremely exciting for us because on Monday we made aviation history in the Faroes as we finally received our Boeing 757 cargo plane,” Jacobsen told listeners.

READ MORE
MAR 73:43 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Pareto: 2024’s salmon growth outlook already a best-case scenario

Salmon production forecasts for 2024 are already coming under pressure after an underwhelming start to the year’s harvests, according to Sander Lie, an equity research analyst with Pareto Securities.

Pareto’s forecast has production down to increase by 4% this year, but Lie admitted that “right now, this is a best-case scenario, not a base-case based on what we have seen so far.”

READ MORE
MAR 73:36 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Polish border blockades impacting Eastern Europe fish trade

Polish farmers’ blockades of roads and rail links over perceived unfair competition in favor of Ukraine have impacted the trade of seafood in Eastern Europe, said Christen Mordal, advisor to the Norwegian Seafood Council.

The issues began in the fall of 2023 and continue now, particularly impacting the trade routes from the important Lithuanian port of Klaipeda through Poland and into Ukraine, said Mordal.

READ MORE
MAR 72:51 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Iceland’s Geo Salmo details roadmap to 22,700t farm in 2031

Icelandic flow-through land-based salmon farmer Geo Salmo began construction work in January 2024 and unveiled its roadmap to having a 24,700-metric-ton facility in 2031.

CEO Jens Thordarson spoke of the company’s “clear, low-risk” capital expenditure plan, which at phase one of production — 7,200t of salmon, head-on, gutted — should entail a CAPEX cost of €26 per kilogram and a production EBIT cost of €5.4/kg.

READ MORE
MAR 612:31 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Kingfish Co anticipates appeals delaying US plans will dry up in ‘four or five quarters’

The various appeals that have so far delayed the Netherlands’ Kingfish Company from moving ahead with its 8,000-metric-ton land-based aquaculture facility in Jonesport, Maine, US, should be defeated in around a year, believes CFO Jean-Charles Valette.

“We have all the permits we need, and we have the support of the local community. We also have some opponents who have made appeals.”

READ MORE
MAR 612:12 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
IFFO: 2024 fish oil demand to remain strong as pharma rebuilds stocks

The 2024 markets for fishmeal, and especially fish oil, look set to continue with very high demand, said Enrico Bachis, market research director with the Marine Ingredients Organisation, IFFO.

“After 2022, we had, as usual, most fishmeal and oil going to aquafeed. For fishmeal, the other two sectors are pig feed and pet food.”

READ MORE
MAR 611:52 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Nordic Aquafarms will aim for 15,000t kingfish in California

Norwegian business Nordic Aquafarms Group has revealed it plans to farm 15,000 metric tons of yellowtail kingfish at its site in California, US, when fully developed.

That’s quite a step up from May 2023, when CEO Bernt-Olav Rottingsnes told Undercurrent News: “It’s possible to see a good farm at 2,000-3,000 [metric tons], and that’s a start. The property is big enough for at least 10,000t, maybe more, but that’s what we’re looking at.”

READ MORE
MAR 611:19 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
SalMar Aker Ocean has shortlist for international expansion

Offshore salmon farming firm SalMar Aker Ocean has looked at a host of other countries and has a shortlist drawn up for the most promising opportunities for international expansion, said CFO Trine Romuld.

“We have the ambition of being present not only in Norway but also internationally. We have four key defined factors we are considering: First, of course, all biological conditions are needed.”

READ MORE
MAR 611:16 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Cermaq: Omega-3 limitations loom large over salmon industry

The salmon industry desperately needs to broaden its sources of omega-3 oils to ensure the healthy growth of salmon, according to Kristin Vibeke Hurum, head of HR for sustainability and quality at Cermaq.

Salmon require omega-3 fatty acids like EPA and DHA because they cannot produce those nutrients on their own. She cited industry studies showing higher omega-3 levels in salmon feed can reduce fish mortality rates.

READ MORE
MAR 610:18 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Performance at Arctic Offshore Farming even stronger than Ocean Farm 1 for SalMar Aker Ocean

Biological performance at SalMar Aker Ocean (SAO)’s Arctic Offshore Farming (AOF) sites — bought from Norway Royal Salmon last year — has looked even stronger than at Ocean Farm 1 as the first harvests come to fruition, said CFO Trine Romuld.

The first harvests at AOF are taking place just about now, she said, while Ocean Farm 1 has recently harvested its third cycle of salmon.

READ MORE
MAR 610:11 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Cape hake harvests recovering after dicey winter

South African production of cape hake is one of the most stable outputs of the global whitefish sector. Routinely, cape hake production hovers around 300,000 metric tons — 25% of global hake supply, and 16% of total whitefish volumes.

However, last year, according to Konrad Geldenhuys, chief operating officer at South Africa’s Sea Harvest Corporation, the sector ran into literal headwinds last year.

READ MORE
MAR 69:08 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Nordic Kingfish harvests first fish in Fredrikstad

Denmark-based Nordic Kingfish — a subsidiary of Norway’s Nordic Aquafarms — harvested its first fish at its Fredrikstad facility on March 5, revealed CEO Bernt Olav Rottingsnes.

More will follow shortly after, and then it will be steady, continuous harvests, he said. You can see Fredrikstad’s first kingfish in the image below.

READ MORE
MAR 68:42 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Gigante content that smolt mortalities nothing to do with facility

Norwegian land-based farmer Gigante Salmon is content the mortalities that hit its first stockings in February 2024 were nothing to do with the newly completed facility itself, said CFO Rune Johansen.

Gigante delivered 640,000 smolt to the facility in January, of which some 20,000 were “dead on arrival.” Ultimately, some 300,000 fish died, representing nearly 50% of the release.

READ MORE
MAR 68:34 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Nordea: Cod prices to peak next year, but 2026 could be turning point

It’s no secret that cod availability is low. Catch quotas have been reduced by 20% for 2024, and a similar, further reduction is expected next year.

“We believe that cod prices will peak in 2025, driven by further quota cuts and economic growth in Europe,” explained Finn-Arne Egeness, a senior analyst with Nordea.

READ MORE
MAR 68:25 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Kontali: Global salmon harvest, market value contracted in 2023

The global market value of salmon harvests contracted nearly 2% last year amid supply challenges, according to Ragnar Nystoyl, chief analyst at Kontali, a seafood market research firm based in Norway.

Nystoyl said average salmon harvest weight in Europe fell 3% in 2023 compared to levels of 2022. This equated to a decline of 150 grams per fish harvested on average.

READ MORE
MAR 68:13 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Proximar anticipates premium price when harvests begin in Q3

Norwegian land-based salmon farming company Proximar Seafood anticipates a price premium for the fish harvested from its facility near Mount Fuji in Japan later this year, said CFO Ole Christian Willumsen.

Its first harvest is due to come in Q3 2024, as it begins to ramp up towards its phase one production target of 5,300 metric tons.

READ MORE
MAR 68:06 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Wild-catch drop is farmed cod’s gain in 2024

Sales of farmed cod in Norway are growing fast to fill at least some of the reduced volumes coming out of the Barents Sea this year, according to Jan Erik Okensvag, a senior analyst with Kontali.

The consultancy’s data shows that farmed cod production is expected to grow to 14,000 metric tons in 2024, from just under 12,000t last year.

READ MORE
MAR 67:52 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Cermaq: Norwegian gov’t has killed offshore potential

On a panel discussing potential future sources of salmon supply growth, Cermaq CEO Steven Rafferty noted how anticipation of offshore aquaculture has completely stalled.

“The Norwegian government has killed the potential for offshore investment at the moment, because there’s no clarity on the regulation,” he said. 

READ MORE
MAR 67:37 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Research body warns Norwegian spring-spawning herring stocks edging below trigger limits

Norwegian spring-spawning herring stocks are declining to the point where fisheries may need to “put on the brakes,” warned Erling Kare Stenevik of Norway’s Institute of Marine Research.

“The stock has been going down; it’s now at, or close to, those areas where we have to put on the brakes, we call it the MSY [maximum sustainable yield] B trigger. It’s an area you don’t want the stock to be, you risk recruitment being impaired,” he explained.

READ MORE
MAR 67:26 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Blue whiting to ‘save’ northern Europe’s fishmeal, oil output in 2024

After “saving” 2023 for northern Europe’s fishmeal and oil sector, blue whiting looks set to do the same in 2024 — despite the North Atlantic Pelagic Advocacy Group holding a “call to action” event later today on the stock’s sustainable management.

That was according to Kontali’s Ragnar Ronning, who noted that — despite the apparent complete lack of an Icelandic capelin quota this year — quotas for reduction pelagics in Europe for 2024 should be the same as in 2023.

READ MORE
MAR 66:36 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Hindar: Salmon profits mask sector’s mortality problems

Jon Hindar, chairman of Olink Proteonics and partner at Summa Equity, told listeners that the supply constraints of salmon are masking several of the sector’s underlying issues.

“This is the only industry I know where the worse you do, the more money you make,” he said.

READ MORE
MAR 66:12 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Cermaq CEO: High salmon feed costs to burden farmers for ‘years’

Sky-high production costs could take “years” to fall back due to a more than 50% increase in aqua feed prices over the past three years, said the CEO of Cermaq Group, the Mitsubishi-owned salmon farmer with operations in Chile and Norway.

Speaking at a panel discussion at the North Atlantic Seafood Forum, industry executives said the high feed costs are cutting into profits and putting pressure on end consumers.

READ MORE
MAR 65:30 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China’s 2023 salmon imports beat pre-pandemic record amid growth in middle-class

China’s salmon imports reached record levels in 2023, recovering strongly after declines during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to Sigmund Bjorgo, China director for the Norwegian Seafood Council.

Bjorgo — who reprised his role as China director last week — revealed that more than 80,000 metric tons of fresh salmon were imported to China last year, above pre-pandemic 2019. The value of salmon imports also grew significantly (see chart from Undercurrent‘s trade portal).

READ MORE
MAR 65:00 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Coastal states to meet for mackerel talks again next week

The Atlantic coastal states fishing mackerel in shared waters will meet again in London, UK, on March 11 and 12 to try and strike a quota-sharing agreement, Roald Oen — senior advisor at electronic auction house Norges Sildesalgslag — told Undercurrent News.

Oen is part of Norway’s delegation, though he was careful not to disclose any more details. He did add that the delegations had already met “several times in 2024.”

READ MORE
MAR 64:51 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Norway capelin fishing kicks off amid uncertain market

Norwegian vessels began their capelin fishing in the past week, but the earliest landings have disappointed when it comes to size, Roald Oen — senior advisor at electronic auction house Norges Sildesalgslag — told Undercurrent News.

Norway’s share of the capelin quota in the Barents Sea — shared with Russia — comes to 117,300 metric tons. So far, vessels have registered just under 18,000t as caught, but the auction house hasn’t confirmed any volumes as delivered to factories.

READ MORE
MAR 64:46 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
SalMar launches $47m R&D lab

SalMar is launching what it describes as the ‘Salmon Living Lab’, CEO Frode Arntsen announced.

The huge Norwegian salmon farmer is looking to reduce the mortality rate in the industry, which hit 16.1% in Norway last year.

READ MORE
MAR 64:16 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Blue Lice takes home Seafood Innovation Award

Sea lice prevention technology Blue Lice has won the 2024 Seafood Innovation Award.

As reported yesterday in this blog, Blue Lice’s lights mimic the flash of sunlight off of salmon skin to attract and kill sea lice before they ever reach the fish, “like a mosquito trap for lice.”

READ MORE
MAR 63:46 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Skretting: Remove self-imposed restrictions to solve feed cost crisis

The average cost of aquafeed in Norway has increased by 90% over the last decade, according to Therese Log Bergjord, CEO of Skretting.

Over the last year especially, the cost of fish oil has spiralled, while other aquafeed ingredients have also been at the mercy of inflation.

READ MORE
MAR 512:12 PM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Advice offered from swine sector on tailoring genomic editing message

The near-science-fiction benefits of genomic editing are certain to play a part in the salmon aquaculture sector at some point in the future, but the regulatory environment and acceptance from the market are key areas the sector must consider, said Craig Lewis, genetics service manager with PIC — the Pig Improvement Company.

He stressed his confidence that “the journey” seen by the pig protein sector will be echoed by salmon in the future. In fact, “genetics is going to transform all our proteins, all of agriculture,” he said.

READ MORE
MAR 511:46 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Young proteomics firm plans €3.5m series A for EU expansion

Young South African proteomics company MariHealth Solutions is planning its international expansion this year, said co-founder and CEO Sarah Carroll.

The firm harnesses proteomics — the study of the interactions, function, composition, and structures of proteins — to analyze protein biomarkers in fish blood and tissue, providing granular insights into fish health and metabolism.

READ MORE
MAR 59:20 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Crunch time approaches for gene-editing effort to make Atlantic salmon resistant to sea lice

Gene editing project CrispResist has involved various research entities and companies across several salmon-farming countries since launching in January 2021, and crunch time is upon them.

The project — which has worked to identify the genes in coho and pink salmon that make them resistant to sea lice, and then to put those genes into Atlantic salmon to try and replicate the effects — ends at the close of 2024.

READ MORE
MAR 59:06 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
iFarm ready to expand beyond Cermaq 

The iFarm project — high-tech salmon-farming pens with sensors recognizing each individual based on its dot pattern — has thus far been a collaboration between BioSort, ScaleAQ and farmer Cermaq Group. 

However, BioSort CEO Geir Stang Hauge revealed at NASF that the time had come for it to seek new farming partners, as it aims to work in new areas and gather new data across Norway.

READ MORE
MAR 58:30 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Swedish mycoprotein startup targets 6,200t production of aquafeed ingredient by 2030

Gothenburg, Sweden-based aquatech startup Seaqure Labs is looking for collaborative partners and raw material supplies as it scales up its mycoprotein feed ingredient production.

In a process not unlike the fermentation of beer, Seaqure utilizes funghi to create a fully circular feed product using industrial biowaste, said co-founder Fred Andersson.

READ MORE
MAR 58:14 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
‘Sh*t in gives you sh*t out’: Norway startup strives to clean up data

It’s all well and good collecting more and more data as aquaculture becomes increasingly digitized, but if that data does not meet a certain quality threshold, it’s of no use. 

That’s the concept behind Manolin, which co-founder Tony Chen said can be thought of as the “janitor” tidying up the data in order to provide actionable information. 

READ MORE
MAR 58:02 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Anti-sea lice tech boasts treatment-free fish cycle working with Grieg

Sea lice-preventing technology firm Blue Lice last year achieved a big milestone, according to CEO Karoline Sjodal Olsen: a salmon production cycle free of lice treatments.

The trial did come in conjunction with Grieg Seafood, and Olsen was keen to credit Grieg’s cleaner fish program as well as her firm’s technology, which mimics the flash of light off of salmon skin to attract and kill sea lice — “like a mosquito trap for lice.”

READ MORE
MAR 57:44 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Fish-finding tech can improve catch efficiency — and earn better prices?

The single startup in the NASF Seafood Innovation Award 2024 targeting wild catches, CatchWise has a compelling mission: making it easier and more efficient to find fish.

Fuel prices, and other factors, mean the difference between a vessel’s good season and bad season can be millions of Norwegian kroner, noted the firm’s Ludvig Loddesol. 

READ MORE
MAR 57:33 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Farmed fish blood sampling startup aims to hit commercial scale

Norwegian startup AquaPredict is preparing to take its fish welfare modeling technology to a commercial scale, revealed CEO Kjetil Korsnes at NASF’s Seafood Innovation Award showcase.

The firm specializes in supplying data for fish welfare decisions in real-time, claiming to be able to deliver actionable information to farmers 12 minutes after taking a blood sample.

READ MORE
MAR 57:19 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Insect meal producers aim for 600,000t by 2030

Christophe Derrien, secretary general of the International Platform of Insects for Food and Feed (IPIFF), said the body was forecasting for a global insect protein capacity of 600,000 metric tons by 2030.

“There would obviously be a lot of factors and a lot of green lights that should come by then,” said Derrien. “But the unlocking of the possibility to use other proteins like meat and fish as substrates will be a key driver for the sector.”

READ MORE
MAR 57:03 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Spread of insect meal ‘a chicken-egg’ problem

The attendee vote on the biggest barriers to insect meal adoption turned up a familiar result at NASF: the scale isn’t there, and neither is the price.

“The problem is it increases the cost of feed compared to existing materials,” said one voter from Skretting. “Our customers need to accept the higher cost of the feed, and that’s an issue.”

READ MORE
MAR 56:43 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
German shrimp RAS Oceanloop finding success with insect meal

Bert Wecker, co-CEO of German land-based shrimp company Oceanloop, explained how insect feed was being incorporated into the farm’s diet as part of a new series of trials.

Oceanloop has set itself the long-term target of eliminating the use of marine resources in its product’s feed, he said, which the company makes itself.

READ MORE
MAR 55:48 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Former Marel Fish top exec in as CEO at processing tech firm Optimar

Siggi Olason, previously the managing director of Marel’s fish and seafood division, has been named CEO of fish processing systems manufacturer Optimar International, he told Undercurrent News at NASF.

He began his role in February 2024, according to LinkedIn, though at the end of that month, Georg Saint-Denis was being quoted as CEO in press releases.

READ MORE
MAR 55:13 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Currency flux leads Norway’s seafood exports to another record in February

An improved share of fillets and other processed salmon products drove Norway to a new export value record in kroner terms for February, even as export values in euros continue to decline, according to the latest update from the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC).

Altogether, Norway exported seafood worth NOK 13.3 billion ($1.26bn) in February, an increase of NOK 339 million, or 3%, relative to the same month last year.

title: Fish International 2024: Norway ‘skrei’ season launches with higher prices
content:
BREMEN, Germany -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from Bremen, Germany, for Fish International 2024.

Taking place from Feb. 25-27, the biennial show is again welcoming visitors looking for the latest developments in the German and broader European markets, organizers said.

Around 320 exhibitors from 30 countries have registered for the 19th edition of Germany's only fish trade show. 

Keep checking back below for the latest updates.

Auto updates: On
FEB 271:35 PM GMT
Norway ‘skrei’ season launches with renewed MSC certification, higher prices

Last year, Norwegian ‘skrei’ cod faced a setback as its MSC certification was temporarily revoked due to the overfishing of local coastal cod, Kristin Pettersen, the Norwegian Seafood Council’s envoy to Germany, told Undercurrent News.

However, the latest update brings a positive turn of events, marking the restoration of the certification. “This is expected to enhance the market position of skrei cod, reinforcing its commitment to sustainability,” she said. 

READ MORE
FEB 271:34 PM GMT
Cromaris sets eyes on international markets with common dentex

Croatian premium whitefish producer Cromaris has strategically positioned common dentex [Dentex dentex] as its main differentiator against competitors, the firm’s chief commercial officer Tin Rukavina told Undercurrent News.

While this product is currently available in Croatian retailers and wholesalers in surrounding markets, Cromaris is actively looking for new opportunities to commercialize it also across Europe.

READ MORE
FEB 2711:13 AM GMT
Dutch seafood distributor launches 12-hour smoked salmon alternative

Dutch seafood distributor Sterk Seafood has launched a new 12-hour smoked salmon alternative under its vegan “Zeastar” product range, Laurens Sterk, founder of the firm’s plant-based branch, explained.

“We have been testing pre-made sushi rolls, aiming for a potential market release in early 2024,” he said. “This product is expected to hit the market by Easter.”

READ MORE
FEB 2710:25 AM GMT
Prime Ocean expects 2024 to be ‘another year of growth’ 

Danish seafood importer Prime Ocean has shown robust financial results for the fiscal year ending on June 30, 2023, the firm’s managing director Eric Stensgaard told Undercurrent News. 

According to Prime Ocean’s latest financial report, the company reported profits of over DKK 35m ($5.1m), notably up from DKK 10.5m in the previous fiscal year ending on June 30, 2022. 

READ MORE
FEB 279:25 AM GMT
Danish processor anticipates coldwater shrimp demand surge after slow start to 2024

Despite facing initial challenges, Danish company Chrisfish Danmark expressed optimism for the company’s performance in 2024.

The firm’s sales manager in Europe, Jorn-Ole Bertelsen, acknowledged the hurdles encountered in the early months of the year, with stocks of coldwater shrimp in Europe quite high. 

READ MORE
FEB 261:47 PM GMT
Dutch shellfish supplier Krijn Verwijs plans to expand product range in 2024

Dutch shellfish supplier Krijn Verwijs’ main focus for 2024 is to expand its product range, the firm’s director Caroline Verwijs told Undercurrent News.

“We are in the midst of a transformative process, evolving from a predominantly shellfish-focused range to a comprehensive seafood selection,” she said. “This aligns with evolving consumer preferences and market demands, presenting an exciting prospect for us.”

READ MORE
FEB 261:23 PM GMT
German innovation cluster fuels blue circular economy projects with €20m

German innovation cluster Blaue Biookonomie aims to support projects focusing on a circular economy using resources from the water, such as mussels, shrimp or micro- and macroalgae.

The cluster — founded in 2019 with €20 million ($21.7m) from the country’s federal ministry for education and research — is now taking “the very first baby steps,” granting the funding to several teams.

READ MORE
FEB 269:29 AM GMT
Eastern Fisheries foresees upward trend in US scallop, flatfish demand

Acknowledging a dip in sales volumes in 2023, Eastern Fisheries, the world’s largest harvester, processor and distributor of scallops, expressed confidence in a positive shift in 2024.

According to Mark Arruda, one of the firm’s two international sales managers, January marked a particularly promising start, hinting at an upward trajectory. 

READ MORE
FEB 267:00 AM GMT
Atlantic salmon sales expected to stay strong long-term despite high prices

Farmed Atlantic salmon prices are expected to maintain their high levels in 2024 and beyond, sources in the industry told Undercurrent News. 

While acknowledging the high cost of salmon, industry sources highlighted the unwavering consumer demand for this product. 

READ MORE
FEB 266:26 AM GMT
India’s optimism prevails in fishmeal trade despite drop in Chinese imports

The reduction in fishmeal production by Peru due to the El Nino phenomenon in 2023 has prompted a shift in dynamics in India. 

Two Indian seafood exporters at the show told Undercurrent News the Indian fishmeal industry remains optimistic for 2024 after 2023 was “a year of many opportunities for the sector.”

READ MORE
FEB 251:31 PM GMT
Greek bass, bream farmer Philosofish introduces MAP for fresh fish

While modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) for fresh fish is not entirely unprecedented for Philosofish, this marks “a significant leap forward”, Kilian Papadimitriou, the firm’s sales manager in central and north Europe, told Undercurrent News. 

Greece’s second-largest producer of seabass and seabream’s new packaging solution uses tray sealing technology from MultiVac, “promising a special design that is expected to make a considerable impact in Central European markets,” he said. 

READ MORE
FEB 2512:52 PM GMT
Momentum grows for alternative seafood yet taste still a challenge

As the demand for sustainable and innovative food options grows globally, the alternative seafood industry finds itself riding a wave of surging momentum. 

“Consumers are increasingly seeking alternatives that not only meet their ethical and environmental standards but also satisfy their taste preferences,” the Good Food Institute (GFI)’s corporate engagement manager, Carlotte Lucas, said.

READ MORE
FEB 2512:22 PM GMT
From vannamei to black tiger, India expects sector to evolve further

After experiencing stagnant exports in 2023, India’s marine products export development authority (MPEDA) is optimistic about the growth of the country’s shrimp sector in 2024.

“We are observing changes in the approaches of producers and exporters, leading us to believe that the situation will improve this year,” MPEDA’s Deputy Director, Manoj Kumar, told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE

Contact the author Maria.Feijoo@undercurrentnews.com

title: Aquaculture America 2024: Israeli startup plans build-and-lease RAS-facility business in US
content:
SAN ANTONIO, Texas -- Undercurrent News was blogging live from Aquaculture America, held Feb. 18-21, in San Antonio, Texas. 

You can recap the 2023 blog here. 

Auto updates: On
FEB 2111:48 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Israeli startup plans build-and-lease RAS-facility business in US

Everblue, an Israeli aquaculture startup, plans to establish land-based facilities in the United States, Nimrod Gliksman, the company’s chief product officer, told Undercurrent News.

The company developed a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) able to filter water with a claimed efficiency of 100%, effectively eliminating off-flavors, which is a persistent challenge in traditional aquaculture, he said.

READ MORE
FEB 217:20 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Filipino shrimp farmer explores expansion to US market, eyes ‘patriotic Americans’

Arvi Velasco, the owner of a Philippines-based shrimp farm, is considering expanding his operations to the US and targeting “patriotic Americans.”

Velasco owns two outdoor shrimp farms in the Philippines. One is in the province of Batangas, situated in the coastal town of Calatagan, with a capacity of 400-600 metric tons per year. The other farm is in Mindoro, located in west-central Philippines, with a capacity of 1,200t annually.

READ MORE
FEB 2112:17 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
US: A nation of competence, coasts and sea spells opportunity for seafood self-sufficiency, says Norwegian DNV director

Per Arild Aland sees substantial opportunities in the US for DNV, an Oslo-based organization that certifies the safety of equipment and products on fish farms. 

In an interview with Undercurrent News at Aquaculture America on Wednesday, DNV’s business development director highlighted the import-centric nature of the US seafood market and underscored the potential for increased self-sufficiency.

READ MORE
FEB 2111:14 AM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Price, product form top consumer concerns

Consumer demand for sustainable products has been a hot topic in recent years, with many companies striving to meet this expectation. Although sustainability is becoming increasingly important, some consumers prioritize price and product features over sustainability concerns, anecdotal evidence suggests.

At the Aquaculture America conference, David Seeley, the North American commercial director at Skretting, a feed manufacturer under Nutreco based in the Netherlands, shared some anecdotal insights with Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
FEB 209:05 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
NOAA programs advance to propel US seafood industry

As many as 25 executives from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) are in attendance at Aquaculture America, where they are sharing updates on the progress of their strategic plan to boost domestic seafood production.

According to NOAA, the Aquaculture Strategic Plan (2023-2028) lays out a framework to help achieve a robust, thriving and diverse US aquaculture industry as part of a resilient seafood sector.

READ MORE
FEB 203:14 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Shellfish closures in Virginia hurt small farmers the most, study finds

Small shellfish farmers in the US state of Virginia are experiencing significant financial losses as a result of recent closures, according to a recent study by the Virginia Seafood Agricultural Research and Extension Center at Virginia Tech.

Researcher Charles Clark told delegates at Aquaculture America on Tuesday (Feb. 20) that closures caused by rainfall and increased temperatures among other reasons have led to reduced sales and loss of marketability for many farmers in the state, with smaller farms being especially impacted.

READ MORE
FEB 2011:07 AM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Offshore site selection evolves, now includes site’s potential economic viability

The industry is on the cusp of understanding the expected impacts of the environment on the financial performance of offshore fish farms,  Innovasea senior scientist Tyler Sclodnick told delegates at Aquaculture America.

He explained how site selection strategies have progressed over time. Incorporating environmental factors into financial models when determining farm sites would lead to a more thoughtful and strategic approach, he said. 

READ MORE
FEB 197:16 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
US offshore aquaculture development gains urgency amid current geopolitical uncertainty 

Drue Banta Winters, an executive at Stronger America Through Seafood (SATS), reiterated the importance of developing the United States’ offshore aquaculture in light of recent geopolitical and ethical issues during a session at Aquaculture America. 

The organization, a coalition advocating for increased US production of sustainable seafood, emphasized the urgency of offshore aquaculture in the face of changing dynamics in the global seafood industry.

READ MORE
FEB 196:49 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Tribal vice chairwoman advocates for preservation of traditional knowledge in aquaculture management

Preserving traditional knowledge and practices is crucial to shaping the approach of tribal nations towards natural resource management and cultural preservation, said Loni Grinnell-Greninger, the tribal vice chairwoman of the Jamestown S’Klallam Tribe on the Olympic Peninsula in the US state of Washington, in her keynote speech on Monday.

She underscored the pivotal stewardship role tribes play in natural resource management and emphasized the critical importance of preserving traditional knowledge and practices, framing them as essential tools in shaping tribal approaches to sustainable aquaculture.

READ MORE
FEB 1912:51 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer 
Maine association head urges long-term economic approach to US aquaculture development

Sebastian Belle, the executive director of the Maine Aquaculture Association (MAA), shared his perspective with Aquaculture America delegates on why the US is lagging behind in terms of aquaculture development.

During a session focused on federal support for the expansion of US aquaculture, Belle emphasized the need for a long-term approach to aquaculture development, as opposed to the short-term grant development cycles that are currently in place. 

READ MORE
FEB 1911:56 AM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Exec at The Nature Conservancy underscores the pivotal role of aquaculture in achieving sustainability

Day one of Aquaculture America 2024 heard Robert Jones, the global lead for The Nature Conservancy’s Aquaculture Program, emphasize the potential of aquaculture in addressing pressing environmental challenges.

With his extensive background in marine affairs and policy, Jones’ keynote speech focused on leveraging aquaculture to achieve ocean health, sustainable seafood, and job creation.

READ MORE
FEB 189:53 PM GMT
By Liza Mayer
Aquaculture America 2024 welcomes over 2,000 delegates

More than 2,000 delegates from across the globe are convening in the city of San Antonio in the US state of Texas for this year’s Aquaculture America conference and trade show. Running from Monday, Feb. 19 to Wednesday, Feb. 21, this year’s event runs under the theme “Setting the table for US aquaculture.”

Attendees can look forward to the latest industry research and development, discussions on federal support to expand US aquaculture and a new track on robotics and advanced technology in aquaculture. 

READ MORE

title: Untitled
content:
ORLANDO, Florida, US -- Undercurrent News reported live from the annual Global Seafood Market Conference (GSMC) which was held this year in Orlando, in the US state of Florida. 

The GSMC is held every year in a different US city, giving participants an outlook on key sectors such as salmon, shellfish, shrimp and whitefish. Recap all our coverage of last year's event, held in La Quinta, California, here. 

Auto updates: On
JAN 2610:58 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Icelandic haddock hike keeps 2024 global supply stable 

Expect global haddock catches to remain relatively flat for 2024, with global catches totaling 265,000 metric tons, down slightly from 269,000t in 2023 and 296,000t the previous year. 

Some of that drop is due to quota cuts in the Barents Sea, which will reduce the catch for Norway and Russia, as previously reported by Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
JAN 267:55 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
US imports of frozen tilapia hold small edge over pangasius in volume, command larger prices

The US imported 187 million pounds (84,822 metric tons) of frozen tilapia fillets during the first 11 months of 2023, giving it a slight 13% advantage over the 166m lbs of frozen pangasius it imported during the same period, GSMC attendees heard on Thursday during the whitefish panel session. 

Though the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has yet to update its seafood trade database to include December 2023, a similar result can be expected for the full year.

READ MORE
JAN 267:10 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Pollock catch in 2024 could be 410,000t higher than 2022

A sizeable increase in the Russian pollock total allowable catch for 2024 means the total volume is up 12% from two years ago, according to data presented by Ron Rogness, of the Genuine Alaska Pollock Producers, on the GSMC whitefish panel.

The two-year increase of 410,000 metric tons in volume is driven by Russia, which has taken its TAC past 2 million metric tons.

READ MORE
JAN 266:52 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
More Alaska pollock fillets staying in US market

Between 7,000-8,000 additional metric tons of Alaska pollock pin-bone out and deepskin fillets were sold into the US market in 2023, said Ron Rogness, of the Genuine Alaska Pollock Producers, on the GSMC whitefish panel.

Rogness explained his data to Undercurrent News. “In 2022, the supply of fillets from domestic production was 59,119t. Domestic production in 2023 was 156,068t,” he said.

READ MORE
JAN 254:21 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
US closing Russian China loophole helps deplete bumper wild salmon inventories, removes lower-cost options from market

Wild Alaska salmon inventories from as far back as 2022 have finally been run down, with the sale of stocks from last year speeding up since the enhanced ban on Russian seafood, said executives during the GSMC salmon panel.

The 2023 inventory from a bumper catch of pink salmon in Alaska and Russia is still being sold off but working through quickly after the expanded Russian-origin ban, according to the panel presentation. This comes after the 2022 inventories from a high Alaskan sockeye catch have gone through the value chain.

READ MORE
JAN 253:22 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
American Seafoods CEO wants more buyers to ‘hedge’ pollock price volatility with multi-year contracts 

The CEO of the largest US at-sea pollock processor, American Seafoods Group, said his company can effectively offer hedging to buyers with multi-year contracts. However, ASG is struggling to get market buy-in. 

During the GSMC whitefish panel Q&A, ASG’s Einar Gustafsson expressed his frustration at what he sees as the lack of long-term thinking in the pollock business.

READ MORE
JAN 252:15 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Slashed quotas, sanctions will mean less cod for US markets in 2024

Delegates at the GSMC were told Thursday to expect another drop in the global supply of cod in 2024.

That category — including Atlantic and Pacific cod — has already seen a 33% drop over the past 10 years, from 1.76 million tons in 2015 to 1.25m metric tons last year.

READ MORE
JAN 257:01 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Salmon led USDA seafood purchases in FY 2023

The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) purchased 89 million pounds of seafood worth $348m in fiscal 2023, a period that ran from Oct. 1, 2022 until Sept. 30, 2023, based on USDA data shared with Undercurrent News by the National Fisheries Institute (NFI).

That was 44% more volume and 31% more value than in FY 2022.

READ MORE
JAN 256:34 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chile’s Atlantic salmon output could drop 15% in 2024, meaning negative growth globally

Although Kontali is forecasting a 5% drop in Atlantic salmon production from Chile to 726,500 metric tons, it could be up to 15%, according to the salmon panel at the GSMC.

A drop of 15% would be 114,705t of volume, taking the 2024 output from Chile to 649,995t.

READ MORE
JAN 2410:29 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Surge in wild pink harvest pushed 2023 global salmon supply past 4.5m metric tons

A bumper harvest of pinks in the US state of Alaska and Russia pushed global salmon supply past 4.5 million metric tons in 2023, according to data from Norway’s Kontali presented at the GSMC.

The wild salmon harvest in 2023 from Russia and the US was 1.09m metric tons, an increase of 57% year-on-year, driven by a record year for pinks of 696,000t.

READ MORE
JAN 245:39 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Salmon has maintained market strength while other seafoods faltered

While many different seafood categories have faltered in the retail and food service market, salmon has maintained a strong presence.

That was one of the key takeaways from a panel discussion of industry players at the GSMC in Florida on Wednesday afternoon.

READ MORE
JAN 244:43 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
NFI president says position on Russia ban was ‘incredibly difficult’ to reach

Lisa Wallenda Picard, president of the National Fisheries Institute (NFI), said her group is continuing to review the approach it took when deciding to criticize president Joe Biden’s expansion for his ban on Russian seafood, a move that led Trident Seafoods to leave the trade association.

Undercurrent News asked Picard Wednesday while she was participating in a panel discussion at GSMC to describe the conversations that were had at NFI prior to the group stating its disappointment about the ban expansion on Dec. 22. 

READ MORE
JAN 241:52 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
US imports of Japanese scallops coming on strong

Don’t be fooled by the chart that shows a reduction in the US import of Japanese scallops in 2023, Jamie Dwyer, chief commercial officer at Northern Wind, in New Bedford, Massachusetts, advised attendees at GSMC on Tuesday. 

The data used by the shellfish panel hasn’t been updated since October. A flood of more Pacific scallops (Patinepecten yessoensis) from Hokkaido, Japan, came into the country over the last two months of the year, and their annual total will surpass what was seen in 2022, he assured.

READ MORE
JAN 2412:44 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Overall Canadian, US lobster exports to Asia climb again despite continuation of trade war

The US trade war with China started by former president Donald Trump in 2018 and continued by current president Joe Biden didn’t have much influence over the amount of North American lobster imported by Asia last year.

Overall lobster exports from Canada and the US to China, Hong Kong and Vietnam had already reached roughly 80 million pounds in the first 11 months of 2023, more volume than accomplished in any full year since at least 2018, GSMC attendees heard on Tuesday.

READ MORE
JAN 2411:40 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Market analysis shows sushi retail sales skyrocketed

The graphics told the story.

When it comes to retail sales of seafood, sushi was the leader of the pack for volume growth over the past four years.

READ MORE
JAN 2410:48 AM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
US company awaiting FDA approval to begin taste-testing for cell-cultured tuna

Lou Cooperhouse is hopeful that by the end of 2024 the appetizer list in some premium sushi restaurants will offer cell-cultured bluefin tuna.

Cooperhouse, co-founder and CEO of US-based Blu Nalu, told Undercurrent News at the GSMC on Wednesday, the company has already accomplished proof of concept and has a library of frozen blue fin cells at its San Diego, California, laboratory.

READ MORE
JAN 2410:41 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
US shrimp sales to foodservice grew 0.5% but that’s not the comparison to make

Foodservice sales of US shrimp grew to 284.5 million pounds in 2023, a 1.4m lb or 0.5% increase over the 283.1 m lbs sold in 2022, based on data provided by Circana, GSMC attendees heard Tuesday.

The increase was not as big as the 1.6% growth seen in 2022 or the 22% increase seen in 2021, but those were also the years the food service industry saw big jumps while bouncing back from the pandemic, pointed out Travis Larkin, the owner and president of Seafood Exchange of Florida, a shrimp importer, and moderator of the six-person shrimp panel.

READ MORE
JAN 248:51 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Walton-backed S2G aims to take positions directly in aquaculture with new fund

S2G Ventures, an investment vehicle backed by Walmart heir Lukas Walton, is looking at investing directly in aquaculture companies globally with its new fund.

The firm has 17 investments from its first oceans and seafood fund, with four recent ones set to be made public in the next few weeks, Larsen Mettler, its managing director, told Undercurrent News on the sidelines of the GSMC.

READ MORE
JAN 235:31 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
US retailers are discounting Canadian snow crab as ‘loss leader’

Canadian snow crab is selling again in the US market but, to clear out the 2023 inventory, a lot of retailers are offering frozen 5-8 oz clusters as “loss leaders” at or below wholesale prices, Roman Tkachenko, CEO of Direct Source Seafood, a major US shrimp and crab importer, said Tuesday at the GSMC 2024 event.

Tkachenko, who was one of the participants in the GSMC shellfish panel, added that much of the snow crab from the 2023 season has been sold.

READ MORE
JAN 234:26 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
US crab meat imports dropping after high prices hit demand; logistical costs rocket

The US imports of crab meat are dropping as high prices have hit demand, as importers also have to deal with a range of logistical issues.

Crab meat prices went higher, then demand dropped, as consumers had less to spend, said Troy Turkin of Supreme Crab & Seafood.

READ MORE
JAN 234:17 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Russian king crab inventories are ‘almost extinguished,’ US supply down 67%

With the US ban on direct imports of Russian seafood, king crab supply to the country has dived.

As Roman Tkachenko of Direct Source Seafood predicted at GSMC last year, there’s no way to replace Russian king crab in the US market.

READ MORE
JAN 233:14 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
GSMC shrimp panel predicts 20% black tiger hike in 2024, slight drop in vannamei

The 2024 black tiger shrimp production forecast from the GSMC is for a 20% increase in 2024 to 580,000 metric tons, with vannamei set to drop.

Black tiger has grown to be 10% of global production, said Robins McIntosh, of Thailand’s Charoen Pokphand Foods, who led the production forecast on the GSMC shrimp panel.

READ MORE
JAN 232:39 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Seafood importers anticipate higher costs as drought continues to impact Panama Canal
 

With an extended drought continuing to impact water levels in the Panama Canal, a major shipping route for North American exporters and importers, the seafood industry is bracing for higher costs.

Since February of 2023, water levels in the canal have dropped so much that about a third of the usual bulk tanker carriers have had to take the longer route around Chile and Argentina.

READ MORE
JAN 231:07 PM GMT
By Barb Dean-Simmons
Data shows salmon has become the winner for dinner 

When consumers are looking for something quick and easy to prepare for dinner, more and more of them are turning to salmon.

Anne-Marie Roerink, president of 210 Analytics, told delegates at the GSMC 2024 on Tuesday that from 2019 to 2023 sales of refrigerated and frozen salmon jumped 42% and 49%, respectively, with overall sales reaching $2.7 billion last year.

READ MORE
JAN 2311:43 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Top 10% of refrigerated seafood shoppers buy 45% of products

When it comes to buying refrigerated seafood at retail, the top 10% of shoppers buy about 45% of the product, speakers Anne-Marie Roerink, the president of 210 Analytics, and Chris DuBois, the executive vice president and practice leader for Circana, told attendees at the GSMC 2024 conference on Tuesday.

And 30% of seafood buyers purchase 70% of the volume.

READ MORE
JAN 2310:03 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Refrigerated, frozen shellfish took much bigger price drop than finfish in Q4 2023

Seafood market experts Anne-Marie Roerink, the president of 210 Analytics, and Chris DuBois, the executive vice president and practice leader for Circana, kicked off the GSMC 2024 conference on Tuesday by taking a deep look at how the retail sector continued to adapt in 2023. 

Shellfish clearly took the biggest hit on price, Roerink told attendees. A graphic illustrated how refrigerated shellfish prices ended the year with an 8.5% drop in price during the fourth quarter of 2024 compared to the fourth quarter of 2023 and frozen shellfish was down 7.6% in the final quarter of 2024 compared to the final quarter of 2022. 

READ MORE
JAN 2210:03 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
‘Everyone is clear, shrimp prices will rise in 2024,’ says Omarsa CEO

Prices for farmed shrimp have hit the bottom in 2023 and will rise in 2024, said Sandro Coglitore, CEO of Omarsa, one of Ecuador’s largest processors.

“Everyone is clear that in 2024 shrimp will be at a higher price and that there will be less shrimp available from certain parts of the world,” Coglitore told Undercurrent News during GSMC. “So, the world of very low shrimp is over. It’s not sustainable anymore.”

READ MORE

title: China summit 2023: More Atlantic salmon now cooked at home; Online seafood sales slide, live streaming on rise
content:
XIAMEN, China -- Undercurrent News was live from the China Seafood Summit, held Nov. 13-15 in the port city of Xiamen.

For all the coverage of the event, which is organized by the China Aquatic Products Processing and Marketing Alliance, recap the blog below.

Auto updates: On
NOV 159:43 AM GMT
More Atlantic salmon cooked at home in China, says Joyvio exec

In the post-pandemic era, the Chinese salmon market has entered a new stage, witnessing changes in consumer scenarios, according to an executive at Joyvio Food, China’s largest salmon company.

Atlantic salmon, valued for its nutritional benefits, is increasingly becoming a seafood choice in home cooking, with a decrease in consumption through foodservice channels, said Liang Qinyao, sales and operations director at Joyvio.

READ MORE
NOV 159:40 AM GMT
Chinese consumers willing to pay premium for sustainable seafood

There has been a noticeable growth in Chinese consumers’ demand for sustainable seafood, a representative from a large supermarket said.

Liu Jun, manager of the seafood sector at CR Vanguard Ole’ Supermarket, said at the China Seafood Summit that in the last five years, the order volume for seafood with sustainable certification labels has increased sixfold.

READ MORE
NOV 153:38 AM GMT
China’s online seafood sales slide, but live streaming on rise

Stuttering online sales of seafood in China have led to the closure of some platforms over the past three years.

During the China Seafood Summit, Researcher Li Yongjian from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences reported that investment in online seafood platforms hit a new low in 2022, almost returning to the levels of 2013.

READ MORE
NOV 153:35 AM GMT
Crayfish production has peaked, says CAPPMA head

Chinese crayfish production is expected to see a significant decrease next year, according to Cui He, the president of the China Aquatic Products Processing and Marketing Association (CAPPMA).

At the China Seafood Summit, Cui said that the growth rate of China’s crayfish production has been excessively rapid, surging from several hundred thousand metric tons over the past decade to 3 million metric tons last year.

READ MORE
NOV 153:32 AM GMT
China’s squid trade surplus shrinks, says data provider

China’s squid import and export trade surplus is continuously narrowing, according to Hucai, a frozen seafood online trading platform.

Zhang Fu, the founder and CEO of Huacai, said at the China Seafood Summit that China’s squid exports have been consistently decreasing, with its trade surplus reduced from $188 million in April to $150m in September.

READ MORE
NOV 1411:07 AM GMT
China’s pollock fillet exports set to fall below 200,000t with ‘worse still to come’ in 2024 

Chinese exports of double-frozen pollock fillets are expected to significantly decline this year, falling below 200,000 metric tons, according to Qu Zhenhai, the chairman of Dalian Haiqing Food.

Qu said at the China Seafood Summit that the export market for all frozen aquatic products, including pollock, is very grim, with a big decrease in overseas orders.

READ MORE
NOV 1411:06 AM GMT
Vietnamese pangasius needs to improve its reputation in China, says Chinese partner of Vinh Hoan

In challenging market conditions, building a strong reputation for Vietnamese pangasius in the Chinese market is necessary and important, said an industrry veteran.

Speaking at the China Seafood Summit, Chen Xindong, the general manager of Octogone, Vinh Hoan Corporation’s joint venture distributor in China, told the audience that pangasius, like other aquatic products, is currently undergoing a very challenging period.

READ MORE
NOV 149:49 AM GMT
China toughens environmental protection in tilapia aquaculture

The Chinese government has placed substantial emphasis on environmental protection, leading to challenges for tilapia farmers and processors, according to tilapia industry members. 

At a tilapia closed-door meeting of the China Seafood Summit, a major exporter noted that the Chinese government has implemented the aquaculture license system as part of efforts to regulate the aquaculture industry. However, due to increasingly strict environmental protection regulations, many licenses cannot be renewed upon expiration.

READ MORE
NOV 145:38 AM GMT
China’s frozen seafood import sector undergoing consolidation, says largest shrimp player

China’s largest shrimp importer believes that the country’s import frozen seafood industry will experience a wave of consolidation, as few importers are able to turn a profit this year.

At the China Seafood Summit, Shi Tongcai, vice chairman of Quanlian Jicai, the largest shrimp importing platform in China, highlighted that the consumption of frozen seafood has not experienced a rebound in growth. This has posed challenges for importers in achieving profitability.

READ MORE
NOV 135:18 AM GMT
Shanghai imports of Russian king crab growing fast amid buyers’ market 

The quantity of live king crab and snow crab imported from Russia to Shanghai, China, has multiplied several times year-to-date, involving both shipping and air transport modes.

Zhang Peng, the vice general manager of Shanghai YWSY Supply Chain Management, a seafood sales company associated with Shanghai’s Changxing Hengsha Fishery Port, told Undercurrent News that his company imported several thousand metric tons of king crab in the previous three quarters.

READ MORE
NOV 135:10 AM GMT
JD.com launches private label for Chinese seafood products

China’s major online platform, JD.com, has launched its own brand of seafood products and will conduct targeted promotions.

At the China Seafood Summit, Li Xinyi, manager of JD Fresh, said that the platform has been supporting online transactions for seafood products. Products from 50 countries and regions around the world are available for sale on the platform.

READ MORE
NOV 135:03 AM GMT
Seafood hotpot market booming 

In the post-pandemic era, Chinese hotpot businesses have shown a growth rate significantly higher than the industry average in catering. Notably, seafood hotpot is experiencing the fastest growth within the hotpot market.

Speaking at the China Seafood Summit, Tian Guo, deputy editor of Hotpot Canjian, a media outlet specializing in the Chinese hotpot market, told the audience that the mid-to-high-end hotpot market is on the rise, with seafood hotpot emerging as a standout.

READ MORE
NOV 134:52 AM GMT
NSC’s Thorud sees more opportunities for Norway’s salmon, mackerel, shellfish in China 

Two to three years ago, the Chinese market accounted for just 2% of Norwegian salmon exports. This year, the figure has doubled to 4%, marking a record-high import volume.

Andreas Thorud, director for China at the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC), told Undercurrent News that the Chinese market has advanced from the 15th to the 8th position, based on the ranking by export share.

READ MORE

Contact the author lewis.hu@undercurrentnews.com
