title: Coronavirus blog: North Carolina seafood chef rises from ashes of pandemic to get Beard nomination
content:
The delta and omicron variants of the novel coronavirus COVID-19 have swept across the majority of countries, hitting both seafood producers and important importing nations hard.

Various vaccination programs are underway, with varying degrees of success and implementation, while many supply chains have sought to adapt to the "new normal" of increased costs and extortionate freight rates. 

Keep up with all the latest seafood-related COVID-19 news with this live blog, below.

Auto updates: On
MAR 11:05 PM GMT
North Carolina seafood chef rises from ashes of pandemic to get Beard nomination

Chef Sunny Gerhart was the only employee at St. Roch Fine Oysters and Bar, in the US city of Raleigh, North Carolina, roughly two years ago after the coronavirus pandemic shuttered the business, WRAL 5, a local television station, reports. 

Now Gerhart’s been named a semi-finalist for the James Beard Award of “Best Chef in the Southeast”. 

READ MORE
MAR 14:53 AM GMT
Sanford faces worker shortage as COVID spreads in New Zealand

New Zealand firm Sanford has appealed for new members of staff to step forward, as COVID-19 has reduced its workforce. 

“With the rapid growth in COVID-positive cases in the New Zealand community, Sanford is facing a shortage of people to process our beautiful fish,” it said. “Our temp agencies are also being impacted and don’t have enough people to send us and we are in urgent need of paid assistance in our Auckland factory.”

READ MORE
FEB 2812:40 PM GMT
Covid-19 partly blamed for Bubba Gump Shrimp restaurant closure in Baltimore 

A Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. restaurant in the touristy Inner Harbor of Baltimore, Maryland, has closed partly due to the coronavirus pandemic, CBS-13 Baltimore reports.

The restaurant “has closed due to COVID-19’s impact on the restaurant industry as well as the landlord’s failure to uphold the building’s maintenance,” said Keith Beitler, executive vice president and COO of Landry’s Inc., the Houston, Texas-based owner of Bubba Gump and other nationwide chains.

READ MORE
FEB 251:06 PM GMT
Pandemic, cold weather driving crawfish inflation

Buyers of crawfish, an important local staple in the US state of Louisiana, are having to contend with prices that continue to rise for a myriad of factors, many of them related to the pandemic.

According to local television station Fox 15, supply chain issues for crawfish harvesting inputs as well as cold weather that causes them to grow more slowly are behind the inflation.

READ MORE
FEB 2411:35 AM GMT
Pandemic prompts tribe to open Dutch Harbor food bank

The remote US community of Unalaska, Alaska, in the Aleutian Islands has opened its first food bank as more community members are facing food insecurity amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

According to Alaska Public Media, the Qawalangin Tribe of Unalaska completed the project with community donations and $392,000 in federal government pandemic aid. The group Unalaskans Against Sexual Assault and Family Violence has long distributed food assistance but the tribe’s new facility is first on the island, which is home to the important fishing port Dutch Harbor.

READ MORE
FEB 2312:52 PM GMT
Australia, US among nations jointly probing skyrocketing shipping rates

Five nations are investigating suspected antitrust violations arising from the pandemic and global container shipping lines’ alleged service failures and unfair pricing, American Shipper reports.

Many buyers of ocean transportation say the carriers have manipulated tight capacity during the pandemic through deferred and canceled sailings, and other measures, to drive rates up, resulting in record profits estimated to top $200 billion last year. 

READ MORE
FEB 2211:31 AM GMT
Alaska is US’ fifth-worst in COVID cases per 100,000

Alaska, the US’ biggest commercial fishing state, is experiencing an average of 547 COVID-19 cases daily, or 75 per 100,000 people, which is the fifth-worst ratio in the country, based on the around-the-nation breakdown by the New York Times published Tuesday (Feb. 22).

The only US territories and states in worse shape were the Northern Marianna Islands (280 cases per 100,000), Guam (215 per 100,000), Idaho (91 per 100,000) and Kentucky (80 per 100,000). The US, for comparison purposes, is averaging 89,024 cases per day, or 27 per 100,000.

READ MORE
FEB 2112:14 PM GMT
California ports sending more empty containers back to Asia

Two vital ports in the US state of California saw an especially busy January and the number of shipping containers “cleared” and sent back empty to Asia, the trade publication Freight Waves reported.

The activity at the Port of Long Beach and the Port of Los Angeles is seen as part of the solution toward unplugging a global trade bottleneck as exports from the US remain low but demand for imports — and the containers to ship them in — remain high.

READ MORE
FEB 215:00 AM GMT
UK hospitality sector pleads for extended VAT aid after billion-pound losses

The UK’s hospitality sector has asked the government to extend VAT support beyond April as inflation hits a nearly 30-year high, reports Sky News.

According to UKHospitality, representing the country’s broad hospitality sector, the pandemic resulted in around £115 billion (€138m/156.8m) of lost sales since March 2020, which equates to 45 weeks of sales over the whole period.

READ MORE
FEB 1810:53 AM GMT
US frozen seafood sales forecast to hit $16.1bn by 2026

Sales of frozen seafood at US grocers are expected to rise by some 20% by 2026 to $16.1 billion annually as shoppers lean more heavily on frozen to reduce the number of trips they make to the store.

According to Supermarket News, IMARC Group, a Sheridan, Wyoming-based market research firm, released the frozen seafood growth forecast, which compares to the estimated $13.4bn spent on frozen seafood in 2020. 

READ MORE
FEB 184:33 AM GMT
Greece to lift some restrictions after infections ease

From Feb. 19 on, Greece will lift some restrictions on the hospitality sector as COVID infections ease from recent highs, the country’s health minister said.

The country’s advisory committee of infectious disease experts recommended the lifting of curbs “barring standing customers at bars and night entertainment establishments and the raising of attendance at sports venues to 50% of capacity,” reports Reuters. 

READ MORE
FEB 1711:17 AM GMT
Container price, production trends foretell easing of global supply crisis

Both the price and production of new shipping containers are trending down, which is a sign that the global supply crisis could be easing, the shipping news service Freightwaves reports.   

The extremely consolidated container manufacturing industry in China built more of the commoditized, corrugated steel boxes than ever before in 2021: 7.18 million 24-foot equivalent units (TEUs), according to the maritime consultancy firm Drewry. 

READ MORE
FEB 1611:39 AM GMT
New Zealand hospitality firm laments ‘high-risk’ designation

The head of a large hospitality business in New Zealand is frustrated with the message being sent out by the country’s Southern District Health Board that depicts bars and restaurants as “high-risk settings” for the transmission of COVID-19.

According to stuff.co.nz, Chris Ramsay of the Invercargill Licensing Trust said that the messaging comes at a time when the industry is struggling yet is keeping in compliance with the board’s requirements.

READ MORE
FEB 152:41 PM GMT
USDA will grant $50m to seafood processors, vessels

The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) will dole out some $50 million in grants to US seafood processors and vessels that process at sea to help defray costs incurred in the response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The department said that it will open its Seafood Processors Pandemic Response and Safety Block Grant Program (SPRS) to processors in 24 states and one US territory.

“SPRS recipients include state agencies, commissions, or departments responsible for agriculture, fisheries, wildlife, seafood, commercial processing, or related commerce activities within Alabama, Alaska, California, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Mississippi, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Texas, Virginia, and Washington, as well as the territory of American Samoa,” the department said.

READ MORE
FEB 1410:47 AM GMT
Police clear key bridge between US and Canada 

Police have cleared the remaining protesters blocking the Ambassador Bridge, in Windsor, Ontario, a key junction between the Canadian province and the US state of Michigan, the CBC reported Sunday. 

Traffic was resumed late Sunday night, according to other news outlets.

READ MORE
FEB 144:47 AM GMT
UK business told to claim last of remaining COVID-19 cash grants

UK businesses are being encouraged to apply for one-off COVID-19 support grants after new government figures show £850 million from its package is still available.

Hospitality, leisure and accommodation businesses can still apply for one-off cash grants of up to £6,000 through the Omicron Hospitality and Leisure Grant (OHLG) scheme.

READ MORE
FEB 1112:54 PM GMT
US truckers group decries Canada ‘freedom’ protests

The American Trucking Association (ATA) has come out against widespread demonstrations on the US-Canada border that originated as truckers’ protest against vaccine mandates.

According to the publication Freight Waves, ATA president and CEO Chris Spears said the group “strongly opposes any protest activities that disrupt public safety and compromise the economic and national security of the United States”.

READ MORE
FEB 1012:28 PM GMT
Owners of closed US seafood restaurant: COVID made us re-evaluate life

The Little Tuna, a seafood restaurant in South New Jersey for 20 years, has closed, citing the coronavirus pandemic as a factor in its decision, the Camden Daily Voice reports.

The owners announced their Feb. 1 closure on Facebook.

READ MORE
FEB 910:26 AM GMT
US West Coast port congestion may have peaked

The number of cargo ships waiting to unload at key US West Coast container ports appears to have stabilized, according to recent statistics, providing some hope that pandemic-related logistics bottlenecks could ease somewhat, Freight Waves reported.

The shipping industry trade publication wrote that the number of container ships waiting for berths at the California ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach fell to 78 on Tuesday, Feb. 9. That’s the lowest count in three months and is off 23% from 101 ships on Feb. 1 and down 28% from the all-time high of 109 ships on Jan. 9 but is still up 160% year on year.

READ MORE
FEB 810:26 AM GMT
US restaurant operators see return to normal as year or more away

More than half of the US restaurant operators to participate in a recent survey published by the National Restaurant Association (NRA) believe it will be a year or more before business conditions return to normal.

That’s one of the findings in the NRA’s 2022 State of the Restaurant Industry Report, which measures the industry’s continued recovery and examines the status of current and emerging trends across key categories including technology and off-premises business, operations, workforce, food and menus.

READ MORE
FEB 712:05 PM GMT
Canadian ‘freedom convoy’ protests expand

Canada’s COVID-19 restrictions have drawn the ire of tens of thousands of people across the country who are demanding that the pandemic safeguards be lifted, CNN reports. 

The “freedom convoy” was initially started by truckers protesting a recent mandate requiring drivers entering Canada to be fully vaccinated or face testing and quarantine requirements. But others have joined the cause. Demonstrators reached Ottawa, Canada’s capital, last weekend, and its organizers said the protests will linger there and elsewhere if necessary.

READ MORE
FEB 41:13 PM GMT
Alaska sees 4,100 cases over two-day span

COVID-19 case counts are continuing to rise in Alaska as the omicron variant spreads across the US state. More than 4,100 cases were recorded over a two-day span beginning Jan. 31, Alaska’s News Source reported on Feb. 2. 

The Alaska Department of Health and Social Services logged 2,242 resident cases and 63 non-resident cases on Jan. 31 and 1,813 resident cases on Feb. 1 with an additional 28 non-resident cases.

READ MORE
FEB 39:07 AM GMT
Big Maine mussel farm expansion hearing delayed due to COVID concerns

An effort by Acadia Aqua Farms to grow the size of its operation a bit larger to battle invasive green crabs has been dealt a minor delay.  
A hearing by the Maine Department of Marine Resources to consider Acadia’s request for an additional 48 acres of lease area that was scheduled to be held live in the town of Bar Harbor on Feb. 9 has been moved to March 28 and made remote via Microsoft Teams “due to COVID-19 and capacity considerations”, the state agency announced on Wednesday.
As Undercurrent News reported earlier, Acadia Aqua Farms is already one of the largest growers of mussels on the US East Coast, maintaining five leases with 158 acres and harvesting about 500t of mussels per year. It seeks the additional acreage to secure a bigger blue mussel (Mytilus edulis) seed supply to compensate for the seed being eaten by the crabs (Carcinus maenas).

FEB 211:45 AM GMT
Canadian police take on truck blockade at US border

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP have begun enforcement actions against a group of commercial trucks and other vehicles that have created a blockade at the US-Canada border in the western province of Alberta, the transportation news service Freight Waves reports.

The participants in the blockade, nearest the town of Coutts, are reportedly protesting COVID-19 vaccine mandates, but the RCMP warned Tuesday that those who remain could face arrest. 

READ MORE
FEB 112:31 PM GMT
USDA leads creation of ‘pop-up’ container yard at Northern California port

The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) announced Monday that it was partnering with the Port of Oakland, California, to create what might be described as a “pop-up” container yard, the transportation news service Freight Waves reports.

The new 25-acre staging area is reserved for US agricultural exports, though the article doesn’t mention the prospect of seafood being included. In addition to covering 60% of the start-up cost, similar to facilities set up late last year by the US state of Georgia Ports Authority, the federal agency will provide shippers using the yard a $125-per-container subsidy to offset logistics costs, according to the news service.

READ MORE
JAN 3110:03 AM GMT
Two Canadian provinces allow restaurants to open at half capacity

The Canadian provinces of Quebec and Ontario on Monday allowed restaurants to take customers indoors again for the first time since issuing COVID-related rules over the holidays, according to multiple media sources. 

The restaurant dining rooms will be allowed to operate at half capacity in both provinces, with no more than four people or two different households at a table in Quebec, according to the National Post. Closing time in Quebec will be midnight with last call at 11 p.m.

READ MORE
JAN 313:18 AM GMT
UK consumer confidence in hospitality back despite omicron

Consumer confidence regarding eating out in the UK remains high despite the spread of the omicron variant, as recent research from CGA — the data and research consultancy of choice for the out-of-home food and drinks market — shows. 

According to the Consumer Pulse survey, two-thirds of 2,000 consumers now feel confident about visiting pubs, restaurants and bars. This is up 34% compared to the start of 2021 and 53% compared to CGA’s research in July, reports Catering Today. 

READ MORE
JAN 281:57 PM GMT
Dutch gov’t to ease strict COVID rules

The government of the Netherlands is preparing to relax strict COVID-19 prevention measures even as case counts rise nationally, the BBC reported.

The government led by prime minister Mark Rutte said that it was “taking a risk” in reducing the restrictions, which have included keeping museums, bars and restaurants shuttered since Dec. 18 as the omicron variant spread.

READ MORE
JAN 2710:47 AM GMT
Bout with COVID, workload cited by Alaska fisheries board member as reasons for stepping down

Indy Walton, a Soldotna, Alaska-based financial advisor and commercial Bristol Bay fisherman, announced this week that he will be giving up his seat on the Alaska Board of Fisheries due to a confluence of health issues exacerbated by stress and a bout of COVID-19, Alaska Public Media reports.  

The seven-member board makes decisions about fish allocation and management in Alaska waters. Walton accepted governor Mike Dunleavy’s nomination in September after a previous nominee was rejected by the state legislature. 
Walton also owns a sport-fishing lodge in Igiugig and has been an outspoken opponent of the Pebble Mine project.

READ MORE
JAN 2612:51 PM GMT
US east coast ports to benefit from shipping congestion

US east coast ports are in for a banner year as data from multiple sources shows that US importers are opening their wallets to avoid pandemic-inspired west coast logjams, American Shipper reports.

“Our data clearly shows that shippers are fed up with the logjam,” said Peter Sand, chief analyst at Xeneta. He added the shippers would be “happy” to pay extra for eastern destinations. 

READ MORE
JAN 264:08 AM GMT
UK has 10,000 more hospitality businesses than before Covid

The number of hospitality businesses in the UK has grown by more than 10,000 compared with before the pandemic, reports Foodservice Equipment Journal, citing Office of National Statistics data.

There were 10,650 more food and drink businesses in the UK in 2021 than in March 2019, and 3,650 more than in March 2020.

READ MORE
JAN 2510:19 AM GMT
US scallop capital New Bedford has higher-than-average positivity rate

New Bedford, Massachusetts, the US’ most valuable commercial fishing port and the nation’s scallop capital, is averaging 365 new COVID cases per day and seeing a whopping 29.9% positivity rate, WBX NewsRadio is reporting. 
That’s more than double the state’s positivity rate of 13.7%.

The city is also lagging in its residents getting booster shots, according to the radio station. More than 55.0% of New Bedford residents are fully vaccinated but only 19.5% have received a booster, well below the state average of 46.0%.
The situation has New Bedford mayor Jon Mitchell urging residents to get booster shots, promoting vaccination clinics throughout the city on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

READ MORE
JAN 249:24 AM GMT
Study points to Alaska seafood’s slow recovery

Given the impact of the pandemic, the value of the US state of Alaska’s commercial fisheries took a sharp but unsurprising drop in 2020 compared to the year before, a new study finds.

The 34-page “The Economic Value of Alaska’s Seafood” report — produced by the McKinley Research Group under contract for the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute — shows that the export value of the state’s fisheries dropped from $3.1 billion to $2.6bn over the two years, although its projected 2021 value rebounded slightly to $2.8bn.

READ MORE
JAN 2111:31 AM GMT
Mintel report: Consumers ready to go to school on seafood

The COVID-19-related shuttering of restaurants definitely pushed more consumers to buy seafood at retail, but there remains a trepidation about how to prepare it at home,  the Mintel Group notes in its 2021 Fish and Shellfish US report, according to Supermarket News.

Shoppers are seeking information on purchase drivers, including sourcing, processing and sustainability, according to the Mintel report. 

READ MORE
JAN 2011:17 AM GMT
Kentucky seafood restaurant delays 98th season due to COVID surge

Mike Linnig’s, a family owned seafood restaurant that’s enjoyed popularity in the US city of Louisville, Kentucky, since 1925, announced recently that it has delayed the opening of its 98th season to Jan. 27, 2022 as a precaution related to a recent COVID surge.

The Linnig restaurant, which is being operated by a third generation of family members, was originally set to re-open on Jan. 13, 2022, but said on social media that it wanted to keep its employees and customers safe. 

READ MORE
JAN 191:11 PM GMT
Fish farm survey: COVID-19 less damaging than climate change

A survey of 585 fish farms worldwide conducted by Northeastern University, in Boston, Massachusetts, has found nearly universal agreement in the aquaculture industry. 

The economic losses from human-caused issues, such as climate change, pollution and flooding, far outweigh those caused by supply-chain hiccups or a loss in buyers related to the COVID-19 pandemic.  At least, that’s what more than 80% of the respondents said, based on a report co-authored by Brian Helmuth, a professor of marine and environmental science at Northeastern, according to an article published by the university.

READ MORE
JAN 188:43 AM GMT
Reefer truck demand unusually high in US for after Christmas holiday

The demand for refrigerated, or “reefer” trucks, in the US is trending higher during what is normally a slower period for the sector,  Freight Waves reports.

The cargo industry news service points to the Reefer Outbound Tender Volume Index (ROTVI), a measure of demand for refrigerated truckload capacity that counts and indexes total electronic requests submitted by shippers to carriers, and the Reefer Outbound Tender Reject Index (ROTRI). The percentage of requests being rejected has risen above 40% in January, the highest it’s been since May.

READ MORE
JAN 179:45 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Vietnam shrimp prices drop with markets slow

Vietnamese shrimp spot prices fell in the second week of 2022, with the markets still slow thanks to the coronavirus pandemic, a trader based in the country told Undercurrent News.

While black tiger prices remain unchanged, vannamei average farm-gate prices for week two of 2022 were down by VND 4,000-VND 5,000 ($0.18-$0.23) week-on-week, to VND 140,000 ($6.16) per kilogram for 40-count; VND 117,000 for 60-count; VND 105,000 for 80-count; and VND 93,000 for 100-count.

READ MORE
JAN 175:09 AM GMT
The Netherlands relaxes restrictions, but restaurants stay shut

The Netherlands — the first European country to go into lockdown as the highly contagious omicron variant of the coronavirus spread to Europe — partially reopened on Saturday, reports Politico.

The country relaxed some of its measures with all non-essential stores and contact professions such as hairdressers allowed to be open until 5 pm, having been fully shuttered since Dec. 19. Restaurants and bars, however, will have to stay closed.

READ MORE
JAN 141:52 PM GMT
Cargo transit times to the US keep rising

A Trans-Pacific cargo move can now take over three months, with average transit times having risen to double pre-COVID levels – and they’re still increasing, American Shipper reports.

The shipping industry trade publication polled four shipping-industry analysts who reported that, while methodologies and data sources differ, each dataset shows the same trend: With every passing month, more vessels, container equipment and goods inventories are getting waylaid in the Pacific Ocean lately.

READ MORE
JAN 1312:37 PM GMT
Ohio city seeks another seafood restaurant to fill marina space

The city of Columbus, Ohio, has voted to sell a building on a marina that once held the popular seafood restaurant Woody’s on the Water, and it appears another seafood restaurant could take the space, the Columbus Dispatch reports.  

The building, which has been the location for multiple restaurants since the marina opened in April 2000, was donated to the city in February 2020 by then-owner John Young of CMR Enterprises, according to the minutes from a council meeting. 

READ MORE
JAN 122:37 PM GMT
Norway steps up prevention efforts ahead of fishing season

The Norwegian government is preparing for the winter fishing season and the influx of foreign workers that it brings by rolling out a host of measures to prevent the spread of COVID-19, it said.

Norway’s Ministry of Trade and Industry said in a press release that Bjornar Skjaeran, the country’s minister of fisheries and marine affairs, met with sector representatives to discuss prevention measures ahead of the fishing season.

READ MORE
JAN 1112:51 PM GMT
Latest COVID wave disrupts Australia’s tourist season

Australian businesses looking forward to the peak summer season are finding their hopes dashed as operations have been impacted by COVID-19’s Omnicron variant. Restaurants and hotels around the country, according to the Guardian newspaper, had looked forward to a busy season but now tourists’ hesitancy and staff shortages are crimping that optimism. 

“We are not as busy as we thought we’d be because a lot of people are being cautious,” Phil Johnson of Aireys Pub in the city of Aireys Inlet said. “It seems like a few families down here got it, so they’re staying away. And a lot of the oldies who we’d normally see just aren’t coming because I think they’re obviously, rightly, concerned.”

READ MORE
JAN 109:03 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden 
China border closure contributes as Vietnam shrimp prices start year flat

Spot prices for farmed Vietnamese shrimp started 2022 flat week-on-week, a trader based there told Undercurrent News.

As previously reported, he expects prices to remain flat or to dip during the first months of this year, with coronavirus dampening global markets.

READ MORE
JAN 73:43 AM GMT
China market likely to remain tumultuous for Vietnam

The Chinese market is expected to retain its status as Vietnam’s single largest for pangasius this year, though the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers (VASEP) anticipates the unpredictability of selling there will remain.

“In 2021, the ‘zero COVID’ policy made localities increasingly tighten the control of imported goods at both the border and official channels. As a result, cross-border goods are constantly opening and closing, full of precariousness, while pangasius for official export is facing difficulties because feeder ships entering China via Hong Kong are suspended,” noted VASEP’s general secretary, Truong Dinh Hoe.

READ MORE
JAN 65:14 AM GMT
Caviar sales soar during COVID lockdowns

When high-end restaurants around the globe had to close their doors during the COVID-19 lockdowns, things didn’t look good for the world’s caviar producers, Undercurrent News‘ Dan Gibson writes for the BBC.

With events canceled and cruise liners unable to leave port, it might have spelled disaster; but the reality has been very different. Online sales are booming as consumers increasingly eat their caviar at home.

READ MORE
JAN 44:16 AM GMT
Norwegian-UK Seafood Summit canceled 

The Norwegian-UK Seafood Summit expected to take place on Jan. 20 has been canceled due to uncertainty around further spread of COVID.

Nevertheless, the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC) will provide a UK relevant webinar on the same date, it stated. 

READ MORE
JAN 312:54 PM GMT
NFI to require proof of vaccination or recent negative test at Florida meeting

The National Fisheries Institute, the US’ largest and most powerful seafood-related trade association, announced a few new pandemic-related safety rules for its annual Global Seafood Marketing Conference, in Orlando, Florida, Jan. 18-20.

Attendees are being asked to provide either proof of vaccination or a negative COVID test taken within 72 hours of the event. Also, masks will be encouraged indoors. 

READ MORE
DEC 313:43 AM GMT
Infofish Tuna 2022 first-ever hybrid event to be held in October

The Infofish World Tuna 2022 conference and exhibition will be held from Oct. 11-13 as the organization’s first-ever hybrid event, with participants to be able to join in-person or virtually. 

With the theme “Strengthening Resilience, Adaptability and Sustainable Growth in the Global Tuna Industry,” the 17th world tuna trade conference will host tuna players to discuss major challenges caused by the pandemic.

READ MORE
DEC 302:25 PM GMT
Grocers’ inventory troubles change shopping habits, survey confirms

Worsening stock availability at grocery stores is perceived as a major hassle for US consumers, a new study states.

According to the publication Chain Store Age, two-thirds of the 1,000 shoppers polled by firm Ipsos agreed that grocers’ inventory levels are worse than they were before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. Nearly half of those surveyed said they shopped at a store in addition to their primary store in order to find out of stock items.

READ MORE
DEC 293:40 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Vietnam shrimp prices dip in week 51

The spot prices of farmed Vietnamese shrimp eased slightly in week 51 of 2021, as COVID-19 cases in the Mekong Delta region also improved a little, a source based there told Undercurrent News.

The provinces of Ca Mau, Bac Lieu, Soc Trang, and Can Tho are still suffering several hundred new cases per day, but the rate has eased and shrimp operations are still running under the “new normal”, said the source, a seafood trader.

United Airlines, a Chicago, Illinois-based company that offers flights to 118 international destinations in 48 countries across five continents, announced this week that it has resumed offering cargo-only flights, the news service American Shipper reports. 

READ MORE
SEP 301:01 PM GMT
Fiji fish markets see COVID disruption

COVID-19 issues have disrupted fishing grounds, raw materials supplies, processing facilities operations and all sorts of product transport in Fiji’s seafood industries, The Fiji Times reports.

Minister for Fisheries Semi Koroilavesau told the newspaper that despite the problems, “fish exports have been able to adjust and meet export market demands due to the stockpile of raw materials that were secured prior to the four and a half months of strict COVID-19 lockdown” over the last eight months.

READ MORE
SEP 2911:10 AM GMT
Singaporean seafood restaurant fined for breaching COVID rules

A Singaporean seafood restaurant has been fined SGD 6,500 ($4,800) after it allowed a 65-person strong dinner, in violation of COVID restrictions, reported Yahoo News.

Ah Yat Seafood Restaurant in the Turf City area was discovered by authorities on Feb. 6 with 65 seated customers across nine adjacent tables. Dining was halted before food could be served.

READ MORE
SEP 2811:03 AM GMT
Georgia harvesters, dealers get access to additional COVID relief funds

Commercial seafood harvesters, wholesale dealers, processors of saltwater species and bait shrimp dealers in the US state of Georgia can now apply for another $3 million in COVID-related relief funds thanks to the late 2020 passage of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2021, reports WTOC. 

The funds follow the $2m earlier made available by the Coronavirus Aid, Relief and Economic Security (CARES) Act, passed in March 2020.

READ MORE
SEP 276:43 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Rise in Vietnam shrimp prices expected to continue, strengthen, in October

Vietnamese shrimp prices are still recovering, with a stronger increase anticipated in October, according to an Undercurrent News source based there.

In week 38 — commencing Sept. 20 — prices lifted again, with factories in the Mekong Delta able to operate at around 50%-70% capacity and demand good, he said.

READ MORE
SEP 2411:54 AM GMT
US seafood restaurant refuses to mandate staff vaccination

The owner of Orlando, Florida-based Grills Seafood Deck and Tiki Bar has refused to mandate COVID vaccination for his employees because God told him “not to take the vaccine”, reports Orlando Weekly.

Joe Penovich has instead imposed weekly testing for his staff at the eateries, according to a memo posted on the restaurant’s Facebook page.

READ MORE
SEP 2312:53 PM GMT
US restaurants recovering, but not back to 2019 numbers yet, NPD reports

Physical restaurant visits in the US continue to recover, but dine-in numbers have yet to rebound to where they were before the pandemic, based on the latest report from the market research firm NPD Group.

Overall US restaurant sales were up 5% in August 2021 over the 10% decline seen in August 2020 but were down 5% when compared to the pre-pandemic level seen in August 2019, NPD said it found. The industry also benefited from a 13% increase in dollars earned through larger average check sizes in August 2021 compared to August 2020, according to NPD. The amount was up 3% from August 2019.

READ MORE
SEP 2212:59 PM GMT
Cali cargo ports to test expanded hours to cut backlog

Two significant shipping hubs in the US state of California, the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, plan to ramp up their hours of operation in order to reduce their share of a global backlog that has snarled supply chains.

According to the publication Freight Waves, the Long Beach port plans to create a test program for trucks hauling goods for short distances to pick up containers at night. Meanwhile, the Los Angeles port is looking to expand its hours on the weekend.

READ MORE
SEP 2110:51 AM GMT
Alaska seafood marketing chief: A third of agency’s revenue disappeared during pandemic

The Alaska seafood industry lost a third of its sales during the pandemic and, even though retail sales exploded, they didn’t make up for the loss, Jeremy Woodrow, executive director of the Alaska Seafood Marketing Institute, said at a recent conference, in Juneau, the radio station KINY 800/94.9 reports. 

Much of the value of the 162 million pounds of fish caught in Southeast Alaska comes from food service, Woodrow told attendees, who largely represented business interests in Southeast Alaska. 

READ MORE
SEP 207:19 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden 
Vietnam shrimp prices go on rising amid processor stability

Vietnamese vannamei prices have continued to increase in week 37 — commencing Sept. 13 — as processors were able to operate under a little more freedom, a source in the country told Undercurrent News.

Cases of coronavirus in the most important Mekong Delta provinces are still on the rise, but remain low, and most are applying only social distancing measures rather than full lockdowns.

READ MORE
SEP 203:39 AM GMT
Shenzhen Bay delays customs clearance of cargo from Hong Kong amid COVID restrictions

Shenzhen Bay Customs has been reportedly experiencing significant delays in clearing imported goods from Hong Kong since Friday (Sept. 17) due to cargo backlog caused by increased COVID testing requirements and staff shortages.

According to Australia’s Seafood Trade Advisory Group (STAG), some cargo has been unable to clear for over 24 hours. Shenzhen customs recommended importers stop buying and selling products that arrived via the Hong Kong market.

READ MORE
SEP 173:38 AM GMT
COVID outbreak in Vietnam causes exports to plummet in August

Seafood exports in August fell by between 16% and 50% compared to the same period of 2020, reports Vietnam Biz. 

This summer, COVID-19 broke out strongly in Ho Chi Minh City and another 18 provinces that account for around 95% of the country’s seafood export turnover and the industry’s labor force.

READ MORE
SEP 164:12 AM GMT
Scottish salmon body warns COVID has made it harder to house staff

The coronavirus pandemic has exacerbated Scotland’s rural housing crisis, the country’s farmed salmon trade body has told the Scottish parliament. 

Tavish Scott, the chief executive of the Scottish Salmon Producers Organisation, told the government that a lack of affordable housing was now a major issue for employers trying to create jobs in rural areas. 

READ MORE
SEP 157:03 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Vietnam shrimp prices creeping up as country gets to grips with outbreak

Vietnamese shrimp prices are creeping up as the country gets a handle on its coronavirus outbreak, according to the latest update from Undercurrent News‘ source there.

For week 36 — commencing Sept. 6 — vannamei prices lifted to VND 119,000 per kilogram for 40-count; VND 93,000 for 60-count; VND 82,000 for 80-count; and VND 70,000 for 100-count, up between VND 2,000 and 3,000 ($0.09-$0.13/kg) week-on-week.

READ MORE
SEP 144:58 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Thai tuna sector implements COVID measures, but costs hurting

Thailand’s tuna sector has worked hard to implement and audit various coronavirus mitigation measures, but it is suffering the costs, said Amornphan Aramwatananont, director of the Thai Tuna Industry Association (TTIA), at the X World Tuna Conference.

The TTIA has been made responsible for auditing supply chain companies under Thai regulations. In the fall of 2020, a number of companies managed to implement COVID-19 measures and get TTIA’s seal of approval:

READ MORE
SEP 138:30 AM GMT
Minh Phu warns of lost customers if plants not allowed to operate

Vietnamese shrimp farmer and processor Minh Phu Seafood has warned that it could lose customers if its factories are not allowed to operate normally, reports Baogiaothing.

Chairman Le Van Quang has petitioned the leaders of Ca Mau and Hau Giang provinces, home to the company’s processing factories, to lift restrictions aimed at stemming the spread of the virus.

READ MORE
SEP 1011:09 AM GMT
Alaska’s COVID hospitalizations keep breaking records

The US state of Alaska, home to some of the country’s largest seafood harvesting and processing operations, continues to break its own previous records for COVID-19-related hospitalizations, Alaska Public Media reports. 

On Thursday, 206 were being treated in Alaska hospitals for the virus, based on data provided by the state. Hospitals in Anchorage, Fairbanks, the Mat-Su and the Kenai Peninsula all report to have ICUs either full or near capacity.

READ MORE
SEP 104:37 AM GMT
Vietnamese firms still hope for greater gov’t aid

Vietnamese seafood processors are still hoping for more government aid, after support measures were granted late in August, reports VIR.

The government has subsidized electricity tariffs for a number of companies that qualify (by implementing social distancing measures), a move that was welcomed by the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers.

READ MORE
SEP 95:37 AM GMT
Seafood firms from Peru, Indonesia, Pakistan, Myanmar face China COVID-related import suspension

China continued its crackdown on seafood imports as it claimed to have detected traces of COVID-19 on the packaging of products from Peru, Indonesia and Pakistan.

According to China’s General Administration of Customs (GACC), on Sept. 4, Peruvian seafood manufacturer Productora Andina de Congelados faced import suspension for five weeks, while Seafrost was suspended from imports for one week. Positive coronavirus nucleic acid tests were detected from samples of the packages of three batches of frozen squid.

READ MORE
SEP 84:04 PM GMT
Florida seafood festival falls foul of COVID

COVID has a fresh victim – Florida’s Destin Seafood Festival.

The annual event had been planned between Oct.1 and Oct. 3, but the organizers said “the logistical challenges and responsibilities of bringing tens of thousands of people together safely” forced them to cancel.

READ MORE
SEP 73:50 AM GMT
Vietnam’s seafood exports down 36% in August

Vietnam’s seafood export turnover reached some $520 million in August, down 36% against the same month last year due to COVID-19 outbreaks across the country last month, reports VNExpress.

In August, only 30-40% of seafood enterprises in the south of the country were able to enact the “3TC” regulation, which saw workers accommodated and fed at their place of work. This meant factory production capacity dropped 50-60%, said the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Processors (VASEP).

READ MORE
SEP 68:22 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Brighter signs in latest Vietnam update

The latest weekly update from Undercurrent News‘ source in Vietnam paints a brighter picture for the shrimp sector, though the situation has been highly volatile over the past month as important aquaculture regions drop into and out of COVID-19 lockdown measures.

In what should be good news, the provinces of Bac Lieu, Ca Mau, and Hau Giang have emerged from strict lockdowns, and now must follow simpler social distancing measures.

READ MORE
SEP 64:15 AM GMT
Minh Phu boss bemoans COVID measures, with firm likely to miss targets this year

The chairman of Vietnam’s Minh Phu Seafood, Le Van Quang, has spoken about the difficulties of implementing the country’s coronavirus measures and warned the firm faces missing its profit targets for the fourth year running, reports VietnamBiz and Vietnam Finance.

As part of Vietnam’s factory worker quarantine, Minh Phu has hired out all the hotels in the vicinity of its plants, but this has still not been enough to house enough staff, he said. 

READ MORE
SEP 31:23 PM GMT
Maryland seafood industry gets $3.4m in second round of COVID relief

The Maryland seafood industry has received another $3.4 million in federal relief funds, courtesy of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2021, DelMarva Now reports.

“The pandemic has slowed our sales down because people aren’t buying our products like before,” Harry Phillips, owner of Russell Hall Seafood LLC in Fishing Creek, is quoted as saying. “Due to lack of (employees) in restaurants and being only at half capacity, that’s why sales have been down. It’s actually possibly getting worse, but we haven’t received assistance like this because our sales were strong last summer.”

READ MORE
SEP 210:37 AM GMT
Peter Pan requires COVID-19 vaccination at plants, but not on vessels

The Alaskan seafood processor Peter Pan Seafood Co. has taken a stance that is growing more common but still somewhat controversial in the US. It is requiring its workers be vaccinated against COVID-19.

Peter Pan, which came under new management after it was acquired in late December by a group of companies led by the Northwest Fish Company, explained its position in a statement published Wednesday.

READ MORE
SEP 23:57 AM GMT
Minh Phu drops processing capacity to 50-70% despite high market demands for shrimp

Vietnamese shrimp farmer and processor Minh Phu Seafood said its factory’s processing capacity fell to about 50-70% amid a workforce shortage and transportation difficulties, reported Vietnam Biz.

During a shrimp industry online forum, Le Van Quang, Minh Phu’s chairman, said his company received many orders but only signed about 50-70% of the factory operating capacity. Only 25% of employees currently work in the factory.

READ MORE
SEP 18:45 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Vietnam’s COVID situation continues to worsen

Vietnam’s coronavirus outbreak continues to worsen as August turns into September.

The capital of Ho Chi Minh is locked down and the military is manning food distribution, according to an Undercurrent News source based there. Meanwhile, the important shrimp production regions of Ca Mau and Bac Lieu continue to operate under lockdowns and the “3TC” regulation (see previous blog posts), which is making business very difficult.

READ MORE
SEP 13:59 AM GMT
UK food chain demands ‘COVID recovery visa’ to tackle labor shortage

The British food and drink sector is calling on the government to introduce a 12-month “COVID recovery visa” to recruit overseas workers and help ease disruption in the food supply chain, including the seafood processing sector.

A report sent to the government on behalf of trade associations representing all areas of the UK’s food chain — including the National Farmers’ Union, the Food and Drink Federation, and the British Meat Processors Association — warned the pandemic and post-Brexit immigration policy had caused workforce shortage, reported the Guardian.

READ MORE
AUG 3111:10 AM GMT
Chinese officials claims COVID first spread to Wuhan via cold chain

China’s Center for Disease Control (CDC) and Prevention has a new theory for where COVID came from – frozen food imports.

It reckons the virus first spread in the Chinese city of Wuhan in December 2019 via a batch of frozen food from another country, reported the Global Times.

READ MORE
AUG 279:17 AM GMT
Vietnam’s seafood exports to China decline amid COVID restrictions

Vietnam’s seafood exports to mainland China and Hong Kong have slipped by 5% year-on-year to $238 million in the first seven months of 2021, according to the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers (VASEP), reports VN Express.

Vietnamese pangasius exports to China have fallen by 11.4% in the second quarter, compared to the same period in 2020.

READ MORE
AUG 273:54 AM GMT
Aussie gov’t invests further in emergency freight support

The Australian government has announced it will go on supporting seafood businesses by providing an additional AUD 260.9 million to subsidize critical airfreight links to international customers.

In total, the government has now provided AUD 1.04 billion to support jobs and exporters through the International Freight Assistance Mechanism (IFAM), which has been running since April 2020 and will now continue to do so until June 2022. 

READ MORE
AUG 265:17 AM GMT
Ecuador’s Guayaquil Aqua Expo to go ahead in October

The Ecuadorian National Chamber of Aquaculture, also known as CNA, has confirmed that the 2021 Aqua Expo in Guayaquil will go ahead in October.

The event will be held in-person at Convention Center Guayaquil, from Oct. 25-28. CNA described the expo as “the most important aquaculture event” in South America.

READ MORE
AUG 2512:29 PM GMT
NFI confident enough to announce dates for live Florida event

In a display of confidence that the US will be far enough returned from the coronavirus outbreak in the next five months, the National Fisheries Institute (NFI) on Wednesday announced that it has begun taking registrations for its Global Seafood Market Conference, Jan. 18-20.

The event is taking place at the Omni Champions Gate Resort, in Orlando, Florida, according to a press release from NFI. The US trade association said it also will be holding its committee/council meetings, Jan. 16-18.

READ MORE
AUG 258:47 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Vietnam shrimp prices dive again, as Ca Mau falls back under 3TC

After a brief flash of some stability in recent days as the important shrimp-producing region of Ca Mau emerged from the strict “3TC” measures (see below), prices have dived again.

On Aug. 24 Ca Mau returned to a full lockdown after new COVID cases were uncovered. Processing plants have had to return to the 3TC measures, which require employers to house and feed its staff — something many plants decide to close rather than do, for cost reasons.

READ MORE
AUG 254:02 AM GMT
Japan’s Nissui reports new COVID-19 outbreak at plant

Japan’s Nippon Suisan Kaisha (Nissui) has reported 30 new COVID-19 cases scattered across its offices and factories over the past month.

Nissui said 25 cases were found in the Hachioji processed food factory in Tokyo, while another worker was diagnosed with coronavirus in the company’s Tokyo Innovation Center.

READ MORE
AUG 2311:40 AM GMT
NSC to attend Saudi show, its first since pandemic

The Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC) is back in the business of attending live trade shows in order to boost the country’s exports, it said.

Next month, NSC representatives will attend Saudi Horeca in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia when the three-day show kicks off on Sept. 5. The show will mark the NSC’s first attendance at a major trade show since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, it said. 

READ MORE
AUG 239:30 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Key Vietnam shrimp province emerges from strict lockdown

The Vietnamese province of Ca Mau, a key one for both shrimp and pangasius production, has emerged from the country’s strict lockdown policy of “3TC”, a local source told Undercurrent News.

As previously reported, the main issue for Vietnamese processors has been the government’s “three-on-site” directive, known as 3TC. This meant processors must keep workers quarantined on-site to stay open. The “three” refers to the need for companies to be able to accommodate staff eating and sleeping on-site, as well as working.

READ MORE
AUG 234:50 AM GMT
Vietnamese shrimp companies vaccinate workers

Vietnamese shrimp companies have begun vaccinating workers in factories amid the country’s COVID-19 wave, according to a client note by Sabina Group. 

At Thai Hoa Food, a shrimp packer, 100% of employees who work on-site have received one shot, said Nguyen Dang Khoa, general director of the firm.

READ MORE
AUG 204:11 AM GMT
Japan announces more prefectures in ‘state of emergency’ amid record daily COVID cases

The Japanese government announced on Friday (Aug. 20) it would impose a COVID-19 state of emergency in seven more prefectures, with restrictions on business activity to curb the nation’s largest wave of infections yet, reported The Japan Times.

Ibaraki, Tochigi, Gunma, Shizuoka, Kyoto, Hyogo, and Fukuoka will be under the state of emergency until Sept. 12, joining Chiba, Saitama, Tokyo, Kanagawa, Osaka, and Okinawa.

READ MORE
AUG 198:14 AM GMT
US red meat exporters largely spared from chaos at Chinese port

The congestion that has roiled operations at China’s Ningbo-Zhoushan Port, the world’s third-busiest marine transportation hub, has thus far largely spared US meat suppliers.

According to Brownfield Ag News, heightened restrictions enacted at the port after a worker tested positive for COVID-19 have largely spared US red meat exporters.

READ MORE
AUG 193:43 AM GMT
Congestion at major Chinese ports worsens as ships divert away from Ningbo

The partial closure of Ningbo-Zhoushan Port in eastern China — the world’s third busiest marine transportation hub — is worsening congestion at other Chinese ports as container ships divert away from Ningbo, reported Al Jazeera.

At the ports of Shanghai, Hong Kong, and Xiamen, congestion has increased due to the increase in the number of container ships berthing and waiting in line for unloading, according to shipping data compiled by Bloomberg.

READ MORE
AUG 181:46 PM GMT
North Carolina opens applications for COVID seafood aid program

North Carolina’s Division of Marine Fisheries (DMF) is now accepting applications from the US state’s seafood sector businesses that saw revenue losses from the COVID-19 pandemic.

According to Coastal Review Online, DMF will distribute funds to “commercial fishers, marine aquaculture operators, seafood dealers and processors and for-hire fishing operators” who can show that their 2020 revenues fell 35% or more compared to the previous five-year average.

READ MORE
AUG 174:44 AM GMT
Thaifex cancels in-person event, announces online 2021 edition

Koelnmesse, the organizer of Thai seafood show Thaifex, has canceled plans to hold the 2021 edition of the event as a partly “in-person” gathering and opted to make it an online-only version instead.

Thus, Thaifex-Anuga Asia “hybrid edition” will now take place on May 24-28, 2022, at IMPACT Muang Thong Thani, Bangkok. In the meantime, a “virtual trade show” will go ahead on Sept. 29- Oct. 3, 2021.

READ MORE
AUG 1610:09 AM GMT
Vietnam extends lockdowns across important producing regions

Vietnam’s seafood sector has suffered over the last couple of months from regional lockdown measures designed to curtail the spread of COVID-19’s delta variant.

The lockdowns – which have seen many processing plants close, and others severely restrict their capacities – were due to end on Aug. 16, but with cases still rising in most provinces, the measures have been extended, according to an Undercurrent News source based in Vietnam.

READ MORE

title: Boston 2019: Indian shrimp production to increase 450,000t by 2022; Antibiotics use in aquaculture ‘in the spotlight’
content:
BOSTON, Massachusetts, US -- Undercurrent News is blogging live from the annual Boston seafood show, the largest event for the US sector, held from March 17-19.

Our team of four reporters will bring you all the news from the show floor. We also did a build-up to Boston, which you can read here. 

 

Auto updates: On
MAR 211:38 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Samuels & Son uses Boston to announce new national expansion plan

Samuels & Son already packed a lot of punch as a Philadelphia, Pennsylvania-based seafood wholesaler and importer, but the expansion plans it announced this week in Boston put it into another weight class altogether. 

The company recently added facilities in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; Orlando, Florida; and Las Vegas, Nevada, growing it to a more than 50 million per year operation. Now it’s also looking to add locations in Boston as well as in Houston Texas; Phoenix, Arizona; and Los Angeles, California.

READ MORE
MAR 211:21 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Canadian trade group hits Boston on mission to promote new national brand

The United States is already the Canadian seafood industry’s best trade market, taking 65% of all its exported products, but the leaders of the Fisheries Council of Canada (FCC) were in Boston this week as part of a new campaign to further increase those sales.

Undercurrent News interviewed Paul Lansbergen, FCC’s president, and Clarke Cross, its director of policy and regulatory affairs, on Saturday, just after both arrived in town. Though they didn’t take one of the event’s more than 1,300 booths, they came loaded with a stack of brochures to hand out as they worked their way around the event, meeting dozens of prospective buyers and even competitors.

READ MORE
MAR 207:17 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Antibiotics use in aquaculture ‘in the spotlight’

Heightened fears about antibiotics resistance have put aquaculture “in the spotlight”, according to Iain Shone, development director at Global Aquaculture Alliance.

A talking point at the Boston show among shrimp industry executives was an investigation by CBC News which found antibiotic-resistant bacteria on samples of frozen shrimp at retail stores in Canada.

READ MORE
MAR 205:25 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
GAA: Innovation, technological advancement driving big increases in productivity of shrimp aquaculture

Global farmed shrimp production could leap to 8-9 million metric tons within the next five years as a new wave of innovation and technological advancement in aquaculture drives big increases in productivity.

Speaking at the Global Aquaculture Alliance (GAA) annual shrimp forum at the sidelines of the Boston show, George Chamberlain, president of GAA, said advancements at all stages of shrimp aquaculture, from improved genetics and live feed replacements for shrimp larvae in hatcheries, to better biosecurity and intensive farming systems on the farm, are “changing the face of the sector”.

READ MORE
MAR 209:21 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
SFEA: Indian shrimp production to increase 450,000t by 2022

Get ready for more Indian shrimp, much more.

READ MORE
MAR 207:23 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Blue Harvest touts groundfish from Atlantic Trawlers acquisition 

Bregal Partners-owned Blue Harvest Fisheries displayed cod, haddock and redfish from its latest acquisition, Atlantic Trawlers Fishing, at the Boston show. 

Although Keith Decker, CEO, was not available for an interview,Undercurrent News understands the company has been telling customers about the new products from Atlantic Trawlers’ five vessels. 

READ MORE
MAR 194:15 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Slade Gorton launches frozen line using raw material from Icelandic investor Samherji 

US importer and processor Slade Gorton & Co. has a new frozen retail line from its Icelandic investor Samherji, using wild cod, haddock and farmed Arctic char. 

The products, under the brand ICYBAY Iceland, tell the Icelandic raw material provenance story, in addition to flagging up Samherji as the supplier. 

READ MORE
MAR 194:02 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Shrimp industry looks to avocado success story for marketing strategy ideas

Shrimp executives have turned to the avocado industry for ideas for a coordinated marketing strategy in the US.

Assessing what ideas could be adopted by the shrimp sector, speaking at the Global Aquaculture Alliance’s (GAA) Annual Shrimp Forum, Travis Larkin, president at US seafood importer and processor Seafood Exchange, pointed to an effort to provide better supply and price forecasting for avocado buyers.

READ MORE
MAR 193:34 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Two retailers want Bristol’s frozen, value-added cod, scallop skin-packs 

Retailers on the east and west coasts of the US have made commitments for Bristol Seafood’s new “My Fish Fix” frozen, value-added range in skin-packs, an executive with the company told Undercurrent News. 

The two retailers want to take the company’s lemon butter scallops, as well a two cod flavors, said Bristol’s Irene Moon. 

READ MORE
MAR 193:13 PM GMT
By Jason Smith
Ocean Beauty’s revamped smoked brand features wild, farmed fish, CDQ story

Seattle, Washington-based processor Ocean Beauty Seafoods has revamped its major Echo Falls smoked salmon brand, in its first major re-fresh effort in over 15 years. 

Ron Christenson, the company’s vice president of domestic sales and marketing, told Undercurrent News that the company completely redesigned the packaging for the hot and cold smoked salmon retail brand, which he said is the top seller in the US. 

READ MORE
MAR 191:20 PM GMT
ASC celebrates its growing presence in China

Chinese shellfish producer Green Life Foods was welcomed to the Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) by CEO Chris Ninnes on March 18 at the Seafood Expo North America.

Green Life Foods became the first ASC certified mussel and oyster producer in China last year, having made the necessary adjustments to its production and processing practices. 

READ MORE
MAR 1911:58 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
US importer Western Edge paid $1m in China tariffs in 2018

Seafood importer Western Edge Seafood paid approximately $1 million in additional duties in 2018 after the US slapped 10% tariffs on imports of Chinese seafood, Don Kelley, vice president at the firm, told Undercurrent News. 

Kelley, whose firm imports tilapia fillets from China, as well as fillets of redfish and catfish produced in the country, said the cost and general uncertainty had “affected certain decisions”, but noted: “This is a dynamic industry, if it’s not tariffs it’s import procedures and regulations, or typhoons and floods.”

READ MORE
MAR 197:37 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Maze plans to take Pescanova into big US retailers, foodservice customers 

Chris Maze, the new CEO of the US arm of Spain’s Grupo Nueva Pescanova, plans to take the business closer to big customers and away from trading. 

“We are looking to not only get the value-added brand going, but really get in the channels where we should be. We are a vertically integrated company, let’s leverage that and get into foodservice, retail and club stores,” Maze, who joined Pescanova after two years at East Coast Seafood Group, told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
MAR 197:21 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Chile salmon brand launch comes with promise to cut antibiotics, work with Monterey Bay

Chile’s salmon industry launched its multi-year marketing campaign with a packed breakfast meeting this week at the Boston seafood show, simultaneously announcing an agreement to work with the Monterey Bay Aquarium’s Seafood Watch program to secure a “good alternative” rating and also cut its antibiotics use in half by 2025.

READ MORE
MAR 197:14 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Triple-size Mowi Miami plant online soon to meet booming US skin-pack demand 

Norwegian salmon giant Mowi’s new plant in Miami, Florida is completed and will start production in the next few weeks, the company’s top downstream executive in the US told Undercurrent News. 

The plant, which is more than three times the size of the company’s current factory in Miami, will be producing to meet the booming demand for skin-packaged products in the US market, said Joe Fidalgo, head of Mowi’s consumer products division in the country. Mowi’s new plant is 106,000 square feet, whereas the current facility in Florida is 30,000 sq. feet, Fidalgo told Undercurrent. 

READ MORE
MAR 197:12 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Martha Stewart’s chef on new seafood offerings: ‘Our goal is not to just be in specialty retailers’

Thomas Joseph, the culinary director for Martha Stewart, told Undercurrent News that he was working with Cooke’s team at the Boston seafood show to identify potential partners that could help the company’s new value-added seafood offerings created with Cooke’s True North brand reach the masses in the US.

Our goal as a company is to give the best products to everybody,” he said. “Our goal is not to just be in specialty retailers. We want to deliver it in a way that anyone can make it.”

READ MORE
MAR 196:40 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Cooke strikes again, buys California distributor 

Acquisitive seafood group Cooke has snapped up a distributor based on the US West Coast, the company confirmed to Undercurrent News during the Boston seafood show. 

Cooke confirmed a deal for All Seas Wholesale of San Francisco, California, having bought JC Seafood, an importer based in Florida, last year. The news of the deal comes days after Cooke confirmed the acquisition of shrimp farmer and processor Farallon Aquaculture de Nicaragua, after also buying Seajoy Group earlier this year. 

READ MORE
MAR 189:25 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
California’s Del Mar in the market for squid fishing vessels

California-based fishing company Del Mar Seafoods is in the market for two-to-three new vessels to fish for Californian market squid (Loligo opalescens).

The company, which catches around 25% of the market squid landed annually, said it is eyeing vessel owners who might be calling time after several years of bad catches.

READ MORE
MAR 187:45 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
The US squid importers who avoid 10% tariffs 

US squid fishing companies which ship squid to China for cleaning and processing are currently not levied US import tariffs of 10% when they bring it back for domestic sale, sources told Undercurrent News.

The situation has arisen due to US country of origin rules and what constitutes “substantial transformation”.

READ MORE
MAR 185:07 PM GMT
By Jason Smith
Ecuador takes another run at getting its shrimp into Brazil

The long-running trade and legal battle to sell Ecuadorian shrimp in the largest country in South America has taken another turn. 

Jose Antonio Camposano, who heads Ecuador’s National Aquaculture Chamber, told Undercurrent News that containers filled with the country’s farmed shrimp left last week bound for Brazil, the latest effort by South America’s biggest shrimp farmer to penetrate a country of 203 million people.

READ MORE
MAR 1812:12 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Dutch Seafood plans to take Foppen smoked salmon into US foodservice, start with shrimp 

Dutch Seafood Company plans to get smoked salmon from its Foppen Groep operation into foodservice in the US, as well as start selling shrimp from Klaas Puul Beheer, executives with the company told Undercurrent News. 

Foppen has a strong retail and club store position in the country in Costco Wholesale, Kroger and others, but is only just taking the step into foodservice, said Remko Vedder, the company’s sales director for the US. 

READ MORE
MAR 1811:47 AM GMT
By Jason Smith
SSP-qualified shrimp from Ecuador could hit shelves soon 

Farmed shrimp from Ecuador that meets additional criteria beyond most certification schemes — including criteria that it is antibiotic free, traceable and has a neutral impact on water quality — will be reaching the market soon if deals are done in Boston, Pamela Nath, the director of the Sustainable Shrimp Partnership (SSP) told Undercurrent News. 

SSP is a farmer-focused sustainability initiative that starts with the requirement that farmers must be Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC) certified but goes beyond those standards, adding the three additional criteria. 

READ MORE
MAR 188:21 AM GMT
Open Blue launches ocean-raised Pacific snapper

Open Blue has launched a premium Pacific snapper (Lutjanus Peru) product, produced by sister firm Earth Ocean Farm, at SENA.

The recipient of the 2018 SeaWeb “seafood champion” award in the “vision category”, the addition of Earth Ocean Farm snapper to the Open Blue portfolio “continues our mission to advance the mariculture industry by offering our customers premium natural fish raised in the open ocean, far away from sensitive nearshore ecosystems”, it said.

READ MORE
MAR 188:01 AM GMT
Legit to unveil new transparency app

Legit Fish, provider of what it claims is a first-of-its-kind seafood traceability technology, has launched an application which allows an “unprecedented level” of transparency for consumers while ensuring a seafood’s origin actually matches its packaging.

“Increasing stories around seafood fraud are eroding consumer trust; we’re seeing repetitive cases where seafood is claimed to be from local waters when it is in fact imported,” said Michael Carroll, CEO of Legit Fish. 

READ MORE
MAR 187:23 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Pearce getting the hang of blue swimming crab, but knows value-added products

Dave Pearce is so new to Handy Seafood, a large blue and blue swimming crab importer and wholesaler in Salisbury, Maryland, that longtime industry acquaintances are confused to see him standing at the company’s booth at Seafood Expo North America (SENA) 2019, in Boston, he told Undercurrent News.

Saturday was Pearce’s first day with the company after leaving Tampa Maid Foods, where he had served 28 years; the last 14 as its president. Tampa Maid is based in Lakeland, Florida, and specializes in value-added shellfish, including heavily shrimp, oyster, scallops, and calamari.

READ MORE
MAR 186:57 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
India’s shrimp exports surpass 600,000t

India’s exports of shrimp surpassed 600,000 metric tons in 2018, according to latest trade data.

Exports of the crustacean grew 8% to 615,690t, according to International Trade Center, equivalent to some 44,495t more Indian shrimp on global markets.

READ MORE
MAR 186:04 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Seachill eyes US ‘partner’ for Saucy Fish range 

Seachill UK is using the 2019 Boston show to find a partner to distribute its The Saucy Fish Co. range in the US market, its sales director told Undercurrent News. 

The company wants to find a US player with strong links into the country, said Amanda Webb, as Seachill presents a new “flexitarian” range for the first time (see below).

READ MORE
MAR 177:26 PM GMT
By Jason Smith
Ventisqueros CEO: Company open to partnership possibility amid salmon M&A wave 

The head of Puerto Montt, Chile-based Productos del Mar Ventisqueros has been watching with interest as his larger salmon farming rivals merge or become acquired. 

The past year has seen a wave of consolidation with Chile’s Agrosuper merging four farmers to create the world’s second-largest salmon producer and China’s Legend Holdings make a $880 million offer for Australis Seafoods. 

READ MORE
MAR 177:12 PM GMT
By Jason Smith
Corbion brings algae-fed salmon message to masses with chef video

Dutch food ingredients maker Corbion has partnered with a US celebrity chef to get its message out about the sustainability of algae oil-fed coho salmon. 

The company works with feed producer BioMar to work its AlgaPrime DHA fish oil alternative into diets fed to Silverside coho salmon, a brand farmed by Chile’s Productos del Mar Ventisqueros and sold through BluGlacier, a US sales joint venture the company operates with fellow Chilean salmon farmer Blumar. 

READ MORE
MAR 174:49 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Lobster firm in Nova Scotia wary of Canada-China tensions 

Chinese-owned Capital Seafood said it has not suffered delays to exports of live lobster to China, but is watching events closely after a Canadian exporter of canola oil recently had its permit revoked by Chinese authorities. 

On March 7, China’s customs agency revoked the permit of Richardson International, one of Canada’s largest grain processors, to export to China. China has said it will also implement more strict inspections of Canadian canola shipments. 

READ MORE
MAR 173:20 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Cermaq launches ‘True Arctic’ B2B brand for Norwegian salmon 

Mitsubishi Corp.-owned salmon farmer Cermaq Group is branding fish from its Norwegian farms from as “True Arctic Salmon”, driven by customer demand. 

Arild Akre, the company’s sales director, said the demand for True Arctic came more from Asian and European customers, but that there is also potential in the US market. 

READ MORE
MAR 172:46 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
China’s shrimp consumption closes on 2m metric tons, says Guolian’s Chen 

China’s consumption of farmed and wild shrimp is getting close to 2m metric tons, said Chen Han, general manager of Zhanjiang Guolian Aquatic Products. 

Chen estimates China’s imports [both direct and via Vietnam] are around 1m metric tons, with around 800,000t of farmed and wild shrimp produced in the country. Chen declined to comment on the crackdown on imports via Vietnam, however.

READ MORE
MAR 1712:18 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
No more pigging out for Atlantic salmon sold in UAE

What happens when the fish on your dish also contains meat? The question has tripped up seafood companies in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, after authorities there banned imports of farmed seafood fed with aquatic feed containing pork meal.

The ban came into effect a year ago and is a “major challenge, as we see it”, Renjith Ganapathy, managing director of Dubai-based Source Global, told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
MAR 1711:22 AM GMT
By Jason Smith
Norway’s Salten Aqua gains Seafood Watch’s first green rating for net-pen raised salmon

The Monterey Bay Aquarium’s Seafood Watch sustainability system has given a “green” rating, the group’s highest rating, to Salten Aqua Group’s Nordic Blu branded Atlantic salmon, a first for a net-pen raised salmon. 

The company’s fish is being shown for the first time at the Boston seafood show and is imported into the US by San Francisco, California-based CleanFish and is being sold by Coastal Seafoods in Minnesota’s Twin Cities region. 

READ MORE
MAR 177:43 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Argentine red shrimp harvesters hope MSC approval will up prices 

A group of companies catching Argentine red shrimp have engaged Bureau Veritas to assess the in-shore fishery against the Marine Stewardship Council standard, which they hope will further open up the North American and European markets and lead to higher prices. 

The companies made the decision after running a fishery improvement project for three years in co-operation with the provincial fishing authorities and the non-governmental organization CeDePesca. 

READ MORE
MAR 165:05 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Still too much shrimp stock in US market, says Siam Canadian’s Gulkin 

Even though shrimp consumption in the US is brisk, prices are still in the doldrums, said Jim Gulkin, managing director of Siam Canadian Group, a frozen seafood supplier.

“There’s too much inventory. Everyone knows that, so people don’t buy and the prices continue to drop,” he told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
