title: China expo 2018: Nissui looks to secure Alaska, Russia crab for China market; Guolian’s new 50,000t shrimp factory
content:
QINGDAO, China -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the China Fisheries & Seafood Expo, held from Nov. 7-9 in a venue close to Qingdao. 

On Nov. 6, we're reporting from various conferences held before the start of the trade show. 

Auto updates: On
NOV 122:19 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Raw material prices of fish processed by Dalian firm ‘relatively stable’

Raw material prices for pollock, wild salmon, yellowfin sole, Atlantic and Pacific redfish, and Pacific hake are all relatively stable, said Tina Wang, sales manager at Dalian Athena Seafoods, with most plants in Dalian, China, busy fulfilling orders. 

Marine Stewardship Council-certified pink salmon from Russia is still around $3,200-3,500 per metric ton for bigger sizes and good quality fish, said Wang. Pollock raw material is around $1,600/t, she said, though Chinese processors are now looking towards next season’s fishing rather than making big orders.  

READ MORE
NOV 1212:00 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Nissui looks to secure Alaska, Russia crab for China market

The world’s second largest seafood company, Nippon Suisan Kaisha (Nissui), reckons “now is the time” to re-start developing the crab market in China, after a period of high prices.

Nissui is targeting sales of bluefin tuna, yellowtail, red snapper, king crab and snow crab in China, as well as Japanese-made EPA and DHA-fortified soya products and surimi ‘cheese’ (see below). 

READ MORE
NOV 1211:15 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese firm producing value-added seafood in Mauritania

Sino-Mauritania joint venture Sunrise Oceanic Resources Exploitation Company (SOREC) is producing whole round, fillets and butterfly fish products at its factory in Mauritania, said Simon Zhang, executive deputy general manager of SOREC.


It sells mainly low value fish, such as sardines, to the domestic market and other African markets.


READ MORE
NOV 1210:38 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
New Zealand rock lobster exporters ‘can’t be complacent’ over premium status

New Zealand rock lobster exporters “can’t be complacent” and firm Fiordland Lobster Company warns of the dangers of rock lobster “becoming commoditized” in the fast-changing Chinese market, David Prendergast, group general manager of sales, told Undercurrent News.

In many high-end restaurants in China rock lobster is the most expensive seafood product in holding tanks. In a Guangzhou restaurant Undercurrent visited in September large-sized Australian rock lobster was priced at an eye-watering CNY 79.9 per 50g ($11.48/50g, see photo).

READ MORE
NOV 125:23 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Guolian’s new 50,000t-capacity factory set to open in new year

Zhanjiang Guolian Aquatic Prorducts’ new plant in Zhanjiang is set for a February opening, deputy general manager Wu Liqing told Undercurrent News. 

The Zhanjiang-based plant will do deep-processing of mainly shrimp and have an annual production capacity of 50,000 metric tons of finished products, said Wu.

READ MORE
NOV 125:08 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Sunkfa: Seasonal seafood products hold less appeal among Chinese buyers

Stable, year-round supply of Boston lobster, salmon, shrimp, Dungeness crabs, brown crabs and king crabs is a key reason for their popularity in China, one of the country’s largest importers told Undercurrent News.

Sunkfa Group sells seafood online and offline and expects online sales to hit CNY 1 billlion ($143.7 million) in 2018. Because of the demand in China for fresh product and live product — particularly from the higher-end market — seasonal imported products tend to be more difficult to market.

READ MORE
NOV 123:44 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Trident plans to launch ‘Ultimate Fish Stick’ in China using US pollock 

Trident Seafoods plans to launch its well-known “The Ultimate Fish Stick” product in the Chinese market in the future, despite the 25% tariffs on US fish for sale to the domestic market in the country. 

The company already has a branded pollock fish finger product in Chinese retailer Yonghui Superstores, which is being produced in its joint venture plant in Weihai, Jeff Welbourn, who heads up Trident’s China business, told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
NOV 123:41 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Young’s showcases product range in China 

Young’s Seafood, the UK’s largest processor, exhibited a range of its frozen products on the booth of Beiyang Jiamei Seafood at the China show. 

The company had four products on show (see below), using cod, pollock and salmon, emphasizing the company’s “made in Britain” credentials. “We have not signed anything. We are out here to gauge views on the products,” Nick Munday, the company’s international sales director, told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
NOV 123:31 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Thai 2018 shrimp output could be sub-300,000t, says Siam Canadian’s Gulkin 

Thailand’s shrimp output in 2018 could even dip below 300,000 metric tons, as farmers enjoy high prices, but processors struggle. 

There is also still a tense situation between the farmers and packers over this, which Undercurrent News covered from the Thaifex show earlier in the year. 

READ MORE
NOV 96:37 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Chile’s New World Currents set to double China salmon sales in 2018 

New World Currents (NWC), a China sales joint venture between a group of Chilean salmon farmers, is set to double its sales into the market in 2018, said its chairman. 

In 2018, NWC expects to export 40,000-50,000 metric tons to China, up from around 25,000t-26,000t in 2017, said NWC’s Eduardo Goycoolea, the former sales director of Blumar and a sector veteran. 

READ MORE
NOV 96:33 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Cooke aims to sell Uruguay red crab in China 

True North Seafood, the sales arm for the Cooke group of companies, is exhibiting red crab from Uruguay in China for the first time. 

Cooke is already selling the crab, which is caught and frozen-at-sea by two company vessels, in Europe and the US, Conne Huang, its marketing manager for emerging markets, told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
NOV 91:34 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
CIMC Raffles building offshore pens to farm Japanese sea bass, puffer fish

CIMC Blue, a subsidiary of one of China’s largest shipbuilders, CIMC Raffles, is currently building two offshore pens which will be used to farm black fish, yellow fish, Japanese sea bass and puffer fish in the Yellow Sea.

The first is a CNY 40 million ($5.78m), 66 meters by 66m offshore pen which will be installed three kilometers off the coast of Long Island near Yantai city, Shandong province. Volume capacity of the pen is 60,000 cubic meters and Chinese firm Changdao Hongxiang plans to farm black fish and yellow fish (Hexagrammos otakii), Michelle Wang Ming, account manager at CIMC Blue told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
NOV 912:57 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Large-sized illex tubes scarce but loligo prices lower

Those willing to brave the market for large, Chinese-processed tubes of Argentine shortfin squid, Illex argentinus, should expect to pay “no less than $6,000 [per metric ton]”, Lian Guochen, co-founder and vice president at Huacai Technology Beijing told Undercurrent News.

That’s if they can find a Chinese processor with stock, he said; currently “nobody has any”. Stocks of Japanese flying squid, Todarodes pacificus, are also low. 

READ MORE
NOV 86:25 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
First steel cut for Nordlaks’ Havfarm

A steel cutting ceremony at Yantai shipyard in China has formally marked the start of construction of Nordlaks’ Havfarm, a 385-meter floating barge which will farm Atlantic salmon off the coast of Norway.

The ceremony on Tuesday (Oct. 7) was attended by executives from the Norwegian salmon farmer and shipyard owner CIMC Raffles, Michelle Wang Ming, key account manager at CIMC Blue told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
NOV 86:19 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Japanese scallop prices under pressure 

Prices for Japanese yesso scallops could face more downward pressure with this year’s harvest in Hokkaido, Japan, expected to be larger than last year’s, said Saiduke Yamamoto, general manager of international business at Japan’s Nippon Suisan Kaisha. 

Last year Hokkaido’s yesso scallop harvest came in at 203,276 metric tons (raw material), a three-year high, according to Japanese figures. This year’s harvest from August to October is expected to be “slightly bigger”, Yamamoto told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
NOV 87:39 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
CAPPMA chief hopes FTA with Norway coming in ‘near future’ 

Cui He, the head of the China Aquatic Product Processing and Marketing Alliance, said he hopes to see a free trade agreement (FTA) with Norway soon. 

He said he hopes relations with Norway and China will be “deepened and further expended” in the future. “We have a free trade agreement with Iceland and we hope will soon sign one with Norway. In the near future, we will have a result,” he said, during the Sino-Nordic Seafood Summit, held during the China expo. 

READ MORE
NOV 87:29 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Norway’s Salmon Evolution aims for 30,000t from land-based farm 

Norwegian firm Salmon Evolution is planning a 30,000-metric-ton land-based salmon farm in the middle of the country, Ingjarl Skarvoy, the company’s managing director. 

The company aims to hit this level in the next three-four years, said Skarvoy, at the Sino-Nordic Seafood Forum. Salmon Evolution will focus on the European market, but is also looking to China, hence why Skarvoy is at the forum. 

READ MORE
NOV 86:49 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
Clearwater launches Chinese brand in Qingdao to get closer to customers

Canadian fishing firm Clearwater Seafoods said the launch of its Chinese brand will bring it closer to customers in the company’s number one export market.

Clearwater took a leaf out of BMW and Coca-Cola’s book by choosing a different name in Chinese; BMW is called Treasure Force and Coca-Cola, Delicious Happiness in Chinese. 

READ MORE
NOV 86:39 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
Bakkafrost taking a balanced view to China growth 

Bakkafrost, the largest salmon farmer in the Faroe Islands, is taking a balanced approach to growth in the Chinese market, marketing manager Poul Jacobsen said. 

The Faroese company has a strategy to sell 25% of its total production between North America, Western Europe, Eastern Europe and Asian markets, Jacobsen said. 

READ MORE
NOV 83:58 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
New BioMar, Tongwei plant to feed China’s salmon farm startups 

Part of the business for a new feed plant from the joint venture between Denmark’s BioMar Group and China’s Tongwei Group will be to feed the numerous salmon farming projects planned in the northeast of the country. 

The joint venture plant in Wuxi, near Shanghai, is doing test runs and the partners are waiting for regulatory approval before full production can start later this year, Henrik Aarestrup, vice president of emerging markets for BioMar, told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
NOV 83:21 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Pacific Andes signs cooperation agreement with Alibaba’s Win-Chain

Seafood giant Pacific Andes has signed an agreement to supply seafood to Alibaba Group subsidiary Win-Chain, a global food sourcing platform.

On Wednesday, Pacific Andes announced it will supply frozen Argentine red shrimp, Alaskan pollock, salmon, Greenland halibut, and king crab through Win-Chain, which uses blockchain technology to track food products in the supply chain. Seafood will be processed at Pacific Andes’ 60,000-metric-ton-capacity Hongdao plant close to Qingdao. 

READ MORE
NOV 82:41 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
NRS exec: Regulation, fish size hold back Norway salmon sales to China

Norway might be increasing salmon sales to China, but the development is being held back by red tape. In addition, the focus on large sizes in China means Norwegian firms find it tough to produce the kind of volumes required, said Stein Martinsen, director of sales and marketing at Norway Royal Salmon. 

“The regulations in Norway and China make it quite difficult to export a lot [to China],” said Martinsen, at a the second Sino-Nordic Seafood Forum, organized by Danske Bank and the China Aquatic Product Processing and Marketing Alliance. 

READ MORE
NOV 76:15 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chang offering Sealord, Sapmer, New World Currents brands in China

 Jerry Chang’s Ocean Gala Marine Resources is offering branded products from several other major seafood companies in China, having started this model with Norway’s Leroy Seafood Group and True North Seafood Company, the sales arm of the Cooke group. 

At the show, Ocean Gala is displaying hoki from New Zealand’s Sealord Group, toothfish from Sapmer, a fishing firm based on the French Indian Ocean island of La Reunion, and salmon from New World Currents, the fast-growing joint venture for a group of Chilean salmon farmers. 

READ MORE
NOV 79:22 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
Guolian predicts shrimp market will increase to 6.5m metric tons by 2025

Zhanjiang Guolian Aquatic Products, China’s largest shrimp company, predicts global shrimp consumption will increase to 6.5 million metric tons in 2025, from 5.2m in 2020 and 4.5m in 2017, deputy general manager Wu Liqing said. 

That implies an annual compound growth rate of 4.75% a year, she said. Much of that growth will be driven by China as private urban consumption is set to increase to CNY 26.5 billion ($3.8bn) by 2022, compared with CNY 10bn in 2012. 

READ MORE
NOV 75:42 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
GlobalPez plans to sell Peruvian conger eel to Europe’s sushi market 

Spain’s GlobalPez is in talks with restaurant chains and wholesalers to start selling Peruvian eel into the European market for sushi, CEO Daniel Vera said. 

Conger eel is subject to a sustainability fishing quota since 2013 in Peru and is fished by artisanal boats, he said. 

READ MORE
NOV 75:41 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
Giant squid market hit by China overfishing, El Nino 

Peru’s catch of giant squid, Dosidicus gigas, has slumped by about 30% this year, as Chinese industrial trawlers may potentially be endangering the sustainability of the industry, according to GlobalPez CEO Daniel Vera. 

Prices for raw fillet have risen to $3.20 a kilogram, versus $2.80/kg last year, as a drop in supply weighs on prices, Vera said. 

READ MORE
NOV 73:30 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
China spooks shrimp market with arrests linked to Vietnamese trade route

Heavy restrictions on shrimp entering the Chinese market through the Vietnamese port of Hai Phong is an early talking point of the 2018 China seafood expo. 

Several arrests have been made of people connected to the Hai Phong shrimp trade. 

READ MORE
NOV 611:53 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
‘Monk who jumps the wall’ hot pot a hoot

All bets are off for who’s going to win the oddest product of the China show award: enter Oceanese Group’s ‘Monk who jumps the wall’ miniature hot pot. 

The hot pot draws on a Chinese story of a monk who catches a whiff of a neighbor’s soup and jumps over a wall to eat it. 

READ MORE
NOV 611:40 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Canada’s seafood exports to China grow 25%

China has surpassed the EU to become Canada’s second-largest seafood export market, after exports to the Asian giant rose by CAD 194 million, or 25%, to CAD 808m in value in 2017.

China now accounts for 14% of Canada’s seafood exports, according to Carrey Bonnell of Canada’s Ocean Choice International (OCI). The country’s main exports to China comprise lobster, crab, shrimp, scallops turbot, flounder and redfish. 

READ MORE
NOV 611:10 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Guolian wants to ‘dominate’ China’s crayfish market 

China’s Zhanjiang Guolian Aquatic Products sees crayfish as being a core product item in the future. 

The company is in the midst of a major crayfish processing and farming expansion plan, Li Zhong, the company’s top executive and co-founder, told Undercurrent News. “I see crayfish as being just as important as whiteleg [vannamei] shrimp in the future,” he said. 

READ MORE
NOV 68:23 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Coast sees ‘semi-farmed’ cod as part of solution to year-round supply 

More “ranching” of wild cod would be one way to guarantee year-round supply of the fish, a key for building markets, said Martin Ovrebo, deputy CEO of Coast Seafood. 

The predictability in supply of farmed salmon has been one of the drivers of the success of the fish in the market, he said, at an event in Qingdao organized by the Norwegian Seafood Council on Nov. 6. Combining wild caught cod with “semi-farmed” and farmed fish would be away to offer annual supply of the fish, said Ovrebo. 

READ MORE
NOV 66:41 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
China focus on imports brings openings, challenges for Norway 

This week, as the seafood sector descends on Qingdao for the China expo, there is a massive import show being held in Shanghai. 

The China International Import Expo – being held this week — was opened by president Xi Jinping, a sign of the government backing to the drive to increase imports. 

READ MORE
NOV 66:39 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
Ocean Supreme says price premium for large salmon will increase 

Norwegian salmon supplier Ocean Supreme said the premium for salmon that weighs over 6 kilograms will increase because of strong demand from Asia. 

“The growth in consumption for big fish is substantially higher than global production,” Botholf Stolt-Nielsen, Ocean Supreme CEO, said at an event held by the Norwegian Seafood Council. 

READ MORE
NOV 66:27 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
China customs will reduce bureaucracy with change in inspections system, official says 

China will streamline the customs process as part of a shake up of the offices that handle inspections of customs, said Zhang Ming, who heads the food supervision department at Qingdao Customs. 

Seafood imports deemed as low risk will be subject to a lower ratio of inspections, Zhang said. 

READ MORE
NOV 66:23 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
Norway in a Box opens Shanghai office 

Norway in a Box, a small-scale Norwegian salmon supplier, has opened an office in Shanghai to open up a sales channel for fresh and smoked salmon, a company source said. 

The company is betting that a growing trend among Chinese consumers to try new cuisines from other parts of the world will open up opportunities.

READ MORE
NOV 66:01 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
China processor calls on Norway to grow larger, redder salmon 

Norway is aiming to sell 150,000 metric tons of salmon to China by 2025, but needs to make some changes on production, according to one buyer. 

Norway could take a big market share in China. But, they should grow salmon larger and redder to meet the demand in China,” said Joseph Xu, of Shanghai Fjord Food Co., a processor in China. 

READ MORE
NOV 65:21 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Norway aims to agree FTA with China in 2019, says official 

The next round of free trade agreement (FTA) talks between Norway and China will be after Christmas in Oslo, the capital of the former, said an official at a Norwegian Seafood Council dinner in Qingdao on Tuesday.

 Gustav Solvang, of the Norwegian embassy in Beijing, China’s capital, said the aim is to conclude an FTA in 2019. “We hope by next autumn.” 

READ MORE
NOV 64:01 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Evergreen: Chinese shrimp output up 15% in 2018

China’s vannamei shrimp output is expected to increase 15% this year to 1.25 million metric tons, up from 1.08m metric tons in 2017, said Chen Dan, chairman of Guangdong Evergreen Group. 

Chinese feed mills report a positive year for sales and therefore estimate production rose, he said at the Global Aquaculture Alliance China marketplace forum.

READ MORE
NOV 63:27 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman, Matt Craze
China MSC’s fastest growing market 

The Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) saw a 20% increase in the amount of products in the market over the last year, according to data presented during the Sustainable Seafood Summit by Nicolas Guichoux, its global commercial director. 

Although Germany and the UK are the largest markets for MSC products and are in growth, China, which is a tiny market in volume, is the fastest growing. 

READ MORE
NOV 62:58 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
Korean salmon demand surging, about to catch up with Japan 

Korean salmon demand is so high that it’s about to catch up with the size of the Japanese market, a source from a major Norwegian producer told Undercurrent News. 

The market has been growing between 20% and 30% a year for the last five years and shows no signs of slowing down, the source said at an event held by the Norwegian Seafood Council in Qingdao, China. 

READ MORE
NOV 62:40 AM GMT
By Matt Craze
Seafoodnorway plans to sell smoked salmon, oil capsules to Chinese market

Seafoodnorway is preparing to launch sales in China, according to CEO Morten Jakobsen. 

Seafoodnorway set up a stand at a trade fair organized by the Norwegian Seafood Council on the sidelines of the China Fisheries & Seafood Expo in Qingdao. 

READ MORE
NOV 62:27 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
China haddock buyers in ‘waiting mode’ over US tariffs 

Chinese processors focused on the US have stopped buying haddock, due to the introduction of 10% tariffs in September, a source with a Norwegian supplier told Undercurrent News. 

“They are in waiting mode, to see what happens,” he said. The prices for headed and gutted (H&G) haddock have been hovering around $3,400-$3,500 per-metric-ton for the past few months. 

READ MORE
NOV 612:23 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
WWF develops seafood sustainability app for Chinese consumers

World Wildlife Fund for Nature has launched a seafood sustainability traffic light system for Chinese consumers. 

Around 50 species of the most popular seafood species are listed in the guide. Many of the species labelled sustainable (green) are farmed freshwater species from China fed largely fish-free diets.

READ MORE
NOV 612:08 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China completes first pilot of fishing quota for marine species

China’s first pilot total allowable catch (TAC) for a marine species was undertaken for swimming crab off the coast of Zhejiang province.

The TAC was set at 3,200 metric tons for a 2,300-square-kilometer area in the East China Sea, according to Zhu Wenbin, deputy director at Zhejiang Marine Fisheries Research Institute.

READ MORE
NOV 511:58 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
CAPPMA: Decrease in freshwater surface area used to farm fish in China

China used less freshwater surface area to farm fish in 2016, according to data presented by Cui He, president of the China Aquatic Products Processing Marketing Association. 

Freshwater surface area used to farm fish in traditional ponds in China decreased by 8.5% to 215,500 hectares in 2016, according to Cui. It followed a smaller decline in 2015. 

READ MORE
NOV 510:38 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Russian pollock fillet, mince block output set to almost triple by 2025

As Russia’s pollock quota comes down over the next few years, the output of fillets, blocks and mince are set to rocket. 

By 2025, the output of fillets, blocks and mince is set to hit 224,000 metric tons, compared to 79,000t in 2018, said Alexey Buglak, vice-president of the Russian Pollock Catchers Association (PCA). 

READ MORE
NOV 510:34 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Iceland gov’t representative in China: We learned the hard way on sustainability 

“We learned the hard way” on the need for sustainable fisheries, said Sveinn Kjartan Einarsson, first secretary for Iceland’s embassy in China. 

Speaking at the annual Sustainable Seafood Forum, Einarsson told the audience that the crash in the country’s herring stock in the late 1970s led to the development of the ITQ approach. 

READ MORE

title: Fuzhou aquaculture show: Chinese firm sells 2,500 USSEC-designed in-pond raceway units in 2017
content:
FUZHOU, China -- This year's Global Aquaculture Summit and Asia-Pacific Aquaculture Expo 2018 are being held in Fuzhou, China. 

The summit is held from May 31-June 1, with the expo following from June 1-3. Both events are primarily attended by Chinese aquaculturists, government officials and seafood companies, but international speakers also will be present. 

Auto updates: On
JUN 57:31 AM GMT
Chinese firm sells 2,500 USSEC-designed in-pond raceway units in 2017

A Chinese manufacturer selling US Soybean Export Council (USSEC)-designed in-pond raceway systems sold 2,500 units in China last year.

At the Asia-Pacific Aquaculture Expo 2018, Suzhou Dingxing Swan Aquatool sales manager Wang Ting told Undercurrent News her company is selling and installing units across the country virtually every day.

READ MORE
JUN 46:33 PM GMT
$80m ‘nuclear breeding center’ would benefit China’s shrimp sector

A director at the Chinese Academy of Fisheries Science (CAFS) said on his wish-list is a CNY 500 million ($77m) ‘nuclear breeding center’ for shrimp. 

Kong Jie, deputy director general of Yellow Sea Fisheries Research Institute, CAFS, said such a breeding center would allow China to reduce its reliance on imported broodstock (see post below), and build a more healthy shrimp sector.   

READ MORE
JUN 45:35 PM GMT
CNFC: Antarctic krill production potential 60,000-100,000t 

Antarctic krill catch potential is 60,000-100,000 metric tons annually, according to a presentation by Wei Yuting of China National Fisheries Corporation (also known as CNFC Overseas Fisheries), a large state-owned fishing company.  

Wei did not state what annual catch is currently, but said the krill biomass in the Antarctic is 650,000-1.0 million metric tons. 

READ MORE
JUN 36:19 PM GMT
Belt and Road initiative offers ‘unprecedented’ opportunities for fishing sector

China’s Belt and Road initiative has brought “unprecedented ” opportunities for the world’s fishing sector, Gu Webing, director of Division of Treaty and Regulations, Department of International Cooperation, Ministry of Agriculture, said.

As of 2016, China has made agriculture investments in 105 regions worth CNY 180 billion ($28bn), said Gu. 

READ MORE
JUN 34:57 PM GMT
NSC: China will ‘definitely’ be Norway’s largest market for seafood by 2030

Sigmund Bjorgo, director of the Norwegian Seafood Council in China, reckons China will become Norway’s largest market possibly by 2025, and “definitely by 2030”.

“It’s not a discussion is whether China will become Norway’s largest market, it’s a question of when,” he said.

READ MORE
JUN 34:56 PM GMT
China’s frozen seafood imports double as consumption habits change

By Hu Luyi


China’s frozen seafood imports have doubled over the past decade, said Cui He, president of the China Aquatic Products Processing and Marketing Alliance.

READ MORE
JUN 34:55 PM GMT
FAO: Value of seafood trade greater than combined trade of pork, beef, poultry 

The value of international seafood trade is greater than the global trade value of beef, pork and poultry combined.

Marcio Castro de Souza, senior fishery officer at the Food and Agriculture Organization, presented the striking finding at the Third Global Frozen Seafood Industry Conference.

READ MORE
JUN 34:41 PM GMT
Chinese gov’t ‘majorly’ supports offshore aquaculture

China is jumping aboard with offshore mariculture judging by several presentations at the Fuzhou show.

Wang Lumin, deputy director of East China Sea Fisheries Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Fisheries Science, said the Chinese government “majorly” supports deep sea aquaculture. 

READ MORE
JUN 36:50 AM GMT
China cooperating with ASEAN countries in aquaculture, maritime research

China is sharing its body of aquaculture and marimtime research and expertise with ASEAN countries as part of its “Maritime Silk Road” initiative. 

He Jianguo, chief scientist of Modern Shrimp and Crab Industry Technology Research System, said China has 140 aquaculture and maritime-related research institutions at provincial level or above, including 83 colleges and universities, four Chinese academies of sciences, 13 Chinese academies of fisheries sciences, one state oceanic administration and 39 provincial research institutes.

READ MORE
JUN 28:59 AM GMT
China exporting its aquaculture expertise abroad

China is no longer just a supplier of farmed fish, but a supplier of the means to produce farmed fish, particularly in Southeast Asia, Africa and the Middle East, said Chen Dan, CEO of Evergreen Group.

Gone are the days when China’s largest firms were satisfied just loading containers with fish and shipping it off somewhere; today greater growth potential lies in undertaking aquaculture projects abroad. 

READ MORE
JUN 15:53 PM GMT
Prices for aquatic feed ingredients down but volatile

Prices for key ingredients used in aquatic feed are down but volatile, Steve Hart, vice president of Global Aquaculture Alliance, said.

Prices for fishmeal — the most expensive component in aquatic feed — have fallen in recent months, while rices for US soybeans — the biggest component by volume — have also recently fallen (see graphs below).

READ MORE
JUN 13:41 AM GMT
American Penaid and Syaqua achieve shrimp broodstock breakthrough in China

American Penaid (API) and Syaqua have surged to become China’s second and third largest suppliers of shrimp broodstock.

Data presented by Kong Jie, deputy director general of Yellow Sea Fisheries Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Fisheries Science, shows in 2016, API and Syaqua supplied just 1% and 6% of China’s imported broodstock respectively.

READ MORE
JUN 13:00 AM GMT
CAPPMA: $3.6bn worth of shrimp imported by China in 2017

China’s top seafood industry association estimates $3.6 billion worth of shrimp was imported by China in 2017.

Imported volumes amounted to approximately 400,000 metric tons of shrimp, according to the China Aquatic Products Processing and Marketing Alliance (CAPPMA).

READ MORE
MAY 319:35 PM GMT
Less than 5% of Chinese aquaculture production insured

Less than 5% of Chinese aquaculture farmers are insured against natural disasters in China, far less than the 70% coverage for China’s agricultural sector as a whole.

This is according to Yang Bin, secretary general of China Fishery Mutual Insurance (CFMI), who is trying to encourage Chinese aquaculture farmers to take out insurance policies.

READ MORE
MAY 316:18 AM GMT
China looks to new models of aquaculture production

China wants to improve on the humble freshwater pond with “comprehensive farming”, offshore aquaculture and aquaponics, a top official said. 

Farming species such as crab, soft-shelled turtles and crayfish in paddy fields, alongside rice, is one way to increase yields, said Hu Honglang, deputy director general of the China National Fisheries Technology Extension Center and China Society of Fisheries, Ministry of Agriculture.

READ MORE
MAY 313:49 AM GMT
Official: Environmental rules pressuring Chinese aquaculture production

Strict environmental law and enforcement were the “main reasons” for a decline in aquaculture production area in China in 2016, according to Li Shumin, deputy director of the Bureau of Fisheries and Fisheries Law Enforcement, Ministry of Agriculture. 

In 2016, aquaculture production area in China decreased by 1.41% to 8.34 million hectares (see photo 2). 

READ MORE
MAY 3010:31 PM GMT
US Soybean Export Council promotes raceway system in China

As part of its promotional activities in China,  the US Soybean Export Council (USSEC) is offering advice and support for Chinese farmers wanting to install its In-Pond Raceway Sytem (IRS) system. 

To help boost demand and improve customer relations in China — the US’s largest export market for soybeans, with significant quantities used in aquatic feed — USSEC promotes IRS systems developed to increase yields and protect the environment.

READ MORE

Contact the author louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com

title: Chatham House IUU Forum: IUU experts divided on transhipment
content:
Undercurrent News is reporting live from the 11th International Forum on illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing in London, UK.

The forum brings together over 100 leading policymakers, researchers, industry representatives and civil society groups from across the world to discuss the latest initiatives, regulations and research in the area of fisheries governance and trade in illegal fish products, according to the organizer, research body Chatham House

Topics for this year's forum will include traceability, enforcement and sanctions, transparency and the links between IUU fishing and slavery at sea, amongst others.

Auto updates: On
MAY 77:15 AM GMT
IUU experts divided on how to tackle transhipment

There is still no consensus on how to tackle IUU related to transhipment, with many of the solutions and counter-solutions raised at last year’s IUU Forum cropping up again this year.

Transhipment involves the transfer of fish from one ship to another, often on the high seas. The purpose is to allow fishing vessels to transfer fish to refrigerator frigates, also known as reefer vessels, which then transport the cargo back to port.

READ MORE
MAY 76:56 AM GMT
More measures taken to protect observer safety

More measures are being taken to protect the safety of observers on fishing vessels.

Observers who monitor fishing on fishing vessels can find themselves in a difficult spot when their work interferes with the goals of fishermen and vessel owners. In 2015, Keith Davis, a fishing observer, disappeared while onboard a Panama-flagged reefer vessel, the Victoria 168, while it was fishing in the Pacific.

READ MORE
MAY 76:29 AM GMT
Public VMS data would reveal far more about world fishing activities

Tech firm SkyTruth showed how Indonesia’s decision to make vessel monitoring system (VMS) data public helped light up a map of the world’s fishing vessels. 

Currently there are two methods of tracking vessels; automatic identification system (AIS) — which is a communications system — and VMS signals. However, while AIS data is public, VMS data is often not. 

READ MORE
MAY 76:11 AM GMT
Tech firm uses machine learning to uncover transhipment’s secrets

Tech firm SkyTruth is tracking where transhipment occurs in the world’s oceans using machine learning and satellite imagery.

The firm tracks fishing vessels using their automatic identification system (AIS) and vessel monitoring system (VMS) signals, to analyse when and where vessels cross paths. Using machine learning, it can establish the likelihood the encounter involved transhipment.

READ MORE
MAY 73:40 AM GMT
Central American states step up fight against IUU fishing

Central American nations have established a governance system to monitor and fight illegal fishing. 

However, additional capacity building, harmonization of regulation among countries, further controls on final products and veda periods, and improvement of traceability in the supply chain are still needed in the region.

READ MORE
MAY 412:30 PM GMT
More transparency needed in EU IUU control regulation 

IUU experts and policy analysts taking part in an ‘ask the audience’ session during the IUU Forum believe the EU’s control regulation on IUU leaves much to be desired.

Grouped into tables, after being given 15 minutes to discuss among themselves the pros and cons of the regulation, many agreed that transparency and consistency are what could be most improved, from sanctions to the EU’s carding system.

READ MORE
MAY 411:27 AM GMT
IPNLF improves tuna traceability in the Maldives with new app

The International Pole and Line Foundation (IPNLF) is improving traceability of tuna fishing in the Maldives with a new application, Ali Manzoom, software engineer at IPNLF, said. 

The new electronic logbook application allows to track tuna stocks through the vessels’ mobile network and to cross-check data provided by different parties. 

READ MORE
MAY 410:03 AM GMT
New England Seafood’s approach on responsible sourcing 

New England Seafood, the UK’s second largest fish and seafood importer, is working to make the supply chain more transparent, the firm’s head of sustainability, Cassie Leisk, said.

The firm, which imports tuna, salmon and bass and bream, among other species, works with NGOs partners as well as with supplying countries to “overcome challenges”, once having identified ares that need improvement in terms of traceability.

READ MORE
MAY 46:39 AM GMT
IMO to update training standards for fishing vessels staff

The international maritime organization (IMO) is working to an updated version of the international convention on standards of training, certification and watch keeping for fishing vessels personnel, which was ratified in 1995. 

It is an “extremely important issue”, Sandra Rita Allnut, head of marine technology and GBS at the International maritime organization, said.
However, the process to revise the convention might take “a few years”, Allnut noted. 

READ MORE
MAY 46:27 AM GMT
New project targets global exchange of seafood catch/trade data

The Seafood Alliance for Legality and Traceability (SALT) is a new alliance for global exchange and action to promote legal and sustainable fisheries through improved transparency in seafood supply chains.

Speaking at the IUU Forum, Mark Richardson, senior project director at FishWise, the American non-profit consultancy FishWise, which launched the project, said SALT aims to bring together the seafood industry, governments and NGOs. 

READ MORE
MAY 31:44 PM GMT
Fish-i: Fishing violations tip of the IUU iceberg

Just 13% of illegal activities by industrial fishing companies fishing off the Horn of Africa are related to violations of fishing regulations, according to Sandy Davies, co-founder of Stop Illegal Fishing and Fish-i Africa Taskforce. 

80% are deliberate enabling crimes, such as forgery, fraud, or corruption, she said.

READ MORE
MAY 312:29 PM GMT
UNODC: Embedded advisors aid West Africa, Horn of Africa maritime security  

One of the main successes of the UN’s Global Maritime Crime Program is having foreign mentors or advisors embedded in institutions in countries with weak maritime security, according to a program director. 

The program is the work of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), explained Siri Bjune, program director at UNODC.

READ MORE
MAY 39:50 AM GMT
Norwegian pension fund: Investigating IUU record of seafood companies in portfolio ‘very challenging’

The Norwegian government pension fund is one of few institutional funds — possibly even the only one — which has conducted its own investigation of the IUU track record of seafood companies in its portfolio, according to Hilde Jervan, chief advisor of Council on Ethics for the fund.

But, Jervan warned that doing so was a “huge challenge”; it requires significant effort, resources, and direct contact with and assistance from seafood companies.

READ MORE
MAY 38:23 AM GMT
Vessels involved in IUU often insured

Insurers need to be aware of what the vessels they insure are up to, said Dana Miller, marine scientist at international ocean conservation and advocacy organization Oceana.


This is because many vessels involved in IUU are insured, according to research by the University of British Columbia. This included the vessel Tiantai, a known offender of IUU.

READ MORE
MAY 37:58 AM GMT
Consultant: Creditors have close links with seafood companies

Kees Lankester, an independent consultant working with financiers involved with maritime investments, showed several diagrams to illustrate how just three banks in Japan are connected with many Japanese seafood companies, through loans and credit.

He said these banks will need a lot of information about these seafood companies, in order to agree a loan. This information is hugely valuable.

READ MORE
MAY 36:44 AM GMT
IUU the sixth-largest global crime

IUU fishing is the sixth-largest crime in the world, according to a recent study by Global Financial Integrity. 

The study estimates IUU is worth up to $30 billion a year (higher than RUSI’s estimate, see below). 

READ MORE
MAY 36:34 AM GMT
Follow the money

Cathy Haenlein — senior research fellow, serious and organized crime at Royal United Services Institute for Defence and Security Studies (RUSI) — says her organization “always focuses on where the money flows”. 

IUU involves artisanal fishing, but it also involves transnational organized crime, she said, with profits funneled around the world through money laundering.

READ MORE
MAY 36:26 AM GMT
Money, control and technology

This year’s two-day event at Chatham House, the home of the renowned think-tank of the same name, will cover some of the key issues relating to IUU around the world and how to combat it. 

Lectures and panel discussions will be by some of the leading experts in the field. 

READ MORE

title: Chile fishermen’s protest blog: Protests over as last holdouts agree to deal
content:
A prolonged blockade of highways in southern Chile has cut off the salmon industry from its main markets, adding another Chilean supply disruption to world markets.

The protests could mean salmon farmers, already incurring losses from fish killed by algal bloom, or red tide, earlier this year, are racking up losses of $10 million a day and many can’t sell their harvest to Brazil and the US.

Fishermen are protesting over the compensation payments offered by the government to tide them over while a ban exists on fishing after toxins were found that are associated with red tide.

Some fishermen have suggested the salmon farmers started the problem in March by discarding dead fish into the sea though scientists dispute this assertion.

Glenn Cooke, CEO of Cooke Aquaculture, called on the Chilean government to deal with the protest, which is damaging the country's reputation.

Auto updates: On
MAY 208:12 AM GMT
Chile fishermen protests over as government agrees deal with last community 

The blockade that has kept Chile salmon exports on the ground for more than two weeks is over as the government reached an agreement with a last holdout group of fishermen. 

The fishermen of Ancud on the island of Chiloe, who had blocked roads leaving the island, have agreed to a compensation payment while a ban on seafood extraction lasts because of red tide sweeping the coastline, according to the economy ministry. 

READ MORE
MAY 1912:56 AM GMT
Key salmon processing town to end protests 

Fishermen in the town of Quellon, a key area for the salmon industry with several processing plants, signed an agreement with the government on May 18 to end protests and lift blockades. 

 Economy Minister Luis Felipe Cespedes is still negotiating an agreement with fishermen in the northern city of Ancud where they have blocked the only road that connects the island with the mainland via a ferry crossing, newspaper El Mercurio reported.  

READ MORE
MAY 183:18 PM GMT
SalmonChile head Sandoval says blockades starting to ease 

Chile’s salmon farmers are beginning to regain access to some processing plants as fishermen from areas of Chiloe island and the southern mainland reached agreements with the government, SalmonChile head Felipe Sandoval told radio station Agricultura. 

The town of Quellon on the south coast of the island, where several salmon processing plants are located, is still cut off by the protests, Sandoval said. 

READ MORE
MAY 1810:53 AM GMT
Chile scientists urge government to adopt red tide monitoring plan 

A commission of scientists who are investigating the causes of the red tide that has swept the Chilean coastline urged the government to dedicate more resources to monitoring equipment and other strategies to warn local communities, newspaper El Mercurio reported. 

Chile needs an alerting system to advise local communities of potential outbreaks, Monica Vasquez, a biologist of Chile’s Catholic University and a spokesperson for the commission told the newspaper. Chile should import monitoring equipment from Japan and teach detection techniques to fishermen, she said. 

READ MORE
MAY 183:06 AM GMT
Chile to investigate accusations of salmon dumping  

Chilean authorities are investigating the country’s salmon-farming industry in light of the algal bloom, reports The Guardian.

Scientists attribute the unusually potent and widespread algal bloom to unseasonably warm water temperatures as a result of the El Nino weather phenomenon.

READ MORE
MAY 1710:07 PM GMT
SalmonChile says farmers have lost $120m in sales 

Chile’s salmon farmers have lost about $120 million in lost sales to the US and other key markets because of the fishermen’s protests that are now in their third week, SalmonChile director Felipe Manterola said. 

There will also be some material damage to report once the blockades end, Manterola said in an interview. 

READ MORE
MAY 174:05 PM GMT
Chile blockades remain as fishermen hold firm over payments

Chiloe’s fishermen maintained key roadblocks to press for higher compensation from the government as the protests entered a third week.

Fishermen in Ancud, one of the island’s main towns located near the only road access point the mainland, will maintain blockades until a definitive agreement is reached, union leader Julio Cardenas told radio station Agricultura. 

READ MORE
MAY 179:42 AM GMT
Chile salmon farmers risk losing 4,000t of fish as blockades linger 

Chile’s salmon farmers have about 800,000 of fish, or 4,000 metric tons, waiting to be processed at plants that might perish if the Chiloe blockades aren’t lifted soon, said SalmonChile chief Felipe Sandoval. 

Fish waiting to be processed shouldn’t be held more than a week in the storage pools, Sandoval told Diario Financiero. Fish held in sea cages are also suffering from a lack of oxygen and feed, he said. 

READ MORE
MAY 164:52 PM GMT
Chile plans further talks with Chiloe fishermen to clear blockades 

Chile economy minister Luis Felipe Cespedes will meet with fishermen in holdout communities to clear road blockades that have left the island of Chiloe cut off for two weeks. 

The government achieved a breakthrough with the Maullin fishermen’s union that has allowed fuel shipments to enter the island. 

READ MORE
MAY 164:43 PM GMT
Chile salmon farmers continue job cuts during protests 

Chile’s salmon industry has continued to shed jobs throughout two weeks of being blocked from its main markets because of a fishermen’s strike. 

About 800 jobs were cut by Cultivos Toralla and Expromar Congelados del Mar, according to radio station Bio Bio, citing union officials and members of Chile’s work inspectorate. 

READ MORE
MAY 168:25 AM GMT
Chile government reaches partial agreement with workers 

Chile’s government reached an agreement with a group of fishermen on the island of Chiloe, newspapers and radio stations reported. 

The government needs to reach an agreement with other key fishing syndicates in the towns of Ancud and Quellon to totally lift the blockade, according to radio station Cooperativa. 

READ MORE
MAY 134:27 PM GMT
Chile salmon price rising on protests blocking shipments 

Some trim D fillets FOB Miami have been sold at between $6 to $6.20 a pound in the US market, said a source at a Chilean-based producer. 

Very little Chilean product is being sold on the spot market, with the few companies able to export preferring to honor fixed contracts, the source said. 

READ MORE
MAY 134:10 PM GMT
Chile’s salmon workers call on fishermen, government to reach agreement

Chile’s salmon industry workers called on the government to reach an agreement with the fishermen blocking Chiloe Island amid fears companies will shed more jobs. 

The salmon in production centers around the island of Chiloe are beginning to die because of a lack of feed, the workers said in a May 13 statement.

READ MORE
MAY 1311:03 AM GMT
Chile’s northern fishermen table claims to government amid Chiloe protests 

Chilean fishermen in the northern Atacama Desert have united to issue a series of demands to the government as it seeks to end the 11-day protest in the south of the country.  

Among the demands, the northern fishermen want to establish a working group to discuss quotas and modifications to Chile’s fishing laws amid diminishing stocks and disruptions to fishing caused by El Nino weather pattern. 

READ MORE
MAY 1310:53 AM GMT
Chile sees string of solidarity protests in support of Chiloe fishermen 

A number of violent protests took place across the country including in port cities Concepcion and Valparaiso to support the Chiloe fishermen who are demanding higher compensation from the government because of a ban on fishing, according to radio station Bio Bio. 

There were 44 arrests in Puerto Montt in protests and another four in Valparaiso. 

READ MORE
MAY 138:05 AM GMT
Chilean salmon farmers respond to regulator on losses amid protests

Some Chilean salmon farmers responded to the Chilean securities regulator requesting information on losses sustained since the fishermen’s strike began on May 2. 

The protests will “very possibly” have a material impact the company’s production and financial results, Multiexport Foods CEO Andres Lyon said in a statement. The company’s reputation is being damaged by the inability to serve its customers, he said. 

READ MORE
MAY 137:18 AM GMT
Chile commerce chamber details losses sustained by salmon industry 

Salmon farmers have registered more than $100 million in lost sales and the fishermen’s strike has hurt the regional economy including a loss of tourism revenue that is also damaging the country’s image overseas, Ricardo Mewes, head of Chile’s national chamber of commerce, told El Mercurio newspaper.

Marine Harvest CEO Alf-Helge Aarskog said the industry is paying the price for a quarrel that fishermen have with the government in a separate interview with the newspaper. 

READ MORE
MAY 121:58 PM GMT
Marine Harvest sees global salmon shortfall arising from Chile production setbacks

Chile’s salmon supply in 2016 will shrink between 19% and 23%, creating a global shortage of salmon, Marine Harvest CEO Alf-Helge Aarskog said on a call with analysts.

Marine Harvest’s supply from Chile will decline 16,000 metric tons this year, Aarskog said. The effect of algal bloom will continue into 2016 because of reduced biomass, he said. Aarskog didn’t refer to the effect of the fishermen’s protests on Chilean supply in the call.

READ MORE
MAY 1211:44 AM GMT
Chileans living in Sweden hold solidarity protests with Chiloe fishermen

Chileans living as far away as Sweden held anti-government demonstrations in support of the Chiloe fishermen amid the arrival of Chilean President Michelle Bachelet, who is currently on a tour of Europe. 

Chileans in Stockholm and Gothenburg held up signs in support of the fishermen who have cut off the island of Chiloe for the past 10 days to demand higher compensation payments while a ban on fishing exists. Sweden has a sizable Chilean community. 

READ MORE
MAY 1211:00 AM GMT
Chiloe comes to a standstill amid fishermen’s protest

The island where two-thirds of Chile’s salmon processing capacity is based has ground to a halt amid a fishermen’s strike that started earlier this month, newspaper Diario Financiero reported. 

Construction workers have stopped work on infrastructure and water projects because of the lack of fuel affecting transportation on the island, the newspaper said. The island is also running out of food, it said. 

READ MORE
MAY 1210:27 AM GMT
Chilean salmon prices surge with limited supplies available

The price of head-on, gutted salmon for delivery in Puerto Montt has shot up to between $10 and $11 a kilo with the limited amount of fish available due to the protests by fishermen that are blocking processing plants, an industry source said. 

The producers are taking advantage of the current situation by hiking up prices, instead of thinking about preserving market share versus other salmon producing nations in the world, the source said. 

READ MORE
MAY 1111:31 PM GMT
Chile’s salmon industry producing at 30% capacity amid protests 

Only a third of Chile’s salmon processing plants are operating and delivering products to the US and Brazil, according to a source at a major salmon farmer. 

Chile’s major salmon farmers are selling the little produce they have to their long-term supply contracts, meaning there is a lack of spot market sales. There is a shortage of salmon in Brazilian and US markets and if purchasers in those countries turn to Norwegian supplies, the consequences will be disastrous for Chile, the source said. 

READ MORE
MAY 1111:17 PM GMT
Australis outlines losses caused by fishermen’s protests 

Australis Seafoods has $2 million worth of salmon held in storage units waiting to be processed that it can’t export because of the blockades, the company said in statement to the Chilean regulator. 

Australis has lost about $3m in lost sales opportunities, while 600,000 smolt worth $1m stuck in truck blockades in southern Chile might perish. The company said fixed costs during the protests have amounted to $300,000. 

READ MORE
MAY 118:10 PM GMT
Union: Prolonging strike hurts Chile’s workers

The head of a 3,000-member union active in southern Chile believes that continuing the fishermen’s strike, which has effectively crippled transportation networks on Chiloe Island, will only hurt the region’s workers.

In a statement from Alejandro Santibáñez, the president of the National Confederation of Workers from the South, said that the situation can affect employment in the short run and that the shortage of basic goods on the island is worrying.

READ MORE
MAY 114:10 PM GMT
Chilean red tide spreads north to Los Rios region

Chilean officials have discovered that the toxicity found in the sea of Los Lagos region has spread north to Los Rios region. 

Health minister Carmen Castillo has declared an environmental catastrophe in Los Rios and has instructed local officials to ban fishing.

READ MORE
MAY 113:37 PM GMT
SalmonChile rules out theory that dead salmon intoxicated seafood on Chile’s coast 

SalmonChile, the representative body of Chile’s salmon industry, ruled out a theory that the throwing of dead fish into the sea resulted in the high levels of toxins in coastal waters that resulted in a ban on fishing and ensuing protests by blockades by fishermen. 

The association cited a study by Chile’s Marine Biologists College that ruled out the theory circulating in Chile that decomposing salmon killed by algal blooms in March were to blame for later intoxication of crustaceans in Chile’s southern coastal waters. 

READ MORE
MAY 112:06 PM GMT
Chiloe business leaders call on fishermen to raise blockades on trucks carrying food and gas 

The chambers of commerce of Ancud and Castro, the two main towns on the island of Chiloe, called on fishermen to lift blockades to let basic items such as food and gas reach the island’s inhabitants, according to a statement. 

The losses after several days of the protest, which has cut off the island of Chiloe from the mainland of Chile, have resulted in millions of lost business from salmon farming and tourism, said Julio Candia, the head of Castro’s chamber of commerce. 

READ MORE
MAY 1111:07 AM GMT
Gov’t willing to hold talks with fishermen, start payments 

Chile’s government is willing to hold talks with the fishermen and has started to payments to the families affected by the red tide because they are in need, Luis Felipe Cespedes, economy minister, told radio station DigitalFMChile.

Protestors cut off roads to Calbuco, a town near Puerto Montt where Australis Seafoods, Camanchaca and Marine Harvest have processing plants, according to a report by radio station Bio Bio.

READ MORE
MAY 1111:05 AM GMT
SalmonChile: Toxins not caused by dead salmon 

Felipe Sandoval, head of producers’ association SalmonChile, ruled out the theory that throwing dead into the sea accounts for the appearance of the toxins that brought about the ban on seafood extraction, according to television channel Tele13.

Most of the salmon that were killed by the algal blooms in March “were sent off to be turned into fishmeal”, Sandoval said.

READ MORE

title: Chile algal bloom blog: Blumar’s $8.5m loss cut to $1.1m by insurance; Industry losses equal to 12% of annual production
content:
A deadly algal bloom has hit the world's second biggest salmon producer and exporter, Chile.

More than 27 million fish have already died and the economic impact from lost production is seen soaring to $800 million.

Unusually high ocean temperatures, due in large part to the El Nino weather phenomenon, have fueled the algal bloom that has affected salmon farms operating in southern Chile. Most of the farms are in ocean enclosures or in estuaries.

Producers Marine Harvest, Australis Seafoods, Pesquera Camanchaca, Blumar Seafoods, Multiexport Foods, Cermaq Group and Empresas AquaChile have all seen some of their salmon farms affected, according to data provided by Chile's Economy Ministry and company filings with Chile's SVS securities regulator.

The latest blow to the local industry comes as Chile's salmon farmers racked up multi-million loses, as a consequence of falling Atlantic salmon prices seen throughout 2015.

Keep clicking back for the latest updates on the impact.

Auto updates: On
MAR 3012:21 PM GMT
Blumar’s $8.5m loss cut to $1.1m by insurance

Salmon farmer and fishing company Blumar’s immediate prospects for 2016 will include an estimated $1.1m net loss stemming from the recent algal bloom, the company said.

In its 2015 earnings report, the company stated it suffered an overall $8.027m loss mitigated by $6.9m in insurance compensation. The company’s Caicura center was struck by the bloom but Blumar’s 10 other centers were unaffected, it said.

READ MORE
MAR 2911:51 AM GMT
SalmonChile: Bloom losses equal to 12% of annual production

Industry group SalmonChile has announced that the recent algal bloom has officially ended, killing 27 million salmon or about 39,000 metric tons.

The losses are equal to about 12% of the industry’s annual production, the group said in a press release.

READ MORE
MAR 283:33 AM GMT
Multiexport pins algal bloom losses at $9m

Chile’s Multiexport Foods lost 45% of the biomass on farms in regions X and XI due to the impact of the algal bloom, the company said. 

In a stock exchange notice, the company said the total losses were $26.6m, but insurance means the cost on its books will be $9m.

READ MORE
MAR 2411:38 AM GMT
Chilean Navy complains to prosecutors over dead salmon

Officials from Chile’s navy have made formal complaints to the country’s prosecutors over the risk that salmon killed in the recent algal bloom could pose if they were consumed by humans.

After receiving the complaint, prosecutors dispatched a team of environmental investigators and local police to ensure that the dead salmon were properly disposed of. 

READ MORE
MAR 245:20 AM GMT
AquaChile puts algal bloom losses at $43m

Empresas AquaChile has lost $43 million due to the algal bloom, it announced in a stock exchange notice.

The company explained that there were five farm areas with affected crops: Herradura, Capera, Guar Island, Huenquillahue and Sotomo. 

READ MORE
MAR 2212:19 PM GMT
AquaChile director wants employees to pray for company
In light of a massive algal bloom that has affected Chile’s major salmon farming operations, a director of one firm is asking his employees to pray for the company, the El Mercurio newspaper reported.


Empresas AquaChile director Mario Puchi said that this is not the first time his company has confronted a challenge from nature. He expects the company to overcome but wants the support of all of the company’s employees.


“I invite all who wish to join in a chain of prayer, praying an “Our Father” or a “Hail Mary” praying for our people, our company and the industry in general, because we are sure that prayer will help us to overcome this moment,” he said.
MAR 2212:04 PM GMT
Camanchaca: ISA crisis ‘more complicated’ than algal bloom

The CEO of Chile’s Pesquera Camanchaca believes that the current algal bloom facing Chile’s salmon farms is not as complicated at the threat previously posed by the disease infectious salmon anemia (ISA), the country’s Diairo Financiero said in an interview.

CEO Ricardo Garcia Holtz told the publication that the algal bloom was “an extreme condition that nobody was prepared for”.

READ MORE
MAR 213:33 AM GMT
Trading resumes on Invermar after 23% surge

Chile’s Santiago stock exchange has resumed trading on salmon farmer and processor Invermar, after its shares surged over 23%.

The stock exchange regulator sent a letter to the company, asking if it was aware of any reason for this.

READ MORE
MAR 213:23 AM GMT
Algal bloom starting to recede

The algal bloom in Chile has started to recede along with the salmon deaths, the government said on Friday.

“What the scientists have told us is that the algae has diminished, and what we also have detected is that fish deaths have ceased,” said Jose Miguel Burgos, head of the government’s fisheries body, Sernapesca. 

READ MORE
MAR 154:22 AM GMT
Blumar estimates $8.5m loss 

Chilean salmon farmer Blumar has estimated losses of $8.5 million linked to red tide, also known as algal bloom.

The company said the phenomenon has affected the center Caicura, located in Chile’s X region for salmon farming.

READ MORE
MAR 149:23 AM GMT
AquaChile’s Verlasso production not impacted by red tide

Empresas AquaChile’s premium farmed salmon brand Verlasso has not been impacted by the algal bloom, also known as red tide, which has caused more than 100,000t in salmon motalities in Chile.

“The algae bloom in Chile has not impacted Verlasso farms or production,” the company said.  “As a precaution we will continue to test both our fish and our waters to ensure our salmon remains unaffected.”

READ MORE
MAR 144:44 AM GMT
Chile dumps 300t of dead salmon out to sea

Chile’s Fisheries and Aquaculture Service (Sernapesca) reported the Navy authorized to dump 300 metric tons of dead salmon out to sea, in a safe area established by authorities.

This is an emergency measure for the fish in advanced decomposition, which can not be used for fishmeal processing, Sernapesca said.

READ MORE
MAR 144:29 AM GMT
Court lifts AquaChile factory suspension in Puerto Montt

Empresas AquaChile will resume activities at his plant in Puerto Montt, as a court has admitted its appeal against the authorities’ decision to fine the salmon farmer.

On Mach 10, AquaChile appealed to a court of Puerto Montt after a fine over activities to overcome the ongoing algal bloom.

READ MORE
MAR 114:47 AM GMT
Cooke: Lots of upside on salmon prices 

Glenn Cooke, CEO of Cooke Aquaculture, said customers had better get ready for more expensive salmon, in the wake of the algal bloom in Chile. 

“I think the market is going to be really, really short of fish. Customers have been used to having cheap fish,” he told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
MAR 101:04 PM GMT
AquaChile appeals fine over activities to overcome algal bloom

Chilean salmon farmer Empresas AquaChile has appealed to a court of Puerto Montt after a fine over activities to overcome the ongoing algal bloom, the company reported.

Puerto Montt labor inspectors had fined AquaChile over its mortalities disposal and emergency harvest after the algal bloom, the company said in a note to Chile’s SVS securities regulator.

READ MORE
MAR 104:48 AM GMT
Algal bloom could have not been foreseen

Chile’s algal bloom could have not been foreseen as it is a “very complex natural phenomenon“, said SalmonChile’s Technological Salmon Institute (Intesal).

“To claim the industry could have foreseen the current algal bloom — both in terms of its magnitude and spread — is wrong and reflects little knowledge about the nature of the phenomenon, statistically and biologically,” Intesal said. 

READ MORE
