title: Untitled
content:
QINGDAO, China -- Undercurrent News is reporting this week live from the China Fisheries and Seafood Exposition, which is held in a venue close to Qingdao, China. 

The event runs Oct. 25-27, but the Global Seafood Alliance and the Norwegian Seafood Council are holding conferences on Oct. 24, which Undercurrent reporters are attending. Keep checking back below for updates from the show. 

Auto updates: On
OCT 278:51 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Blumar starts selling Oshen Salmon branded skin-packs in US market

Chile’s Blumar has been producing salmon in skin-packs for private label customers in the US market in a plant in Florida for a while now but has just started using its own brand, Oshen Salmon.

Blumar started selling into a couple of “small to mid-sized” retailers from the Miami plant at the end of 2022, sales director Daniel Montoya told Undercurrent News during the Qingdao seafood show.

READ MORE
OCT 278:49 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Russians see China’s live king crab market booming, frozen push next

Russian companies are seeing very strong demand in China for live king crab, with opening the market for frozen goods the next step, a top executive told Undercurrent News.

“The China market is booming for live crab,” said Dmitry Gusev, sales director for Okeanrybflot, one of Russia’s largest fishing companies, with four vessels in the Far East crab fisheries.

READ MORE
OCT 278:45 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Royal Greenland-backed Chinese importer starts Canadian snow crab retail line

Chinese importer and exporter Beiyang Jiamei Seafood Co. has used the drop in snow crab prices as an opportunity to launch a retail line using the crustacean.

Beiyang Jiamei is sourcing the snow crab for the product from multiple suppliers in Canada, including plants owned by Royal Greenland, which has a minority stake in the Chinese firm.

READ MORE
OCT 278:41 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Huge gulf in price, size between Russian, US pink salmon

The price and size gap between headed and gutted (H&G) Russian and US pink salmon is very wide, said Dmitry Gusev, sales director for Okeanrybflot, one of Russia’s largest fishing companies.

According to sources at the Qingdao show, Russian H&G prices delivered to China are under $2,000 per metric ton, with fish from the US Alaskan fishery commanding a much higher return.

READ MORE
OCT 273:53 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Peru processor invests in new plant but battles weak giant squid market

Rising costs and falling demand have squeezed profit margins for Peruvian giant squid processors like Pecepe, which recently invested $9 million in a new processing plant.

Pecepe owner Daniel Sebastia Llana told Undercurrent News the company is losing money on tentacles and wings it exports to China due to high raw material costs and weak demand. Prices for whole giant squid have soared from around PEN 1 per kilogram ($0.26/kg) in previous years to PEN 5/kg currently.

READ MORE
OCT 273:45 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Chinese pangasius market shows recovery signs in Q3

In the third quarter, Vietnam’s pangasius exports to China showed signs of recovery, according to Chen Xindong, the general manager of Octogone, Vinh Hoan Corporation’s joint venture distributor in China.

“Pangasius sales started to rebound in July, and the recovery continued throughout August and September,” Chen told Undercurrent News. 

READ MORE
OCT 2610:46 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Omani state fisheries group courts China market under new trade pact

Oman is seeking to expand exports of its seafood products to China following a recent trade agreement, sending a delegation from its state fisheries company to promote its offerings at the Qingdao Show this week.

Fisheries Development Oman (FDO), the Sultanate’s state investment arm for fisheries, is showcasing its range of fish, shrimp and other seafood. It’s part of an Omani push to grow exports under a new cooperation pact signed last month with China on seafood safety standards.

READ MORE
OCT 2610:36 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
China’s nascent pangasius farming can’t yet compete with Vietnamese imports 

The pangasius farming industry in China is still in its early stages and cannot directly compete with Vietnamese products, according to a seafood entrepreneur.

Lin Xiaowen, the general manager of Hainan Xiangtai Fishery, told Undercurrent News at the Qingdao show that his company has recently overcome challenges in pangasius farming and has explored some farming methods.

READ MORE
OCT 2610:21 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu 
Top Chinese salmon importer sees gradual market decline after strong start to 2023 

The sluggish consumer demand in China has also impacted the salmon market, especially after the National Day holiday in October, leading to a decline in total salmon consumption.

Dennis Cai, chief operating officer of Shanghai Chuner Group, a major salmon importer in the region, told Undercurrent News that demand during the National Day holiday was less than 70% of usual levels, and it worsened after the holiday. Consumers who used to eat fresh salmon have reduced their consumption frequency and shifted to frozen salmon.

READ MORE
OCT 2610:06 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Prices in China for Irish shellfish down 20% since 2019

Chinese demand for Irish shellfish has declined but it remains an essential market for Galway-based Cannemara Seafoods, according to managing director Pat Mulloy. 

The 150-year-old exporter has seen China prices fall 20% from 2019 peaks. “It’s not great in China at the moment but it’s not great anywhere, including in Europe,” Mulloy told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 269:14 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Clearwater sees China’s ‘3R’ food trend hike demand for clam meat

Canadian shellfish giant Clearwater Seafoods is seeing increased demand in China for surf clam body meat and propeller clam raw material for value-added products, an executive told Undercurrent News.

Clearwater’s flagship product in the Chinese market is the high-end, sashimi-grade Arctic surf clam, but the “3R” seafood craze in the country is driving demand for lower-value clam raw material for re-processing, said Royce Ruan, associate marketing director with the Shanghai, China office of Clearwater.

READ MORE
OCT 269:09 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Grey trade continues to be a major obstacle for pangasius importers

Cross-border trade between China and Vietnam, which avoids import tariffs and inspections, remains a headache for pangasius importers in the post-pandemic period.

At the Qingdao show, a trader, who asked not be named, told Undercurrent News that there was still a significant prevalence of “grey trading” in the pangasius market. 

READ MORE
OCT 269:01 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Chilean mussel production in 2024 expected to remain stable

In 2022, China imported 638 metric tons of mussels from Chile, with St. Andrews Smoky Delicacies supplying 470t, or 74%, said Eduardo Piccolo, the company’s marketing director.

Based on the company’s research, many Chinese consumers seek the most cost-effective products, he said. The market is struggling with a lack of consumer confidence, and the future challenge lies in developing products that consumers are willing to pay for.

READ MORE
OCT 268:50 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Best time to promote wild salmon in China

The current global surplus in wild salmon production and subdued international demand make it the perfect time to tap into China’s market for wild salmon, a top executive said.

“This year provides the optimal opportunity to promote wild salmon in China,” Deng En Tang, chairman of Dalian Rich Group, told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 264:55 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Chinese shrimp buyers ‘shopping around,’ says Ecuadorian supplier

Chinese vannamei shrimp buyers at the Qingdao show are showing interest but not placing orders, a senior executive with Ecuador’s Sociedad Nacional de Galapagos (Songa) told Undercurrent News at the end of the first day.

“The show has been very busy, a lot of interest, but little concrete business as many people are shopping around. That’s the Chinese way. By Friday [Oct. 27], everything will be solved,” he said.

READ MORE
OCT 264:16 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Mowi ready to ‘go deeper’ into China salmon market

Mowi, the world’s largest salmon farmer and the only one with processing plants in Asia, is ready to go deeper into the Chinese market after the re-opening at the start of 2023, its top sales executive told Undercurrent News.

“Post COVID, we’re seeing strong growth in China. We’re following the same strategy we take in Europe or the US, to go deeper into the market and get closer to the end user,” said Ola Brattvoll, chief operating officer for sales and marketing with the company.

READ MORE
OCT 263:59 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Norway’s fresh salmon sales to China on track to hit 40,000t record

Sales of fresh Norwegian Atlantic salmon to the Chinese market are on track to hit 40,000 metric tons (head-on, gutted, HOG) in 2023, which will be a new record.

Andreas Thorud — still the Norwegian Seafood Council’s director for China for a few more months before he takes the reins at Nordic Aqua Partners in-country — said the country is on track to import a record 80,000t in HOG fresh salmon in 2023, he said.

READ MORE
OCT 263:42 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Tight Chinese tilapia supply expected to continue until Q2 2024

China’s farmed tilapia supply remains highly constrained, making significant price reductions unlikely. This situation is expected to persist until the second quarter of next year, top industry executives feel.

Zhou Yunfeng, general manager of Hainan Qinfu Foods Co., told Undercurrent News at the Qingdao show that compared to August-September, the current raw material supply has slightly improved. Still, it remains very tight, as large processors are only operating at 50% of their peak capacity.

READ MORE
OCT 2511:15 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Turkey’s Nordzee eyes Asian expansion for ‘salmon trout’

A Turkish seafood company is looking to expand into Asian markets like China and Japan with its rainbow trout, which Turkish producers call ‘salmon trout’.

Nordzee, a Turkish aquaculture company, sees strong potential in China and other Asian countries as a lower-cost alternative to premium salmon species like Atlantic and coho salmon. The company currently exports seabass, sea bream and trout mainly to Europe but is attending the China Fisheries & Seafood Expo for the first time this week to connect with potential new buyers.

READ MORE
OCT 2510:57 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Western sanctions open frozen red king, snow crab ‘opportunities’ in China for Murmansk fishing giant

An executive with a crab fishing company based in Murmansk, northwest Russia, credited Western sanctions against Russia for opening up “new opportunities” in Asian markets like China.

North West Fishing Consortium (NWFC) previously exported most of its frozen red king crab and snow crab to the US and Europe, largely thanks to its proximity to those markets. But commercial director Iakushin Aleksei told Undercurrent News sanctions have forced it to reinvent itself and explore new markets.

READ MORE
OCT 256:35 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu 
Shrimp exporters face high inventories in China

International shrimp exporters, including companies from Ecuador and India, might find it challenging to make substantial profits at the Qingdao show, an importer said.

Song Changgui, the general manager of Guangdong Rainbow Aquatic Development, told Undercurrent News that many importers are hesitant to make large purchases due to unfavorable market conditions.

READ MORE
OCT 256:25 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Russian wild salmon prices ‘challenging,’ says trader

Challenging market conditions for Russian wild salmon are expected to continue in the near term, but opportunities lie beyond that, according to an executive with one of Russia’s largest wild salmon trading companies. 

Risovanyy Grigory, head of exports of Vladivostock-based Vikta, told Undercurrent News this year’s large Russian salmon harvest has led to a significant drop in prices, with headed and gutted (H&G) pink salmon now selling for below $2,000 per metric ton. That’s down from around $4,600-$4,700/t last year. 

READ MORE
OCT 254:45 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Ecuador’s vannamei shrimp dominates China’s seafood imports

The number one imported seafood for China by a long way is vannamei shrimp from Ecuador, according to data presented at the Norway-China Seafood Forum on Oct. 24 by Joe Qiao of importer Qingdao Meichu Foods.

China imported $3.56 billion worth of seafood from Ecuador in 2022, the bulk of which was vannamei, with Russia being the next largest supplier at $2.76m, then Vietnam at $1.68bn.

READ MORE
OCT 254:40 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Farmed salmon fillets are ‘future’ of China market

China mainly takes head-on, gutted (HOG) salmon, but fillets are the “future” of the market, said Paul Tsai of the Norwegian Seafood Council.

Only 470 metric tons of fillets were sent from Norway to China in 2022, but the volume “will break 1,000t” in 2023, said Tsai during a panel at the Norway-China Seafood Summit on Oct. 24.

READ MORE
OCT 254:35 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
China‘s grouper production hit 200,000t in 2022

In 2022, the production of grouper in China exceeded 200,000 metric tons, according to the China fishery yearbook.

Grouper is a valuable cultivated marine fish in China, consisting of more than a dozen farmed species, including hybrids. Over the past decade, the grouper aquaculture industry has experienced rapid growth due to advancements in breeding and feeding technologies, experts said at the China Seafood Forum on Oct. 24.

READ MORE
OCT 254:28 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
‘One dish’ has made Vietnamese pangasius into a Chinese bestseller

The popularity of boiled pangasius with Sichuan pickles has made the Vietnamese farmed fish into one of the most popular dishes in China, said Joe Qiao, of importer Qingdao Meichu Foods.

“One dish has turned basa into one of the best-selling fish in the Chinese market,” said Qiao.

READ MORE
OCT 254:26 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Top Chinese importer talks economic slump, cod’s potential as kids’ food

Joe Qiao, of Chinese importer Qingdao Meichu Foods, spoke bearishly on the country’s economy but was bullish on the possibility of growing domestic cod sales during the Norway-China Seafood Forum on Oct. 24.

According to Qiao, sales at some retailers are down as much as 20-30% due to China’s slowing economy. Foodservice sales have also been “soft” after a strong showing during the May 1 holiday, he said.

READ MORE
OCT 2410:13 PM GMT
By Lewis Hu
Alibaba exec: Online seafood sales face growth, profit challenges

Many businesses have observed that the online sales of seafood products is encountering growing challenges after several years of development in China, according to an executive from Alibaba.

“We observe that online seafood merchants are primarily facing challenges related to slowed user growth, weak traffic, and declining profit margins,” said Wang Xia, director of Tmall Fisheries.

READ MORE
OCT 2410:07 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Best Aquaculture Practice growth faster for Chinese domestic market than exports

The Global Seafood Alliance (GSA) is expanding its sustainability certification program in China beyond exported seafood to the domestic market, according to vice president of market development Steve Hart.

Over the past three years, new GSA certifications in China have focused on seafood being sold domestically rather than for export. “Previously, before then, most of the certifications in China were for export markets,” Hart told Undercurrent News.

READ MORE
OCT 245:02 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
China overtakes Japan as Norway’s largest mackerel market

China outstripped Japan as the main market for Norwegian mackerel in 2022, while Asia has also overtaken Europe in terms of purchasing volume of the pelagic fish.

Norway exported close to 60,000 metric tons of mackerel to China in 2022, compared to around 55,000t for Japan, according to Jan Eirik Johnsen, key account manager for pelagics with the Norwegian Seafood Council.

READ MORE
OCT 244:08 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Further 20% cut likely for Barents Sea cod quota in 2025, frozen supply to be most impacted

A further cut of 20% for the Barents Sea cod quota is likely in 2025 after a reduction at this level was confirmed for next year by the Norwegians and Russians last week, said an industry analyst.

Including Pacific cod, the total supply of the species will drop to 1.12 million metric tons in 2024, having been at 1.63m in 2018, according to data presented at the Norway-China Seafood Summit by Eivind Hestvik Braekkan, an analyst with the Norwegian Seafood Council.

READ MORE
OCT 243:37 AM GMT
By Lewis Hu
China’s seafood trade deficit ‘the new norm,’ says Ministry of Agriculture researcher

China’s seafood trade deficit is expected to become the norm, according to a Chinese government researcher. 

At the China Seafood Summit, Xie Zhongmin, a researcher from China’s Agricultural and Rural Affairs Ministry, projected that the growth rate of China’s seafood imports will significantly surpass that of exports.

READ MORE
OCT 243:27 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Norwegian salmon interest booming on Chinese social media platform RED

Chinese consumer interest in Norwegian salmon is growing fast on RED, a giant social media platform akin to Instagram with a massive — and largely female — user base.

According to social media expert Zhang Yu Hu, founder of consultancy Hangzhou Bu Xi Management, searches for Norwegian salmon on the platform have risen dramatically with promotions he’s overseen with the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC). 

READ MORE
OCT 243:15 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Sustainability top concern for Chinese seafood shoppers after food safety, says GSA

Seafood sustainability is gaining traction among Chinese consumers, according to the results of a survey shared by the Global Seafood Alliance (GSA) before the China Fisheries and Seafood Expo.

Steve Hart, vice president of market development at GSA, said the survey of 3,000 Chinese consumers found that environmental responsibility now ranks second only to food safety as a priority when buying seafood.

READ MORE
OCT 243:04 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
China is now Norway’s top salmon market in Asia

China has become the largest market in Asia for Norwegian salmon exporters for the first time in 2023, as sales of pelagics and whitefish to the country drop.

“China is the top market in Asia for Norwegian salmon, we haven’t had that before. It’s an interesting trend that we think will continue,” said Andreas Thorud, China director for the Norwegian Seafood Council (NSC).

READ MORE

Contact the authors tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com, lewis.hu@undercurrentnews.com

title: Untitled
content:
BOSTON, Massachusets, US -- The Undercurrent News team is reporting live from Seafood Expo North America (SENA), held March 12-14.

Keep clicking back to our blog for all the news from SENA, the largest trade show for the North American seafood sector.

Auto updates: On
MAR 155:55 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Momentum grows to sell last year’s snow crab as new Canadian seasons draw near

Concern is growing about the amount of snow crab still in inventory in Canada from the 2022 season just weeks before the 2023 seasons begin in Newfoundland and Labrador and the Gulf of Saint Lawrence. But Les Hodges, a widely respected crab consultant based in the US state of Washington, says “momentum” is growing to sell last year’s product. 

Undercurrent News caught up with Hodges on the sidelines of the Boston seafood show this week. 

MAR 147:29 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Guangdong farmed whitefish processor expands for value-added 

A Chinese processor of farmed whitefish species, Zhenye Aquatic, is installing at least two new production lines this year at its facility in Guangdong to produce value-added products for China’s domestic market and export sales in Asia.

Jimmy Chan, deputy general manager of the company, told Undercurrent News the company will add two but possibly four processing lines this year to its existing eight lines. The lines will process locally farmed tilapia, barramundi, Japanese seabass, red drum, and catfish.

MAR 146:29 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Oshen salmon to launch at select Mariano’s grocery stores this month

Oshen Salmon, BluGlacier’s brand for US e-commerce channels, will also debut at grocery stores for the first time this month.

The brand will be launched at stores belonging to the grocery chain Mariano’s, which boasts 44 locations, mostly around the major city of Chicago, Illinois.

MAR 146:21 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Higher prices expected for illex squid in 2023 amid poor fishing

Chinese squid processors anticipate higher prices for Argentinian illex amid reports of poor catches.

According to data from Agroindustria, Argentinian vessels landed 42,796 metric tons of illex in the first two months of 2023, down by 7% compared with the year-ago period and the lowest volume in the past five years.

MAR 146:01 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Patagonia SeaFarms launches new salmon brand, widens skin-pack portfolio

US salmon supplier Patagonia SeaFarms has launched a new brand for its coho salmon called Patagonia Coho and widened its skin-pack products offering.

Patagonia SeaFarms was born in 2012 out of a collaboration between Yadran and Marine Farm, two of Chile’s original salmon producers. The farmers came together in a strategic alliance to distribute their product in the North American market, and set up shop in the US state of Florida.

MAR 144:54 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
New top Red Lobster director sees return to long-term shrimp contracts, eyes Ecuador 

Red Lobster’s new top seafood director sees the price and supply situation for farmed shrimp as leading to a return to long-term contracts.

 Sidney Azambuja, who has been promoted to director of strategic sourcing at Red Lobster following the exit of Joe Zhou to Slade Gorton & Co., said contracts became “very short” during the pandemic. 

MAR 142:34 PM GMT
By Nick Sambides Jr.
Ocean Beauty Seafoods targets foodservice with smoked sockeye, launches new offerings

Seattle, Washington-based Ocean Beauty Seafoods (OBS) came to the Boston seafood show with a mission: To capture a great big slice of the US foodservice sector.

Ron Christianson, the company’s vice president of sales and marketing, told Undercurrent News that the company is keeping an open mind about what that means as it looks to broaden the appeal of its Echo Falls Tapas Sliced Smoked Sockeye product.

MAR 142:03 PM GMT
By Nick Sambides Jr.
The US Atlantic salmon market needs more fish — a lot more fish, one wholesaler says

To hear David Simpson tell it, there just isn’t enough farmed Atlantic salmon to go around anymore.

Simpson is director of business development at wholesaler Wheeler Seafood in the US city of Puyallup, Washington. 

MAR 1412:52 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Carp name change pays off for Schafer Fisheries

Changing the name of Asian carp to copi roughly two years ago has made it easier for Schafer Fisheries, a Thomson, Illinois-based processor, to sell more of the fish that has invaded waterways in multiple Midwestern US states and created a nuisance for boaters and other species, reports James Schafer, the company’s general manager.

In 2022, more than two dozen distributors, processors and restaurants — mostly in Illinois, but with some multi-state delivery — signed onto the five-year, $600,000 carp rebranding project. It was funded through the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative (GLRI).

MAR 148:12 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese breaded shrimp company bemoans crushing US 25% tariffs

To find evidence of the impact of US tariffs of 25% on imports of Chinese seafood, look no further than breaded shrimp. Once a trade worth almost $200 million, US imports of Chinese-made products have crumpled.

Maggie Wang of Fujian province-based Longhua Seafood told Undercurrent News her company is one such casualty. It used to export 700 containers of breaded shrimp and shrimp trays a year, mainly to the US market, but shipped just 300 containers last year. 

MAR 146:22 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Cooke promotes Orkney organic salmon to US ahead of July supply hike

Canada-based seafood giant Cooke is promoting farmed salmon from Scotland’s Orkney Islands to the US market for the first time, ahead of having increased supply in July.

Cooke has an existing US customer base for the salmon and is not taking on new customers until July. That’s when the higher volumes will be available, said Jill Cronk, vice president of marketing for True North Seafood, Cooke’s sales arm.

MAR 1311:52 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Argentina’s red shrimp season nears closing date with record-high catches

Argentina’s shrimp fishing season in provincial waters will likely end in the coming weeks, probably between the middle and the end of March, according to industry sources at the Boston seafood show. 

Tomas Gerpe, general manager at squid and shrimp exporter Illex Fishing, told Undercurrent News that the authorities had not yet set the closing date for the red shrimp fishery in the provincial waters.

MAR 1311:44 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Argentina’s former fisheries undersecretary joins up-and-coming shrimp, squid exporter

Tomas Gerpe, who was Argentina’s fisheries and aquaculture between 2015-2017, has recently joined Illex Fishing as its general manager, he confirmed to Undercurrent News.

After four years of service to the Argentine government, where he focused on fishing-related issues between Argentina and China, Gerpe joined the private seafood sector. 

MAR 138:06 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
China could grow caviar production despite lower prices

China’s second-largest caviar producer, Sichuan Runzhao Sturgeon Import, could increase its output to 100 metric tons a year. 

That target represents around quarter of current global output, potentially putting further pressure on world caviar prices. 

MAR 137:03 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Red Chamber Argentina commissions new vessels

Red Chamber Group, an Argentine shrimp and hake exporter with a base in Puerto Madryn, Chubut, has recently commissioned two new fishing vessels. 

A new 39-meter long trawler for the red shrimp fishery, named Patagonia Queen, will be delivered to the Argentine firm by the end of the month from the Spanish shipowner Armon, according to Valentina Bragagnolo, the company’s corporate communications manager. 

MAR 131:54 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
West Bengal’s ‘biggest recent investment’ in shrimp processing

Kolkata shipbuilding industry figures have backed a company to build a plant processing 80 metric tons of raw material per day in West Bengal, claimed as the Indian state’s “biggest recent investment” in the shrimp industry. 

NDM Seafood Processors and Exporters told Undercurrent News that its plant — located 65 kilometers from Kolkata — opened in 2021. It exported 160 containers of shrimp mainly for South Korea and Japan last year.

MAR 131:53 PM GMT
By Nick Sambides Jr.
Rich Products looking to diversify Morey’s, lessening dependence on salmon

US-based seafood and food conglomerate Rich Products’ purchase of Morey’s Seafood International three years ago has broadened Rich’s reach into the far corners of the US and solidified its name as a seafood provider.

“When we acquired them, it gave us a capability that that we didn’t have doing marinated salmon and other fish, so it was a really a nice tack-on for us. It was very complementary to our business,” said Ciera Womack, director of marketing at Buffalo, New York-based Rich. 

MAR 131:24 PM GMT
By Nick Sambides Jr.
SeaPak concentrating on making partnership with Budweiser, beer-battered seafood a success

Beer Battered Flounder Strips. Beer Battered Cod. Beer Battered Shrimp and Beer Battered Crab Poppers.

Budweiser is a long-established beer brand and making inroads into a new space with its partnership with SeaPak Shrimp & Seafood Company, said Ciera Womack, director of marketing at Buffalo, New York-based Rich Products, which produces the SeaPak branded line of seafood.

MAR 1312:50 PM GMT
By Nick Sambides Jr.
Paine getting out there to meet Boston show as new Australis Aquaculture president

New Australis Aquaculture president Jason Paine is using the Boston seafood show as a chance to get out and meet people while his staff works to expand the company’s retail and foodservice opportunities to sell barramundi.

“This is an important year for us,” said Jonathan Daen, chief financial officer at Australis. “He knows lots of folks within the industry and he is walking a little bit of a different walk and talking a little bit of a different talk after 23 years in the salmon space. Plus we’re entering into a significant growth period.

MAR 1312:23 PM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Canadian lobster sector in strong position as spring seasons near

The Canadian lobster sector is in better shape than it’s been in recent times as the country’s multiple spring fisheries near their opening start dates, Geoff Irvine, executive director of the Lobster Council of Canada, told Undercurrent News on the sidelines of the Boston seafood show Sunday (March 12).

Both live and frozen Homarus americanus inventory has been worked down, as previously reported by Undercurrent. We have just enough product to get us into early May, he said.

MAR 139:03 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Luke’s Lobster back in restaurant, retail expansion mode

The US lobster roll restaurant chain and processor Luke’s Lobster is back in expansion mode after a long struggle through the pandemic, co-founder and chief marketing officer Ben Conniff told Undercurrent News on Sunday during a stop by his booth (#2132).

The Portland, Maine-based company is getting ready to open its 21st “lobster shack” in Las Vegas, Nevada, at a location outside the New York-New York Hotel and Casino, its second in the city where, according to a long-running tourism advertisement, things that happen are not to be spoken of elsewhere.

MAR 138:58 AM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Zoneco North America brushes off scandal at China HQ with ‘banner years’

Zoneco Group’s North American division in Burlington, Canada, achieved “banner years” despite the company’s chairman and high-level executives at its China headquarters being forced out during the pandemic over an accounting scandal.

Zoneco – formerly China’s largest listed seafood company by seafood sales — still faces numerous shareholder lawsuits in China, after hundreds of millions of renminbi-worth of scallops farmed in Bohai Sea were allegedly faked to boost Zoneco’s share price and assets.

MAR 138:17 AM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Brazilian tilapia producers expand production, eye higher US sales

Several Brazilian tilapia producers are expanding production and aim to gain  larger market share in the US, beating the competition by competing on quality and freshness. China is the currently the US’ largest tilapia supplier.

One of Brazil’s largest farmers, Copacol, currently produces 200,000 tilapia per day, of which it exports about 15% to various markets, according to Tiago Anderle, a sales manager with the firm. 

MAR 137:13 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Ecuador shrimp packers enjoy China ‘honeymoon’ after end of zero COVID

With the end of China’s zero COVID policy, demand is back for shrimp, said Sandro Coglitore, the second largest supplier from Ecuador.

With shrimp prices set low, it’s a buyers’ market, multiple sources told Undercurrent News during Seafood Expo North America. The price situation and lifting of the zero COVID policy mean demand in China is strong.

MAR 1210:26 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Cyclone Yaku delays Ecuador’s shrimp harvest

Heavy rains caused by Cyclone Yaku produced severe flooding and landslides in western Ecuador and Peru, according to industry sources attending the Boston seafood show. Peru’s national meteorology and hydrology service described Yaku as an unusual tropical cyclone.

“In one day, it rained as much as in a month,” one Ecuadorian source at the show said. 

MAR 129:58 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Homegrown Shrimp USA targets April first harvest from land-based RAS

Land-based aquaculture company Homegrown Shrimp USA has stocked shrimp in 12 of 40 tanks using recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) as it targets its first harvest by late April.

The Florida-based company, which is run by Robins McIntosh, vice-president at Thai conglomerate Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF), stocked its first tank at its facility in early 2023.

MAR 129:49 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Multi X promotes carbon-neutral salmon, antibiotic-free brand

Chilean salmon farming giant Multi X is promoting its new 100% CarbonNeutral certified Chilean salmon products at the Boston seafood show along with its previously launched antibiotic-free salmon brand.

The 100% CarbonNeutral certification means that the product is manufactured in accordance with the requirements of the CarbonNeutral protocol as administered by Climate Impact Partners. That group specializes in carbon market solutions for climate action.

MAR 129:11 PM GMT
By Matilde Mereghetti
Camanchaca partners with Frime on tuna products, launches new salmon skin-packs

Chile’s Salmones Camanchaca has launched a new line of skin-pack coho salmon products for the US retail market and e-commerce channels. The firm has also debuted a range of ready-to-cook yellowfin tuna steaks and burgers in collaboration with Spanish company Frime.

Camanchaca aims to expand its ready-to-cook range with different species and flavors, Daniel Silva, the firm’s chief commercial officer, told Undercurrent News. 

MAR 127:20 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Chinese processor follows High Liner to Indonesia

A Chinese whitefish company has partnered with an Indonesian contract processor, following the example of Canadian seafood giant High Liner Foods.

Olly Wang of Dalian, China-headquartered Ocean Pearl, told Undercurrent News that he thinks he’s the “only one [from China] in Indonesia, or maybe the first one”. 

MAR 123:39 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Southwind set to ramp up skin-pack output with $20m Salt Lake City facility

Southwind Foods plans to spend $20 million on the processing and coldstorage expansion in Salt Lake City, in the US state of Utah.

The company, which trades as Great American Seafood Co., will put “two or three” skin-pack lines in the 40,000-square-foot facility, Sam Galletti, president of the Vernon, California-based firm, told Undercurrent News.

MAR 123:36 PM GMT
By Louis Harkell
Hainan tilapia company expects to open $72m facility by 2025

Chinese tilapia company Hainan Qinfu expects to complete its new CNY 500 million ($72.4m) factory by 2025.

The plant — which will process up to 500 metric tons of tilapia daily — will replace Qinfu’s existing factory near Wenchang, which processes and exports mainly tilapia fillets for North America and Europe.

MAR 122:41 PM GMT
By Nick Sambides Jr.
For some shrimpers, diversification is key to getting through a lean year

California-based wholesaler Sunnyvale Seafood is using a bevy of tilapia, swai, sea bass, crawfish and pangasius products imported from China, and Vietnam — plus some Argentine red shrimp — to vary and bolster its commercial base and get through a lean year in the US shrimp market.

In all, close to two dozen ready-to-eat frozen seafood meals lined its display case at the Boston seafood show as Sunnyvale reached out with products geared toward young millennials looking for alternatives to more traditional seafood, said Yinghai Li, vice president of Sunnyvale, a division of Zhanjiang Guolian Aquatic Products of China.

MAR 1212:55 PM GMT
By Nick Sambides Jr.
When it comes to US shrimp, ‘I don’t think anybody knows what’s going to happen in six months’

After more than 40 years in the shrimp business, farmer and importer Al Nasti has never seen it as bad as it is right now, he told Undercurrent News.

The director of US and international shrimp sales at BMR Seafood Group of New York said that sure, the US economy is teetering on the edge of recession, the shrimp market is glutted like it has never been and competition in the shrimp space is fierce.

MAR 1212:16 PM GMT
By Nick Sambides Jr.
US shrimp importer: We’ll bear with you if you bear with us

We’ll bear with you if you bear with us.

That’s the message Al Nasti is giving his customers. The director of US and international shrimp sales at BMR Seafood Group of New York said that in a bear market, which US shrimp sales have been over the last year, finding a way to help his clients through the hard times is the most important use of his time in Boston.

MAR 1211:40 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Beaver Street brings in foodservice VP from Aqua Star

Beaver Street Fisheries has added a veteran foodservice seller to grow its business in this sector, Mark Frisch, executive vice president of Beaver Street, told Undercurrent News.

Mario Pullara has joined Beaver Street from Aqua Star, having worked for Eastern Fish for two years and Tampa Maid Foods for 13 before that. “We’re excited to have Mark onboard to grow our foodservice business,” Frisch told Undercurrent.

MAR 1211:36 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Beaver Street sees opening to promote shrimp with high-priced inventory ‘selling through’

US importers are in the process of selling through inventories of shrimp and other shellfish, with cheaper products on their way from overseas.

“There’s a big opening to promote shrimp this year, with the prices as they are,” Mark Frisch, executive vice president of Beaver Street Fisheries, told Undercurrent News.

MAR 128:31 AM GMT
By Jason Huffman
Florida-based importer in Boston with an eye on retail sales growth

Beacon Fisheries, a Jacksonville, Florida-based seafood importer, processor and wholesaler, counts on food service for 94-95% of its roughly $100 million in annual sales, but founder and CEO Mike Eddy hopes to up his percentage of sales at large retail outlets soon.

His company (booth #2645) is one of the roughly 1,150 exhibiting at the Boston seafood show, which started Sunday (March 12).

MAR 127:33 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
North Coast partners with Maine kelp farmer on raw material for burgers, meatballs

North Coast Seafoods, a large processor on the US East Coast, has partnered with a Maine kelp farmer to supply the raw material for some new value-added products.

Boston, Massachusetts-based North Coast is using kelp from Atlantic Sea Farms (ASF) in vegan burgers and meatballs, as well as a “flexitarian” salmon/kelp burger, company executives told Undercurrent News.

MAR 117:15 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Southwind snaps up West Coast US processor, plans new Salt Lake City plant

Carson, California-based Southwind Foods has inked a deal to acquire Caito Fisheries, a processor with four operations in the West Coast US state.

In addition to announcing the deal for Caito, Southwind revealed plans to build a 40,000-square-foot processing, storage and distribution facility in Salt Lake City, Utah.

MAR 117:13 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
US East Coast B2C entrepreneurs to use S2G investment for Cali facility 

The founders of a US East Coast startup targeting consumers with build-your-own, traceable seafood boxes will use an investment from Lukas Walton-backed venture capital (VC) firm S2G Ventures to open a second distribution facility in California. 

KnowSeafood, based in New Bedford, Massachusetts, will use the California facility “to reduce shipping costs, drive customer acquisition, increase product variety, and build out its data and analytics team for direct insights into consumers’ behaviors toward seafood”, said the VC, in a statement. 

MAR 117:11 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Exhibitor numbers up 35%

On the eve of the Boston show, 1,148 exhibitors are registered.

That’s a 35% increase on the level seen in 2022 when the omicron COVID wave was in full force.

Contact the authors tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com, jason.huffman@undercurrentnews.com, nick.sambides@undercurrentnews.com, matilde.mereghetti@undercurrentnews.com, louis.harkell@undercurrentnews.com

title: Untitled
content:
BANGKOK, Thailand -- Undercurrent News is reporting live from the World Tuna Trade Conference & Exhibition, held in Bangkok, Thailand, from Oct. 11-13. 

The tuna conference will address global production and trade trends, technology developments, stock management, and other topics.

The full program for the conference can be viewed here. Keep checking back below for the latest updates.

Auto updates: On
OCT 178:00 AM GMT
Yellowfin stock in the Indian Ocean is the IOTC’s top concern 

The top challenge for the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC) is the status of the yellowfin tuna stock in the Indian Ocean, which has been overfished for a few years.

Gerard Dominigue, IOTC compliance manager, pointed out that the last stock assessment was carried out by the commission’s scientific committee in 2020. 

OCT 175:17 AM GMT
Tri Marine CEO: Industry should ‘get together’ to promote tuna value

The tuna industry should “work together” to ensure effective management of fishing activity and stocks as well as to better promote tuna’s value, said Juan Corrales, CEO at Tri Marine Group.

He said joint efforts by the whole industry were needed to promote tuna’s health benefits and value, going beyond the commercial interest of individual firms, and beyond promoting one fishery over another. “Competition is healthy, but we should be doing much more,” he noted.

OCT 1310:06 PM GMT
Independent adjudicator determines PNA cannot have bigeye, FADs certified

News has emerged that an objection to the Parties to the Nauru Agreement (PNA)’s tuna fisheries in the Pacific Ocean — lodged through the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC)’s own objection process — has been upheld by an independent adjudicator. 

Adjudicator John McKendrick ruled that PNA’s fishery should not be MSC-certified for two points, bigeye and fish aggregating devices (FADs). 

OCT 132:28 AM GMT
Rio Mare expands into new product categories

Earlier this year, Italian tuna brand Rio Mare launched a new range of tuna-based pesto, which includes three variants, tuna black olives and chilli, tuna pistachios and lemon and tuna, almonds and pecorino. 

The new line is already available on the Italian retail market and is also in the process of being launched in other international markets, where the brand has a presence.

OCT 1211:28 AM GMT
MSC raises the bar for certified tuna fisheries

At an event on the side of the Infofish tuna conference, taking place in Bangkok, Thailand, the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) presented to stakeholders its new fisheries standard, which includes a higher set of requirements on harvest strategies. 

The event attracted a lot of interest from stakeholders, who asked numerous questions about the impact on tuna fisheries, particularly in the Western and Central Pacific Ocean, and on the new timelines for delivering harvest strategies.

OCT 1211:13 AM GMT
Demand for higher-value tuna rises in Southeast Asia

Consumer demand for higher-value tuna, both fresh and frozen, is on the rise in Southeast Asia and the Far East, according to Fatima Ferdouse, an international expert in fishery trade from Malaysia. 

Southeast Asia is the world’s largest processing and export base of canned tuna, Ferdouse noted. Thailand is the largest Asian exporter of canned and processed tuna, followed by China, the Philippines, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, Vietnam, Fiji, Maldives, Solomon Island and Iran. 

OCT 1210:24 AM GMT
Faster sales of loins to North America boost Vietnamese tuna exports

In the first eight months of this year, Vietnamese tuna exports overtook their level for the whole of 2021. The increase was driven by a rise in shipments to the North American market, highlighted Le Hang, communications director at the Vietnamese association of seafood exporters and producers (VASEP). 

In 2022 so far, Vietnam’s tuna exports have risen by 9.1% year-on-year, she said. 

OCT 129:15 AM GMT
Middle East tuna market stabilizes after COVID-19 boom

Following an “unprecedented” boom in canned tuna demand during the first year of the pandemic, the Middle Eastern market has stabilized post-COVID, according to Arnab Sengupta, deputy CEO at JMB International, Thailand.

“COVID-19 created unprecedented demand for canned tuna. However, following post-COVID adjustment, the result has been a cumulative shrinkage,” Sengupta said. 

OCT 128:23 AM GMT
Peru’s tuna industry aims to recover processing activity

The Peruvian private sector aims to recover the industrial level it registered in 2019 within the next 18 months, according to a local industry association. Currently, the Peruvian tuna industry is working at 50% of its installed capacity.

The recent enactment and publication of a new law to promote the extraction of highly migratory hydrobiological resources, however, is expected to help Peruvian processing plants to return to import tuna from foreign vessels with Peruvian fishing permits, according to Alfonso Miranda Eyzaguirre, president of the fishing and aquaculture committee of Peru’s National Society of Industries (SNI). 

OCT 123:06 AM GMT
Manta premium on Bangkok skipjack tuna price widens

Skipjack tuna prices for delivery this month in Bangkok, Thailand, fell significantly month-on-month to $1,600 per metric ton, according to industry sources. 

Some market participants are expecting prices to decline further in Bangkok, Thailand. “Packers are pushing for $1,550/t,” one source with a large Asian supplier told Undercurrent News.

OCT 1212:23 AM GMT
WTO: agreement on fisheries subsidies a major step forward for ocean sustainability

On June 17, 2022, the World Trade Organization (WTO) adopted a new agreement on fisheries subsidies (the FSA), prohibiting member countries from funding illegal fishing and fishing of overexploited stocks.

The agreement marks a major step forward for ocean sustainability by prohibiting harmful fisheries subsidies, which are a key factor in the widespread depletion of the world’s fish stocks, according to the WTO.

OCT 1212:00 AM GMT
Spain’s Jealsa sees double-digit growth in Brazil

Spanish canned seafood firm Jealsa Rianxeira has managed to rapidly grow its share of the Brazilian market, thanks to its investment in a plant in the state of Ceara, according to Dario Chemerinski, business director at SSP — Selecting Strategic Partners — in Brazil. 

The firm has grown its canned tuna sales in the Latin American country, with its brand Robinson Crusoe achieving an 11% share last year, Chemerinski said. 

OCT 1111:46 PM GMT
Pacifical: EU canned tuna imports decline in 2021 as euro weakens against dollar

The weakening of the euro against the dollar has made canned tuna more expensive for EU consumers, said Henk Brus, CEO of Pacifical. 

About 60% of tuna is still bought from countries that quote and sell in dollars, according to Brus.  

OCT 112:04 PM GMT
WCPO tuna catches decline in 2021

The total value of tuna catches in the Western and Central Pacific Ocean (WCPO) in 2021 was estimated at $4.6 billion, 9% down year-on-year. 

This is a drop from a record level reached in 2018 (see graph below), according to Feleti Teo, executive director of the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission (WCPFC).

OCT 1110:59 AM GMT
FAO: Value of total tuna exports dropped y-o-y in 2020

Overall tuna catches declined in 2020 from a record high in 2019, according to data presented by Stefania Vannuccini, senior fishery officer at the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations. 

The overall rise in exports of prepared or preserved tuna during the year was offset by a drop in the export of frozen and fresh tuna, according to FAO data.

OCT 119:42 AM GMT
Papua New Guinea, Global Fishing Watch to share vessel tracking data

In a newly established partnership with the Global Fishing Watch, Papua New Guinea (PNG) has committed to sharing vessel tracking data from its Fishing Industry Association (FIA) on the organization’s public map.

Through this agreement, the Pacific island nation is taking action to enhance the monitoring of fishing vessels operating in its waters and increase the transparency of its seafood supply chain, it said.

OCT 114:46 AM GMT
Tuna is a women’s business too: Percentage of women employed in WCPO on rise

Recent research has found that women are increasingly present in the tuna supply chain, and particularly in the processing sector. 

Professor Kate Barclay, from the University of Technology Sydney, Australia, presented the main findings of a gender analysis of the fisheries sector in the Western and Central Pacific Ocean (WCPO).

OCT 113:02 AM GMT
Thailand on track to return to 2020 export levels this year

Although Thai tuna exports had fallen somewhat in 2021, exports to most regions — apart from Latin America — are on track to recover, according to Narin Niruttinanon, vice president of the Thai Tuna Industry Association.

During the period January-June 2022, exports to the US, the largest market for Thai tuna exports, have shown an increase of 16% year-on-year, he said.

OCT 112:58 AM GMT
PNG to review its rebate, vessel day schemes to offset rising energy prices

Over the coming months, Papua New Guinea (PNG)’s government will implement a series of new policy incentive packages aimed at attracting foreign direct investments to companies operating and processing tuna in the country, representatives announced.

“We are working with other state institutions to provide preferential arrangements to [PNG-]based processing companies,” said the country’s minister for fisheries and marine resources, Jelta Wong.

OCT 112:53 AM GMT
Maldives: Despite sustainable practices, no rewards for pole-and-line tuna 

The Maldives receives little to no reward for its long-held commitment to sustainable fishing methods, despite the market recognizing the number of positive ecological and social aspects of its fishery, said Hussain Rasheed, the country’s minister of fisheries, agriculture and marine resources. 

The minister pointed out that the Maldives continues to use pole-and-line fishing, despite the lower efficiency and the fact that other fishing methods would be cheaper.

OCT 112:48 AM GMT
Ecuador tuna exports rise in 2021

The Ecuadorian tuna industry has adapted to a constantly changing and disruptive industry environment, according to Andres Arens Hidalgo, Ecuador’s vice minister of fisheries and aquaculture. 

During 2020, the most challenging year of the pandemic, Ecuador managed to maintain tuna exports, with shipments dropping only 2% year-on-year, Arens said. 

OCT 112:46 AM GMT
Princes: Market disruption, inflation challenge global tuna industry

Characterized by the ongoing impacts of COVID-19, alongside market disruption and inflation pressure, the last 12 months have been a particularly difficult time for the tuna sector, pointed out Neil Bohannon, seafood director at Princes Group.

However, tuna producers and processors have been able to respond to those challenges. Bohannon defined 2020, 2021 and 2022 as a “period of resilience, innovation and progress, which has taken our industry from strength to strength”.

Contact the author matilde.mereghetti@undercurrentnews.com

title: NASF 2022: If cod is the new salmon, is pollock the new cod?; Chances of full NE Atlantic pelagic quota sharing agreement ‘slim’
content:
Undercurrent News is reporting live from the North Atlantic Seafood Forum (NASF) in Bergen, Norway, held June 21-23, 2022. 

It is the event's return to a large-scale, in-person format since the coronavirus pandemic lockdowns. It is also being streamed online.

Day one features a "global aquaculture summit", before a panel on gender equality in seafood and a look at sector innovations. Days two and three will move on to the familiar sector-specific events on salmon, whitefish and coldwater shrimp, among other topics.

Day three will then see numerous listed companies present at Pareto Securities' "investor seminar", while dedicated events on land-based aquaculture and pelagics will also take place. Keep checking back to read the latest updates below.

Auto updates: On
JUN 2411:13 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
If cod is the new salmon, is pollock the new cod?

The rising prices for cod saw Morten Jensen, the chief operating officer for whitefish for Insula, ask if the fish was becoming the new salmon in terms of its position in the market, in an interview with Undercurrent News a few weeks ago.

During the NASF whitefish summit on Wednesday, Jensen expanded his question to reflect the pressure the cod market could experience from cheaper species such as Alaska pollock.

READ MORE
JUN 2410:26 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Fisheries management expert warns chances of full northeast Atlantic pelagics quota sharing agreement are slim

The chances of the northeast Atlantic’s coastal states agreeing a full quota sharing agreement on mackerel, blue whiting, and Atlanto-Scandian herring are slim, believes Fishfacts founder and fisheries management expert Oli Samro.

Having literally written the book on fisheries management in the region, Samro said there was just one factor that decides quota-setting: politics.

READ MORE
JUN 243:45 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Data shows extent to which Faroese rely on Russian pelagic market

Data presented by Ragnar Ronning, global sales and marketing director with Kontali, shows the extent to which the Faroe Islands has relied on the Russian market for exporting mackerel and herring.

In 2021, Russia imported 48,250 metric tons of mackerel from the Faroes and 62,060t of herring, as well as 13,851t of salmon. It also brought in 8,300t of blue whiting and nearly 6,000t of capelin.

READ MORE
JUN 243:30 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
‘Eco-anxiety’ means a new food market segment

There is a growing food market segment driven by the “eco-anxiety” of consumers, according to Julius Palm, deputy CEO and head of strategy and brand with Followfood.

The German company first launched in 2007 as Followfish, and had the first “360-degree” sustainable, fully traceable and trackable canned tuna product, he said. It is focused on and built around full sustainability and “doing things differently” in the food production sector, and the encouraging thing is that this outlook has found its market, he said.

READ MORE
JUN 2310:08 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Specialized realtor builds $68m Norwegian salmon slaughterhouse

Liv Malvik, CEO of industrial real estate agent KMC Properties, shared details of a new processing facility her firm is building for Norwegian processor Slakteriet.

The new slaughter and filleting facility is being built in Floro, Vestland county, and will come with robotic and automated tools, she said.

READ MORE
JUN 238:57 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Arnalax ups volumes of fresh salmon shipped to US by sea

Icelandic Salmon, which owns the farming subsidiary Arnalax, is increasing the volumes of fresh fish it’s transporting to the US market by sea.

The company, which is part-owned by Norway’s SalMar, used sea transport to move 89% of its fresh volumes for North America in Q1, compared to 71% in Q4 of 2021 and 67% of Q3, said CEO Bjorn Hembre.

READ MORE
JUN 238:40 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Belgian RAS farmer Columbi Salmon plans to go public

Cast your mind back a couple of years, and it was hard to move in the salmon industry without news breaking of another land-based farmer hitting the stock market.

Times may have changed, and the investor market cooled, but that isn’t deterring the Oostende, Belgium-based recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) project Columbi Salmon, according to chief financial officer and former Nordea analyst Kolbjorn Giskeodegard.

READ MORE
JUN 238:10 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Atlantic Sapphire to push for higher price premium in coming months

Having marketed itself as a full alternative to conventional, imported fish, Atlantic Sapphire’s ‘Bluehouse’ salmon has remained largely unaffected by the spiking spot prices that have hit the market in the first half of the year.

Instead, it has maintained a fairly consistent price range — $12/kg for its premium 3kg+ salmon product, and $7.5-$8/kg for the rest of its harvest. 

READ MORE
JUN 237:48 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Atlantic Sapphire focused on stability in 2022, says CFO

After a disastrous set of incidents in 2021 — a year which saw a fire wipe out its Danish land-based facility — recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) salmon farmer Atlantic Sapphire is thus far enjoying a largely under the radar 2022 marked by steady biomass growth at its main US plant.

“In the very short term, our key focus is stability,” chief financial officer Karl Oystein Oyehaug told listeners. “With the same stability that we’ve had since last summer, we’ve been able to do what we consider the funnest part of the job: focus on improvements.”

READ MORE
JUN 236:38 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Chang: Another 20-30% of China whitefish plants will go under in next five years

The wave of consolidation in the Chinese whitefish processing sector will be sped up by the COVID pandemic, said the CEO of Chang International, a big player in the sector.

A further 20-30% of Chinese processing plants will go under in the next five years, said Jerry Chang, delivering his NASF presentation remotely from Shanghai, during the lengthy lockdown in the Chinese city.

READ MORE
JUN 236:34 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
China whitefish pipeline to US now ‘twice as long’

The so-called “pipeline” of moving headed and gutted (H&G) cod and haddock from Norway or Russia to China for processing and back to markets in Europe or North America is now twice as long, said a top sector executive.

“The [H&G] fish we are buying now in the north of Norway is what we will sell at the start of next year,” said Frank Bodin, chief financial officer of Nordic Group USA, an importer based in the US.

READ MORE
JUN 236:09 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Land-based yellowtail fetching ‘incredible’ EU prices in 2022

Earlier this year, the land-based recirculating aquaculture system farmer (RAS) Nordic Aquafarms made the decision to demerge its farming operations in Europe from its planned sites in the US, and focus its efforts entirely on yellowtail production at its Danish and Norwegian farms.

It’s a decision that looks very promising in the current market, according to CEO Bernt Olav Rottingsnes.

READ MORE
JUN 235:32 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Large smolt is ‘driver’ of Bakkafrost’s 150,000t by 2026 target

Faroese farmer Bakkafrost sees increasing its large smolt production in its home country and the UK, where it acquired what was formerly known as the Scottish Salmon Company.

A “big driver” of the company’s plan to hit 150,000 metric tons in Scotland and the Faroe Islands is large smolt, farmed on land to around 500 grams, said CEO Regin Jacobsen.

READ MORE
JUN 235:19 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman
Grieg plans move further downstream into ‘processing partnerships’

Grieg Seafood, which is focused on farming salmon in Norway and Canada after selling its Scottish farms, is looking to move further downstream.

The company has ended its former sales joint venture with Bremnes Seashore, Ocean Quality, and built an in-house commercial team.

READ MORE
JUN 234:35 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Mowi eyes UK post-smolt production 

Norway-based global salmon giant Mowi is looking at investing in post-smolt production in the UK, where it farms in Scotland.

“We’re looking at a post-smolt program in Scotland as we speak,” said Ivan Vindheim, CEO of Mowi, speaking during the Pareto Securities investment forum on Thursday at NASF.

READ MORE
JUN 233:30 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Cermaq: Chilean salmon regulations ‘not suitable for purpose’

Addressing listeners at the start of the second day’s salmon aquaculture summit, Steven Rafferty, CEO of multinational farmer Cermaq Group, discussed the downsides of Chile’s aquaculture framework.

“There is a misunderstanding of the Chilean industry in my view,” said Rafferty. “I’ve got many comments from other farmers, other suppliers that say that Chilean companies just make a mess of it in Chile. Of course, I’m one of those farmers, so I take it a little bit to heart, but it’s not true.”

READ MORE
JUN 233:10 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Game of Thrones actor the face of upcoming Mowi ad campaign

Mowi intends to launch a new range of commercials this fall starring Norwegian actor Kristofer Hivju, known globally for playing the role of Tormund Giantsbane on TV series Game of Thrones.

The new commercials feature Hivju eating Mowi-branded salmon at various remote fjords in Norway.

READ MORE
JUN 232:24 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Norway braces for up to 20% cod, haddock TAC cuts in 2023

The Barents Sea cod and haddock total allowable catch (TAC) could be cut by as much as 20% in 2023, said the CEO of Norway’s largest whitefish harvesting firm during the NASF whitefish summit on Wednesday.

“The forecast for next year is a 20% decrease for both species [cod and haddock],” said Eldar Farstad, CEO of Leroy Havfiske, the trawler company owned by salmon and trout farming giant Leroy Seafood Group. Then, on saithe, there will be an increase.”

READ MORE
JUN 221:38 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Family-owned Norwegian salmon farmer ‘nuts’ about cutting CO2 

Norwegian salmon farmer Eide Fjordbruk has reduced its CO2 emissions from 4.04 per kilogram produced in 2018 to 2.56/kg in 2021, said CEO Sondre Eide.

The company has overtaken frozen pollock fillets for the low level of CO2 produced, according to data Eide, a third-generation salmon farmer, presented at NASF.

READ MORE
JUN 221:37 PM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Cargill’s Ewos opens ‘world’s first’ decarbonized aquafeed factory

US agribusiness giant Cargill has just officially opened what it claims is the world’s first aquafeed factory without local CO2 emissions.

“We were really proud last week to open our factory in Bergneset, in the north of Norway, as a fully decarbonized factory,” said Dave Robb, head of Cargill’s SeaFurther sustainability initiative, during a panel at NASF.

READ MORE
JUN 2211:53 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
UK’s struggle for chefs an opportunity for coldwater shrimp?

After the coronavirus pandemic and new Brexit regulations, the UK foodservice sector is sorely short of skilled chefs and other staff, noted Mike Berthet, director of consultancy Aquasea.

While this means tough times for the restaurant and pub sector — especially when inflation and recessionary trends are taken into account — it could be an opportunity for coldwater shrimp, he suggested.

READ MORE
JUN 2211:00 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Global coldwater shrimp landings up 2.5% in 2021

Global coldwater shrimp catches were up 2.5% year-on-year in 2021, at 282,076 metric tons, according to an update by Gemba Seafood Consulting.

Essentially each of the important harvesting regions saw landings climb with the exception of Russia, where catches fell from 28,000t to 22,000t.

READ MORE
JUN 2210:48 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
US West Coast jordani landings hit six-year high in 2021

US West Coast landings of pandalus jordani hit a six-year high in 2021, according to an update from Pacific Seafood director Charles Kirschbaum.

Catches by fishers in Washington, Oregon and California have been climbing steadily since 2019, and in 2021 rose to 30,752 metric tons; higher than the five-year and 20-year averages.

READ MORE
JUN 2210:43 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Analysts agree modest salmon production growth, price drop on the cards for H2

Despite a clear reluctance to forecast the long-term salmon market in such unusual times, market analysts from both Kontali and Pareto Securities said they foresaw year-on-year production growth from nearly all major producing countries in the second half of 2022.

“We see that most of the production regions will see a shift from a notable decline to a moderate, marginal supply growth,” commented Ragnar Nystoyl, chief analyst with Kontali. 

READ MORE
JUN 227:00 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Nuseed’s Aquaterra claims genetically enhanced canola could meet all fish oil demand by 2030

Aquaterra – a company producing fish oil from genetically enhanced canola – claims its products could meet all the global demand for fish oil by 2030.

The firm, which is owned by agritech firm Nuseed, also claims it could do that with 1.5 million hectares of land – less than 5% of the current canola crop area.

READ MORE
JUN 226:50 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
Seafood’s low carbon footprint needs to be better communicated

The far lower carbon footprint of seafood compared to land-based protein needs to be better communicated to consumers, said executives on a panel at NASF.

Mowi’s total salmon production creates 2.1 million metric tons of CO2, compared to 4m for the corresponding amount of land-based animal production, said Catarina Martins, chief sustainability and technology officer for the Bergen, Norway-based global aquaculture giant.

READ MORE
JUN 226:46 AM GMT
By Tom Seaman 
DNB head: ‘Green’ industries like seafood will get cheaper financing

“Green” sectors, such as seafood production, will get cheaper financing compared to unsustainable “brown” industries, said the top seafood banker from Norway’s DNB.

It’s “becoming more expensive to finance ‘brown’ [unsustainable] industries, even if you can get capital at all”, said DNB’s Anne Hvistendahl, during a panel at NASF. “Banks are stopping the financing of the oil industry”, she said, as an example.

READ MORE
JUN 226:26 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Insect meal producer eyes 230,000t production by 2030

French biotech firm Agronutris has called on the aquaculture industry to embrace insect meal, stressing that such firms need partnerships to achieve the economy of scale necessary.

Mehdi Barrada, CEO and co-founder of Agronutris, said the company is preparing to open its initial production facility in 2023. The 15,000-square-meter plant in Rethel, northeast France, will be fully operational early in 2023, he said, with a production capacity of 5,000 metric tons of protein derived from black soldier fly.

READ MORE
JUN 226:03 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Veramaris looking to solve aquaculture’s waste problem

Novel feed ingredients have a big role to play in reducing mortality rates among salmon farmers, believes Ian Carr, global business development director with Dutch algal oil producer Veramaris.

According to the FAO, 35% of all fish, crustaceans and molluscs are wasted before reaching plates. In Norway alone, the mortality rate is around 20%, with the feed conversion ratio gradually increasing year-on-year, Carr said.

READ MORE
JUN 225:45 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Aquafeed ingredient prices unlikely to ease until 2023 or later, warns Rabobank

Prices for some of the key aquafeed raw material ingredients are unlikely to ease until 2023 at the earliest, according to Carlos Mera, analyst and head of agri commodities markets, with Rabobank’s RaboResearch division.

Since late 2021, fishmeal prices have lifted strongly, as have soymeal prices, both of which can be found at Undercurrent‘s prices portal.

READ MORE
JUN 225:28 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Aquafeed sector faces ‘unprecedented’ challenges, says Skretting Norway chief

Kicking off the NASF’s aquaculture feed summit, May Helene Holme, CEO of Skretting Norway, addressed the exceptionally strained market situation for aquafeed at present.

“Prices are going through the roof, and availability is coming down,” said Holme. “12 months ago, our experts said that this is unprecedented. It really goes to show that we need an alternative approach, we’re already struggling to get high quality raw materials.”

READ MORE
JUN 224:41 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
BioFeyn wins Seafood Innovation Award

US biotechnology firm BioFeyn was announced as the winner of this year’s Seafood Innovation Award by Bjorgolfur Havardsson, innovation manager with the NCE Seafood Innovation Cluster.

“BioFeyn micropackage nutritions and vitamins so they are easily transported to the digestive tract of the fish, and taken up at the right place. To a large degree they reduce the spill through the feces,” Havardsson explained.

READ MORE
JUN 223:54 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Even with new sources, salmon supply likely to be short of demand by 2030

Anders Milde Gjendemsjo, associate partner with US consultancy firm McKinsey, addressed the unprecedented rise in salmon prices in 2022.

According to McKinsey’s consumer feedback, salmon is widely regarded as the highest quality fish species on offer among most western European countries, and hence consumers are willing to keep paying as prices rise.

READ MORE
JUN 223:29 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
DNV: Demand for ocean space to rise nine times over by 2050

Maritime economy advisor DNV has forecast that demand for ocean and coastal space will intensify dramatically by 2050, Lisa De Jager, the organization’s global seafood director told listeners at the start of the event’s second day.

Much of this will be the spread of offshore wind farms, which DNV forecasts will require 82% of the available coastal area to meet energy demands. 

READ MORE
JUN 219:54 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
PwC urges businesses to begin reporting green credentials with investment in mind

PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is encouraging seafood sector businesses to begin voluntary reporting of their green credentials, even if the EU’s “taxonomy for sustainable activities” won’t require them to yet.

PwC’s Daniel Næsse and Kristine Twomey outlined the EU’s classification system, which aims to establish a list of environmentally sustainable economic activities and to “play an important role helping the EU scale up sustainable investment and implement the European green deal”. 

READ MORE
JUN 219:30 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
The carbon footprints of farmed salmon broken down

Norwegian research body SINTEF has also been working on “climate accounting”, the term it gives to establishing the climate impacts of a business or industry.

As shown below, it has combined both an “environmentally extended input–output analysis” approach — a very macro-view of a sector — with an “environmental life cycle assessment”, which is far narrower, to come up with its best estimate of different seafood items’ carbon footprint.

READ MORE
JUN 219:10 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Eutrophication, mariculture ‘shading’ biggest issues for Norwegian kelp

As the European seaweed industry continues to grow, there are now a number of issues that have become fairly commonplace across the sector, explained Cecilie Linn Wathne, project manager of the Norwegian Blue Forests Network.

Chief among these is eutrophication — as the waters around the coast of Norway are repeatedly enriched by salmon farm waste nutrients, so too is the spread of fast-growing algae presenting a greater threat to the survival of kelp forests, as algal blooms form a blanket that effectively suffocates the underwater ecosystem.

READ MORE
JUN 219:08 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
SINTEF breaks down which salmon development licenses have been successful

Norwegian research body SINTEF has been looking into the nature of the country’s applicants to the development aquaculture license scheme, according to senior research scientist Trine Thorvaldsen.

As can be seen in the image below, almost one-third of applications were based on closed-containment units like Hauge Aqua Solutions’ “Egget”, while 25% were based on PE rings — the traditional plastic net-pen in use now.

READ MORE
JUN 218:49 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Polar, North Sea cod stocks most at risk from climate change threat

Presenting the results of a paper co-produced by Norwegian researchers, Olav Kjesbu, principal scientist at the country’s Institute of Marine Research, examined how sensitive separate fishery stocks are to climate change.

Kjesbu’s paper, published earlier this year, measured the impacts of increased temperature on a variety of proxies, including adult fish mobility, prey specificity, and spawning cycles, among others.

READ MORE
JUN 216:59 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Einar Wathne advises shrimp sector to follow in salmon’s footsteps for innovation

Aquaculture sector veteran Einar Wathne — investor, adviser and lecturer and assistant professor at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences — laid out his advice for the shrimp industry to try and go some way to catching up with salmon in terms of development.

He noted the Norwegian salmon sector had benefitted from strong government backing, including investment in R&D and a licensing model that absorbed a good deal of innovation risk for companies.

READ MORE
JUN 216:51 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
Egypt, Nigeria setbacks see African aquaculture volumes decline

Looking at the production of farmed fish and crustaceans worldwide, Manuel Barange, director of the FAO’s fisheries and aquaculture division, noted that all continents around the world had seen reasonable production growth in 2020 — except for Africa.

“The contribution of African aquaculture, 2.6% [of the global whole] — this is actually a contraction. The production of Africa’s aquaculture was contracted by 1.2% [in 2020].”

READ MORE
JUN 216:20 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
EU soon to launch new communications effort to improve aquaculture’s image

The EU’s Directorate-General for Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (DG MARE) is preparing to launch a new Europe-wide communications effort that will aim to improve perceptions of aquaculture, said Emilia Gargallo Gonzales, trade officer with DG MARE.

An important part of increasing the supply of sustainably farmed seafood in the EU is to improve public acceptance, DG MARE knows. Hence, part of its current strategy is to try and increase trust levels in aquaculture produce.

READ MORE
JUN 215:55 AM GMT
By Neil Ramsden
Multi-use ocean plans have aquaculture potential, but many barriers

There is great scope for EU member states with ocean access to engage in multi-use spatial planning, said Bela Buck of the Alfred Wegener Institute Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research.

As the EU strives to plan wind farms to safeguard future energy needs, joint planning from the earliest stages could open the door to mussel and seaweed farming, he said.

READ MORE
JUN 214:57 AM GMT
By Dan Gibson
123m metric tons from aquaculture in 2020

Kicking off this year’s forum, Manuel Barange, director of the fisheries and aquaculture division at the FAO, broke down the latest global aquaculture production data.

According to Barange, 123 million metric tons of aquaculture produce (live weight equivalent) were harvested worldwide in 2020 — the most recent year in the FAO’s records — of which 87m metric tons was animal protein, and the remaining 35m metric tons were a combination of seaweed, algae and cyanobacteria.

READ MORE
JUN 213:56 AM GMT
Program still set despite Norwegian airline strikes

NASF’s organizers expect the event’s program and schedule to go ahead as planned this week, despite a strike of aircraft technicians in Norway adding to difficulties in traveling around Europe.

Over 100 technicians were expected to be striking as of June 20, reports News in English, with some international and domestic Norwegian flights likely to be canceled.

READ MORE

Contact the authors neil.ramsden@undercurrentnews.com, dan.gibson@undercurrentnews.com, tom.seaman@undercurrentnews.com
